articles.title: Microsoft Outlook en panne : la messagerie ne fonctionne plus ce soir, l'entreprise confirme l'incident
articles.text:
De nombreux utilisateurs de la messagerie Outlook n'ont plus accès au service ce jeudi soir. Une panne affecte en effet une partie des fonctionnalités de la suite Microsoft 365, qui confirme l'incident.
La messagerie Outlook est inaccessible ce soir, en France et dans de nombreux pays du monde, pour un grand nombre d'utilisateurs. Microsoft a signalé ce jeudi 12 novembre en fin de journée une « dégradation de service » sur Microsoft 365 (offres Business et Entreprise). Selon l'entreprise, des utilisateurs pourraient ne pas réussir à se connecter à leur boîte aux lettres Exchange Online.
Ça coince pour Microsoft Outlook, en panne mercredi soir
Le problème touche plusieurs moyens d’accès. Microsoft cite notamment la version web d'Outlook, l'interface MAPI utilisée par le client Outlook de bureau, Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), qui synchronise la messagerie sur les smartphones, et l'API REST sur laquelle s’appuient de nombreuses applications tierces. Sur mobile, ça ne semble plus fonctionner non plus, notamment côté Outlook.
L'éditeur américain dit avoir repéré des erreurs de connectivité sur une partie de l'infrastructure d'Exchange Online qui reçoit et traite les demandes d'accès des utilisateurs. Ses équipes ont recueilli des journaux réseau pour trouver l'origine de ces erreurs et décider de la suite. Microsoft a constaté une surcharge de l'infrastructure concernée dans plusieurs régions, qui serait « probablement » à l'origine des erreurs de connectivité.
Pour rétablir la capacité, les équipes redémarrent et réparent les parties touchées de cette infrastructure. Elles examinent aussi une hausse inattendue du trafic venant d'un type de service précis, pour savoir si elle a causé cette surcharge. Microsoft ne dit pas de quel service il s'agit. En parallèle, l'entreprise cherche à rediriger le trafic vers une autre infrastructure afin de résoudre le problème plus vite. Elle ne donne toujours aucun délai de rétablissement, ni le nombre d’utilisateurs touchés.

articles.title: Webinar: See How Identity Blind Spots Put Your SOC at Risk and How to Close Them
articles.text:
Security teams have more alerts, logs, and monitoring tools than ever. Yet when an attack happens, one simple question can still take too long to answer: Who or what is behind this activity, and what can they access?
A suspicious login might belong to an employee. An unusual API call could come from a machine account. Or an AI agent might be accessing sensitive systems using permissions nobody has reviewed recently.
Your SIEM or EDR may catch the activity. But without knowing who owns that identity, what permissions it has, and which systems it can reach, your SOC is missing a critical part of the story.
And that missing context can turn a manageable incident into a much bigger problem.
Join this expert-led webinar to learn how real-time identity context can help your SOC investigate threats faster, understand what's at risk, and respond with confidence.
The Blind Spot Between Identity and Security Operations
Here's the problem.
Identity and access management (IAM) teams know who has access to what. Security operations teams monitor suspicious activity and respond to threats.
But these teams often work with different tools, different data, and different priorities.
When an alert comes in, SOC analysts may know what happened but still struggle to understand what it means.
Consider a compromised service account. An analyst might detect suspicious activity, but several questions remain:
- What applications and systems can this account access?
- Could an attacker use it to move deeper into the network?
- How much damage could it cause?
- Can the account be disabled without breaking a critical business process?
These answers matter. Blocking the wrong identity can disrupt production. Waiting too long can give an attacker more room to move.
And with machine identities and autonomous AI agents becoming part of everyday operations, the problem is getting more complicated.
More Identities, More Access, More Risk
Traditional security monitoring was largely built around users, devices, and network activity.
Today, organizations also rely on service accounts, API keys, automated workloads, and AI agents that can act without direct human involvement.
These identities often have access to important systems and data.
If one is compromised, detecting the suspicious action is only the beginning. Security teams also need to understand its permissions, connections, and potential impact.
That's where identity context changes the investigation.
Instead of treating every alert as an isolated event, analysts can connect suspicious activity to the identity behind it, understand how far an attacker could move, and choose a response that limits damage without unnecessarily interrupting operations.
What Does a Better SOC Response Actually Look Like?
The goal isn't to add another dashboard or generate more alerts.
It's to give analysts the information they need when an incident is unfolding.
That means connecting identity intelligence with existing SIEM and EDR alerts, so teams can:
- Investigate faster: Understand which human, machine, or AI identity is involved.
- See the real risk: Identify permissions, connected systems, and potential lateral movement.
- Contain threats safely: Respond to compromised credentials without unnecessarily disrupting critical automation.
- Work better together: Give IAM and SOC teams shared workflows, clear escalation paths, and common response goals.
The difference is simple: knowing that something suspicious happened is useful. Knowing what it can affect and how to stop it is far more valuable.
Learn How to Close the Gap
In the upcoming webinar, Fuel the SOC with Identity Context: Securing Humans, Machines, and AI Agents, security experts will explore how organizations can bring IAM and security operations together.
Drawing on real-world enterprise deployments, the session will cover practical approaches to enriching security alerts with identity context, investigating lateral movement, understanding the potential blast radius of an attack, and improving incident response without disrupting production systems.
It will also explain how teams can align around shared metrics, escalation processes, and response playbooks.
Your SOC already has the alerts. Now give it the context to act.

articles.title: La France lance un centre international de l’IA de défense à Rennes, et veut y rallier ses alliés
articles.text:
La France va lancer à Rennes l'ICAID, un centre international dédié à l'intelligence artificielle de défense. Ouvert aux armées alliées, il sera officiellement lancé le 20 novembre et doit devenir opérationnel courant 2027.
Le ministère des Armées a officialisé ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026 la création de l'International Center for Artificial Intelligence in Defence (ICAID), un centre international pour l'intelligence artificielle de défense qui sera implanté à Rennes. Il sera officiellement lancé le 20 novembre, lors d'une conférence d'établissement de deux jours fermée à la presse, certes, mais qui on le sait réunira les nations prêtes à s'engager aux côtés de la France.
Un centre pour aider les armées à mieux choisir leur IA
Le ministère des Armées l'a constaté depuis un moment. Les champs de bataille se transforment à grande vitesse, et l'IA pèse désormais lourd dans la supériorité militaire. Le fameux centre devra aider ses membres à mieux en comprendre les enjeux. Il devra surtout développer l'expertise et les méthodes pour concevoir, acquérir, déployer et évaluer des services d'IA dans la défense. Autrement dit, savoir bâtir, acheter et jauger ces outils, et pas seulement les utiliser.
On en sait un peu plus sur la feuille de route de l'ICAID. D'abord, le centre va devoir créer une communauté d'intérêt entre partenaires pour accélérer l'adoption de l'IA. Ensuite, il aura pour rôle de circuler les bonnes pratiques et d'anticiper les évolutions technologiques. Enfin, il fera remonter les retours d'expérience des forces, pour coller au plus près de leurs besoins.
Cette exigence n'est pas farfelue en tout cas, puisqu'on se souvient qu'en septembre, CNN avait révélé qu'une hallucination d'IA, transformée en rapport de renseignement, avait failli provoquer un affrontement armé entre les États-Unis et la Chine.
Sur l'IA de défense, la France joue désormais en équipe
Alors pourquoi le ministère des Armées a-t-il choisi Rennes ? Certains l'ont compris avant qu'on vous l'écrive. La ville bretonne, souvent considérée comme la capitale française de la cybersécurité, est au cœur de l'écosystème numérique et IA de défense français. L'AMIAD, l'Agence ministérielle pour l'intelligence artificielle de Défense, a déjà des équipes à Bruz, à quelques kilomètres. Son directeur, Bertrand Rondepierre, parle de « rupture technologique » et veut en accélérer la maîtrise « aux côtés de nos alliés ».
L'ICAID prolonge une année chargée pour l'agence. En janvier, elle a été chargée de piloter l'accord-cadre signé par le ministère avec Mistral AI pour équiper toutes les armées en IA générative. En février, elle a créé avec l'ENSTA le LARIAD, un laboratoire consacré à la robotique et à l'IA de défense.
De l'autre côté de l'Atlantique, aux États-Unis, l'intelligence artificielle militaire passe d'abord par des contrats avec les géants de la tech, comme OpenAI, Google ou NVIDIA, qui a une nouvelle patronne. Avec l'ICAID, Paris ajoute une dimension diplomatique à sa stratégie et mise sur une coalition d'États. Il faudra toutefois patienter, car le centre n'atteindra sa capacité opérationnelle que courant 2027. Et la question des moyens consacrés se pose encore. Cet été, un rapport sénatorial sur les drones notait qu'aucun financement n'était prévu pour l'IA de défense dans l'enveloppe qu'il examinait.

articles.title: A new off-grid fiber-optic system spots underwater targets 100km out
articles.text:
'Detect an oil tanker at 66 miles': Navies queue up for billion-dollar European miltech company which humbles fiber-optic to 'listen' to acoustic vibrations underwater
35 navies line up to test this military technology
- Optics11 is discussing underwater surveillance systems with dozens of navies
- Its sensors reportedly detect oil tankers from approximately 100 kilometers away
- The company has already secured between five and ten naval customers
Dutch defense technology company Optics11 is attracting interest from dozens of navies with fiber-optic sensors designed to detect underwater activity across long distances.
According to its CEO, Paul Heiden, the company already serves between five and ten naval customers, while approximately 35 paid evaluations are planned for 2026.
The technology uses light traveling through optical fibers to identify acoustic disturbances, offering an alternative to conventional underwater detection systems used by naval forces.
Optics11 attracts naval customers with fiber-optic underwater detection technology
Optics11's equipment monitors underwater acoustic activity by measuring tiny changes in light traveling through specialized optical fibers installed along the seabed or deployed behind vessels.
The company sells two principal systems, including OptiBarrier for fixed underwater surveillance and OptiArray, which operates as a towed sensor arrangement.
Heiden said the technology can identify an oil tanker from approximately 100 kilometers (66 miles) away, through underwater acoustic monitoring.
That detection capability could make the technology particularly useful for monitoring maritime traffic, identifying unusual underwater activity, and supporting anti-submarine surveillance operations.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The company is developing a towed sensor system for the Royal Netherlands Navy's future Orka-class submarines, which France's Naval Group will supply.
Its existing industry relationships include Saab, Rheinmetall, Fincantieri, Thales, and Exail, alongside Ocean Infinity, which Britain selected for its Atlantic Bastion underwater surveillance initiative.
Optics11 also works with several European naval forces, with ongoing evaluations involving Germany, Sweden, the United Kingdom, Belgium, and France.
The technology produces substantially more acoustic information than conventional piezoelectric sonar sensors, requiring specialized software to interpret the resulting underwater measurements.
Third-party software cannot handle Optics11's data density
Optics11 has developed proprietary software to process its sensor readings after finding that existing third-party sonar applications could not handle its unusually dense datasets.
“Initially I thought we could work with a partner, but our data density is so high that we couldn't derive any value from third-party sonar processing software,” said Paul Heiden.
AI also reduced the number of software developers required, allowing the company to employ about 10 specialists instead of the 60 to 80 previously anticipated.
Heiden said those savings allow Optics11 to concentrate more resources on acoustic specialists who understand underwater sound propagation across different seabed conditions.
The Royal Netherlands Navy has supported the company for at least eight years, providing millions of euros through subsidies, technical guidance, and submarine testing opportunities.
Optics11 raised about €100 million in the past 15 months, including €25 million in venture debt from the European Investment Bank.
The company will pursue another funding round in 2027, potentially seeking a valuation exceeding $1 billion despite remaining unprofitable.
Optics11 is expected to achieve a positive cash flow in 2028, while planned expansion includes additional offices and recruitment across Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
The company is keeping its most important developments under wraps through confidential business information rather than patents.
Publicly documenting sensitive military technology could expose valuable technical capabilities.
“You can’t publish this, you can’t patent it, so it all has to be kept secret, and we’re getting great help from the Dutch government to keep it truly secret,” Heiden said.
Via Defense News

Efosa has been writing about technology for over 7 years, initially driven by curiosity but now fueled by a strong passion for the field. He holds both a Master's and a PhD in sciences, which provided him with a solid foundation in analytical thinking.

articles.title: Estos son los correos electrónicos que recibieron los empleados de Nvidia sobre la renuncia de Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Nvidia atraviesa un período complejo: Jensen Huang, cofundador y ex CEO, renunció tras escándalos de infidelidad, entre ellos uno con una presunta espía china, de acuerdo con New York Times.
Los empleados de la compañía tecnológica conocieron la renuncia de Huang y el nombramiento de Colette Kress como CEO interina, así como su primer pronunciamiento a través de correo electrónicos.
Qué dicen los correos electrónicos que recibieron los empleados de Nvidia
Según The Verge, el correo en el que confirmaron la salida de Jensen Huang como CEO fue el siguiente:
“Asunto: Comunicado del presidente de la Junta Directiva de NVIDIA
Estimados empleados de NVIDIA:
Les escribo para compartir una actualización importante. Jensen renunció como CEO y miembro de la Junta Directiva, y la Junta le pidió a nuestra directora financiera, Colette Kress, que se desempeñe como CEO interina mientras realiza la búsqueda de un sucesor permanente, considerando candidatos internos y externos. Yo asumiré como el primer presidente de la Junta Directiva en la historia de la compañía.
Como directora financiera durante más de 13 años, Colette ha sido una figura clave en la estrategia de crecimiento y capital de NVIDIA. Posee un profundo conocimiento de este negocio y de los mercados en los que operamos. La Junta tiene plena confianza en la capacidad de Colette para cumplir nuestros compromisos con los accionistas, clientes, socios y con cada uno de ustedes.
Las contribuciones de Jensen a NVIDIA son profundas. NVIDIA es una de las empresas tecnológicas más influyentes del mundo. Fuimos pioneros en la computación acelerada, definimos la GPU moderna y construimos la plataforma que impulsó la inteligencia artificial.
La Junta toma con seriedad su deber como administradora de esta gran compañía.
La fortaleza de esta compañía reside en sus empleados, su equipo directivo, su capacidad técnica y su ecosistema de socios. Confío en que, bajo el liderazgo de Colette y con el pleno respaldo de la Junta, continuaremos haciendo crecer nuestro negocio y liderando el avance de la industria. Gracias por su enfoque, su profesionalismo y su compromiso con NVIDIA.
Harvey Jones."
De acuerdo con el mismo medio estadounidse, el primer correo firmado por Kress fue:
“Asunto: RE: Comunicado del presidente de la Junta Directiva de NVIDIA
Estimados integrantes de NVIDIA:
Creo profundamente en esta compañía y en su futuro. Por encima de todo, creo en cada uno de ustedes, en nuestros clientes y socios, y en el papel fundamental que desempeñamos cada día en la economía global.
La Junta Directiva, Estaff y yo reconocemos que este ha sido un período extraordinariamente difícil, y quiero que sepan cuánto agradecemos su resiliencia, profesionalismo y dedicación continua. Gracias.
Esta compañía ha logrado tanto gracias al trabajo que cada uno de ustedes aporta todos los días. Ustedes son nuestra mayor fortaleza. En los próximos días recibirán más información de parte del equipo directivo sobre nuestro futuro conjunto, y realizaremos una reunión de toda la compañía el 18 de noviembre a las 9.00, hora del Pacífico.
Desempeñamos un papel fundamental en la construcción de la tecnología que impulsa la revolución de la inteligencia artificial, y tenemos un trabajo importante por delante. Avancemos juntos, entonces, con la misma determinación y el compromiso que siempre han definido a esta compañía.
Gracias por todo lo que hacen.
Colette."
Qué ocurrió con Jensen Huang
Jensen Huang renunció este jueves 12 de noviembre de 2026 a la presidencia, dirección ejecutiva y junta directiva de Nvidia, cargos que ocupaba desde la fundación de la empresa.
La salida se produjo después de que la compañía abriera una investigación independiente por reportes de un posible intento de inteligencia extranjera para influir sobre él. Según AP, la renuncia ocurrió tras la difusión de denuncias sobre relaciones extramatrimoniales.
Nvidia nombró de inmediato a su directora financiera, Colette Kress, como CEO interina mientras busca un sucesor permanente entre candidatos internos y externos.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: 59 Linux Kernel Bugs, Falcon Spyware, GSocket Backdoors + 17 More Stories
articles.text:
A search result isn't always safe. An access request isn't always harmless. And a familiar account doesn't always mean a familiar person is using it. Simple things to remember. Yet a surprising amount of this week's trouble starts right there.
Attackers are using fake websites, stolen access, and trusted tools to get into places they shouldn't be. AI is helping them build attacks faster, while also giving them new systems to target. Some intruders are staying hidden even after security holes are fixed. Others are moving stolen money through a maze of transactions. And researchers keep finding small coding mistakes that can cause much bigger problems. Different stories, but much of the trouble comes down to making something dangerous look normal.
There is some good news, too. Criminal servers have been seized, and a few defenses are getting stronger. Still, plenty of things are going wrong in ways that shouldn't be this easy. Here's what turned up this week.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  North Korea's crypto laundering network The North Korean threat actors linked to the record-breaking theft of $6.43 billion from Binance are using a highly complex and clearly automated method to launder the illicit proceeds. "Since the theft it has used more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions," Dr. Tom Robinson, Elliptic's founder and chief scientist, said. "Around $3.0 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, mostly as ETH and BTC. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out." The attackers have also been observed creating six meme coins on the NEAR blockchain network (FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI, and SINU) to launder a slice of the ill-gotten funds, passing through about $430,000 of the stolen cryptocurrency. The goal is to disguise the path of money and make it harder to trace where the assets eventually end up. Other tactics used to make funds tracing more difficult include moving between blockchains through bridges and cross-chain swap services, swapping between assets on DEXs, hopping through lending vaults and liquid-staking services, and mixing bitcoin through coinjoins, and ETH and SOL through the Privacy Cash privacy pool. The Binance breach is by no means the first to affect a major cryptocurrency exchange, but it is the biggest ever by magnitude. North Korean spokesperson Kim Yo Jong denied the country's role in the attack, calling it an "absurd" effort to "damage the international image of the DPRK."
- 
  
  GSocket detections surge 356% Microsoft said it has observed multiple incidents in which threat actors deployed GSocket, an open-source remote access tool, on internet-facing Linux servers to maintain access after the original vulnerabilities were addressed, turning a single web application compromise into persistent access. "Because GSocket relays traffic through a shared public network, there is no threat actor-owned IP address or domain to block," Microsoft said. "Defenders should look for GSocket deployment, persistence, privilege escalation, and outbound connections on affected hosts, not treat application patching alone as complete remediation." According to telemetry data, devices with GSocket-related detections increased 356.2% from March through August 2026, with most of them associated with PHP web applications, cPanel hosts, and Apache. The majority of targets of GSocket activity are in the education and research sector, followed by technology and communications, manufacturing, and government entities.
- 
  
  235 servers seized in Europol takedown Europol, along with global partners, has disrupted the criminal infrastructure behind GootLoader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware, seizing 235 servers and 257 domains. "The operation targeted 'cybercrime-as-a-service' models, where these tools enabled further crimes like ransomware attacks and data theft," Europol said. As part of the operation, authorities have identified over 6 million victim credentials. "The suspects were using these credentials, stolen from the victims after they infected them, to sell them and later be used for other cyber-attacks such as ransomware," Europol added.
- 
  
  Browser-based espionage targets governments A command and control (C2) framework called Falcon (aka XG or Xiàng Gē) has been found compromising victims' browsers by running malicious JavaScript. Falcon shares near-identical URL structures, payload delivery mechanisms and communication protocols with PeckBirdy, another JavaScript C2 framework that came to light early this year. It's assessed that Falcon and PeckBirdy represent variants of the same core framework. "An actor leveraged Falcon to compromise visitors of webmail portals and government web applications by placing malicious JavaScript directly within these sites," Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 said. "Operating entirely inside the browser context, attackers have used the framework to sideload malicious Chrome extensions and steal the following information: passwords, emails, session cookies, [and] communications." Falcon has also been used to deliver an implant dubbed Antino, which uses Microsoft OneDrive as a C2 channel. The activity has targeted government entities in one Middle Eastern country and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026. "The campaigns we observed targeted ministries of foreign affairs, defense and interior, and law enforcement agencies, consistent with strategic intelligence collection objectives," Unit 42 said.
- 
  
  59 Linux kernel bugs uncovered Microsoft said its scan of a subset of Linux kernel subsystems from late May to mid-June 2026 unearthed 26,502 raw findings using MDASH, which subsequently formed the basis for 59 public upstream reports and 33 assigned CVEs. This includes working root privilege-escalation exploits for eight of those CVEs, such as CVE-2026-64563. "CVE-2026-64563 is a one-line state-reset bug in rhashtable, the Linux kernel's shared resizable hash table," Microsoft said. "Because callers trust the object pointers returned by a table walk, this small library flaw enabled a stable local privilege escalation on Linux -- and affected Android with SELinux enforcing -- without requiring special kernel configurations or user namespaces."
- 
  
  AI-assisted espionage in Central Asia An exposed Silent Lynx server has uncovered cyber espionage operations targeting Central Asian governments and critical infrastructure from April to October 2026. "The directory held the group's tooling alongside data from active intrusions into government and critical infrastructure organisations across the region, and the AI agent the operator relied on to run them," CloudSEK said. "We assess with medium confidence that the operator has a Kazakhstan nexus: the operation runs in Russian, and the operator's own test traffic came from a residential Kazakh connection, which supports existing vendor assessments. The collection priorities, spanning transport, defence correspondence and resource ministries in neighbouring states, point to regional intelligence gathering rather than financial motive."
- 
  
  Contractor access fuels ransomware attacks A new Russian-speaking ransomware group called Citrus is targeting Windows systems in corporate environments. The attackers have been found to gain access through compromised contractor accounts and leverage AI-generated PowerShell scripts, batch files, and commands during later stages of the intrusion. In an attempt to reduce visibility, the threat actor removes tools and output files after execution, clears command history, and deletes event logs. The group also disguises tools and related artifacts with benign-looking names to make them appear legitimate by using a trusted brand name. The ransomware is a Sn00py-family ransomware variant written in Go. On Windows systems, the malware encrypts user files and appends the .citrus extension, while taking steps to hinder recovery and incident response. Kaspersky said the activity shares several similarities with Toy Ghouls. "Citrus stands out for the way AI-generated content appears to support hands-on intrusion activity on compromised systems," said Stanislav Larinsky, Kaspersky Security Services expert. "In the cases we investigated, the attackers combined third-party account access, privilege-escalation attempts and domain-wide deployment techniques. These incidents show how limited contractor access can become a path to broader compromise if it is not tightly controlled and continuously monitored."
- 
  
  Malicious AI agents exploit OAuth consent Proofpoint has disclosed details of a new technique called BluePhishing that's described as the "next evolution of OAuth consent abuse," enabling bad actors to leverage agent identities like Microsoft Entra Agent ID for initial access. BluePhishing "socially engineer[s] victims into granting consent to a malicious agent blueprint for initial access," it said. "Analogous to app consent phishing where attackers use client credentials to gain initial access to a tenant, BluePhishing extends this technique to the agent ecosystem. By exploiting gaps in visibility and governance around emerging AI agent adoption, attackers can abuse one-time consent links to create agent identities in target tenants, obtain access tokens, and operate with the privileges assigned to those agents."
- 
  
  AI age checks expand worldwide Meta has announced that it's expanding its AI age-estimation technology globally to automatically place millions of teens in Teen Account protections on Instagram. "We use AI technology to find people we suspect to be teens, even if they use an adult birthday, and place them in Teen Account protections," Meta said. "As a result, millions more teens across the world who use Instagram will receive these built-in protections, even if they've misrepresented their age." In Australia, Meta has opted to use Apple's age-range signal as another method to help understand age.
- 
  
  OAuth support for Exchange migrations Microsoft 365 Mailbox Replication Service (MRS) has added support for OAuth as an authentication method when migrating mailboxes between Microsoft 365 and an on-premises Exchange environment. "Once OAuth for MRS is configured, tenant administrators can create an OAuth migration endpoint and use it in migration batches or in onboarding and offboarding move jobs," Microsoft said. "You can use this method in both hybrid and non-hybrid organizations."
- 
  
  NTLM signing hardened against relay attacks In more Microsoft-related news, the tech giant has incorporated additional protections into Windows starting November 10, 2026, that address CVE-2026-118737 (CVSS score: 8.1), a critical remote code execution flaw in Remote Procedure Call Runtime that could allow an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network. "These updates represent the first phase of improvements to NTLM message signing," Microsoft said. "These changes help ensure that authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing, reducing exposure to relay attacks." To that end, Windows servers will begin requiring NTLM signing by default starting May 2027.
- 
  
  Exposed cloud credentials lingered 18 months Details have emerged about a now-patched security flaw affecting the Planning Inspectorate, an executive agency of the United Kingdom's Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG). The issue involved a complete Microsoft Entra ID application credential that was committed in plaintext to a GitHub repository. "Although removed from the branch, the commit was orphaned via a force push and remained retrievable via GitHub's raw object CDN for 18 months," ControlPlane said. The client secret was deleted about 20 minutes after responsible disclosure on August 26, 2026.
- 
  
  Fake software sites spread infostealer An SEO poisoning campaign is using fake websites impersonating the Chocolatey package manager and the Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS) tool to distribute a Python-based malware called Armorsteal. "The installer deployed a Python 3.11 runtime environment and three main components providing remote access, surveillance, and information stealing capabilities, with the Python code protected by Pyarmor," Zscaler said. "The remote access component communicates with a command-and-control (C2) server, downloads additional modules, and executes remote tasks. The surveillance component logs keystrokes, monitors the clipboard, captures screenshots, and displays fake cryptocurrency wallet notifications. The information stealing component targets browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, saved passwords, SSH keys, and Steam data."
- 
  
  Localized phishing delivers banking trojan A new Grandoreiro banking malware campaign is targeting users across Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru through country-specific phishing lures that are tailored to each region. "The campaign uses localized phishing lures, primarily in Spanish, with some observed using Portuguese even when targeting Spanish-speaking countries," Arctic Wolf said. "The phishing chain relies on recently registered domains and layered redirection to hinder detection. The final payload is retrieved through a Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) seeded with the current date. The downloaded ZIP archive uses a deeply nested folder structure populated with two legitimate PE files and two benign PDF documents. A VBScript file located in the archive's root directory acts as the primary payload, employing junk code and multiple layers of obfuscation before reconstructing and launching a Delphi-based loader." The loader masquerades as a PDF reader and is used to fetch and run the banking trojan.
- 
  
  AI search results targeted by scam sites Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 said it detected an indirect prompt injection (IDPI) campaign across 26 domains. "These are attempting black-hat Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to game AI-powered search results," Unit 42 said. "Almost all of the 26 pages have very similar content, presenting as AI-powered digital asset trading platforms. These sites appear to be scam sites designed to collect user information. The injected prompt is set to be hidden from a regular web user but likely visible to an AI agent. These attacks intend to poison SEO and manipulate AI agents to eventually get users to visit these sites."
- 
  
  PyPI adds release verification signals The Python Package Index (PyPI) has added a security tab to its project pages, giving developers easy access to security signals. "The new security tab communicates release provenance states and displays per-file attestations, giving you a dedicated place to verify where the release files came from," PyPI said. "PyPI calculates each release's provenance state by checking whether each release file has an attestation."
- 
  
  100+ domains spread credential stealer The information stealer known as RevStealer is being propagated as part of an "industrial-scale, financially motivated campaign" that uses game cheats and AI tools as lures. The payload is distributed through more than 100 interconnected domains, trojanized Electron applications masquerading as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, and hijacked YouTube distribution channels, per Akatsuki Legion. "Once executed, the malware performs a ten-point weighted sandbox-evasion scoring routine, decrypts an AES-256-CBC in-memory payload, and leverages fourteen indirect syscall wrappers and FNV-1a API hashing to bypass user-mode hooks before systematically harvesting credentials from browsers, password managers, cryptocurrency wallets, Steam, Roblox, Battle.net, EA Desktop, and Minecraft; then exfiltrating the loot as streamed, encrypted typed records over HTTPS, with a resilient Polygon blockchain dead-drop resolver standing by as a fallback command-and-control channel," the independent adversary research group said.
- 
  
  AI infrastructure becomes an attack target Threat actors have increasingly targeted AI orchestration platforms over the past few months, according to Sekoia. This is because "they concentrate API keys, enterprise data, and access to external tools," it added. This includes Flowise, which has been affected by multiple security flaws like CVE-2025-59528 and CVE-2026-41264. In one exploitation attempt recorded in August 2026, a suspected Chinese-speaking actor abused legitimate Flowise functionality to conduct automated reconnaissance and attempted to hijack the LLM agent to serve as an offensive analysis vector against external targets. "The attacker attempted to turn the AI agent into an interactive offensive assistant, submitting real-world reconnaissance data (Nightingale/Redis infrastructure) to generate custom exploitation playbooks and target analysis," Sekoia said.
- 
  
  AI-built phishing kits multiply LevelBlue has disclosed details of a family of phishing kits named BlackApex, DarkApex, SPY, XXX101-TOKEN, OGPARKER1, W1-TOKEN, and ALIBOBO-TOKEN that are used to facilitate device code phishing attacks using shared document lures. The findings once again demonstrate how AI can speed up the development of a convincing multi-brand phishing kit. "Across all of its lures, the source shows traits we associate with AI-generated code, whether from direct prompts to a language model or from a person working alongside an AI coding assistant," LevelBlue said. "The code, endpoints, and interface are the same across all of them. We cannot say whether these names reflect separate operators, resellers or customers of a single kit, but the pattern is consistent with a shared product being rebranded and redeployed."
- 
  
  AI verifies Signal security properties Google's DeepMind has introduced AlphaProof Code, which brings together human experts and AI agents to verify software and mathematically demonstrate that it works as intended. The multi-agent AI framework has been used to prove key security properties of libsignal, the Signal protocol's reference implementation, at the machine-code level. "AlphaProof Code consists of a human-guided agent for writing Lean specifications of code, a formal semantics of AArch64 machine code, and a team of autonomous prover agents whose proofs are accepted only if Lean’s kernel checks them against the approved specification," DeepMind said. "Applied to libsignal, our agents generated about 6.5 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof code, resting on about 26,000 lines of trusted specifications and AArch64 semantics. The proofs cover Signal’s post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, establishing forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy."
That's the lot for this week. Some attacks were carefully planned. Others relied on old mistakes, trusted accounts, or someone clicking the wrong thing. AI is showing up on both sides, making attacks easier to build while helping researchers find problems faster. The tools keep changing, but attackers still seem happy to use whatever works.
The good news is that some of these threats are being stopped, and defenses are slowly catching up. The bad news is that fixing a bug, removing a file, or blocking an attacker doesn't always mean the problem is gone. Sometimes the damage sticks around longer than anyone expects. Worth keeping in mind before the next batch of headlines arrives.

articles.title: Synchron, rival de Neuralink, frenó las pruebas de su implante cerebral por una falla en un cable
articles.text:
Synchron, la empresa de Brooklyn que compite con Neuralink, de Elon Musk, frenó los ensayos clínicos de la segunda generación de su implante cerebral porque el dispositivo no funcionó como esperaba en los primeros voluntarios. Lo informó la revista Wired, que también supo de despidos y de un cambio de sede.
La compañía confirmó la pausa en una declaración a Wired. Dijo que la decidió ella misma, tras detectar un problema de rendimiento en el cable que lleva las señales desde el implante hasta la electrónica implantada. Aseguró que la falla no está en el implante y que no se identificaron problemas de seguridad.
Synchron precisó que se trató de una decisión propia y no de una orden de la FDA, la agencia que aprueba medicamentos y dispositivos médicos en Estados Unidos. La empresa dijo además que pasó a fabricar y diseñar ese cable en sus propias instalaciones.
Un implante que no requiere cirugía cerebral
El dispositivo se llama Stentrode. Es un tubo de malla similar a un stent, el pequeño resorte que abre arterias, que entra por la vena yugular, en la base del cuello, y se guía con un catéter hasta apoyarlo sobre la zona del cerebro que controla el movimiento. Por eso la empresa lo presenta como menos invasivo.
La primera versión se conectaba con un cable externo apoyado sobre el pecho. 10 voluntarios de Estados Unidos y Australia la recibieron, según Wired, y enviaron correos y mensajes, navegaron por internet y compraron con el pensamiento. También controlaron Alexa, un iPad y el visor Vision Pro de Apple sin usar las manos ni la voz.
La segunda generación tiene menos electrodos y es totalmente inalámbrica: se conecta por Bluetooth. Synchron inició este año, en primavera, un ensayo en varios centros de Estados Unidos, con sedes asociadas en Australia y Canadá. Algunos participantes ya tenían el dispositivo implantado.
Fuentes cercanas a los ensayos, que pidieron no ser identificadas, dijeron al medio citado que esos centros pausaron recientemente la incorporación de nuevos voluntarios porque el aparato no funcionaba como debía. Dos de los cinco centros estadounidenses con los que habló la revista confirmaron que el reclutamiento está detenido.
Un coordinador de uno de esos centros afirmó que la pausa no se debía a un problema de seguridad, sino a que Synchron revisaba el aparato para comprobar que obtenía los datos que busca.
Despidos y un nuevo dispositivo en San Diego
Synchron también se reestructura, según Wired: elimina puestos de trabajo, reduce su presencia en Nueva York y arma un equipo en San Diego. Su sitio web y su perfil en LinkedIn listan alrededor de una docena de vacantes allí, entre ellas ingenieros eléctricos y mecánicos, diseñadores de microchips y especialistas en materiales.
Ese equipo trabajará en el cable y el implante mejorados, y en un dispositivo distinto que la empresa aún no reveló. Su página dice que ese aparato irá “más allá de los vasos sanguíneos”, y su director ejecutivo, Tom Oxley, había dicho al medio mencionado que planeaba uno capaz de alcanzar varias regiones del cerebro a la vez.
Los ensayos en curso son un paso necesario hacia un estudio más grande, llamado pivotal, que la FDA exige antes de autorizar la venta de un dispositivo. Oxley dijo a la revista que la empresa mantiene “mucha confianza” en que el implante pueda ser una terapia de primera línea.
Synchron fue valuada en casi USD 1.000 millones tras una ronda de USD 200 millones el otoño pasado. Entre sus inversores figuran Khosla Ventures y los fondos de Bill Gates y Jeff Bezos. Neuralink, en cambio, alcanzó una valuación de hasta USD 42.000 millones en operaciones del mercado secundario este verano.
En 2024, el implante de Neuralink también falló en su primer voluntario, Noland Arbaugh: varios de sus hilos se salieron del cerebro semanas después de la cirugía y perdió el control del cursor, que la empresa recuperó modificando su algoritmo de lectura.
Synchron dijo que retomará la incorporación de voluntarios cuando termine las mejoras de hardware, sin precisar una fecha.

articles.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
articles.text:
Public exploit code released earlier this week claims that a local Windows user can gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver.
The proof of concept, called SignDrop, targets a log-authentication feature added to the driver last year. It abuses how clfs.sys creates companion files when a privileged process opens a prepared log, using path redirection to take control of the operation. Microsoft has not confirmed the claimed flaw, assigned a CVE, or released a fix.
The researcher behind the exploit, who publishes under the name MSNightmare, released the code and a detailed writeup on GitHub on Tuesday, the same day the company published its November security updates.
CLFS is a logging subsystem built into Windows. Its driver has been a frequent target for privilege escalation: 10 CLFS flaws appear in CISA's catalog of vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in attacks, including one used in ransomware campaigns in April 2025.
To reduce that exposure, Microsoft added an authentication check to CLFS log files in updates for Windows 11 25H2, 26H1, and Windows Server 2025 shipped in October 2025. The check attaches a hash-based message authentication code, built from log data and a key unique to each machine.
The driver then parses only log files it wrote. A companion .cnpf file stores recovery data beside each log and is created with the same security attributes as the original, according to the company's logfile authentication page.
SignDrop targets the creation of that companion file. According to the proof-of-concept code, a standard user prepares a CLFS log and container with paths the user controls. When a privileged process later opens that log, the driver creates the .cnpf file in the privileged process's security context rather than the user's.
The exploit uses object manager symbolic links to redirect that file creation to a location the attacker chooses. In the published code, the privileged process is the Defender antimalware service, triggered through its update interface.
"Everything is done properly by Microsoft here but the logic allows abuse," the researcher wrote.
Because the .cnpf file inherits the original log's permissions, the result is a file created as SYSTEM that the standard user can write to. The researcher says that can be chained into a SYSTEM shell.
The exploit was tested on Windows 11 26H2, a Windows 11 26H2 Experimental build, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental, according to the repository. Systems are affected when the CLFS authentication registry mode is set to 0 (enforced) or 1 (learning). Systems older than 90 days typically move from learning to enforcement automatically, so the default configuration on established installations is the one the exploit targets.
A registry value of 2 or 3 means the mitigation is disabled. That takes the system outside the claimed attack surface, but the researcher and the driver's own documentation both warn against it: disabling lets CLFS parse tampered log files, reopening the memory corruption flaws the protection was built to prevent.
Independent Test
Sungyup Nam, head of research at Korean security firm 78researchlab, reported in a published assessment today that researcher Heewon Song of the firm's PurpleHound offensive content team tested the exploit and found that it works. Song assessed that it does not run reliably enough for operational use, Nam wrote.
Defender must be enabled for the published chain to succeed. Running the exploit changes every UAC prompt to open a standard user shell and a SYSTEM shell, blocking other actions and making the attack noticeable to anyone at the machine.
The repository claims the technique can work against any antimalware engine whose process runs with elevated privileges. That broader claim has not been tested.
What Defenders Can Do
No CVE, advisory, or patch for SignDrop appeared in the November security updates. The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog does not list it, and no attacks using the exploit have been reported.
Administrators can check their exposure by reading the CLFS authentication mode at HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication, where a Mode value of 0 or 1 falls within the researcher's claimed scope. The vendor's mitigation guidance describes the setting and the risks of disabling it.
The researcher has released a series of exploits targeting Windows and Defender since April. The vendor confirmed an earlier Defender exploit called RoguePlanet in June as CVE-2026-50656 and patched it the following month.
The ShieldBreak bypass followed in August and was assigned CVE-2026-69414. Three of the researcher's earlier Defender flaws have been exploited in attacks.
SignDrop is a different class of issue. Where the earlier exploits targeted race conditions in Defender's file handling, this one targets the CLFS driver's own authentication feature. The vendor's security update guide is the place to watch for a response.

articles.title: Anthropic pourrait abandonner rapidement son partenariat avec SpaceX... ce qui réjouit Elon Musk
articles.text:
La capacité de calcul devient une denrée de plus en plus convoitée dans le monde de l'IA. La preuve avec cette réaction étonnante d'Elon Musk !
Au printemps temps, Anthropic concluait un accord d'ampleur avec SpaceX afin de louer les capacités de calcul de ses supercalculateurs. Mais six mois plus tard, on semble être sur une tendance inverse, avec SpaceX qui n'aurait aucun problème à récupérer cette capacité, dans un univers très fluctuant défini par Elon Musk lui-même comme relevant du « casino ».
Anthropic pourrait mettre fin à son partenariat avec SpaceX dès l'an prochain
Anthropic se prépare à une année 2027 exceptionnelle, juste après l'entrée en Bourse du créateur de Claude. Et il pourrait y avoir du bouleversement, d'après ce qui a été dit dans une rencontre effectuée chez Anthropic.
Les dirigeants de la firme auraient ainsi expliqué dans une réunion avec des analystes financiers que le contrat avec SpaceX ne serait pas prolongé au-delà de la mi-2027. Pour rappel, le contrat passé entre les deux parties intègre une clause de résiliation à partir de l'année prochaine, qui permet d'y mettre fin dans un délai de 90 jours.
Elon Musk réagit positivement à cette annonce !
La même rencontre, dont le twitto Jukan se fait l'écho, a aussi été l'occasion d'autres annonces. La direction d'Anthropic a ainsi affirmé posséder la stabilité et les meilleurs talents pour faire mieux que le secteur de l'open source, et avoir aussi investi 10 milliards de dollars pour l'entraînement de la famille de modèles Claude 5.5.
Pour ce qui est de la capacité de calcul de SpaceX, il est à noter qu'Elon Musk semble loin d'être chagriné par l'idée d'une perte potentielle de contrat. « Nous serions ravis de reprendre la capacité de calcul. Pas de problème » a-t-il ainsi lancé dans un message sur X. Mais l'homme le plus riche du monde est dubitatif quant à l'idée. « Je pense que c'est tout le contraire qui va se produire » a-t-il ainsi pronostiqué.

articles.title: Un gobernador de la Reserva Federal pidió prepararse para graves trastornos en el empleo por la IA
articles.text:
El gobernador de la Reserva Federal Michael Barr dijo que Estados Unidos debe prepararse para “graves trastornos de corto plazo” en el mercado laboral por la inteligencia artificial. Lo planteó este jueves 12 de noviembre en la Universidad de Yale, en un discurso sobre IA y desigualdad.
Barr aclaró que no hace una predicción: sus palabras sugieren prepararse para tensiones sociales, no anticiparlas. El gobernador reconoció que hasta ahora hubo “relativamente poco desplazamiento” de trabajadores por la IA y que hay datos de que la tecnología mejora la productividad de algunos empleados.
También hay señales en sentido contrario. “Ya vemos indicios de que la IA puede sustituir mano de obra en algunos sectores, en especial a los trabajadores más jóvenes y con menos experiencia”, afirmó. Las tareas fáciles de automatizar, con reglas claras y resultados predecibles, podrían sufrir una sustitución rápida. En cambio, las que exigen criterio, coordinación, relaciones personales o creatividad tendrían más probabilidades de que la IA complemente al trabajador en lugar de reemplazarlo.
El trabajo recibe una parte cada vez menor del ingreso
Barr citó un dato central: la participación del trabajo en el ingreso nacional cayó a un mínimo histórico de 52,8% en el segundo trimestre de 2026. Entre el fin de la Segunda Guerra Mundial y 2001 se había mantenido entre el 60% y el 65%.
La caída se aceleró después de la pandemia y fue especialmente fuerte en el último año, según el gobernador. Parte del descenso refleja problemas de medición, reconoció, pero aun después de ajustarlos persiste “una clara tendencia a la baja”.
Barr apoyó el diagnóstico en la última Encuesta de Finanzas del Consumidor de la Reserva Federal. El 1% más rico de los hogares posee cerca de un tercio de la riqueza del país, unos USD 60 billones, mientras que la mitad inferior tiene apenas el 2%.
Dos escenarios para la IA, según Barr
El gobernador describió dos caminos. En el primero, la competencia entre las empresas de IA convierte la tecnología en un producto barato y de uso masivo, con beneficios compartidos. Allí la IA podría “democratizar el acceso a habilidades e información” que necesitan los pequeños negocios para prosperar.
En el segundo, unas pocas empresas dominan el mercado y se quedan con la mayor parte de los rendimientos. “La ventaja de los líderes de la IA podría resultar sin precedentes”, dijo Barr. En ese caso, la participación del trabajo en el ingreso bajaría, la concentración de mercado subiría y la desigualdad aumentaría.
La rapidez del cambio pesa en ambos caminos. “Si los cambios en el mercado laboral ocurren rápido, será difícil que los trabajadores se ajusten y las dislocaciones podrían ser grandes”, señaló. Una adopción gradual permitiría ajustes más ordenados.
Barr dijo que el alcance del trastorno dependerá en parte de que la sociedad invierta en crear empleos, capacitar trabajadores y conectarlos con nuevos puestos. “Ahora es el momento de que la sociedad empiece a considerar cómo abordar estos posibles desafíos”, afirmó, cuando la adopción de la IA está en una etapa temprana. Barr aclaró en una nota que habla a título personal y no por sus colegas de la Reserva Federal.
El lunes, un grupo de trabajo designado por el presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, realizará un foro público en San Francisco para analizar qué puede significar la IA para la economía, según Reuters.

articles.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite All Private Container Images in a Registry
articles.text:
A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay allows an attacker who can access a Quay registry to read and overwrite private container images in every repository.
Quay enables anonymous access by default, and while it is enabled, the attacker needs no account. When it is off, anyone with a valid account can still exploit the flaw, Red Hat said yesterday. The company has released fixed builds for eight Quay 3 branches.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-123710 (CVSS score: 9.8).
Quay uses keys it trusts to sign the access tokens that allow image pushes and pulls. The flaw lets an attacker add their own key to the keys Quay trusts, with no expiry date. Quay then accepts tokens signed with that key for any repository.
With those tokens, an attacker can retrieve private images and any secrets or credentials stored within them. The attacker can also push or overwrite images, and the change propagates to every system that later pulls those images.
The planted key survives restarts until someone removes it. It can also be used to delete the keys that running Quay instances use, so normal pushes and pulls start failing with authentication errors.
Quay's key server checks that a request to replace a key carries a token signed by a trusted key, with the expected audience and issuer. It does not check whether the token was issued for key rotation. An anonymous token from Quay's /v2/auth endpoint passes: Quay signs it with a trusted key, and the caller chooses its audience.
A second critical flaw, CVE-2026-110697 (CVSS score: 9.9), was disclosed at the same time. It lets a Quay user who can create a namespace steal other tenants' robot account tokens and use them to read, push, or overwrite those tenants' images.
This flaw is in the code that lists robot accounts. It builds an SQL LIKE pattern from the namespace name without escaping wildcard characters, and in SQL LIKE an underscore matches any single character.
So a namespace with an underscore in the right place can match another tenant's namespace and return its robot accounts, with their decrypted tokens. The attacker needs no elevated privileges, and the victim does not have to do anything.
Deleting the attacker's namespace also deletes the corresponding robot accounts, which can cut off systems that rely on them. Where Quay is the integrated registry for OpenShift, stolen robot credentials can be used to inject malicious images into CI/CD pipelines, the company says.
Red Hat's Dave O'Connor found both flaws. The logic behind CVE-2026-123710 has been in Quay since its first public commit, according to the bug report for that flaw.
Red Hat lists every version of Quay 3 and Quay 5 as affected by both flaws. For CVE-2026-123710, its guidance names standalone installs, Quay deployed by the Quay Operator on OpenShift, and the mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift as affected.
Any Quay instance that untrusted clients can reach is exposed, including internal registries, the company says.
When checked today, the CVE entry for CVE-2026-123710 still showed every Quay package as affected, with no fix, even though each advisory lists the flaw.
The company recommends these steps:
- At the proxy or load balancer, block the /keys endpoint for everything except trusted internal components.
- Search the audit logs for service_key_rotate and service_key_delete events where expiration_date is null.
- Remove any approved service keys you do not recognize.
- Install the fixed release. Until it is running, an attacker can add a new key the same way, so deleting one does not last.
"Turning off anonymous access doesn't protect you," the company says in its key remediation article. A planted key also continues to work after password resets and changes to the robot token.
For CVE-2026-110697, the company's CVE page names the same eight releases as fixed, calls updating the only complete fix, and says Quay.io is already fixed. But none of the eight advisories list CVE-2026-110697.
Until an update is in place, the company suggests limiting who can create organizations or namespaces containing an underscore, rotating robot tokens for any namespace that matches an underscore namespace, and watching for pulls or pushes that do not fit normal robot use. These steps reduce the exposure, but the flaw remains.
The upstream fix adds the missing rotation check, requires keys added through the key server to have an expiry date, and stops callers from choosing a token's audience. The same change fixes the robot account search too.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026 : 10 offres FOLLES chez Amazon jusqu’à -42%, avant même le 27 novembre
articles.text:
Amazon n’attend pas le vendredi 27 novembre pour dérouler ses remises de Black Friday sur la tech. Nous avons retenu dix offres, du casque d’entrée de gamme au smartphone haut de gamme, en commençant par celles qui portent sur des produits que nous avons testés.
Cette sélection s’ouvre sur les produits que nous avons testés, avant de passer à ceux que nous n’avons pas encore eus entre les mains. Elle couvre quatre usages, le mobile, le salon, la maison et l’audio, avec des remises de 8 % à 42 % par rapport au prix de référence. La plus forte économie en euros concerne le Galaxy S26+, à plus de 400 €, la plus forte en pourcentage le casque Soundcore Q20i.
- Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 Go à 1 241 € au lieu de 1 479 € (-16 %)
- Google Pixel 11 256 Go à 779 € au lieu de 999 € (-22 %)
- Apple Watch Series 11 à 429 € au lieu de 465 € (-8 %)
- Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 Lite à 369 € au lieu de 399 € (-8 %)
- Samsung Galaxy S26+ 256 Go à 965 € au lieu de 1 369 € (-30 %)
- TV Samsung Mini LED 4K 55 pouces à 399 € au lieu de 519 € (-23 %)
- Vidéoprojecteur XGIMI MoGo 2 Pro à 339 € au lieu de 479 € (-29 %)
- Aspirateur laveur Tineco Floor One S7 Stretch Ultra à 249,99 € au lieu de 399,99 € (-38 %)
- Écouteurs Huawei FreeBuds SE 5 Max à 49,99 € au lieu de 79,99 € (-38 %)
- Casque Soundcore Q20i à 28,99 € au lieu de 49,99 € (-42 %)
iPhone 17 Pro Max : noté 10/10 par notre rédaction, à 1 241 €
Notre test de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max lui a attribué 10/10. Le plus grand des iPhone 17 réunit la puce A19 Pro, un écran de 6,9 pouces à 120 Hz qui monte jusqu’à 3 000 nits et une chambre à vapeur qui limite nettement la chauffe par rapport aux générations précédentes. C’est aussi l’iPhone le plus endurant qu’Apple ait conçu.
✅ Points forts
- Une autonomie sur deux jours : lors de notre test, il restait 35 % de batterie après six heures et demie d’écran en usage intensif.
- Un téléobjectif qui progresse : le module 4x passe à 48 Mpx et autorise un zoom 8x de très bonne qualité.
- À savoir : il pèse 233 g et l’iPhone 18 Pro Max l’a remplacé en haut de la gamme. Pour comparer, consultez notre guide des meilleurs iPhone.
Google Pixel 11 : le plus équilibré de la nouvelle gamme Pixel, à 779 €
Il a décroché 8/10 dans notre test du Google Pixel 11, qui salue son écran OLED de 6,3 pouces à 120 Hz parfaitement calibré et sa puce Tensor G6. Le design s’affine, avec une barre photo qui ne dépasse plus que d’un millimètre, et des outils d’IA comme la dictée Rambler complètent l’ensemble.
✅ Points forts
- Une endurance en hausse : 17 h 43 sur PCMark, soit environ deux heures de plus que le Pixel 10.
- Un suivi sur la durée : sept ans de mises à jour, et la recharge sans fil Qi2.2 à 25 W.
- À savoir : le GPU peine en jeu 3D, le Wi-Fi 7 reste réservé aux modèles Pro et certaines fonctions d’IA agentiques ne sont pas disponibles en France.
Apple Watch Series 11 : 24 heures d’autonomie annoncées, à 429 €
Notre test de l’Apple Watch Series 11 lui a attribué 9/10. Apple s’y attaque à son défaut historique, puisque l’autonomie annoncée passe de 18 à 24 heures. L’écran OLED LTPO3 de 2 000 nits reste très lisible et la finition irréprochable.
✅ Points forts
- Près de 36 heures mesurées : c’est ce que nous avons relevé avec une séance de sport en 4G, et la recharge de 0 à 80 % prend une demi-heure.
- Un suivi santé plus complet : détection des signes d’hypertension et score de sommeil, d’autant plus utile que la montre peut rester au poignet la nuit.
- À savoir : elle ne fonctionne qu’avec un iPhone, et la Series 12 lui a succédé cet automne. Pour comparer les modèles, consultez notre guide des meilleures Apple Watch.
Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 Lite : une tablette livrée avec son S Pen, à 369 €
Elle a obtenu 8/10 dans notre test de la Galaxy Tab S10 Lite. Son écran LCD de 10,9 pouces à 90 Hz est bien calibré, sa conception soignée pour 524 g, et le S Pen est fourni dans la boîte, un vrai plus pour prendre des notes ou faire les devoirs.
✅ Points forts
- Une belle endurance : 12 h 38 en usage polyvalent sur PCMark, de quoi tenir deux à trois jours avec quelques heures d’utilisation quotidienne.
- Galaxy AI à bord : Entourer pour chercher et Samsung Notes avec saisie manuscrite assistée.
- À savoir : l’écran plafonne à 600 nits, l’Exynos 1380 chauffe vite en jeu et il n’y a pas de capteur d’empreintes. Pour des alternatives plus puissantes, consultez notre comparatif des tablettes.
Samsung Galaxy S26+ : plus de 400 € de remise sur le grand format, à 965 €
Le Samsung Galaxy S26+ décline le S26 en 6,7 pouces, avec un écran Dynamic AMOLED 2X QHD+ à 120 Hz et la puce Exynos 2600, la première gravée en 2 nm. Nous ne l’avons pas testé, mais le Galaxy S26, dont il reprend l’essentiel de la fiche technique, a obtenu 9/10 pour son écran et ses fonctions d’IA.
✅ Points forts
- Une recharge plus rapide : 45 W en filaire pour une batterie de 4 900 mAh, contre 25 W sur le modèle compact.
- Un suivi logiciel actif : One UI 9, basée sur Android 17, se déploie avec de nouvelles fonctions Galaxy AI.
- À savoir : la partie photo (50 Mpx, ultra grand-angle 12 Mpx, téléobjectif x3 de 10 Mpx) ne change pas, et aucun chargeur n’est fourni.
TV Samsung Mini LED 4K 55 pouces : le rétroéclairage Mini LED à 399 €
Ce 55 pouces fait partie de la gamme Mini LED 2026 de Samsung. Son rétroéclairage par petites zones garde des hautes lumières franches sans délaver les noirs voisins, et le processeur Mini LED 4K améliore les contenus de définition inférieure. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une Smart TV complète : Tizen, Vision AI, Gaming Hub pour le jeu en streaming et compatibilité HDR10+.
- Une diagonale pensée pour le salon : 55 pouces et trois ports HDMI pour la box, la console et le lecteur.
- À savoir : c’est le modèle d’entrée de la gamme Mini LED et son son de 20 W gagnera à être épaulé par une barre de son. D’autres modèles sont à retrouver dans nos bons plans TV.
XGIMI MoGo 2 Pro : un vidéoprojecteur Full HD à installation automatique, à 339 €
Compact, le MoGo 2 Pro projette une image Full HD de 400 lumens ISO, compatible HDR10, et se déplace facilement d’une pièce à l’autre. Sa force est son installation automatique : mise au point et correction trapézoïdale se font seules, et il contourne même les obstacles. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Android TV intégré : les applications de streaming sont accessibles directement, sans boîtier supplémentaire.
- Des couleurs soignées : 90 % de l’espace DCI-P3 annoncés, et une source LED prévue pour durer 25 000 heures.
- À savoir : il n’embarque pas de batterie et sa luminosité le réserve aux pièces plongées dans la pénombre.
Tineco Floor One S7 Stretch Ultra : l’aspirateur laveur qui passe sous les meubles bas, à 249,99 €
Cet aspirateur laveur nettoie les sols durs en un seul passage. Sa conception Stretch lui permet de s’incliner à 180° pour se glisser sous des meubles de 13 cm de haut, et son capteur iLoop adapte le nettoyage au niveau de saleté détecté. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Un anti-emmêlement efficace : le système DualBlock évite que les cheveux s’enroulent autour de la brosse, un plus dans un foyer avec animaux.
- Un entretien automatisé : la fonction FlashDry nettoie et sèche la brosse après chaque usage, pour 50 minutes d’autonomie annoncées.
- À savoir : il pèse 4,5 kg, se destine aux sols durs et ne sait pas aspirer à sec.
Huawei FreeBuds SE 5 Max : jusqu’à 80 heures d’écoute avec le boîtier, à 49,99 €
Tout juste lancés, ces écouteurs misent sur l’endurance : jusqu’à 80 heures d’écoute boîtier compris, et quatre heures de musique après 10 minutes de charge. Avec 4,3 g par écouteur, ce sont les modèles à réduction de bruit les plus légers de la marque. Nous ne les avons pas encore testés.
✅ Points forts
- Une réduction de bruit modulable : jusqu’à 52 dB, avec plusieurs modes dont un mode dynamique qui s’adapte à l’environnement.
- Une connectivité à jour : Bluetooth 6.0, connexion simultanée à deux appareils et codec LDAC.
- À savoir : l’autonomie tombe à 7 heures par charge avec la réduction de bruit, et le LDAC ne profite qu’aux smartphones Android compatibles.
Soundcore Q20i : la réduction de bruit active sous la barre des 30 €, à 28,99 €
Avec le Q20i, Anker propose la réduction de bruit active à moins de 30 €. Son système hybride à quatre micros atténue jusqu’à 90 % des bruits continus, comme celui d’un moteur, et ses transducteurs de 40 mm s’appuient sur le mode BassUp pour étoffer les graves. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une autonomie fleuve : 40 heures avec la réduction de bruit, 60 sans, et cinq minutes de charge donnent quatre heures d’écoute.
- Hi-Res et LDAC : une meilleure qualité audio en Bluetooth avec les smartphones compatibles, et un usage filaire possible.
- À savoir : la réduction de bruit vise surtout les bruits de fond continus, et l’application Soundcore est nécessaire pour accéder à tous les réglages.
Black Friday 2026 : comment Amazon étale ses remises jusqu’au Cyber Monday
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre, et le Cyber Monday le lundi 30. Entre ces deux dates, Amazon déroule ses promotions par vagues plutôt qu’en un seul pic, ce qui explique les offres déjà visibles aujourd’hui. Les tarifs évoluent d’un jour à l’autre, parfois à la baisse, parfois à la hausse : suivre dès maintenant les produits qui vous intéressent permet de comparer calmement au lieu de décider au dernier moment. Pour garder le fil sans y passer vos soirées, notre page Black Friday réunit chaque jour les offres retenues par la rédaction, chez Amazon comme chez les autres enseignes.
Comment savoir si une promo high-tech est vraiment intéressante ?
Le premier réflexe consiste à comparer le prix affiché au tarif réellement pratiqué ces dernières semaines, car le prix barré correspond souvent au tarif conseillé par le fabricant. Regardez ensuite qui vend et expédie le produit : Amazon lui-même, ou un vendeur tiers de la marketplace, dont les conditions de livraison et de retour peuvent différer. Le calendrier des sorties joue aussi, puisque l’arrivée d’une nouvelle génération, comme l’iPhone 18 Pro Max ou l’Apple Watch Series 12 cette année, fait souvent baisser le prix de la précédente, qui reste très recommandable. Enfin, la note obtenue en test protège d’un mauvais achat : un produit bien noté avec une remise modeste vaut mieux qu’un modèle moyen affiché à moitié prix, et nos tests de smartphones comme nos comparatifs aident à faire le tri.
Où suivre les offres du Black Friday ?
Tout au long de novembre, nous publions chaque jour des sélections thématiques qui rassemblent les meilleures offres du moment.
Toutes les promotions du Black Friday 2026 sont à retrouver sur notre page consacrée à l’événement.
Sur X, notre compte Clubic Bons Plans signale les meilleures offres en direct.

articles.title: Firefox temporarily drops its monthly VPN data cap
articles.text:
Mozilla Firefox VPN has unlimited data until January 31, 2027, to fight back against Chrome and Edge, but is it already too late?
Firefox's built-in VPN currently supports desktop and Android users only
- Mozilla removes Firefox's free VPN data restrictions until January 31, 2027
- Firefox users get unlimited VPN data without purchasing another subscription
- Firefox's free VPN protects browsing activity on shared Wi-Fi networks
Mozilla has removed the monthly data restriction on Firefox's free VPN, giving desktop and Android users unlimited browsing protection through January 31, 2027.
The temporary offer began November 10, 2026, and requires only a Mozilla account, without asking users to purchase an additional subscription.
Mozilla is trying to make Firefox more attractive as it competes with Chrome and Edge, which held 68.79% and 5.36% of the global browser market, respectively, in October 2026.
Firefox removes restrictions on its free VPN service
The extended allowance gives Firefox users an opportunity to browse through shared Wi-Fi connections without exhausting their monthly VPN data allocation during the promotional period.
This matters particularly during holiday travel, when passengers frequently depend on airport terminals, hotels, restaurants, and other public internet connections.
Mozilla says its integrated free VPN conceals browsing activity from operators of shared networks while making it harder for websites to determine someone's location.
The service also obscures users' IP addresses, reducing opportunities for websites to associate separate browsing sessions through their network addresses.
“Most importantly, you’re not trading your browsing data for that protection,” said Mozilla, explaining its approach to privacy within the free VPN service.
The company also says it does not monetize users' browsing information through advertising or maintain records identifying the websites they visit.
However, unlimited data should not be confused with complete anonymity, because websites can still recognize visitors through cookies and accounts.
Firefox's built-in protection also does not erase browsing records stored locally, meaning users must consider Private Windows for additional privacy.
Availability comes with some limitations
Availability is limited by platform and geographical restrictions, so users must check regional eligibility before expecting access.
The complimentary service currently supports Firefox desktop and Android installations, but the company says iOS support is coming.
Another restriction concerns application coverage, since the complimentary VPN protects internet activity inside Firefox rather than every application installed on devices.
Mozilla directs customers seeking device-wide protection toward its separate Mozilla VPN product, which requires a paid subscription.
Getting started requires signing into a Mozilla account, selecting the VPN control in Firefox's desktop toolbar, and completing the activation instructions.
Android users can access the feature through the browser's three-dot menu, followed by Settings and the VPN configuration section.
The timing allows Mozilla to attract privacy-conscious users, although a temporary allowance alone cannot guarantee sustained growth against established rivals.
Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge retain substantial advantages through their established user bases, existing services, and integration with their respective technology ecosystems.
Mozilla therefore needs more than a temporary privacy promotion if it expects dissatisfied Chrome and Edge users to consider switching browsers.
Removing the data ceiling makes Firefox's complimentary protection more appealing, particularly for people who regularly depend on shared connections.
However, whether those users remain after the promotional period depends partly on the service's future restrictions and Mozilla's ability to maintain interest.
