articles.title: BYD a-t-il désossé un Land Rover Defender en secret pour copier sa technologie ? La justice s’en mêle
articles.text:
Land Rover attaque BYD en justice : pourquoi le SUV chinois Ti 7 est accusé de copier le Defender
Land Rover poursuit BYD en justice aux Pays-Bas, soupçonnant la marque chinoise d’avoir démonté un Defender pour copier sa technologie sur son nouveau SUV hybride rechargeable Ti 7.
Écoulé à plus de 100 000 exemplaires par an depuis 2023, l’imposant Land Rover Defender de seconde génération a largement inspiré l’industrie automobile… dont BYD. Le groupe chinois aurait poussé la ressemblance bien trop loin. Résultat : le constructeur britannique aurait engagé une procédure judiciaire aux Pays-Bas concernant le BYD Ti 7, suspecté d’être une copie technique du Defender.
Une accusation d’espionnage technologique avant un lancement au Royaume-Uni
Au-delà de la silhouette très carrée de ce grand SUV hybride rechargeable de 5 mètres, c’est surtout ce qui se cache sous la carrosserie du BYD Ti 7 qui motive cette offensive judiciaire, révélée par le Sunday Times. Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) soupçonne en effet BYD d’avoir carrément démonté un Defender afin de pratiquer de la rétro-ingénierie et d’en copier étroitement certaines technologies.
Dans le cadre de ce litige examiné par un tribunal néerlandais, les bureaux de BYD aux Pays-Bas ont été perquisitionnés au mois d’août pour saisir des fichiers numériques. Si aucune des deux marques n’a souhaité commenter l’affaire sur le fond, le géant chinois a toutefois contesté la quantité de documents visés par l’opération.
Cette attaque en justice intervient d’ailleurs à un moment clé : les débuts européens du BYD Ti 7 en janvier 2027 au Royaume-Uni, soit sur les terres mêmes de Land Rover. Le SUV chinois s’affiche en prime à un tarif particulièrement agressif fixé à partir de 47 995 £ (environ 58 000 €). En face, le Defender 90 débute à 58 655 £ (près de 70 000 €), tandis que le Defender 110, au gabarit similaire au Ti 7, réclame au moins 64 315 £ (environ 77 000 €).
Avec 23 % des immatriculations britanniques captées par les marques chinoises en septembre 2026, éviter l’arrivée d’un modèle concurrent aussi bien positionné serait une belle victoire. Reste maintenant à patienter quelques semaines pour voir si Land Rover réussira ou non à faire barrage au BYD Ti 7.

articles.title: IBM Quantum and the race to make scientific advantage useful to industry - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM Quantum and the race to make scientific advantage useful to industry
QDC26 shows progress in the hardware, software and tooling around quantum computing as customers look for evidence of better outcomes.
IBM Corp.’s Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week marked a change in emphasis. IBM claims that researchers have demonstrated quantum advantage in 2026 by working with the classical computing community. Its public presentations showed progress in processors, error correction, scientific software and the integration of quantum with conventional computing.
The company’s quantum leader, Jay Gambetta (pictured), also set a new target. The next big milestone comes by demonstrating industry impact by 2028, conditional on collaboration across enterprise application researchers and the classical and quantum communities.
Our key takeaway is that IBM is assembling more of the full system required to turn a quantum experiment into useful scientific work. Hardware is important, but the real innovation will come from software. Importantly, the tools that help a scientist formulate a problem, run it across different computing resources, check the result and understand the economics are where much of the innovation is headed. These capabilities address several of the barriers customers described to us in our spring quantum tour of major scientific research labs; and the issues discussed with technologists on our Quantum 101 Series at theCUBE’s NYSE studio.
Despite the progress being made, the remaining gaps and challenges are many. Quantum science is advancing but impact on industries is still years away. Better software is the key to making dramatic improvements in quantum performance and a new service capability can attract researchers. But if a chemist needs to understand the deep nuances of quantum computing, it limits adoption. We believe the next phase of innovation will focus on abstracting quantum complexities and making measurable improvements in simplicity to drive further usage.
In this Special Breaking Analysis, we examine IBM’s public QDC proclamations through the prism of our spring interviews with six quantum and supercomputing experts. We add customer perspectives from our partner Qualitate, assess the implications of IBM’s foundry investments and consider what evidence would signal that progress is moving from scientific advantage to industry impact.
Three milestones with different proof points
IBM’s progress comes into better focus when evaluating its milestones separately. IBM’s goal of demonstrating Quantum Advantage by 2026 is generally accepted as met, based on achieving particular computation superiority relative to today’s classical methods. But to truly show industry impact, IBM needs to show results make a difference to an organization. Milestones around fault-tolerant architectures will increasingly focus on the ability to sustain reliable computation in the face of errors. Progress in one category will definitely support another but it’s useful to look at milestones and proof points separately as shown below.
IBM deserves high marks for achieving that advantage but is subject to scrutiny. Gambetta’s keynote described classical researchers overtaking quantum results, claims being withdrawn as classical makes improvements, and subsequent quantum work moving the needle in favor of quantum again. This of course is how a competitive scientific ecosystem should operate. We’re eager to see the leapfrogging end and await a day where a quantum advantage becomes sustainable with clear evidence that classical computing has no chance of catching up for specified use cases.
Observers can rightly be concerned that incorrect inferences may be drawn from the term “advantage.” The phrase can sound like a statement of superiority. But if that advantage is not consistently held, then the broader industry might remain skeptical. The same applies to verifying that a customer outcome is attributable an underlying scientific model powered by quantum.
A public Allstate example is useful and illustrates the difference. IBM described underwriting-optimization results as comparable to classical optimization schemes. That can represent progress, but it does not show that quantum has delivered a superior underwriting outcome. Customers need to decide how much they are prepared to invest in learning before a measurable benefit appears. IBM, in our view, is working hard to simplify the heavy lift and broaden adoption.
Our 2026 spring interviews provide practical research lab data points
The researchers we interviewed in spring 2026 for World Quantum Day were already thinking beyond the hardware. Their concerns included application selection, reliability, integration, software complexity and the ability to preserve optionality as hardware evolves. These were six independent editorial interviews conducted on theCUBE, made possible by Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., across five institutions, offering a view of the work required to make quantum useful. The discussions were hosted by this author and Paul Gillin, managing editor at SiliconANGLE.
The following table highlights the to priority stated by each researcher at the time and our take on how IBM has responded in the past 6-9 months.
| Expert and affiliation | Priority in Q1 | How the public QDC material responds | 
| Laura Schulz Argonne National Laboratory | Let scientists work without mastering every hardware detail. | AI skills and application tools reduce some assembly work; independent use still needs more proof. | 
| Amir Shehata Oak Ridge National Laboratory | Coordinate quantum and conventional resources efficiently. | Managed workflows expose execution stages and combined resource usage. | 
| Dr. Pascal Elahi Pawsey Supercomputing Centre | Identify the quantum portion of a larger scientific problem and supply expertise. | Problem-mapping tools and hybrid workflows support that approach. | 
| Dr. Mikael Johansson CSC, Finnish IT Center for Science | Find useful applications and build skills across diverse technologies. | Chemistry, materials and optimization tools create more ways to experiment. | 
| Tom Beck Oak Ridge National Laboratory | Connect promising science to reliable computation while preserving hardware options. | Materials workflows and error-correction work address parts of that requirement. | 
| Dieter Kranzlmüller Leibniz Supercomputing Centre | Judge application performance and economics while retaining technological independence. | Usage visibility helps assess economics; portability remains a customer requirement. | 
IBM is directing effort toward problems that these practitioners identified months earlier. We believe that is a strong indicator of product relevance, an even more important than hardware milestones.
It also gives us a more reasonable test of true progress. A scientist must be able to attack a meaningful problem with less setup effort, run it more reliably and compare the result with a credible classical alternative. IBM’s public announcements show capabilities intended to support that progression and the gaps identified this spring by our researcher friends. Thus far, however, they don’t show how broadly researchers can complete their tasks without specialist assistance. IBM shared additional capabilities to a small group of industry analysts under NDA, which look encouraging.
The practical measure is in running the experiment end-to-end
Some of the most interesting material in Chicago concerned ordinary operational friction. In the public developer sessions, IBM described experiments interrupted by sleeping laptops, dead notebook sessions, running out of memory or tokens, and lost work in process. In quantum research, as with AI YOLO training runs, they add expense and blockers to work that already requires specialized expertise.
Managed workflows address this through simplification by moving execution into a hosted environment with conventional computing resources and tools to capture and save work in process. Researchers can associate quantum jobs with the workflow and monitor consumption across both quantum and classical support infrastructure. That creates a basis for repeating experiments and understanding where resources are consumed and how to optimize the complete process.
Take the chemistry approaches discussed at the event. Researchers can divide a larger molecular problem into smaller parts, use quantum or classical computing methods for appropriate parts and combine the results. At QDC26, IBM described improvements in classical algorithms that support the processing of quantum jobs. Classical solving steps can become a major bottlenecks and represent opportunities for optimization.
The relevant focus is increasingly the complete research workflow. Here we’re referring to the preparation, the quantum work, the classical processing and the validation. This expands the opportunity for IBM and its partners because more of the work can be supported through its software and services. It also shines a light on how the economic case needs to evolve, with a focus on the cost of an outcome.
Faster quantum hardware alone is not the answer. Conversely, better classical software can make quantum experiments much more productive. Both are developments that came into focus at QDC26. Customers need enough visibility to identify the bottlenecks and implement improvements.
AI’s role in reducing the cost of quantum
IBM’s pronouncements about AI are expected to address barriers raised in our spring interviews – the complexity of translating domain knowledge into a working quantum experiment. IBM must provide skills that assist with choosing methods, workflows, applying classical algorithms and the like. And validating implementations before longer, more expensive runs take place. Our developer conversations at the event underscore demand for AI assistance with calls for simpler packaging and managed services.
We believe this marks is an important near-term relationship between AI and quantum. AI can help scientists use quantum computing more effectively before quantum delivers a broadly demonstrated improvement in AI itself. The immediate opportunity is to simplify – reducing the effort required to apply specialized software and infrastructure.
This requirement has implications for how scientific software is packaged. A library contains reusable code. Increasingly, skills will supply context and guidelines for selecting and applying that code. As skills improve, we expect more of the integration work to be assisted by software. The value of a mature library will still depend on its performance and suitability for the task at hand. The public QDC releases include libraries, mapping tools and AI skills together; they hint toward an evolution in how software will be used in the future.
Another gap is accountability. For example, what happens if a workflow executes but uses invalid scientific assumptions. An AI-generated configuration can appear valid while making a poor trade-off between accuracy and cost, for example. In our view, a useful abstraction must maintain the ability to understand those AI decisions and validate them in terms that a domain expert/scientist comprehends.
This is where customer evidence must become more specific in our view. For example, can a chemist repeat useful work without a vendor team guiding them every step? Can another scientist reproduce the result? Can the organization see what exactly changed between runs? We would place considerable weight on those conditions when judging whether easier programming translates into broader scientific adoption.
Chemistry offers a clear fit but still requires more proof
Chemistry and materials are fields that provide a strong connection between our spring interviews and the public QDC discussions. Johansson at CSC emphasized the challenge of modeling interacting electrons. Beck at Oak Ridge described materials and chemistry research with potential relevance to fusion and biology. IBM’s sessions discussed tools for decomposing problems and processing results across quantum and conventional systems working in tandem.
We view these fields as particularly credible places to look for early useful applications because the scientific problems involve quantum behavior. That is a reason to prioritize research that benefits from quantum. Problem scope, accuracy and economics (or feasibility) relative to conventional methods will determine the ultimate usefulness of quantum.
The economics must include the full result
IBM’s performance progress is notable, but its points of comparison are instructive. Its headline 25-fold improvement in maximum circuit throughput compares Nighthawk r2 with Heron. Several application improvements also compare newer IBM quantum systems with earlier ones. Those figures demonstrate progress within IBM’s generations but a customer still needs a comparison with the best practical classical approach to the same problem.
The mot useful metric in our view is the cost and time required to obtain a validated outcome. The calculation should include all aspects of conventional preprocessing and post-processing, the quantum work done, job completion times and the intensity of the technical skills required perform and validate the result. Importantly, an important future measure is whether the process can be consistently repeated at scale.
Customers should absolutely invest before quantum consistently wins. The key is to identify those investments as a learning experience.
Qualitate customer data reveals little enterprise focus outside of PQC
Post-quantum cryptography or PQC is a topic we unpacked at theCUBE’s Quantum Readiness Day this past September. Qualitate customer survey findings add another dimension to our PQC analysis. But don’t confuse PQC spend with quantum application adoption.
A query of Qualitate’s interview data on quantum adoption focuses heavily on PQC, a tactical topic that is top of mind for enterprises today. Organizations are spending to prepare existing information systems to resist future quantum-enabled attacks. The data include customers already taking action, as well as those evaluating.
“Now is the time we’re really starting to go all in on post quantum cryptography.”
The same participant, a technology lead at a professional services company, explains the rationale in terms of future loss avoidance:
“We anticipate that this will significantly save us on dealing with enormous crises in the future.”
Today’s enterprise focus as it relates to quantum is on modernizing cryptography. This is far ahead of investing to find useful applications for a quantum computer. Today’s practitioners are consumed with deploying and securing agents and making AI trustworthy. Quantum applications, other than PQC, are not top-of-mind for most enterprise customers. Security work to protect conventional systems is tactical and there’s little evidence of interest in running workloads on quantum hardware within organizations today.
NIST released its first three finalized post-quantum cryptography standards in 2024 and encourages organizations to begin transitioning. Its guidance also explains the risk that adversaries collect encrypted information today for possible decryption later. Unlike Y2K, which had a definitive date associated wth the risk, the timing of a capable quantum attack remains uncertain. As such, migration planning is sensible now, independent of IBM’s application and hardware milestones.
The following competitive signals are seen in the Qualitate data and are almost exclusively security-related:
| Vendor | Perception reported in the Qualitate surveys | 
| IBM | Quantum-safe cryptography breadth and hybrid solutions, with existing relationships and executive sponsorship influencing interest. | 
|  | Some participants associate quantum hardware expertise with credibility in defending against the future threat. | 
| Microsoft | An existing Azure environment makes Microsoft a natural extension of the customer’s current platform relationship. | 
The opportunity for specialists also remains open. One participant states:
“The field is still not crystallized. And probably we will not necessarily rely on the hyperscalers. Probably will rely on specialists.” – Global head of analytics, financial services and insurance, large U.S. corporation (Source: Qualitate)
Our take is that technical credibility and existing relationships, combined with the ability to affect a successful migration, may all influence these purchases. IBM has many assets, but customers are still evaluating alternatives. Success in quantum-safe security strengthens its commercial position without, by itself, resolving which quantum computing architecture or application platform will prevail when quantum goes mainstream.
Quantum chip manufacturing adds another dimension to the competition
Quantum computing also needs to progress from building exceptional devices to producing dependable systems repeatedly. The manufacturing announcements around IBM’s roadmap deserve scrutiny in that context.
In September, IBM acquired, Anderon, finalizing a $1 billion CHIPS award supported by an additional $1 billion IBM investment. IBM has reported it has an Albany, New York-based, 300-millimeter quantum wafer foundry serving customers across the ecosystem, with initial wafers already running through the facility.
Our view is that the learning curve will be as important as any single milestone. More repeatable production can confer experience advantages to IBM (Wright’s Law), much in the same way Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. has demonstrated its leadership in semiconductor manufacturing. Serving multiple customers could help support volume across shared infrastructure. Whether those benefits emerge depends on demand, process stability, yields and the ability to protect each customer’s intellectual property. In addition, IBM can learn from Intel’s missteps and its own foundry challenges.
The industry needs to watch for manufacturing progress alongside qubit performance. Capital investments are followed by innovation. IBM’s August acquisition of HRL Laboratories adds a related strategic chess move. The rationale explained by IBM is to acquire expertise in silicon-spin qubits, sensing, materials, cryogenics, controls, packaging and interconnects. IBM describes that expertise as complementary to its superconducting work and identifies opportunities to collaborate with Anderon.
We interpret the acquisition as a way for IBM to control its destiny in a return to its vertically integrated mainframe past. At the same time, it doesn’t have the volume economics to achieve its objectives purely as a captive/integrated systems player. So it must open up its manufacturing capability to other parties, including its competitors.
IBM is competing to organize the work around quantum
Taken together, the public announcements at QDC26 suggest a broader platform ambition. IBM is connecting access to quantum hardware and software with classical computing, application functions, development tools and the like. We believe this could increase its role in the customer’s research process and create more opportunities for ecosystem partners to package specialized capabilities.
The competitive advantage will come from making useful work easier to perform and repeat. A customer that can move from a scientific experiment to a reliable result at scale, with less effort, has a reason to stay with a vendor and invest more. That advantage still has to be earned through application quality, performance, service reliability and superior economics.
There is also a customer tradeoff – the classic lock-in risk. An integrated service can reduce operational complexity while increasing dependence on the provider’s tooling and ecosystem. Open-source tools help minimize the risk, but portability also depends on whether models, workflows, validation and operational models transfer to another platform. Our spring conversations with Kranzlmüller – and his emphasis on technological independence – along with Shehata’s interest in interoperable specifications – make that point clear.
We would not declare IBM as a decisive winner from this conference. But the company has presented an impressive combination of hardware, software and infrastructure progress. Customers will determine its value through repeated use and outcomes. Competing systems from specialists and hyperscalers – as well as progress from classical methods – will continue to shape the narrative.
Gambetta’s 2028 gambit
If Jay Gambetta’s prediction holds true, the next two years will produce a more tangible conversation around industry impact. Look for significantly more quantum POCs, more named customers solving consequential problems and a measurable change in a scientific or business decision. We would also want enough evidence for an independent team to assess the contribution; and for the customer to explain the full cost of achieving an outcome.
Some additional items to watch:
- We believe chemistry and materials deserve close attention;
- Research workflows must be easier to use;
- Track whether more domain scientists can work independent of highly skilled quantum experts;
- Whether quantum advantage survives a sustainable lead vis a vis classical;
- Whether chip manufacturing shows up as reliable, consistent and independent.
For enterprise leaders, the sensible approach is to separate cryptographic readiness from quantum application programs tied to specific problems and economics.
IBM has made a stronger case that the surrounding machinery for useful quantum computing is coming together. The future test is whether customers can show what changed because of quantum. A demonstrably improved scientific result or an economically superior workflow would make the 2028 ambition impressive.
That is the evidence we will be watching.
What’s on your quantum radar? Let us know.

articles.title: Surfshark proves it does not record your data with a fresh independent no-logs audit
articles.text:
Surfshark proves it does not record your data with a fresh independent no-logs audit
Big Four accounting firm KPMG inspected Surfshark's network and found no signs of activity logging
- KPMG confirmed Surfshark does not log browsing traffic or IP addresses
- The evaluation covered standard, static, and multi-port servers
- While single snapshots, regular audits still set a clear privacy benchmark
Surfshark has once again called in outside experts to inspect its infrastructure. Independent Big Four accounting firm KPMG examined the provider’s server setup and confirmed that its systems follow its strict no-log claims.
For anyone shopping for the best VPN, privacy commitments can sound like empty marketing phrases. Almost every service advertises that it leaves no digital trace. Independent checks help bridge the gap between promises and actual technical proof, which is why Surfshark regularly opens its doors to outside inspectors.
This latest verification confirms that the provider does not store browsing histories, IP addresses, connection timestamps, or outgoing traffic. According to Surfshark's official announcement, the audit specifically tested whether user traffic can be monitored or retrieved from live server memory.
Surfshark – the best cheap VPN
Surfshark is a fast, easy-to-use VPN that seriously beats the competition when it comes to subscription pricing. Its two-year Starter plan works out at $2.49 a month (plus tax), but we think Surfshark One is the best value plan as it adds an antivirus, data breach monitor, alternative ID, and now new anti-scam tools. All of this starting from the equivalent of  just $2.79 a month. 
Surfshark's no-log audit: what KPMG actually inspected
Auditors reviewed the technical configuration of Surfshark's production servers, covering standard nodes, static IP locations, and multi-port routing setups. The inspectors assessed whether operational practices matched the guarantees outlined in the service's no-logs policy.
The final assessment found no discrepancies. Surfshark's infrastructure runs entirely on RAM-only servers. Because these machines lack traditional hard drives, all temporary operational data is wiped clean the moment a server reboots or powers down.
This is not the company’s first trip through the review process. Last year, Surfshark cleared an independent audit with Deloitte, following an earlier review that verified its first no-logs audit years ago.

Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
What an independent VPN audit actually mean for your privacy?
It is worth asking the hard question: does an audit guarantee absolute anonymity? No, it does not.
An audit provides a point-in-time assessment. It proves that on the days KPMG tested the network, the configurations complied with stated policies. It cannot monitor changes an engineering team might make months later, nor does it turn a VPN into a magic shield against online fingerprinting, account tracking, or malware.
Still, routine testing remains the gold standard for consumer privacy. When providers make full audit findings public, users can verify that their personal internet traffic is not quietly sitting in a log file.
You can read the specific methodology and findings directly in the full KPMG audit report, and learn more about why VPN audits matter in our detailed guide.

articles.title: Quién es Colette Kress, la mujer que asumió el control de Nvidia tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Colette Kress asumirá la dirección ejecutiva interina de Nvidia, una de las compañías más importantes de la industria tecnológica y protagonista del auge mundial de la inteligencia artificial. La ejecutiva, que desde 2013 ocupa el cargo de directora financiera de la empresa, quedará al frente del fabricante de chips tras la renuncia de su cofundador y hasta ahora CEO, Jensen Huang.
El nombramiento representa un cambio relevante para Nvidia, cuyos procesadores se convirtieron en componentes fundamentales para el desarrollo de centros de datos, supercomputadoras y sistemas de inteligencia artificial. Kress conoce desde dentro la evolución financiera de la compañía y participó durante más de una década en sus presentaciones de resultados ante los inversores.
Según informó Reuters el 12 de noviembre de 2026, la junta directiva decidió apartar a Huang en medio de informaciones sobre presuntas relaciones extramatrimoniales, una de ellas vinculada a una mujer señalada como posible espía china. La designación de Kress la coloca ahora al frente de una empresa que experimentó un crecimiento extraordinario durante los últimos años.
Colette Kress, la ejecutiva que lleva más de una década en Nvidia
Kress ingresó a Nvidia en septiembre de 2013 como vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera. Desde entonces, ha sido responsable de supervisar las finanzas de la compañía y acompañó a Huang en las llamadas trimestrales en las que Nvidia comunica sus resultados y explica su estrategia a los mercados.
Su trayectoria dentro de la empresa coincide con una transformación de gran escala. Cuando llegó, Nvidia registraba ingresos anuales de 4.130 millones de dólares. Para el ejercicio fiscal 2026, esa cifra alcanzó los 215.900 millones de dólares, de acuerdo con los datos recogidos por Reuters.
El crecimiento estuvo impulsado, principalmente, por la demanda de unidades de procesamiento gráfico (GPU), chips que inicialmente se asociaban con los videojuegos y que hoy son esenciales para entrenar y ejecutar modelos de inteligencia artificial. La expansión de este mercado convirtió a Nvidia en una de las empresas más valiosas del sector tecnológico.
La experiencia financiera de Kress será uno de los principales activos de su gestión interina. Su conocimiento de las cuentas, los negocios y las operaciones de Nvidia podría facilitar la continuidad de la estrategia mientras la junta busca definir el liderazgo permanente de la compañía.
Su trayectoria en Microsoft, Cisco y Texas Instruments
Antes de incorporarse a Nvidia, Kress desarrolló una carrera de casi 25 años en departamentos financieros de grandes empresas tecnológicas. Sus primeros años profesionales estuvieron vinculados a Texas Instruments, donde trabajó durante ocho años en distintas funciones relacionadas con las finanzas.
Posteriormente, pasó a Microsoft, compañía en la que permaneció entre 1997 y 2010. En 2006 asumió como directora financiera de la división Server and Tools, con responsabilidades sobre la estrategia financiera, la planificación y los informes de resultados de esa área.
En 2010 se incorporó a Cisco como vicepresidenta sénior y directora financiera de la organización Business Technology and Operations Finance. Allí estuvo a cargo de la estrategia financiera y del desarrollo de negocios de esa unidad. Tres años después dejó la compañía para sumarse a Nvidia.
Esta experiencia le permitió conocer distintas áreas de la industria tecnológica, desde la fabricación de semiconductores hasta los servicios empresariales y la infraestructura informática.
Dónde estudió y cuál es su patrimonio
La formación académica de Kress también está vinculada al ámbito financiero. Obtuvo una licenciatura en Finanzas en la Universidad de Arizona y posteriormente completó una maestría en Administración de Empresas (MBA) en la Southern Methodist University, según el informe anual de Nvidia presentado ante la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos.
Su participación en el crecimiento de Nvidia también se refleja en su patrimonio. La revista Forbes la ubicó en el puesto 32 de su lista de las mujeres estadounidenses que construyeron sus fortunas por cuenta propia en 2026.
Reuters señaló que sus acciones en Nvidia estaban valoradas en aproximadamente 750 millones de dólares al cierre de la jornada del miércoles 11 de noviembre. Esa participación había superado los 1.000 millones de dólares cuando el precio de los títulos de la compañía alcanzó su máximo durante el mes anterior.
El desafío de dirigir una de las empresas clave de la inteligencia artificial
La llegada de Kress a la dirección ejecutiva ocurre en un momento decisivo para Nvidia. La compañía ocupa una posición central en el mercado de chips para inteligencia artificial, un sector en el que compite por mantener su liderazgo mientras crece la inversión de empresas tecnológicas en centros de datos y capacidad de procesamiento.
Su nombramiento es interino, por lo que no significa necesariamente que permanecerá como CEO de manera definitiva. La junta directiva deberá resolver quién ocupará el puesto de forma permanente después de la salida de Huang.
Mientras tanto, Kress tendrá que garantizar la continuidad de las operaciones, mantener la confianza de los inversores y conducir una compañía cuyo desempeño influye en buena parte del mercado tecnológico mundial. Su principal ventaja es que conoce desde hace 13 años las finanzas y el funcionamiento interno de Nvidia, una experiencia que ahora deberá trasladar a la máxima responsabilidad ejecutiva.

articles.title: Una catedral finlandesa suena cada día con el eco de estallidos de radio de hace miles de millones de años
articles.text:
Los estallidos rápidos de radio (FRB) son uno de los fenómenos más misteriosos del Universo. Hay varias hipótesis sobre su origen, pero sigue sin estar del todo claro. Entre otros motivos, son difíciles de estudiar porque no pueden verse ni oírse. Por eso, un profesor de física del MIT se ha asociado con un compositor para convertir algunas de estas ráfagas en música. ¿Han resuelto el misterio? No, pero ahora pueden escucharse cada día en una catedral finlandesa e incluso tendrán una representación acompañada de un coro el próximo 21 de noviembre.
Sonificación. Kiyoshi Masui, del MIT, y el compositor y tecnólogo creativo Andrew Melchior han utilizado los datos de 4.539 estallidos, procedentes de 3.641 fuentes, detectados entre 2018 y 2023 con CHIME (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment). Este es un radiotelescopio ubicado en Canadá que se concibió para mapear el hidrógeno neutro entre los corrimientos al rojo 0,8 y 2, pero que ha resultado ser un gran detector de FRB gracias a su enorme campo de visión y el caudal de datos que puede manejar.
Las distintas señales se han transformado en sonidos, de modo que los estallidos lejanos suenan como zumbidos, retumbos, chasquidos y silbidos. Además, cada estallido cae de agudos a graves, un efecto real causado por su viaje a través del gas intergaláctico. Todo esto se convierte en música, porque, al llegar las distintas frecuencias de radio en momentos ligeramente distintos, se generan armonías entre los tonos altos y bajos.
Una catedral finlandesa. La creación del científico y el compositor se cargó en un dispositivo llamado The Logos, que se instaló en la catedral finlandesa de Oulu el pasado mes de abril de 2026. Consta de 12 altavoces repartidos por todo el edificio, que se ponen en marcha cada mediodía. Además, el próximo 21 de noviembre se pausará la grabación y se hará una emisión en directo a cargo del propio Melchior, que interpretará las FRB al teclado, y un coro de 30 personas que cantarán distribuidas entre el público.
Ráfagas de origen desconocido. Las FRB son ondas de radio extremadamente energéticas. En un solo milisegundo liberan energía equivalente a la que emite el Sol en tres días. Se descubrieron en 2007 y aún no se sabe bien cómo se producen, aunque hay algunas hipótesis. Por ejemplo, se cree que pueden formarse en las magnetosferas de las estrellas de neutrones o los agujeros negros. También existe una corriente de pensamiento que apunta a púlsares jóvenes como la principal fuente de emisión. Finalmente, se cree que podría tener relación con la fusión de estrellas de neutrones.
En el caso de las FRB que se han grabado para The Logos, solo se sabe que se formaron hace entre 8 mil y 50 mil millones de años, pero su fuente original es un misterio.
¿Podría ayudar la sonificación? En algunos casos, transformar las señales difícilmente tangibles en sonidos, mucho más fáciles de interpretar, ayuda a estudiar el origen de esas señales. Por ejemplo, en 1981 un patrón sonoro ayudó a detectar un problema de la sonda Voyager 2 causado por colisiones con micrometeoroides. También son útiles para ayudar a las personas ciegas a disfrutar de fenómenos como los eclipses.
Desgraciadamente, no parece que la sonificación de las FRB vaya a ayudar a los científicos a determinar su origen. Pero sí puede ayudar a que la sociedad conozca este fenómeno. Para que la ciencia avance, es importante divulgarla a la sociedad. Y si la divulgación es en forma de arte, mejor que mejor.

articles.title: Nintendo vai encerrar login com Google e Apple; veja o que muda • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nintendo vai encerrar login com Google e Apple; veja o que muda
Usuários precisarão utilizar senha ou chave de acesso para entrar na Conta Nintendo a partir de janeiro de 2027.
A Nintendo deixará de permitir o login com contas do Google e da Apple a partir de 26 de janeiro de 2027. A mudança afeta usuários que utilizam esses serviços para acessar a Conta Nintendo, responsável por recursos como compras digitais, assinaturas e funcionalidades online do Switch e Switch 2.
A fabricante recomenda que os jogadores configurem uma senha própria ou uma chave de acesso (passkey) antes do prazo. A decisão foi comunicada na terça-feira (10/11), mas a empresa não explicou os motivos para encerrar a integração.
Além de impedir o login com Google e Apple, a Nintendo deixará de permitir a criação de novas contas utilizando as credenciais dessas empresas. A opção de vincular contas também será removida. Outra função que será descontinuada é a missão do programa My Nintendo, que oferece pontos de platina para usuários que associam suas contas do Google. Esses pontos podem ser utilizados para resgatar recompensas.
A mudança não significa que os jogadores perderão suas contas. Quem já estiver conectado em um dispositivo poderá continuar utilizando o serviço. Entretanto, caso seja necessário entrar novamente, o acesso deverá ser feito com e-mail/ID de usuário e a senha da Conta Nintendo, ou com uma passkey previamente cadastrada.
O encerramento também não impede o uso de endereços do Gmail como e-mail cadastrado. A restrição vale para a autenticação realizada pelos serviços do Google e da Apple.
Para evitar problemas, a Nintendo orienta que os usuários verifiquem seus métodos de autenticação antes de janeiro. Quem ainda não possui uma senha própria pode configurá-la no site oficial da Conta Nintendo. O procedimento é relativamente simples.
A empresa também recomenda o uso de passkeys, tecnologia que permite entrar em serviços sem digitar uma senha tradicional. A autenticação pode ser realizada por impressão digital, reconhecimento facial ou desbloqueio do dispositivo.
Para cadastrar uma chave de acesso, é necessário entrar nas configurações de segurança da Conta Nintendo e selecionar a opção correspondente. É possível registrar até dez passkeys em dispositivos compatíveis.
Quem não lembra os dados de acesso pode seguir o guia de recuperação da Conta Nintendo. O aviso oficial informa que a mudança poderá sofrer atraso, dependendo do andamento das alterações no sistema.

articles.title: Militarisation de l’espace : l’armée US veut déployer une constellation de satellites autour de la Lune
articles.text:
L’armée américaine veut placer des satellites militaires en orbite autour de la Lune. Ce premier pas, encore discret, montre à quel point l’espace est devenu un terrain stratégique.
Car ces dernières semaines, l’enjeu du spatial militaire s’est clairement matérialisé. Notamment avec le satellite russe Kosmos 2612 qui s’est approché d’ICEYE-X36, un satellite d’observation, lors d’une manœuvre très curieuse. Et le secteur s’y prépare, avec des startups qui se lancent dans le développement de technologies spécifiquement dédiées à la défense en orbite. Il n’est donc pas étonnant que le Pentagone accélère dans ce sens.
Un premier pas vers une flotte militaire autour de la Lune
Ce 2 novembre, l’ARMée américaine a publié une demande d’informations destinée aux industriels concernant un » Cislunar Space System ». Il s’agit d’un ensemble de cinq satellites au maximum, à déployer dans l’espace cislunaire, c’est-à-dire la région qui entoure la Lune. Elle vise une mise en service d’ici à la fin de 2029.
Si le document ne précise pas encore la mission de ces engins, il détaille en revanche ce que le Pentagone attend des entreprises : fournir les satellites, y intégrer la charge utile confiée par l’État, assurer le lancement, puis piloter l’ensemble depuis le sol. Surtout, l’ARMée réclame une solution rapide et à faible risque, sans développements coûteux.
Autre fait notable : ces dispositifs serviraient de » véhicules de départ « pour préparer une constellation bien plus vaste. Mais l’ARMée prévoit d’abord d’attribuer jusqu’à cinq contrats d’études à prix fixe pour choisir, ou non, un partenaire industriel.
L’ARMée ne veut pas rester spectatrice face à la Chine
Plusieurs usages sont envisageables : suivre les objets présents autour de la Lune, assurer la navigation et les communications, ou encore surveiller l’activité d’autres pays. À noter qu’aujourd’hui, les satellites américains les plus lointains restent en orbite géostationnaire, à 36 000 kilomètres de la Terre.
Car le Pentagone a déjà accéléré sur l’exploitation de notre satellite. La mission Oracle-M doit par exemple décoller à la mi-2027 pour expérimenter des techniques de suivi d’objets dans l’espace cislunaire. Oracle-Prime devrait suivre d’ici la fin de l’année prochaine et surveiller satellites et débris depuis un point d’équilibre gravitationnel, situé aux trois quarts du chemin vers la Lune.
Un intérêt qui s’explique aussi par la course à la Lune entre Washington et Pékin. Le général Stephen Purdy, chargé des programmes avancés de la Space Force, rapporte que les plus hauts responsables du Pentagone parlent désormais publiquement d’un « domaine de combat ». Ambiance.
L’espace cislunaire désigne la zone d’influence entre la Terre et la Lune, incluant les trajectoires et orbites autour de la Lune. On y trouve des distances et des contraintes bien supérieures à l’orbite terrestre (basse, moyenne ou géostationnaire), avec des temps de trajet radio plus longs et des fenêtres de manœuvre plus limitées. La dynamique orbitale y est dominée par l’interaction gravitationnelle Terre-Lune, ce qui impose des plans de vol plus complexes que “tourner autour de la Terre”. C’est aussi une région stratégique car elle se situe sur les routes naturelles vers la Lune et ses points d’équilibre gravitationnels.
Un contrat d’étude à prix fixe impose un montant prédéfini pour une phase d’analyse (architecture, conception préliminaire, estimation de coûts et de planning), plutôt qu’un remboursement au fil des dépenses. Pour l’État, cela limite les dérapages budgétaires sur la phase amont et force les industriels à cadrer précisément le besoin et la solution. Pour l’industriel, le risque est de sous-estimer l’effort, mais la portée est généralement limitée à une étude, pas à la fabrication complète. Ce type de contrat sert souvent à comparer plusieurs options techniques avant de sélectionner, ou non, un partenaire pour la réalisation et l’exploitation.

articles.title: Silicon Motion Showcases Next-Generation Enterprise Storage Solutions at SC26
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Silicon Motion Showcases Next-Generation Enterprise Storage Solutions at SC26
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation, a global leader in designing and marketing NAND flash controllers for solid-state storage devices, today announced that it will showcase its PCIe Gen 5 and PCIe Gen 6 MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers and reference platforms designed to address the evolving storage demands of AI factories, Agentic AI, and large-scale inference deployments at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), taking place November 16 to 19 in Chicago, Illinois, at Booth #6816. The company will also highlight its enterprise PCIe NVMe boot drive solutions, including a demonstration featuring the NVIDIA DPU platform, alongside its Ferri-eMMC embedded storage solution with the ASPEED AST2600 BMC, showcasing storage technologies for AI servers and next-generation data center infrastructure.
Alex Chou, Senior Vice President of Enterprise Storage & Display Interface Solution Business at Silicon Motion"As AI infrastructure evolves to support multi-agent and increasingly complex agentic workloads, storage performance is becoming a critical factor in overall system performance and efficiency," "Our PCIe Gen 5 and Gen 6 enterprise SSD controllers are designed to address these challenges by delivering high performance, low latency, scalable capacity, and power efficiency, helping customers build the next generation of AI infrastructure."
At SC26, Silicon Motion will demonstrate how its enterprise SSD controllers, reference platforms, and boot drive solutions address evolving storage requirements across two key areas of AI infrastructure:
Enterprise SSD Controllers for AI Factory Storage Applications
- SM8366 MonTitan SSD Reference Design Kit for KV Cache Offload and Agentic AI Infrastructure: Built on Silicon Motion's PCIe Gen 5 SM8366 enterprise SSD controller, the MonTitan development platform supports multiple form factors, including U.2, E1.S, E3.S, and E1.L, with TLC and QLC NAND. Supporting high-capacity SSD configurations of up to 256 TB with QLC NAND, the platform enables scalable storage deployments for AI inference and KV cache offload. Powered by Silicon Motion's patented PerformaShape QoS Engine, the platform is designed to deliver low latency and predictable performance for demanding AI infrastructure workloads.
- SM8466: PCIe Gen 6 enterprise SSD controller delivering up to 28 GB/s sequential throughput and 7M random IOPS, supporting enterprise SSD capacities beyond 512 TB. Designed for high-performance AI computing and data-intensive applications, the SM8466 enables scalable, high-bandwidth storage architectures for next-generation AI infrastructure.
- SM8388: A power-efficient PCIe Gen 5 enterprise SSD controller optimized for high-capacity nearline SSD applications. Featuring a single-controller architecture, the SM8388 provides an efficient approach to scaling flash-based storage capacity while balancing performance, power consumption, and total cost of ownership for hyperscale data centers and AI infrastructure.
Enterprise Boot Drive Solutions for AI Server Ecosystems
- Enterprise PCIe NVMe DRAM-less Boot SSD Solutions: Designed for enterprise servers, DPUs, networking platforms, and AI storage nodes, Silicon Motion's DRAM-less boot SSD solutions offer flexible M.2 and BGA form factors, delivering compact, reliable, and power-efficient storage for diverse server architectures. The solutions are optimized to meet the endurance, reliability, and operational requirements of modern enterprise and AI infrastructure.
- Enterprise PCIe NVMe Boot SSD Solution with DRAM: Designed for near-CPU storage applications requiring frequent data access and consistent performance, this PCIe Gen 5 enterprise boot SSD controller solution supports M.2 2280 and E1.S form factors, with user capacities ranging from 480 GB to 3.84 TB. Delivering sequential read speeds of up to 14 GB/s, the solution supports demanding server workloads such as system logging, metadata management, and frequent read/write operations, where efficient data handling and predictable performance are essential.
Visitors are invited to experience Silicon Motion's latest storage innovations at booth #6816 during SC26.

articles.title: Agile Robots raises $500M funding led by SoftBank at $8.5B valuation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agile Robots raises $500M funding led by SoftBank at $8.5B valuation
German artificial intelligence robotics startup Agile Robots SE announced today that it has raised $500 million in new late-stage funding at an $8.5 billion valuation.
Japanese multinational investment holding company SoftBank led the Series F funding round. Other participants included AI chip leader Nvidia Corp., Japanese group Hitachi Ltd. and T Capital. The financing brings the total capital invested to $2 billion.
Founded in 2018 as a spinoff from the German Aerospace Center, Agile is one of Europe’s leaders in humanoid and mobile robots, robotic arms and dexterous robotic hands, along with the AI models needed to control them. The company combines robotic hardware with sensing, computer vision and AI software to automate physical work.
At the center of its hardware and software is force-sensitive manipulation. It allows robots to control how much force they use to handle delicate parts, perform precision assembly, and adapt to changing situations.
“Physical AI will fundamentally change how the world builds, moves and makes things,” said founder and Chief Executive Dr. Zhaopeng Chen. “Our vision is intelligent robots working alongside people in factories and warehouses everywhere, and Agile Robots is determined to lead that shift.”
Agile’s established flagship arm Diana 7 allows for precise manipulation and assembly; it includes torque sensors in all seven axes of movement that can detect and respond to the amount of force required to grab, lift and manipulate objects.
Agile One, the company’s humanoid robot, was publicly unveiled in November 2025 as an industrial-first platform. The launch extended the company’s approach into human-shaped platforms intended to carry out tasks across a production floor. It includes dexterous hands, advanced perception and human collaborative capabilities, allowing it to operate readily alongside personnel in manufacturing and logistics settings.
The company now offers an entire family of Agile One human-shaped robots, including the Agile One S, a compact humanoid reference platform built for research labs, universities, and developers. The company also offers Agile One SN, equipped with Dual Wuji five-finger hands and preconfigured for Nvidia Corp.’s Isaac GR00T AI models that act as robot “brains,” designed to let industry developers rapidly train, evaluate, deploy and test new robotic skills.
“We bring Physical AI out of the lab and into industrial production, across logistics, automotive, electronics and manufacturing,” added Chen.
The funding will support expansion into the United States, hiring more engineers and accelerating development of intelligent robotics applications. Additionally, the company said it intends to expand production, including in Germany, where it opened a facility in Fürstenfeldbruck, near Munich, in early 2026 to meet rising demand. Agile said the site can produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually.
Agile has deployed around 20,000 industrial robotic solutions for customers across the automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries. It boasts a growing portfolio of subsidiaries, including BÄR Automation, Franka Robotics, Idealworks and Krause Automation. articles.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: founder accused of multiple affairs, including with a Chinese spy
articles.text:
Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: founder accused of multiple affairs, including with a Chinese spy
Move comes after extramarital affairs were made public
Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has resigned from the company, following accusations of the CEO having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and subsequent details of a second alleged affair emerging.
The Board of Directors announced that the resignation is effective immediately, and that Colette Kress, who is currently Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, will be the interim CEO.
In a press statement, Nvidia said: “Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named.”
The board also said that a search for a new permanent CEO has begun, and that the successor to Huang could be either an internal appointment, or an external candidate could get the job.
Because of the importance of both Huang and Nvidia in the tech industry, there could be a lot of fallout from this, so we'll be keeping this story updated live as more information and and reaction to this news emerges.
Won't somebody think of the gamers?
There's been a lot of focus on the AI impact of Huang's departure, but what will it mean for gaming fans who've felt let down by Nvidia's focus on other areas more recently? It may not be good news, as our report Darren Allen explains.
Opinions from a noted analyst
Ming-Chi Kuo is a famous tech analyst, with great connections inside the supply side of the industry. He's laid out his opinion on what the initial takeaway should be from the market — though it sounds like Elizabeth Warren may disagree on his first point, because she certainly doesn't think Huang cutting ties with Nvidia should mean Nvidia remaining executives can breathe easy now…
Resigning may not be the end of the battle for Huang
US Senator Elizabeth Warren has laid out a clear message that she wants to investigate further what kind of information may have been compromised from Jensen Huang's relationships. It may not be a comfortable few months for Huang on many fronts…
Jensen Huang’s decision to resign from NVIDIA does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws. They still owe Congress answers.
— @warren.senate.gov (@warren.senate.gov.bsky.social) 2026-11-12T16:19:51.546Z
US President Donald Trump has just weighed in with his suggestion for Nvidia CEO:
What is going on with the GPU side of Nvidia? We have just reported that the Nvidia RTX 5080 Super GPU is rumored to have been canned, presumably due to high memory costs. This is a big blow to anyone hoping Nvidia would release new, sensibly priced, gaming GPUs any time soon.
I'm not sure if those tweets are embedding properly, but the last one was from Elon Musk being rather gleeful at the idea that he could hire Jensen Huang.
Well, it seems like Jensen Huang won't have much of a problem finding a new job after this.
Here is Colette Kress' apparent message to staff today:
Colette Kress will continue to serve as chief financial officer while also being interim CEO. There's a possibility she will be chosen as a full-time replacement, depending on how she copes with the next few challenging weeks.
Many PC gamers, including myself, will be hoping that whoever the new CEO of Nvidia is, they'll continue to make gaming GPUs. Whilst Nvidia made its name with graphics cards, the incredible success of its AI hardware has meant that the gaming division sometimes felt like an afterthought. There's a fear that any new CEO could double down on AI and further neglect Nvidia's gaming roots.
As for who comes next, because Huang was so integral to Nvidia, there hasn't been any real speculation until now who would take over from him.
As the company explains in its statement:
"Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."
Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985, so his admission of an affair was a shock, so when there were reports that he had been having a second extra marital affair, this time with someone working at Nvidia, it quickly became apparent that Huang's position was no longer tenable.
Even so, the suddenness of his removal has also been shocking. Nvidia's board of directors issued a statement saying: “Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."
US intelligence has been watching Alice Huang, and accused her of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The information behind this accusation is confidential, but it has added an extra layer of drama and betrayal to this whole saga.
After this disclosure, Nvidia's valuation plummeted by $430bn, and the company appointed an external law firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation.
Still, Jensen Huang is such an important and integral part of Nvidia and its success that it was still difficult to imagine him not being CEO.
This whole debacle started when Huang admitted that he had formed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, who was once an executive of Megaspeed, a Singaporean company that is a customer of Nvidia. 
In a message to his then-employees, Jensen Huang wrote that "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children."
But this was just the start.
Outside of Apple's CEOs and AI leaders, Jensen Huang was arguably the most recognisable tech CEO. In his trademark black leather jacket, he successfully made Nvidia the dominant player in consumer gaming graphics cards, before pivoting to AI chip powerhouse.
This made Nvidia one of the most successful companies in the world, so the importance of this dramatic fall from grace really can't be understated.
For some background about what's led to this, check out our article by Lance Ulanoff on why this is more than just a tech soap opera.

articles.title: Shipping giant Maersk confirms data breach as hackers demand $5 million ransom
articles.text:
Shipping giant Maersk confirms data breach as hackers demand $5 million ransom
World, say 'hi' to WhiteArmor, a new ransomware player on the block.
- Maersk discloses cyberattack on a legacy system from an acquired logistics company, with attackers allegedly stealing 100GB of data
- A ransomware group is demanding $5 million and threatening to leak records, passwords, and logistics information
- Maersk says core operations remain unaffected while investigating the breach and assessing the validity of the stolen data claims
One of the world's largest shipping and logistics companies, A.P. Moller–Maersk (often just called Maersk) has confirmed it recently suffered a cyberattack in which it lost sensitive data from one of its earlier acquisitions.
The criminals are now trying to pressure the company into paying a ransom, threatening to release all of the stolen information on the dark web.
Maersk issued an incident report, saying cybercriminals broke into a unnamed company it had previously acquired which reportedly operated a legacy system that the attackers managed to pierce.
“Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed,” Maersk said, “The incident is isolated to a local system, and we have found no indication that there has been any impact on other Maersk systems or customer and partner systems that connect to Maersk through integrations such as APIs and EDI.”
WhiteArmor takes the blame
The company said it does not expect the attack to disrupt its operations, and told its customers they can continue using its platforms to book and manage their shipments as usual.
But just because the data has not yet leaked, it doesn’t mean it won’t happen. According to BleepingComputer, a hacking group calling itself WhiteArmor added Maersk to its data leak site and told the company to pay $5 million in bitcoin - or else.
"Your contract-logistics arm, the former LF Logistics, runs fulfillment for many of the world's largest consumer brands. Five million dollars is roughly four hours of that EBITDA," the threat actor said. "You have 30 days to contact us and pay USD 5,000,000 in bitcoin."
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Companies usually don’t jump on the opportunity to pay the cybercriminals, so it’s safe to assume Maersk will ignore this invitation, and the data will leak.
However, we now know who it was stolen from - LF Logistics. This was an independent Hong-Kong-based third-party logistics company specializing in warehousing and ecommerce fulfillment. Maersk bought it in 2022 for $3.6 billion and integrated it into its own global Logistics & Services division, where it effectively ceased to exist as a separate entity.
Risky business
WhiteArmor claims to have stolen 100GB of data, including almost 30,000 driver records, passwords in plaintext, 33 SUPER_ADMIN accounts, signed delivery receipts, and 14.44 inventory rows with purchase orders and Advance Shipping Notices (ASN). Furthermore, it claims to have nabbed 27,842 mobile device logs containing phone numbers, email addresses, and even IMEI numbers.
If the claims are true, then this could be a major issue for Maersk. Passwords in plaintext and SUPER_ADMIN accounts means the company’s IT team will have to rotate all secrets to secure their premises. If any of the passwords are also used elsewhere, those services are at risk, as well. Details such as phone numbers and IMEI numbers are ideal for phishing and vishing attacks which have proven, time and time again, their destructive potential.
As one of the world’s largest container shipping companies, Maersk employs more than 100,000 people and generates more than $50 billion in revenue, as its global network includes more than 60 terminals and over 500 warehousing facilities.
In 2017, cybercriminals utilized the infamous NotPetya attack to wreak havoc on Maersk and bring its entire global network to a standstill, leading to damage that cost the business between $250 and $300 million.

articles.title: La carrera hacia 'GTA VI' se libra antes en consolas que en PC. En la era de la IA eso es un problema
articles.text:
Queda exactamente una semana para que 'GTA VI', el juego más ambicioso de la historia (al menos por presupuesto), llegue a PS5 y Xbox Series. Y, si no se sigue la información sobre videojuegos, es fácil que haya quien se pregunte cuándo saldrá 'Grand Theft Auto VI' en PC. La respuesta es que no hay respuesta por el momento porque Rockstar tiene una forma peculiar de hacer las cosas, con una versión de consolas que llega antes que el lanzamiento en PC.
El problema es que este año hay algo que puede romper los esquemas de la compañía: la opción de un port no oficial gracias a la IA o, directamente, llevando la versión de PS5 al PC.
Cuánto han tardado. Antes de abordar ese espinoso asunto, vamos con un repaso de la trayectoria de lanzamientos de la compañía. En la mayoría de casos, funciona para intentar adivinar cuánto tardará en llegar el juego a compatibles, aunque hay un par de casos que desentonan:
|  | Consola | pc | espera | 
|---|---|---|---|
| gta iii | Octubre de 2001 | Mayo de 2002 | Siete meses | 
| GTA Vice City | Octubre de 2002 | Mayo de 2003 | Seis meses y medio | 
| GTA San Andreas | Octubre de 2004 | Junio de 2005 | Siete meses y medio | 
| GTA IV | Abril de 2008 | Diciembre de 2008 | Siete meses | 
| GTA V | Septiembre de 2013 | Abril de 2015 | 19 meses | 
De los de esa lista, 'GTA V' fue el que más tardó porque querían que la versión en PC fuera la más completa. Fuera de la saga GTA, 'Red Dead Redemption 2' se hizo de rogar poco más de un año, y otros como 'Max Payne 3' o 'L.A. Noire' tardaron dos semanas y seis meses respectivamente. El caso más sangrante fue el de un Red Dead Redemption que salió en 2010 y que no llegó a PC hasta octubre de 2024. Los jugadores se tiraron 14 añazos pidiendo el port.
Tres buenos motivos. Esto no es un capricho y se mezclan varias cosas:
- Negocio. Strauss Zelnick, CEO de la empresa que posee a Rockstar, comentó que siempre empiezan por consola porque es ahí donde está el público principal y que siempre habían ido primero a consola. No es cierto, ya que el primer y segundo 'GTA' salieron antes en PC, pero lo que sí es cierto es que ahí está la pasta. En una filtración reciente se pudo ver que, mientras 'GTA Online' en PC tendría 894.621 jugadores semanales que aportan 264.273 dólares a Rockstar, Xbox One tendría 1.129.023 jugadores gastando 1.867.947 millones... y PS5 3.474.021 aportando 4.486.346 millones a las arcas cada semana.
- Técnico. John Ricchio, que fue productor de Rockstar en 'GTA V', 'Max Payne 3' y 'Red Dead Redemption', comentó que no es una postura contra el PC, sino de gestión de recursos. Rockstar desarrolla primero para consolas porque es donde están las limitaciones del hardware y considera que es mejor partir de esas limitaciones para luego dar rienda suelta en PC. Otro ejemplo lo puso Obbe Vermeij, quien fue director técnico de 'GTA III' y contó que hacer el port a PS1 desde la versión de PC obligó a recortar mucho, por lo que decidieron cambiar las tornas cuando empezaron a diseñar 'GTA III'.
- El port es otro proyecto.Ligado a esto, la versión de PC es un proyecto totalmente distinto que tiene más margen para retrasarse si algo sale mal (bugs, por ejemplo) o si quieren añadir más contenido, como los Atracos o 'GTA Online' desde el primer día en el caso de 'GTA V'.
Espera que suele valer la pena. Evidentemente, si sólo se juega en PC, que uno de los juegos más esperados de la historia tarde aún más en llegar a esa plataforma es un palo, pero estas versiones llegan o bien con más contenido o con mejoras visuales que no están presentes en la versión consolera. Hay excepciones, claro, como el desastroso port de 'GTA IV' que sólo se ha arreglado gracias a la comunidad, y ahí está algo positivo de estas versiones: los mods.
En PC, la comunidad es muy activa y, por la propia naturaleza de la plataforma, pronto llegan modificaciones que permiten arreglar cosas que la compañía no ha solucionado, añaden contenido o crean experiencias para las que el juego no se diseñó en un principio, como el caso de las comunidades de rol en 'GTA Online' que tanto éxito tuvieron hace unos años.
Miedo de 2026: el port con la IA. Visto esto, podríamos pensar que en un margen de entre seis y doce meses tendremos la versión de 'GTA VI' en PC, pero aquí entra en juego algo que no estaba presente en los anteriores lanzamientos y con lo que Rockstar no contaba hasta hace bien poquito: los ports que se están haciendo a PC gracias a la inteligencia artificial.
Debido a su naturaleza, es algo que no hemos tratado demasiado en Xataka, pero estas últimas semanas están apareciendo muchísimos juegos de consola en versiones "nativas" para ordenador gracias a lo que se conoce como "recompilaciones". Durante años se ha trabajado en versiones así y proyectos como 'Dusklight' de 'The Legend of Zelda Twilight Princess' lo demuestran, pero ahora con la IA se está haciendo a una velocidad pasmosa.
Muchos ni funcionan bien, pero sí se ejecutan en ordenadores y viewndo el interés por 'GTA VI', Rockstar debería tener miedo a que el lanzamiento no oficial en PC se realice más pronto que tarde. Entra en juego otra cosa, y es que han reventado la seguridad de PS5 y, aunque Sony la ha parcheado de cara al lanzamiento del juego, nada garantiza que puedan volver a violar esa seguridad, sacar los datos de 'GTA VI' de la consola y realizar esa recompilación a PC. Y esto noe s especulación, ya que Vermeij dijo que Rockstar debería darse prisa antes de que esa versión llegue primero.
La larga espera. Pero bueno, recompilación aparte, si sólo jugara en PC no tendría problema en esperar unos meses más. Como se suele decir, qué es una raya más para un tigre, o seis meses para algo que muchos llevamos esperando 13 años. Pero claro, la conversación no se va a detener alrededor de uno de los juegos más esperados y con esto arrancamos una programación de artículos que, esperamos, te resulten interesantes tanto antes... como después del lanzamiento de 'GTA VI'.

Galaxy Z Flip 7 recebe desconto imperdível na Black do Mercado Livre
Galaxy Z Flip 7 (256 GB) tem tela flexível de 120 Hz e câmera de 50 MP; dobrável da Samsung sai por menos da metade do preço no Pix durante a Black November 2026
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 de 256 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 4.499 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O dobrável da Samsung, com tela AMOLED flexível de 120 Hz e câmera wide de 50 MP, atinge um dos menores preços do ano durante a Black November 2026, com desconto de 51% sobre o original de R$ 9.199.
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 é um “quase gêmeo” do novo Z Flip 8, sendo a única diferença o processador: o modelo de 2025 possui um Exynos 2500 de 3 nanômetros, enquanto o novo vem com um Exynos 2600 de 2 nm. Ambos possuem 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB de espaço interno para guardar fotos e vídeos.

Sua bateria de 4.300 mAh suporta carregamento rápido de 25 W via cabo USB-C e de 15 W sem fio, e tem autonomia de até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung, ideal para usuários com agendas corridas.

articles.title: Avant même le Black Friday, Amazon fait descendre l’ampoule connectée Tapo L520E à 7,59€
articles.text:
Rendre une lampe de bureau ou un plafonnier pilotable à la voix ne demande ni pont domotique ni installation, à condition de choisir une ampoule Wi-Fi au bon culot. En pré-Black Friday, Amazon affiche la Tapo L520E à 7,59 € au lieu de 10,99 €, une ampoule E27 à la lumière du jour de 4000 K, pensée pour les pièces où l’on travaille plus que pour les ambiances tamisées.
La gamme Tapo de TP-Link, que nous croisons souvent pour ses caméras de surveillance, compte aussi des ampoules pilotées depuis la même application. La L520E en est la version la plus simple : un culot E27, une seule teinte de blanc et une intensité réglable. Amazon la propose à 7,59 € au lieu de 10,99 €, soit 31 % de remise sur le prix conseillé, dans le cadre de son opération pré-Black Friday.
L’offre parle d’abord à ceux qui veulent goûter à la maison connectée sans investir dans un écosystème complet, ou équiper une pièce de travail d’un éclairage programmable.
L’ampoule connectée Tapo L520E passe à 7,59 € au lieu de 10,99 € chez Amazon, avec la commande vocale Alexa et Google Assistant sans hub à ajouter.
Pourquoi choisir la Tapo L520E ?
- Aucun pont à acheter : Elle se connecte directement à votre réseau Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz, sans hub domotique. Le prix affiché correspond donc au coût total de l’installation, ce qui n’est pas le cas des systèmes qui passent par un pont Zigbee.
- La voix ou le smartphone : Elle répond aux commandes d’Amazon Alexa et de Google Assistant, et se pilote à distance depuis l’application Tapo. Vous pouvez ainsi l’éteindre à distance si vous l’avez oubliée en partant.
- Des automatismes utiles : Programmation horaire, minuterie et calage sur le lever et le coucher du soleil évitent d’y penser au quotidien. Le mode absence allume et éteint la lampe pour donner l’impression que le logement est occupé pendant vos congés.
Du bureau à l’entrée, là où cette lumière du jour trouve sa place
Une température de 4000 K donne une lumière neutre, ni jaune ni bleutée, qui convient à une lampe de bureau, à une cuisine ou à une salle de bain. Avec 806 lumens au maximum, soit l’équivalent d’une ampoule classique de 60 W, elle éclaire correctement une petite pièce ou un plan de travail. La gradation permet de la baisser le soir sans changer d’ampoule, et son angle de diffusion de 220 degrés répartit la lumière autour du luminaire. Dans une entrée, la programmation calée sur le coucher du soleil allume la lampe avant votre retour.
Le profil type est celui d’un premier équipement : vous avez une enceinte Echo ou Nest à la maison et voulez commander une lampe à la voix sans rien installer d’autre. Elle convient aussi aux locataires, puisqu’il suffit de la visser à la place de l’ancienne ampoule. Elle est en revanche moins indiquée pour un salon ou une chambre, où l’on cherche souvent un blanc plus chaud en soirée : sa fiche technique n’annonce qu’une seule température. Les utilisateurs d’iPhone qui comptent sur Siri et l’app Maison n’y trouveront pas leur compte, TP-Link ne citant qu’Alexa et Google Assistant.
Wi-Fi sans pont ou écosystème complet : où se situe cette ampoule
Dans notre comparatif des meilleures ampoules connectées, nous rappelons que des systèmes comme Philips Hue passent par un pont Zigbee, plus complet mais plus coûteux à l’entrée. La Tapo L520E se place à l’opposé : une ampoule Wi-Fi autonome, sans couleurs ni nuances de blanc, qui fait l’essentiel pour un prix très bas. Le même comparatif retient la WiZ Color E27, autre ampoule Wi-Fi sans pont, pour qui veut des couleurs. Dans la gamme Tapo, la L530E joue ce rôle multicolore, et nous en avions déjà relayé une promotion en mai 2025.
✅ Les points forts
- Connexion Wi-Fi directe, sans hub
- Compatible Amazon Alexa et Google Assistant
- 806 lumens, équivalent 60 W, intensité réglable
- Programmation, minuterie, lever et coucher du soleil
- Mode absence pour simuler une présence
❌ Les limites
- Une seule température de couleur, 4000 K
- Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz uniquement
- Pas de compatibilité Apple HomeKit annoncée
- Classe énergétique E
Avant le Black Friday, Amazon vend la Tapo L520E 3,40 € sous son prix conseillé, de quoi équiper plusieurs pièces à petit prix.
À 7,59 €, la Tapo L520E apporte la commande vocale, la programmation et le mode absence sans aucun équipement supplémentaire. La remise de 31 % reste modeste en euros, mais à ce prix, équiper trois lampes de bureau ou de cuisine coûte moins de 25 €. Pour un foyer déjà doté d’une enceinte Alexa ou Google, c’est une façon simple de mesurer l’intérêt de la domotique au quotidien.
Elle ne remplacera pas pour autant un éclairage d’ambiance. Pour un blanc chaud ou des couleurs, la L530E est plus adaptée, et pour l’app Maison d’Apple, mieux vaut choisir une ampoule qui affiche explicitement la compatibilité HomeKit, comme le conseille notre guide. Pour une lumière franche là où vous lisez, cuisinez ou travaillez, elle fait exactement ce qu’on lui demande.

articles.title: Le Graal de la voiture électrique se rapproche : la Silicon Valley fait tenir 1 000 recharges à une batterie 100 % solide, sans presse géante
articles.text:
Le Graal de la voiture électrique se rapproche : la Silicon Valley fait tenir 1 000 recharges à une batterie 100 % solide, sans presse géante
Cinq minutes pour passer de 10 à 80 % de charge, sur une batterie entièrement solide : QuantumScape, l'allié de Volkswagen installé dans la Silicon Valley, a dévoilé son exploit le 11 novembre. Son livre blanc révèle pourtant que la cellule était chauffée à 80 °C, quand le chinois CATL annonce déjà 3 minutes 44 avec une batterie classique. La vraie prouesse se cache ailleurs.
Le 11 novembre, QuantumScape a présenté Osprey, sa nouvelle plateforme de batterie entièrement solide. Ses cellules sont passées de 10 à 80 % de charge en 4,8 minutes, mais à 80 °C, un détail que le communiqué tait et que seul le livre blanc dévoile. La société de San José travaille avec Volkswagen depuis 2012 et a aussi signé avec Honda. Son avancée majeure tient ailleurs : ses cellules ont enchaîné 1 000 cycles de charge complets en conservant environ 80 % de leur capacité, sous la seule pression de l'air ambiant. Selon elle, aucune batterie dotée d'une cathode au sulfure n'avait publié un tel résultat dans ces conditions.
L'ironie n'échappera pas aux observateurs de longue date. En 2021, l'entreprise publiait sur son blog un billet intitulé "Le problème des sulfures", qui jugeait ces matériaux inaptes à servir de séparateur. Osprey garde donc le séparateur en céramique maison et l'anode en lithium métal, qui se forme lors de la première charge. En revanche, l'électrolyte liquide qui imprègne encore la cathode de la cellule QSE-5 cède sa place à un sulfure solide.
Recharge en cinq minutes : la Chine fait déjà mieux à température ambiante
Le test de recharge éclair a été mené sur une cellule à deux couches chauffée à 80 °C, bien au-delà du préchauffage habituel d'une voiture électrique. QuantumScape le reconnaît sur sa propre diapositive : la chaleur rend cette prouesse possible. Les anciens abonnés d'Autolib' s'en souviendront, les batteries Bolloré des Bluecar devaient rester chauffées, même à l'arrêt.
Sur ce terrain, la Chine a pris une large avance avec des batteries lithium-fer-phosphate classiques. En mars, BYD a lancé une batterie Blade de deuxième génération qui passe de 10 à 70 % en 5 minutes. En avril, CATL a présenté sa Shenxing de troisième génération, annoncée de 10 à 80 % en 3 minutes 44 secondes à température ambiante. Geely a suivi en septembre avec un 10 à 70 % en 4 minutes 30, rappelle l'agence Associated Press. QuantumScape assure seulement qu'aucune batterie solide au sulfure n'en était capable jusqu'ici. Le froid reste un point faible d'Osprey : à -20 °C, une minuscule cellule a restitué 68 % de sa capacité en décharge lente.
Batterie tout-solide : la pression, cauchemar des constructeurs
Les sulfures séduisent l'industrie par leur excellente conductivité, jusqu'à BYD, qui promet sa batterie solide pour 2027. Mais il faut comprimer la cellule en permanence pour que ses couches solides restent en contact. D'après l'analyse d'Electrek, les prototypes de laboratoire réclament souvent plusieurs dizaines d'atmosphères.
QuantumScape chiffre l'enjeu : à 20 atmosphères, une seule cellule de 10 cm sur 24 encaisse environ cinq tonnes, le poids de trois berlines. Pour tenir cette pression, un module a besoin de plaques d'acier de 22 mm, contre 4 mm pour un module lithium-ion classique. Siva Sivaram, PDG de QuantumScape, résume le problème : "L'industrie a massivement investi dans les batteries au sulfure, mais elle bute toujours sur les mêmes limites fondamentales." Sa parade consiste à cantonner le sulfure à la cathode, où il fait circuler les ions avec brio, et à confier le contact avec le lithium métal à la céramique.
	
L'industrie a massivement investi dans les batteries au sulfure, mais elle bute toujours sur les mêmes limites fondamentales.
L'essai d'endurance tient la route. Il a été mené sous une seule atmosphère, à 30 °C, sur une cellule à deux couches dont la cathode a la même surface que celle de la QSE-5 et une charge en matière active au niveau des meilleures batteries de voitures électriques actuelles. Sa capacité ne représente toutefois qu'une petite fraction de celle d'une cellule commerciale. Quant aux 1 100 Wh/L annoncés, contre 844 Wh/L pour la QSE-5, ils restent une projection fondée sur une pile bouton testée sur 100 cycles.
Osprey dans une voiture : aucune date
QuantumScape propose Osprey en licence ou en co-développement, et ses clients peuvent y greffer leur propre cathode. Le livre blanc reconnaît qu'un travail considérable reste à fournir sur les procédés industriels. La concurrence avance : Samsung SDI vise une production de masse au second semestre 2027, Toyota parle de 2027 ou 2028, et la batterie semi-solide de Svolt entre déjà en production. En France, ProLogium promet ses premières cellules solides à Dunkerque en 2028. Osprey devra convaincre avant que les constructeurs n'aient arrêté leurs choix.
