articles.title: I reviewed the new Apple TV 4K (4th Gen) as a long-time Apple TV fan — and Siri AI is very, very far from justifying this new high price
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Apple TV 4K (4th Gen) has very little meaningful improvement over the model from four years ago, yet the minimum price has doubled. It remains the best streaming device for those with lots of Apple devices, or those who care about data privacy — but its price now feels less proportionate to its advantages, and it hasn't kept up with the rest of the world in areas such as game streaming. The new remote that emits a noise is genuinely useful, but Siri AI is far too inconsistent to be useful upgrade.
- 
Features Excellent format support and great Apple integration, but no game streaming and half-baked Siri AI are disappointing.
- 
Performance Best-in-class video quality, and general performance in the OS is as slick as it gets for streaming boxes.
- 
Design A nice small box and hardy aluminum remote, though the latter is maybe too simple in places. Not everyone will love the built-in mics.
- 
Value The difference in quality and features between this and a cheaper streaming stick is not easy to justify, even it does bring better privacy.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent picture quality and format support
- + Features such as instantly entering passwords from your phone are great
- + New findable remote is useful
Reasons to avoid
- - The new price is hard to justify
- - Siri AI is inconsistent and not smart enough even at its best
- - Integrated mics will put off some people
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Apple TV 4K (4th Gen) review
The Apple TV 4K (2026) has been a strange product to review. I’ve been an Apple TV user since the Apple TV 3rd Gen, released in 2012 — in over a decade of sticking with it, I upgraded to the first 4K version, and the 2021 4K version with the better remote. I skipped the Apple TV 4K 2022 version, since the upgrades were minimal.
Despite this, I still recommended that version wholeheartedly to people buying for the first time, for the same reason that home theater enthusiasts online have recommended it. Its picture quality is best-in-class, its format support is excellent, and it offers more privacy protection (and an ad-free home screen) than its rivals from the likes of Roku, Amazon and Google — even though it’s more expensive than those models. The premium was worth paying.
But the premium has changed. The 2022 model launched at $129 / £149 / AU$219 as the starting price. In the middle of 2026, the price rose to $199 / £249 / AU$399. Now the new model is $299 / £299 / AU$449.
This is compared to $84.99 / £99.99 / AU$149 for the Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max, which has also had a price rise this year. The two products have basically the same format support, too.
I should mention here that the Nvidia Shield Pro is also now $299, but has much older tech in it than that this new Apple TV 4K. So the new model isn't bad value compared to the most direct competitor, the question is whether anyone really wants to pay this much for what's on offer from either of these compared to the cheaper equivalents.
Let's address it bluntly. Is the Apple TV 4K worth its higher price for upgraders from previous 4K models? Short answer: no.
Is it worth its higher price if you’re new to Apple TV boxes? Only if you care a lot about image quality and privacy.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Let’s start with the basics. The box runs tvOS, which is software specific to these devices, and is a spin-off from the iOS software used on iPhones. As a result, the Apple TV 4K is more versatile than most other streaming boxes. Yes, you have all the big streaming apps, but you also have practical apps that might be useful for some people — though obviously 99% of people will be focused on streaming.
The Apple TV 4K (2026) also supports games, in the sense that it works like a mini console, and you can connect games controllers to it (including the official PlayStation and Xbox controllers). This all works well enough, and there are some pretty decent games on there… though there are no game streaming services, due to restrictions in Apple’s policies, and I think this is a huge miss here in 2026.
We didn’t mind this too much when Apple released the last version, but cloud gaming has only grown in that time — and with the price of consoles and PCs spiking too, it’s becoming an increasingly tempting option.
It’s one of the slicker bits of streaming software in terms of performance, opening apps super-quickly and generally feeling perfectly smooth to move around. It does have its foibles — rearranging apps is theoretically an intuitive process, and yet suddenly this is where performance became less predictable. But I would say it’s generally the least annoying of the streaming systems.
That’s partly because it doesn’t have the same aggressive advertising right on the home screen that all the other platforms do. When you highlight a particular app, it might show recommendations from the app at the top of the screen, but you never have shows pushed on the home screen unless you’re already hovering over the app.
Apple also has, predictably, included some excellent integrations with its own products. The most useful is easily the ability to share passwords saved on your iPhone's Passwords app instantly with the Apple TV when you try to log into a service or app, though the ability to your iPhone's on-screen keyboard to search or type information in is also excellent.
There are lots of other integrations as well, some of which will be more useful than others to individuals. You can see your iCloud photos and use them as a screensaver (though the Apple TV's beautiful built-in screensavers are one of its highlights). You can use your iPhone for FaceTime calls, where you see other people on the big screen, and your iPhone camera beams your image over to the TV and then to the person you're calling. You can beam audio or video over to the box from your phone using AirPlay.
The remote that comes with the latest Apple TV is relatively easy to use. You don’t have lots of buttons for directly launching streaming services, for better or worse — this is, let’s be clear, a form of advertising of its own, but it’s one that can be pretty useful. That said, there is a button that looks like a TV, and pressing this once launches the Apple TV app, which includes the Apple TV streaming service’s wares — but it’s also a hub for things you’ve been watching in other services, so it’s not purely a play to get you to watch Apple’s own stuff.
Unfortunately, the Apple TV hub doesn’t work with every major streaming app, with Netflix being the most egregious omission. Netflix also doesn’t work with Siri’s ability to play movies or the universal search function. So it’s possible to ask Siri to find a particular movie, the system will tell you which of your apps have it so you can watch it right away… except you have to check Netflix separately.
There’s a button on the side of the remote to invoke Siri if you want to use your voice to find and control things, but Apple has now also added microphones to the Apple TV box itself, so you can — in theory — use the device hands-free. Just say ‘Siri’ and ask what you want to ask.
And the reason Apple has included these new mics is because Siri has now been upgraded to Siri AI, and the company is surely hoping you’ll want to use Siri way more now that it’s smart. The problem is that while Siri itself may have become smart, its implementation often still isn’t.
The most obvious gripe for me was the information presentation, and the density of that information. Sometimes it’s too crowded, packing paragraphs of information with no formatting to aid readability into a small window on the side of the screen. At other times, it’s too simple, taking over the full screen yet displaying text so large that only a few words fit in before the cut off (and if you click the remote hoping it will open the rest of the text, it doesn’t — a different part of the screen is selected by default). It’s always too much or not enough, and it’s somehow never just right.
How smart Siri is at recognizing things within a movie/show is really variable. This might be tied to whether the default tvOS player is used by the app, because in some of them I’d ask Siri a question about what I’m looking at, and it would claim there’s a blank screen.
Watching Netflix, it told me it couldn’t see what I was viewing, and asked me to just tell it the name of the movie — but if I paused it, causing the name to appear on screen, and asked the same question, it was now able to see the title. A system that responds so differently per-app is not really a reliable system.
I asked it to identify the music playing in the background of a scene of Tony on Prime Video, and it claimed the song was… the movie Tony on Prime Video. I asked it who the guy on the screen was, and it recognized Dominic Sessa, bringing up info about his work. Then I asked the same question when Stavros Halkia was on screen, and it brought up info about Dominic Sessa again.
It worked better when I watched a documentary about chefs, and the system was able to identify Marco Pierre White instantly when I asked — but that was on a service that used the native player, so I don’t know if that helps Siri have better visibility of what’s on-screen.
Later, I asked the system to show me some good Jason Statham movies available on the streaming services I have. It was able to suggest some movies on the services I have, but there was no visible info on how they were rated, even though the results took up the whole screen. So I asked a follow up question about whether any of them were actually worth watching, and then it showed movies it considered to be good, but not whether they’re available on my services. So I asked a third time if any of these good movies were available on my services, and it finally narrowed down to a list of what I originally asked… except the first movie on the list wasn’t accessible on any of my streaming apps.
I browsed to The Pelican Brief’s page on Netflix, and I asked if I would like this movie. I thought maybe it would use the fact that I own a lot of ’90s thrillers — including Grisham thrillers The Firm and The Rainmaker — in my Apple TV Store library to make a recommendation.
Instead, it gave me an OK text-based answer about what people generally think of the movie, presented in the dullest way possible as just a column of text. I really hoped it might do something clever here, because not only do I own movies like the ones mentioned above, but I also own The Pelican Brief. So it was a trick question, but I really thought a smarter system would be able to spot that I might like a movie that I went to the trouble to buy already.
One thing it pointed out in its description of whether I might like it is that some people think the movie is overlong. So I asked for similar but shorter movies available on all my services, and it gave me exactly two middlingly reviewed options. I own Witness in my Apple TV library, so couldn’t it pull that recommendation out for someone looking at an on-the-run potboiler thriller lasting under two hours?
Incidentally, it offers source citations for answers, but you can’t open them to check if it’s actually pulled correct information from the pages. It’s an attempt at being reassuring, but I have witnessed LLM answers cite a source where the source says something totally different to the answer, so I personally see little use in citing a source I can’t click to verify.
Another challenge: I asked Siri which episode of Taskmaster has Ed Gamble melting down over transporting some ducks in the garden. It identified the episode. It didn’t offer to play it, so I prostrated myself and asked if we could watch it, please. It fired up the relevant app and played… the most recent episode, not the correct one. That could be an issue with the app rather than Siri AI, but the result is a failure either way.
I tried the same thing with another show I thought might work better, because I owned it in my Apple TV library. I asked which episode of 30 Rock had a particular quote from Alec Baldwin (which I got slightly wrong). While it identified the episode correctly, yet again it didn’t consider whether maybe I’d like to watch it. So again I asked to play it, and this time it took me to the correct episode, presumably because it has better access to individual episode data, given I own them within the Apple TV app. But also, it didn’t automatically play it even though that's what I'd asked; I still needed to click to play it. So if I’m trying to do all of this hands-free with the new mics on the box, without touching the remote, it was a failure.
Ultimately, Siri still feels half-baked on Apple TV. It’s just that now it’s a much more elaborate type of bread that’s been half-baked. And sure, it’s technically in beta still, so Apple might say it should be no surprise that it’s been half-baked — but what are we paying so much more for the elaborate chip inside the new Apple TV 4K for, if not the AI powers? It’s not like the movies play any differently.
I know that the mics that are always listening will be contentious with people. And while it’s possible to turn this functionality off in the settings, there’s nothing like the switch Sonos has on its products that electronically disconnects the mics so they literally cannot hear any more — it’s just a software change, which won’t reassure everyone.
However, the built-in mics are useful for one of the few truly notable new tricks of this Apple TV, which is that you can now use these hands-free mics to ask Siri to find your remote when it’s lost. The remote will make a noise, saving you from hunting in vain.
Crucially, this even works while the Apple TV 4K is in standby mode — you don’t get any sign from the box itself that it’s heard you (I thought maybe its little white light might flash). But sure enough I asked “Siri, where’s the remote” while my whole system was off, and it started chirping from under a cushion.
I mentioned early on that image quality is one of the most important elements that draws enthusiasts to the Apple TV, and that’s for a few reasons. One is its support for both Dolby Vision and HDR10+ advanced HDR formats, not to mention the HDR10 and HLG standard formats.
It can also change formats on the fly, including switching to 24fps output for movies, so that you get more natural movie motion, especially if you have a 120Hz TV.
But it also has excellent upscaling of lower-resolution content, better than the vast majority of TVs people own at home. The latest flagship TVs with good neural-network-based upscaling might beat it, but there’s also a lot more mediocre ‘AI upscaling’ in TVs — the Apple TV takes non-4K content and makes it look naturally sharp, consistently, without looking like it’s been messed with.
On top of this, the other factor is that the Apple TV movie store offers basically the highest-quality streaming you can get outside of expensive specialist services such as Kaleidescape. These moves come at a higher bitrate (meaning the amount of data transferred per second) than anything like Netflix or Disney+ offers, so they look cleaner and more detailed, especially in scenes with lots of motion.
And while you can buy movies from the Apple TV store on other devices, the highest bitrate quality is reserved for Apple TV 4K boxes only — and the movies look fantastic. It’s a big part of why I use them to this day. The problem is that these movies look exactly the same as they do on the previous 4K model, which was less than half the price at launch.
So let’s talk about whether there’s really anything here for upgraders. I already said I think there basically isn’t, but I should at least show my working. When it comes to picture and sound performance, there are no meaningful changes.
Even if I thought Siri AI was a great upgrade, it is coming to the last two generations of Apple TV 4K too, so that isn't a reason in itself. Some people obviously might like the hands-free mics, and the remote that can play a noise so you can find it. The latter is a truly useful upgrade; it just isn’t worth the price if you have one of the previous models.
The new model does have faster Wi-Fi. Again that doesn’t mean much in itself, but it appears to have enabled this version to support a full surround system using HomePods for the first time (seemingly due to lower latency in the wireless tech, based on what Apple's said about it).
You can have four HomePod or HomePod Mini 2nd Gen speakers (two at the front, two at the back), or two HomePod 2nd Gen (at the front) and two HomePod mini 2nd Gen (at the rear). Because these are separate products, I’m not going to factor them into reviewing the Apple TV 4K — however, I have been very impressed with the HomePod 2nd Gen as TV speakers with Apple TV in the past.
The price of getting a setup like these used to be highly competitive too, though after HomePod price rises they’re a little more middle of the pack compared to wireless home theater speaker options from the likes of Hisense and Sonos.
Ultimately, I'm dropping our score for this model to 3.5 stars from 4.5 stars for its predecessor, and it all comes down to value. Yes, prices are rising everywhere, but I think this Apple TV box has simply fallen outside of the point where I can argue that it's good value despite being more expensive than the competition.
If the money is no problem to you, I strong recommend it. But compared to the Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max, is the extra privacy and slick Apple integration worth an extra

articles.title: Computer vision startup Tristar AI pulls in $12.4M to automate quality control for manufacturers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Computer vision startup Tristar AI pulls in $12.4M to automate quality control for manufacturers
All too often, manufacturing defects seem to slip past human eyes, with the result that high-speed production lines turn into expensive scrapheaps. Computer vision startup Tristar AI Inc. has just raised $12.4 million in early-stage funding in order to try to put an end to these costly mistakes.
Today’s Series A round was led by Isogon Ventures and saw participation from Blackhorn Ventures, Ford Street Ventures, NextView Ventures, TenOneTen and Capgemini’s ISAI Cap Venture Fund.
Tristar AI is gearing up to transform quality assurance in manufacturing at a critical moment for the industry. Manufacturers have found themselves squeezed by a combination of rising raw material costs and growing labor shortages, and these problems have been made even more acute by the U.S. government’s insistence on bringing more manufacturing back home.
According to data from the Capgemini Research Institute, 48% of U.S. companies have invested in reshoring projects this year. But 83% say they’re worried about the lack of skilled industrial workers needed to fulfill those initiatives.
One of the major challenges for manufacturers is that they’re still encumbered by inefficient inspection protocols that rely on either manual checks, or in a best-case scenario, rigid, rule-based machine vision systems. Quality control is essential for any manufacturing operation, but the inefficiency of these protocols makes it a significant roadblock too.
It forces companies to take skilled workers off production lines and sometimes even bring their entire operations screeching to a halt. Yet there are many occasions where they still miss subtle flaws in their products, resulting in wasted materials, downtime, missed deadlines and sometimes even very expensive customer claims.
Founder and Chief Executive Salem Karani is all too familiar with the inefficiency of manual inspection. He told SiliconANGLE that while growing up, he would often accompany his father to his family’s plastic film manufacturing plant in Houston, turning up at all hours of the day and night in order to troubleshoot production issues that could spring up at any moment. Because the company’s margins were so tight, any period of extended downtime could threaten its profitability, so he would spend hours with his dad frantically troubleshooting line errors.
It was this experience that ultimately inspired Karani, who studied computer vision at Harvard and MIT, to develop an automated quality inspection system that can operate continuously without slowing down production. “The problem was never that people didn’t care about quality,” Karani said. “It’s that people catch problems after the fact, once they’ve already cost time, materials and customers. Tristar gives every production line a live record so teams can act when it matters most.”
Computer vision in manufacturing operations is not a new concept, but where Tristar differs is through its use of more sophisticated artificial intelligence models that can adapt to changing conditions, materials and defect types. The startup’s platform looks at machine telemetry, the quality of the products coming off the line and the activity of human operators, allowing it to uncover issues the moment they emerge and immediately understand where the problem is, and why it occurred.
Best of all, the system can integrate with factories’ existing systems, such as cameras, sensors, programmable logic controllers, enterprise resource planning systems and so on That enables them to get up and running without an expensive overhaul.
Isagon Ventures General Partner Paco Riberas said he’s backing Tristar because manufacturers are losing far too much money to avoidable defects. “In today’s industry, precision isn’t optional, and Tristar makes it possible,” he said. “Its AI vision catches defects in real time, directly on existing production lines. Salem and his team are building the quality standard for modern manufacturing.”
Tristar’s early traction has been encouraging. Its system already monitors more than 500 production lines across North America and Europe.
Customers include global packaging giants such as Amcor, DuPont and Klöckner Pentaplast, and also some of the biggest suppliers to automakers such as Toyota, Honda and Mercedes, Karani said. Those customers report defect detection accuracy rates of between 95% and 99%, and say the platform pays for itself in an average of just four months.
Karani said the goal now is to expand Tristar’s platform into new manufacturing sectors and enhance the capabilities of its computer vision AI to try and improve its accuracy even further. Ultimately, he sees the company as the operational system of record for factory floors, giving manufacturers more visibility into everything about their production operations, from the raw materials to the finished product.
“Physical AI will play a critical role in the future of manufacturing,” said Capgemini Ventures’ Matthieu Eyriès. “Tristar combines advanced AI capabilities with a strong understanding of industrial environments, addressing concrete manufacturing challenges with measurable impact.”

articles.title: Black Friday Amazon: 5 climatiseurs réversibles de retour en stock, pour l’hiver comme pour l’été
articles.text:
Le prix repère du gaz augmente encore de 5,8 % au 1er décembre, et les climatiseurs réversibles, qui se faisaient rares pendant les canicules de l’été, reviennent en stock sur Amazon à l’approche du Black Friday. Nous en avons retenu 5, du modèle mobile pour une chambre à la console murale pour un séjour, en regardant de près ce que chacun annonce vraiment en mode chauffage.
Cet été, les climatiseurs mobiles ont disparu des rayons à chaque vague de chaleur, au point que nous suivions leurs retours en stock d’une canicule à l’autre. Ceux qui reviennent aujourd’hui sur Amazon sont réversibles : ils rafraîchissent en été et produisent de la chaleur en hiver. Les acheter maintenant, c’est s’éviter la course aux stocks de juin prochain, et disposer dès cet hiver d’un chauffage d’appoint pour une pièce.
Côté chauffage, le contexte s’y prête : la Commission de régulation de l’énergie a relevé son prix repère du gaz de 6,6 % au 1er novembre, puis de 5,8 % au 1er décembre, à 206,26 €/MWh TTC. Un climatiseur réversible ne remplace pas une chaudière, mais il permet de chauffer une seule pièce sans monter le thermostat de tout le logement. Les prix indiqués sont ceux affichés sur Amazon le 12 novembre : il s’agit d’une disponibilité retrouvée, pas encore de remises Black Friday, à une exception près, signalée dans la liste.
5 climatiseurs réversibles de nouveau disponibles sur Amazon
- Climatiseur mobile réversible CREATE Silkair Dual Connect 9000 à 270,95 €
- Climatiseur mobile réversible MovAIR MOV16-12-BC 3,5 kW à 499,90 €
- Climatiseur monobloc mural réversible Sannover Fresho 12 HP 2,5 kW à 890,99 €
- Climatiseur mobile chaud et froid ZJUNLI à 516,21 € (15 % de réduction appliqués au passage de la commande)
- Climatiseur mobile LIFEZEAL 14 000 BTU avec chauffage à 719,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Chambre, séjour, grand volume : à chacun son climatiseur réversible
Ces cinq appareils n’ont ni la même puissance, ni la même installation, et leurs fiches ne sont pas toutes aussi détaillées. Point commun : aucun n’est vendu par Amazon lui-même, mais par des vendeurs tiers de sa place de marché, qui assurent aussi l’expédition. Voici ce que chacun annonce, et ce qu’il faut vérifier avant de commander.
- CREATE Silkair Dual Connect 9000 : le moins cher de la sélection vise les pièces jusqu’à 20 m², une chambre ou un studio. Il annonce 9 000 BTU en froid, une pompe à chaleur de 7 000 BTU en chaud, une déshumidification jusqu’à 42 litres par jour et un pilotage depuis l’application Create. Il est livré avec un kit pour fenêtre coulissante ; pour une fenêtre battante, le fabricant renvoie vers une autre version. Sa note moyenne de 3,3 sur 5, sur 12 avis, invite à lire les retours avant de commander.
- MovAIR MOV16-12-BC : c’est le modèle mobile dont la fiche chauffage est la plus précise : 3,20 kW en chaud avec une classe énergétique A+, 3,50 kW en froid en classe A. Il ajoute le Wi-Fi, une déshumidification de 40,8 litres par jour et un niveau sonore annoncé entre 51 et 53 dB(A). Comptez 26 kg à déplacer d’une pièce à l’autre.
- Sannover Fresho 12 HP : ce n’est pas un climatiseur mobile, mais une console monobloc qui se fixe au mur, sans unité extérieure : il faut percer deux ouvertures pour l’entrée et la sortie d’air. En échange, c’est le seul de la liste à annoncer un coefficient de performance, un COP de 3,98, en classe A+, pour 2,5 kW (9 000 BTU) et 46 dB. Supports, grilles et tuyaux sont fournis, mais la pose demande des travaux. Avec 4 sur 5 sur 27 avis, c’est aussi le mieux noté des cinq.
- ZJUNLI : sa fiche est la moins claire de la sélection. Le titre annonce 18 000 BTU en froid et 9 000 BTU en chaud, mais le lien mène à une variante intitulée « 5000 BTU », et la page ne donne ni surface conseillée, ni classe énergétique. Une réduction de 15 % s’applique au passage de la commande, et l’expédition est annoncée sous 6 à 7 jours. À réserver à ceux qui prendront le temps de vérifier la variante avant de payer.
- LIFEZEAL 14 000 BTU : avec 14 000 BTU annoncés pour des pièces jusqu’à 40 m², une oscillation automatique sur 70° et l’application Smart Life, il vise les grands séjours. Il promet un mode chauffage, mais sans puissance chiffrée, et sa fiche technique ne mentionne que le refroidissement. Pour un usage d’abord estival, il a sa logique ; pour chauffer, les fiches du MovAIR et du Sannover sont plus complètes. Amazon n’en affichait plus que 11 exemplaires le 12 novembre.
Chauffer avec un climatiseur réversible, est-ce vraiment rentable ?
Un climatiseur réversible chauffe en pompe à chaleur : il prélève des calories dans l’air et restitue plus d’énergie qu’il ne consomme d’électricité. Avec le COP de 3,98 qu’annonce le Sannover, un kilowattheure d’électricité produit près de 4 kilowattheures de chaleur. À ce rendement, la chaleur revient bien moins cher qu’avec un radiateur électrique classique, et soutient la comparaison avec le gaz, dont le prix repère moyen atteindra 206,26 €/MWh TTC au 1er décembre.
Les modèles mobiles, eux, n’annoncent pas de COP, et leur rendement en chauffage reste plus modeste : comme le rappelle notre comparatif des meilleurs climatiseurs mobiles, la dépression d’air créée par l’évacuation pénalise les monoblocs. Ils conviennent pour tempérer une chambre ou un bureau quelques heures, pas pour chauffer un logement entier. Si vous pensez d’abord à l’été prochain, ce comparatif classe aussi les modèles par usage, du plus silencieux au plus adapté aux grands espaces.
Climatiseur réversible en hiver : vos questions
Un climatiseur mobile réversible peut-il remplacer un chauffage au gaz ou au fioul ?
Non, il sert de chauffage d’appoint pour une pièce. Les modèles mobiles de cette sélection annoncent de 20 à 40 m² quand leur fiche précise une surface, et leur rendement en chauffage reste en retrait d’une pompe à chaleur fixe.
Faut-il percer un mur pour installer ces climatiseurs ?
Pas pour les quatre modèles mobiles, livrés avec un kit pour fenêtre qui fait passer le tuyau d’évacuation. Le Sannover Fresho 12 HP fait exception : cette console murale demande deux ouvertures dans le mur.
Quelle puissance choisir selon la taille de la pièce ?
Les fiches donnent un repère : 9 000 BTU pour une pièce jusqu’à 20 m² sur le CREATE, 14 000 BTU jusqu’à 40 m² sur le LIFEZEAL. Le Sannover annonce 9 000 BTU et le MovAIR 3,5 kW, soit environ 12 000 BTU, sans préciser de surface.

articles.title: El sube y baja de Bitcoin: cuál es su valor este 12 de noviembre
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
Pese al avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
Mientras el debate se acalora cada día más sobre la conveniencia o no de su uso, bitcoin cotiza este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) en 72494.74 USD, lo que supone un cambio de -1.63% con respecto a las últimas 24 horas y una variación de 0.0% con referencia a su valor alcanzado en la última hora.
En cuanto a su capitalización de mercado, ha mantenido el puesto #1 entre las monedas digitales.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Más allá del debate sobre su éxito, el 11N deja una pregunta: para qué sirve realmente una huelga general en 2026
articles.text:
El 11N ha sido una huelga especial por varias razones. Además de ser la primera gran convocatoria nacional en 14 años y llegar en plena campaña preelectoral, su detonante fue la crisis de la vivienda, un problema grave que sin embargo no está directamente relacionado con los derechos laborales. Dejando claro todo eso, el 11N también ofreció algunas imágenes previsibles que habíamos visto en huelgas anteriores: piquetes, manifestaciones, negocios cerrados y un encontronazo entre la patronal y los sindicatos a la hora de estimar el éxito de la convocatoria.
Más allá de todo eso, de las peculiaridades y el guion esperable del 11N, hay algunas preguntas que quedan botando: ¿Para qué sirven las huelgas en 2026? ¿Tienen el mismo impacto que en los años 90 u 80 o han perdido capacidad de presión? Y sobre todo, ¿cómo diablos medimos su alcance?
¿Cómo fue el 11N? La respuesta más rápida es ‘depende’. Depende de a quién le preguntes. Aunque en un principio hablaron de un seguimiento “dispar”, con un nivel de respaldo que oscilaba entre el 41 y 75% en función de la región, los sindicatos acabaron celebrando la jornada como “un éxito rotundo”.
La cosa cambia si consultamos a la CEOE. Para la patronal española fue un “fracaso” sin paliativos, una movilización que alcanzó un “mínimo histórico” con un apoyo de apenas el 5%. Por si no fuera suficiente, a ese baile de cifras se suman las que han ido desgranando las instituciones de uno y otro color.
En realidad, nada de eso resulta sorprendente. Los desacuerdos en torno a los niveles de seguimiento son la tónica habitual en estos casos (lo noticioso sería que no lo hubiera), igual que lo son otras imágenes que dejó el 11N: piquetes, carreteras cortadas, retrasos en el transporte, manifestaciones multitudinarias y disturbios con decenas de detenidos, como vimos en Barcelona o Madrid.
¿Cómo medir el alcance real? Esa es la pregunta que se han hecho no pocos analistas en las últimas horas. El 11N dejó una demostración de fuerza innegable en las calles, pero… ¿Y a nivel laboral y económico? ¿Cómo se puede medir su impacto real? Hace tres o cuatro décadas la respuesta sería sencilla. Contabilizar los paros en cadenas de producción industrial, obras, terminales de trenes o aeropuertos resulta fácil; pero en los últimos años la economía española ha experimentado varios procesos que complican considerablemente la foto.
¿Qué cambios? Para empezar, España ha visto cómo el sector terciario ganaba peso desde mediados del siglo pasado hasta representar más del 65% del PIB. Si hablamos de empleo, los servicios aglutinan el 76,5% de la población ocupada, cifra que se dispara por encima del 80% en ciertas comunidades autónomas.
A esos datos se añade el aumento del teletrabajo, que si bien sigue en niveles inferiores al promedio europeo se ha convertido en un concepto familiar para cientos de miles de españoles. Se calcula que alrededor de 3,2 millones ya desempeñan sus tareas en remoto al menos de forma ocasional.
Hay otro factor que complica valorar el impacto real de una huelga: la automatización y digitalización, favorecida por la inteligencia artificial. No es una cuestión menor. En 2025 la firma Redwood Software estimaba que el 73% de las empresas habían aumentado su partida para automatización. Se trata de un dato internacional y en España todavía son minoría quienes aseguran trabajar en fábricas plenamente digitalizadas, pero aun así es un dato elocuente.
¿No hay forma de medirlo entonces? Sí, sí la hay. Como recuerdan Kiko Llaneras y Jacob Vicente en El País, los analistas que quieren medir el alcance del 11N tienen varios recursos a su alcance, incluido el que tal vez más se ha repasado (y citado) durante las últimas horas: el consumo de energía eléctrica.
Red Eléctrica Española (REE) publica a diario un informe con dos datos reveladores: su previsión de demanda de energía y el consumo real, que va actualizando sobre la marcha. Para el primer valor (el pronóstico) los técnicos de REE tienen en cuenta factores como el día de la semana o la época del año, pero no variables como una convocatoria de huelga general.
Es un matiz importante porque la brecha entre su estimación inicial y el consumo real nos habla de una anomalía que se explica, al menos en parte, por cambios en la producción y consumo del país. Como se puede ver en los gráficos de arriba, ayer ese desfase llegó a ser considerable a media mañana y media tarde, una ‘fotografía’ muy distinta a la que dejaron los últimos miércoles.
¿Cómo de preciso es? Esa es la clave. No es lo mismo medir el seguimiento de una huelga fijándonos en los parones de cadenas de montaje o el absentismo en unas oficinas que hacerlo tirando de los indicadores de REE. Al fin y al cabo, en la demanda eléctrica influyen otras variables, como la meteorología.
Eso sin contar con que no todos los sectores tienen el mismo impacto en el balance eléctrico (una fábrica puede pesar más que muchas tiendas juntas) y los servicios mínimos de una empresa siguen apuntalando parte de la demanda, independientemente del porcentaje de plantilla que secunde la huelga.
¿Es el único desafío? No. Hay otra pregunta aún más complicada. Si tenemos en cuenta el peso creciente del sector servicios, el aumento del teletrabajo, el abanico de posibilidades creado por la IA o el aumento de autónomos y freelances en España, ¿hasta qué punto son efectivas las huelgas en 2026? ¿Conservan la misma capacidad de presión que hace 20 o 30 años, cuando frenar una fábrica tenía un impacto directo y evidente en los ingresos de la empresa?
Al fin y al cabo en modelos de negocio digitales y automatizados, los trabajadores pueden parar un día sin que eso afecte a la demanda y el flujo de ingresos. Por ejemplo, es el caso de las plataformas de streaming, las lavanderías automáticas, servicios self-service o banca online, por citar algunos casos. En un mundo donde negocios de ese tipo son más habituales… ¿Pierden capacidad de presión las huelgas, más allá de su alarde de fuerza en las calles?

articles.title: Fairphone CEO says new US carrier partnership will free consumers from ’a system built on planned obsolescence and constant, expensive upgrades'
articles.text:
Fairphone signs first US carrier partnership, making the easily repairable Fairphone 6 Plus more widely available: ‘For too long, US consumers have been captives of a system built on planned obsolescence’
Giving the Fairphone 6 Plus a boost
- The Fairphone 6 Plus is now available via Boost Mobile in the US
- This gives buyers a way to get the phone without paying one lump sum
- The Fairphone 6 Plus is modular and therefore easily repairable
Having offered repairable, long-lasting smartphones to consumers in Europe for years, Fairphone finally got a foothold in the US with the Fairphone 6 Plus, which launched in both regions back in August. But until now, you could only buy the phone outright in the US, limiting its appeal in a market dominated by carrier plans.
Today, though, that’s changed, as the company has announced that it's partnered with Boost Mobile to offer the Fairphone 6 Plus with a monthly plan through the carrier’s network. And with Boost Mobile having over seven million subscribers, that massively increases Fairphone’s potential audience.
This is a particularly important step for the Fairphone 6 Plus specifically, whose $649.99 retail price is quite expensive for the specs on offer — so splitting that figure across the length of a contract could make it seem more affordable and, Fairphone hopes, more popular.
And in the long run, you could save money with Fairphone anyway, since the Fairphone 6 Plus is designed to be held onto for a long time — it's got 12 user-replaceable parts, long-term software support, and a five-year warranty.
Built to last
Raymond van Eck, CEO of Fairphone, said of this Boost Mobile partnership that “for too long, US consumers have been captives of a system built on planned obsolescence and constant, expensive upgrades,” adding that “we’re thrilled to team up with Boost Mobile to give more Americans access to a device built to be opened, repaired, and kept alive for years.”
The Fairphone 6 Plus has a mid-range Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset, 12GB of RAM, Android 16 — with software support promised through 2033 — and a 6.31-inch (1116 x 2484) 120Hz screen.
It also has a 50MP main camera, a 13MP ultra-wide, a 32MP front-facing camera, a 4,415mAh battery, 256GB of storage, and a microSD card slot.

articles.title: Senado vai fornecer iPhones 18 Pro a senadores em contrato de R$ 6 milhões • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Senado vai fornecer iPhones 18 Pro a senadores em contrato de R$ 6 milhões
Pregão Eletrônico prevê comodato de 95 unidades do iPhone 18 Pro para senadores e diretores. Licitação também inclui 330 celulares Android a servidores.
O Pregão Eletrônico 290/2026 tem causado polêmica. Trata-se de uma licitação criada pelo Senado Federal para contratar serviços de telefonia móvel. O detalhe que chama a atenção é que, entre esses serviços, está o fornecimento de 95 unidades do iPhone 18 Pro para os 81 senadores, enquanto os servidores da Casa receberão 330 celulares Android.
Aberto em 27 de outubro deste ano, o Pregão 290/2026 tem um teto estimado em R$ 6.045.048. A previsão é a de que a proposta vencedora entre em vigor em fevereiro de 2027, quando os senadores eleitos em 2026 iniciarão seus mandatos.
O contrato determina o fornecimento, em regime de comodato, de 95 unidades do iPhone 18 Pro com 512 GB de armazenamento aos senadores e à cúpula administrativa do Senado. Esses aparelhos terão que ser substituídos dentro de dois anos para que seus usuários possam acompanhar a “evolução tecnológica”.
Também é necessário haver uma reserva técnica correspondente a 5% das unidades para substituição imediata de iPhones quebrados, perdidos ou roubados.
Para os servidores da Casa, a licitação prevê a contratação de 330 celulares de nível intermediário, com modelos como Samsung Galaxy A37 5G e Motorola Moto G86 5G servindo de referência — modelos similares poderão ser fornecidos.
Também fazem parte do contrato o fornecimento de modems 4G/5G, de 150 chips SIM adicionais, entre outros recursos.
O Pregão 290/2026 visa substituir um contrato firmado em 2022 que forneceu 93 unidades do iPhone 13 Pro a senadores e diretores, e 290 celulares intermediários a servidores.
Um dos pontos de questionamento é: por que os senadores precisam de um celular tão avançado e caro? No site da Apple, o iPhone 18 Pro de 512 GB custa a partir de R$ 13.499.
A veículos como a CNN, o Senado enviou a seguinte nota sobre o assunto:
A respeito do Pregão 290/2026, informamos que a escolha de marca e modelo é fundamentada em critérios técnicos, dentre os quais a compatibilidade com o padrão tecnológico adotado desde 2022, que possibilite a continuidade operacional e a migração integral de aplicativos e dados.
Os modelos iPhone 18 Pro em comodato serão destinados aos senadores e a alguns diretores. Os outros modelos serão destinados ao desempenho de atividades previstas no Ato da Comissão Diretora nº 10/1996.
Em tempo: se levarmos em conta o mês atual (novembro de 2026), o salário bruto de um senador no Brasil gira em torno de R$ 46 mil, sem contar outros “benefícios”, como auxílio-moradia e verbas de gabinete.
Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil), presidente do Senado, contestou o modo como o assunto vem sendo abordado, especialmente pela imprensa. O senador destacou que o pregão explora um modelo de comodato (um tipo de empréstimo), ou seja, os iPhones e demais celulares não estão sendo comprados pela Casa:
Todos os órgãos do Estado brasileiro fazem comodato de aparelhos de telefone, mas a narrativa é maior que o fato. Não é compra de iPhones. A mentira está prevalecendo em cima da verdade.
Davi Alcolumbre, senador da República pelo Amapá

articles.title: Axelera AI Unveils Titania Architecture
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Axelera AI Unveils Titania Architecture
Axelera AI, the leading provider of purpose-built AI hardware acceleration technology, unveiled the details behind Titania, its third-generation silicon architecture in a chiplet design. Titania is highly programmable and energy efficient and will deliver high performance at interactive speeds, all within the power and cooling limits of existing data centers, rather than the 100-kilowatt-plus liquid-cooled racks that today's highest-density GPU systems require.
Performance expectations for Titania are up to 7x the throughput per watt compared to the best data center grade servers available, and up to a 20x better TCO. Each Titania-based system-in-package (SiP) will contain two Titania chiplets which are then packaged in a range of form factors, including standard PCIe cards as well as OCP-compliant UBB baseboards with eight Titania OAM modules connected in a scale-up network. In support of over $300 million in confirmed Titania commitments, these form factors will be available via OEM partners in an inference server configuration in both air- and liquid-cooled configurations.Titania builds on the programmability, performance and efficiency of its shipping predecessors, Metis and Europa, and further expands the product line from embedded, edge and enterprise AI into large-scale data center inference. Designed for interactive and highly variable AI workloads of enterprises, sovereign clouds, decentralized and modular data centers, telcos and AI factories, Titania combines Axelera AI's high-performance, energy efficient Digital In-Memory Computing (D-IMC) architecture with a new chiplet-based design, high-capacity LPDDR6 memory, high bandwidth scale-up connectivity and programmable RISC-V compute in one package. Available in multiple form factors including industry standard PCIe cards as well as OCP-compliant boards, Titania offers customers the flexibility to solve for their inference needs. Supported through the Voyager toolchain, Titania deployments will support tensor, expert and pipeline parallelism, as well as speculative decoding, KV cache offloading and disaggregation out of the box. In practice, that means large models use every card in the servers, each user gets tokens faster and operators get more useful work per kilowatt from the rack they already own.
Fabrizio Del Maffeo, co-founder and CEO of Axelera AI"The biggest challenge most organizations face as inference becomes the dominant AI workload is the tokenomics of their infrastructure. For enterprises, it's becoming impossible to own their own AI infrastructure due to high CAPEX expenditures including rebuilding their data center footprint. So they choose between a server that can only compute small or medium models and paying over one million dollars for a data center server that requires specialized infrastructure. Titania solves this problem and gives enterprises, neoclouds, telcos and sovereign clouds alike the opportunity to take advantage of owning and controlling their own inference infrastructure."
Designed for the infrastructure customers already have
Titania builds on the D-IMC architecture first introduced with Axelera AI's Metis platform and extended through Europa, enhanced with floating-point support, more and smaller cores, and better coordination of data movement to deliver exceptional performance for generative AI and data center scale.
The Titania architecture's highly efficient data movement and compute engine enables it to use low-cost, readily available LPDDR6 memory rather than relying on scarce high-bandwidth memory (HBM). LPDDR6 gives each package 128 GB of capacity at lower memory power than HBM, while avoiding any dependence on HBM supply or packaging requirements. Sparse mixture-of-experts models are large in total parameters but small in active parameters, so memory capacity and effective utilization matter more than peak bandwidth if it goes unused. The result is a platform designed to deliver high-performance inference while reducing power, cooling, and infrastructure requirements.
Titania will scale from PCIe cards for standard servers and OAM modules to multi-accelerator servers and larger AI infrastructure deployments. An eight SiP accelerator Titania reference server (codenamed AX8) is designed to provide 20 PFLOPS of FP8 compute, 1 TB of accelerator memory, and 19.6 TB/s of memory bandwidth within a standard 4U, air-cooled server, at 5-6kW typical, enabling large AI models to run within existing data center power and cooling environments. One Axelera server will hold a 1.6 trillion-parameter model at FP4 with the headroom for KV cache, two fit within a legacy 15 kW rack and five fit within a 30 kW air-cooled rack.
Evangelos Eleftheriou, CTO and co-founder of Axelera AI"We don't ask anyone to trust a simulator. The architecture behind Titania already turns 88 percent of its memory bandwidth into tokens on Europa silicon that is shipping today, and Titania builds on that capability as the third generation of our architecture. It's not simply about maximizing peak compute. It's about how efficiently we can turn power, memory, and infrastructure into useful AI performance at scale."
One architecture and software foundation from edge to data center
Titania is Axelera AI's third-generation AI acceleration technology, following Metis (optimized for performance and energy efficiency) and Europa, which extended the company's architecture into enterprise AI infrastructure.
The same Voyager SDK and AxeleraScript (AxScript) software foundation extends across all three generations, allowing customers to develop and optimize AI applications on Axelera AI technology today and carry those workloads forward as the portfolio expands. The Titania PCIe card is designed as a drop-in replacement for the Axelera Server 250p (a FHFL four-chip Europa card), so models deployed on Europa today move to Titania in 2028 without re-porting.
One card serves LLMs, vision-language models, and video: on-chip 8K decode and 4K encode with H.265 and AV1 codecs remove the host-CPU cost of video pipelines, so a single Axelera AI system runs language, speech and vision models alongside live video.
Titania will be offered across multiple form factors, with OEM and ODM partners building the technology into servers and larger systems. Axelera AI's Titania goes into production in Q3 2027 and already has customer deployment commitments through the beginning of 2028.
Designed in Europe, trusted globally
Designed in Europe with support from the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking's DARE initiative, Titania extends Axelera AI's mission to make high-performance, energy-efficient AI infrastructure more accessible to enterprises, cloud providers, governments and AI infrastructure operators globally. 
Axelera AI will provide a deeper technical look at the Titania architecture during SC26, November 15-19, in Chicago, IL., at booth 3251 in McCormick Place.

				Axelera AI

articles.title: Vous n’arrivez pas à installer le Patch Tuesday de novembre sur Windows 11 ? Le correctif est en route
articles.text:
Le Patch Tuesday de novembre provoque des erreurs d'installation sur plusieurs PC Windows 11. Microsoft a annoncé une solution, mais le retour à la normale pourrait encore prendre un peu de temps.
Déployée le 10 novembre, la mise à jour de sécurité KB5132061 devait corriger un sacré paquet de vulnérabilités et apporter aux PC compatibles les dernières améliorations de Windows 11. Seulement voilà : depuis sa sortie, les signalements d'échecs d'installation se multiplient. Microsoft vient tout juste de reconnaître l'incident et de confirmer qu’un patch était dans les tuyaux.
Des échecs d’installation persistants
Les difficultés concernent Windows 11 25H2 et 26H2, mais aussi les éditions Entreprise et Éducation de Windows 11 24H2. Comme le rapporte Windows Latest, l'installation de KB5132061 peut progresser jusqu'à 99 % avant d'échouer et d'afficher l'un des codes d'erreur 0x800f0993, 0x80070306 ou 0x800f0989. Les tentatives suivantes aboutissent souvent au même résultat, y compris lorsque la mise à jour est téléchargée manuellement depuis le catalogue Microsoft.
Redmond a bien confirmé le problème et annoncé une réparation automatique, dont le déploiement a débuté le 11 novembre à 19 heures, heure de Paris. Distribuée par Windows Update, elle devrait parvenir aux PC concernés sous 24 à 48 heures, sans intervention de leur part.
Que faire si KB5132061 refuse de s'installer ?
Pour les PC concernés, le plus simple consiste donc à laisser Windows Update faire son travail. Vérifiez que les mises à jour ne sont pas suspendues et que votre ordinateur est bien connecté à Internet.
Vous pouvez également ouvrir les Paramètres > Windows Update, puis cliquer sur « Rechercher des mises à jour » pour vérifier si la réparation est disponible. Si Windows vous propose de télécharger et d'installer KB5132061, suivez les instructions et redémarrez votre PC si nécessaire.
Si le blocage persiste au-delà des 48 heures annoncées par Redmond, vous pourrez lancer l'utilitaire de résolution des problèmes de Windows Update, accessible dans Paramètres > Système > Résolution des problèmes > Autres utilitaires de résolution des problèmes. Cet outil permet de détecter et de corriger les anomalies susceptibles de perturber l'installation des mises à jour. Si rien n'y fait, Microsoft recommande de contacter son assistance.
Le « Patch Tuesday » désigne la vague mensuelle de correctifs publiée par Microsoft, généralement le deuxième mardi du mois. Elle regroupe surtout des mises à jour de sécurité qui corrigent des vulnérabilités exploitées ou exploitables dans Windows et certains composants associés. Ces correctifs peuvent modifier des fichiers système sensibles, des pilotes ou la pile de sécurité, ce qui explique qu’ils aient parfois un impact sur la stabilité ou la compatibilité. En environnement pro, ils sont aussi un élément clé de la conformité (gestion des risques, politiques de patching) et de la réduction de la surface d’attaque.
Ces codes sont des indicateurs techniques renvoyés par Windows Update quand une étape de l’installation échoue (vérification, copie de fichiers, intégration dans l’image système, etc.). Ils pointent souvent vers un problème de composants de mise à jour (Component Store), de dépendances manquantes ou de corruption/état incohérent dans les packages à installer. Le fait que l’installation monte jusqu’à 99 % puis échoue suggère fréquemment un échec au moment de l’« application » finale (commit) et du nettoyage. Sans analyse des journaux (CBS.log, WindowsUpdate.log), le code seul ne suffit pas à diagnostiquer précisément, mais il permet de classer le type d’échec côté maintenance système.
Une réparation automatique est un correctif que Windows Update peut pousser pour rétablir la capacité à installer une mise à jour, sans forcément livrer immédiatement une nouvelle cumulative complète. Concrètement, cela peut prendre la forme d’un petit package correctif, d’une mise à jour de la pile de maintenance (Servicing Stack) ou d’un ajustement de logique côté déploiement (détection/conditions d’installation). L’objectif est de débloquer l’échec d’installation en corrigeant le mécanisme ou le prérequis qui coince, puis de relancer l’installation du correctif principal. C’est différent d’une cumulative, qui embarque directement un ensemble de correctifs fonctionnels et sécurité pour l’OS.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal
Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors today announced the resignation of Jensen Huang, now former chief executive and president of the artificial intelligence chipmaker, amid a scandal, naming Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO.
The news arrives following numerous industry reports that the board intended to replace Huang as CEO after revelations of a second extramarital relationship with an executive at Nvidia, coming mere days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
News initially broke over the weekend that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, no relation, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and an alleged Chinese spy. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang facilitated $7.5 billion in chip sales to China. According to another report, Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who serves as vice president of healthcare.
The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities concluded Alice Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset. Upon revelations of the affair, the Associated Press reported that President Trump announced that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the allegations, while adding, “I think that he’ll be in good shape.”
Late Wednesday, the Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust Huang and discussed a potential replacement as CEO. Huang has no obvious single successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. Reportedly, the board sought counsel from an outside firm to find someone to fill the role.
With the announcement, Nvidia stock was falling more than 5% in trading today, backing off an even steeper loss at the opening. Yahoo Finance calculated that Nvidia has lost more than $600 billion in market value since the previous Thursday, likely with more shocks to come.
“Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.”
Kress has served as executive vice president and CFO since joining in September 2013. Her accolades include leading the company’s finance organization and working to build the company’s dominance in the AI chip industry. Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp.
The CFO was intimately involved with Nvidia’s widespread financing of AI compute providers, in particular its backing of not only AI leaders OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC — the latter set to go public as early as next week — but also neoclouds such as CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV. Those financings have been criticized by some as “circular,” meaning Nvidia essentially invested in customers so they could use the money to buy more of its graphics processing units.
The potential successors to Huang, who had 30 direct reports, include no one obvious choice and a succession plan apparently was not in place. Candidates that some have speculated about include Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia years ago, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing and creator of its CUDA software considered the real moat for its business.
“The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Forrester Vice President and Group Research Director Stephanie Balaouras told SiliconANGLE in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.””
Balaouras added that “tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers and investment plans.”
Huang is best known for co-founding Nvidia in 1993 in a San Jose Denny’s and has served as its CEO since. His departure will likely send further ripples through the AI silicon and software industry. He has been deeply involved in Nvidia’s product strategy and built longstanding customer relationships, helming the company as it became the behemoth it is today.
Nvidia commands roughly 80% of the data-center AI chip market, although industry estimates vary by methodology. Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. puts its share of AI computing power shipped at 63% in the second quarter of 2026. Other market carve-outs include custom chips built by cloud companies within the broader supply, including Google LLC’s tensor processing units at 25%, Amazon Inc.’s custom silicon at 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI hardware accelerators at 4%.
Nvidia is expected to report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 17.
With reporting from Robert Hof

articles.title: La dimisión de Huang hace que Nvidia se deje 550.000 millones de dólares en valor de bolsa
articles.text:
Tras la publicación de una exclusiva de The New York Times, Jensen Huang admitió en un memorando a sus empleados que había tenido una aventura extramatrimonial. La polémica tal vez no habría llegado mucho más lejos si no fuera porque su amante ya estaba siendo investigada por presunto espionaje para China.
La respuesta de los accionistas de Nvidia no se hizo esperar: a partir de ese momento, sus acciones iban a iniciar un desplome bursátil superior al 14%, lo que implica una pérdida de capitalización cercana a los 550.000 millones de dólares en solo cuatro días.
El primer romance le costó muy caro. Nvidia venía de marcar un récord histórico durante el mes de octubre, con unas acciones valoradas en unos 243,37 dólares y una capitalización cercana a los 6 billones de dólares. Sin embargo, el viernes 6 de noviembre el precio de sus acciones se había templado y su cotización afrontaba el fin de semana con unos nada despreciables 186,64 dólares por título, fijando la capitalización total de Nvidia en unos 4,5 billones de dólares.
Sin embargo, tras conocerse la aventura de Huang y la posterior investigación por espionaje, el lunes dibujaba un panorama muy distinto. La acción comenzó un rápido descenso que llegó a registrar el 8% de pérdidas, pero al final del día recuperó su precio y se situó en unas pérdidas de "solo" el 4,3%. Por ponerlo en contexto, eso son más de 200.000 millones de capitalización. El martes no mejoró.
La tendencia bajista siguió su curso, y Nvidia cerraba un martes de pesadilla con una caída del 5,47% que se sumaba a los malos resultados del lunes, dejando el precio de las acciones a 168,89 dólares. En solo dos días, la compañía había perdido 400.000 millones de capitalización.
La segunda infidelidad y el castigo nocturno. En la apertura de los mercados del miércoles, todo apuntaba a que la tormenta había arreciado y el indicador bursátil aparecía por primera vez en verde marcando una subida del 2,92%. La alegría les iba a durar poco.
El NYT publicó que Huang había tenido una segunda aventura con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta que depende directamente de Huang. El artículo, además, deslizaba que la junta preparaba la destitución de Huang y su salida de la compañía. Tras el cierre, las acciones perdieron todo lo ganado y se desplomaron por debajo del 8,4%.
La dimisión le da la estocada. Para terminar de rematar a los accionistas, Nvidia anunció que Huang dejaba la presidencia, la dirección ejecutiva y el consejo, con efecto inmediato. Colette Kress, hasta ahora directora financiera, será la CEO interina hasta que la compañía designe a un sucesor definitivo.
La noticia ha caído como un jarro de agua fría entre los inversores, que hundieron la cotización de Nvidia un 14%, hasta los 148,80 dólares. No obstante, cuando se recuperaron del susto, se moderó la caída fijando el descenso en el 7% al momento de publicar esta noticia, con un precio de 165,15 dólares por título. En total, en poco menos de cuatro días, Nvidia se ha dejado un 13%, lo que supone una capitalización de 4,01 billones de dólares. Es decir, la tormenta Huang se ha llevado por delante casi 550.000 millones de dólares del capital de Nvidia.
Ahora la principa preocupación para Colette Kress es qué explicaciones va a dar a los inversores en la presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre que la empresa mantiene para el martes 17 de noviembre. 550.000 millones es muchísimo dinero incluso para Nvidia.

articles.title: Nvidia sans Jensen Huang : qui pourrait remplacer l’illustre PDG ?
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, dorénavant ex-PDG de Nvidia, a avoué avoir entretenu une relation extraconjugale avec Alice Huang, dirigeante de l’entreprise singapourienne Megaspeed. Le problème : celle-ci est soupçonnée par Washington d’être une espionne au service de la Chine. Depuis cette révélation, Trump a défendu Jensen Huang, Pékin a démenti et le FBI a ouvert une enquête.
Mais la situation s’est encore empirée avec une nouvelle information : le dirigeant de Nvidia aurait entretenu une autre relation, cette fois-ci avec une salariée de l’entreprise. Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia a tenu une réunion ce jeudi 12 novembre pour décider du sort du PDG de Nvidia, mais c’est finalement Jensen Huang lui même qui a remis sa démission, avec effet immédiat. Colette Kress, la directrice financière de Nvidia, assurera la direction de l’entreprise jusqu’à la nomination d’un successeur permanent. Bloomberg affirme de son côté que Nvidia a fait appel à une entreprise externe pour identifier des candidats au poste de PDG. Mais qui cela pourrait-il être ?
Qui pourrait remplacer Jensen Huang au poste de PDG de Nvidia ?
La première hypothèse, sans doute la plus probable, serait que Nvidia choisisse un successeur parmi ses propres dirigeants, déjà en poste au sein de l’entreprise. Colette Kress, directrice financière de NVIDIA depuis 2013 et actuellement chargée de diriger l’entreprise, pourrait être définitivement nommée à ce poste. D’autres candidats sont également considérés : Ian Buck (ingénieur et spécialiste de l’IA chez Nvidia depuis 2004), Michael Kagan (directeur technique de NVIDIA) ou encore Bryan Catanzaro (vice-président de la recherche en deep learning appliqué).
Seconde hypothèse : Nvidia pourrait faire appel à une personnalité extérieure à l’entreprise pour succéder à Jensen Huang. Dans ce cas-ci, les possibilités sont multiples. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, expert en gouvernance d’entreprise et doyen associé principal des études sur le leadership à la Yale School of Management, estime que Nvidia pourrait faire appel à nul autre que Tim Cook, qui a cédé sa place de PDG d’Apple en septembre dernier à John Ternus. Pour rappel, Tim Cook avait succédé à Steve Jobs, soit le fondateur d’Apple. Dans l’hypothèse où il deviendrait CEO de Nvidia, il succéderait donc à Jensen Huang, cofondateur de Nvidia.
D’autres noms, externes à Nvidia, sont également évoqués : Eric Schmidt (ancien CEO de Google), Lisa Su (CEO d’AMD soit le principal concurrent de Nvidia) Lip-Bu Tan (PDG d’Intel) ou encore Bret Taylor (président du conseil d’administration d’OpenAI).
Elon Musk est prêt à embaucher Jensen Huang
Elon Musk semble d’ores et déjà prêt à embaucher le dorénavant ex-dirigeant de Nvidia. En effet, un utilisateur de X a demandé à Elon Musk d’embaucher Jensen Huang, ce à quoi il a répondu : « Ce serait un honneur ». Il reste maintenant à voir ce que décidera Jensen Huang, même s’il risque de se faire discret pendant un petit moment.
De son côté, Tim Sweeney, fondateur et PDG d’Epic Games, ne doit pas bien accueillir la démission de Jensen Huang. Sur le réseau social X, il avait indiqué : « Sauvez Jensen. Ce serait, de la part du conseil d’administration de NVIDIA, un niveau de stupidité comparable à celui d’Apple lorsqu’il a licencié Steve Jobs, et cela porterait gravement atteinte aux intérêts des États-Unis ». Jensen Huang n’aura finalement pas été sauvé, la situation étant devenue trop tendue.
