articles.title: L'IA de Gemini s'invite sur Apple Car Play
articles.text:
Google déploie depuis quelques jours l’application Gemini sur Apple CarPlay. Les utilisateurs d’iPhone peuvent y discuter à voix haute avec Gemini Live pendant qu’ils conduisent.
Gemini manquait encore à l’appel sur CarPlay, là où ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot, Meta AI et Grok sont déjà installés. Google rattrape ce retard avec un lancement global, pour tous les utilisateurs iOS.
Une onde sonore, deux boutons et un historique synchronisé
Gemini Live, c’est le mode conversation de Gemini. Le conducteur peut parler, l’IA répond à voix haute, et il est possible de la couper pour ajouter un détail, de changer de sujet ou de faire une pause. Sur CarPlay, l’écran se limite à une onde sonore qui indique si Gemini écoute, réfléchit ou répond. Deux boutons, en haut à gauche, permettent de couper le micro ou de mettre fin à l’échange. En ouvrant l’app, on reprend un chat récent ou on en démarre un nouveau.
A l’arrivée de ChatGPT sur CarPlay, nous apprenions que les assistants de cette catégorie n’ont droit qu’à des interactions vocales, sans texte ni image à l’écran. Gemini arrive plus de sept mois après l’IA d’OpenAI. Jusqu’ici, il n’était présent sur CarPlay qu’à travers Google Maps, sans conversation Live ni application dédiée.
Google met l’accent sur la connexion à sa suite Google Workspace. Gemini peut ainsi lire votre agenda, vous dire à quelle heure partir pour votre prochain rendez-vous, vous donner votre résumé du jour, faire le point sur vos mails non lus ou résumer un long fil d’e-mails, puis vous aider à dicter une réponse. Il peut aussi recommander un lieu à proximité, raconter l’histoire d’un monument ou servir de partenaire pour répéter une présentation ou préparer une conversation difficile. Tout se synchronise avec l’app Gemini de l’iPhone et une fois garé, les résumés et les notes sont déjà dans l’historique.
Pour en profiter, il faut avoir mis à jour l’app Gemini sur l’iPhone, autorisé le micro et utilisé Gemini Live au moins une fois sur le téléphone. Précédemment, Gemini Live avait été déployée sur Android Auto. Siri dispose de son côté d’une app autonome dans iOS 27, elle aussi compatible CarPlay.

articles.title: Google presenta AlphaGenome 2, la IA que busca anticipar enfermedades a partir de cambios en el ADN
articles.text:
Google DeepMind presentó AlphaGenome 2, una nueva herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) diseñada para analizar el ADN humano y predecir cómo pequeñas modificaciones genéticas pueden alterar el funcionamiento de las células y favorecer el desarrollo de enfermedades. El sistema busca ayudar a los científicos a identificar qué variaciones del código genético afectan la actividad de determinados genes y en qué tipos de células se producen esos cambios.
El desarrollo representa un avance respecto a la primera versión de AlphaGenome, presentada el año anterior, y forma parte de los esfuerzos de Google por utilizar la inteligencia artificial para comprender procesos biológicos complejos. La herramienta no está diseñada para diagnosticar pacientes, sino para ofrecer información que permita a los investigadores estudiar el origen de distintas patologías y encontrar nuevas pistas para desarrollar tratamientos.
El desafío que intenta resolver está relacionado con la forma en que funciona el material genético. Aunque prácticamente todas las células del cuerpo contienen el mismo ADN, no todas utilizan los mismos genes. Una célula muscular y una célula del sistema inmunitario, por ejemplo, activan diferentes instrucciones genéticas para cumplir sus respectivas funciones.
Por eso, comprender cómo una modificación del ADN puede alterar ese comportamiento resulta fundamental para investigar enfermedades hereditarias, trastornos inmunológicos y otras patologías complejas.
Cómo funciona AlphaGenome 2 y qué puede descubrir
La nueva IA de Google DeepMind analiza las variantes genéticas para estimar cómo pueden modificar la actividad de los genes en diferentes tejidos y tipos celulares.
Una de sus principales mejoras consiste en pasar de estudiar promedios generales de tejidos a identificar comportamientos específicos de células individuales y sus distintos estados. Esto permite obtener información más detallada sobre dónde se produce una alteración genética y qué consecuencias podría tener.
Según sus desarrolladores, Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli y Žiga Avsec, el rediseño de la arquitectura del modelo permitió mejorar su capacidad para predecir los efectos de las variantes del ADN.
Entre los resultados destacados figura su capacidad para identificar cambios genéticos relacionados con enfermedades. En un conjunto de datos correspondiente a 28 tipos de células inmunitarias, la primera versión reconocía el 16% de las variantes causales, mientras que AlphaGenome 2 elevó esa proporción al 30%.
Esta mejora permitiría a los investigadores detectar más modificaciones genéticas relevantes y comprender mejor qué procesos celulares intervienen en determinadas enfermedades.
La IA también estudia cómo responde el sistema inmunitario
Otra de las novedades de AlphaGenome 2 es su capacidad para analizar células en diferentes estados de actividad. Esto resulta importante porque una misma variante genética puede tener consecuencias distintas dependiendo de las condiciones en las que se encuentre una célula.
Los investigadores utilizaron datos de un estudio sobre una vacuna de ARN mensajero contra el COVID-19 para comprobar esta capacidad.
El modelo consiguió distinguir las células T del sistema inmunitario que habían sido activadas por la vacuna de aquellas que permanecían en reposo. Además, identificó que una variante genética relacionada con los casos graves de COVID-19 modificaba la actividad de determinados genes con mayor intensidad cuando las células estaban activadas.
Este comportamiento no habría sido detectado de la misma manera al analizar únicamente células en reposo. El hallazgo demuestra por qué resulta importante estudiar el contexto en el que actúan las variantes genéticas y no solamente su presencia en el ADN.
AlphaGenome 2 busca pistas sobre enfermedades complejas
La herramienta también incorpora mejoras para estudiar células que no habían sido analizadas previamente. Según Google DeepMind, puede incorporar información procedente de nuevos experimentos con células individuales sin necesidad de volver a entrenar todo el modelo.
Esto facilitaría el trabajo de los científicos que investigan diferentes tejidos y condiciones biológicas, al permitirles ampliar sus análisis con nuevos datos.
Otro de sus objetivos es relacionar las variantes genéticas con genes específicos y tipos celulares concretos. Esta capacidad podría contribuir a investigar enfermedades complejas, como la diabetes tipo 2, cuyo desarrollo puede involucrar múltiples factores genéticos y ambientales.
Antes de esta actualización, Google ya había presentado AlphaGenome Atlas, una plataforma que reúne predicciones sobre cerca de 9.000 millones de posibles cambios de una sola letra en el genoma humano. Esta herramienta complementa el trabajo de AlphaGenome al ofrecer información sobre las posibles consecuencias moleculares de esas variaciones.
Sin embargo, AlphaGenome 2 todavía es una herramienta de investigación. Sus predicciones no equivalen a un diagnóstico médico ni demuestran por sí solas que una variante genética provoque una enfermedad.
Su importancia está en ofrecer a los científicos nuevas pistas para comprender cómo funciona el ADN, identificar mecanismos biológicos relacionados con distintas patologías y orientar futuras investigaciones. Google busca así que la inteligencia artificial contribuya a descifrar algunos de los procesos más complejos del cuerpo humano.

articles.title: Harari Warns Tech Leaders Against Pursuing AI Superintelligence - EE Times
articles.text:
BARCELONA, Spain — Addressing corporate technology executives at the Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo, historian and philosopher Yuval Noah Harari warned that the tech industry’s race to create artificial superintelligence is a historic market failure driven by ideological fantasy rather than economic rationality.
In an onstage conversation with John Thornhill, editor of The Financial Times, Harari argued that treating autonomous software as a mere tool fatally misjudges its nature.
Urging CIOs and policymakers to halt the pursuit of uncontrollable digital gods, he called for redirecting capital and research away from general superintelligence and toward narrow, verifiable systems that address tangible problems.
Emergence of the digital agents
When asked whether AI represents a rupture comparable to fire, the printing press, electricity, or computing, Harari pointed to agents: “AI is the first technology which is an agent,” he said. While the use of fire and nuclear power depends on human intent, artificial intelligence acts independently. “It’s your decision whether to use fire to cook your meal or to burn a forest. It’s not a fire’s decision. AI is different because it can make decisions on its own. It can invent new ideas on its own. It can invent the next technology on its own. The printing press could not invent the radio. AI can invent better AI.”
Viewing AI systems as tools is an error: “It’s better to think about them as animals, or creatures, or aliens to really understand. This is not something in our hands. This is something in our relationship with us,” Harari said. When Thornhill asked whether autonomous agents could remain subservient, he replied: “Not if they are far more intelligent than us.”
That dynamic exposes an unresolvable commercial fallacy. “The first question: Will it be far more intelligent than us? And the industry bets it will,” Harari said. “The second question is: Do you know how to keep far more intelligent entities under your control? And the answer is obviously no,” and added: “If you create gods with the assumption that they will be your slaves and you can use them to do what you want, you don’t understand what gods mean.”
Addressing researchers who view superintelligence as an evolutionary upgrade, Harari separated intelligence from consciousness: “There is zero love and zero beauty, also zero pain and zero sadness,” he said. “It’s a completely dark universe, and there is no value in that kind of civilization.”
AI is a bureaucratic native
Turning to societal consequences, Harari argued that AI targets civilization’s bureaucratic operating system: “Bureaucracy is the underappreciated hero of history,” he said, noting that institutions generate trust through language. Software has now entered that realm: “AIs are bureaucratic natives. For us, bureaucracy is alien, strange, or foreign because we are millions of years older than it. We were born in the forest, and bureaucracy came along late in human evolution,” he said. “AIs are bureaucratic natives. They’re all born in the office, not in the forest, and they’re poised to take over all the bureaucratic systems of the world, from finance to religion.”
Rather than an accident, Harari identified human displacement as the primary danger: “Everything goes right, and the AI simply creates a new world which is way beyond the human ability to understand. Humanity will face a situation of collective dementia. Once upon a time, you were the most intelligent, capable, powerful agent around, and you understood and controlled everything in your own life, and then things changed, and you’re left behind.”
Harari expressed disbelief that markets are bankrolling their own demise: “The market is supposed to be rational. Nobody can calculate what would be the return on investment on creating gods.” Pointing to Elon Musk’s prediction that money could vanish within a decade, and prospectuses admitting existential risk, Harari characterized the race as an ideological crusade rather than a rational business enterprise.
Dumb refrigerators and European sovereignty
Addressing immediate dilemmas facing corporate executives and citizens, Harari cautioned against fragile complexity: “Stupid refrigerators are much better than smart refrigerators,” he said, referring to recent hacks on supermarket fridges. “It’s like a chain with a hundred links. If just one link is not secure, everything crashes.”
When integrating software agents into operations, Harari advised executives to think sociologically: “We cannot think about them as tools. We need to think about them as agents, as entities. We are bringing new kinds of immigrants into our societies—not human immigrants, but digital immigrants. They are likely to have their own goals, their own way of doing things, increasingly their own tribes, their own networks of cooperation.”
For Europe, technological dependency represents a loss of sovereignty: “If you are a citizen of a country whose entire infrastructure, from hospitals and airports to the army, is based on AI technology that comes from across the ocean and that can be shut down at the press of a button, you are no longer sovereign,” Harari said.
He outlined three strategic paths: accept vassal status to the U.S. or China; build independent national systems costing over €500 billion (~$554 billion); or establish shared European infrastructure through deeper federalization.
He said that the third option would be the best, but he warned that “Option number one is the trajectory in which Europe is going at present. And if you look at the issues that dominate politics in countries such as Spain, Germany, and the U.K., it’s clear that this is at present the direction,” he said, arguing that, being more preoccupied with human migration, Europe is sleepwalking into vassalage by ignoring digital immigration.
Call for limited AI and human collaboration
In his final recommendations, Harari urged CIOs to reject general superintelligence and focus on bounded applications: “I’m not talking about stopping all research in AI. It’s just directing it in other directions,” he said. “First of all, invest far more in safety, and secondly, don’t race to superintelligence. Focus on creating limited intelligence and deploying it here and now for beneficial results, whether in healthcare, transport, or ecology.”
Harari highlighted a psychological paradox: Developers justify racing ahead because they distrust human rivals, yet trust alien software. “With humans, at least we have thousands of years of experience. We know they can manipulate and cheat, and lie, but we also have substantial experience in how to overcome this and create robust systems of cooperation,” Harari said. “AIs already know that they can cheat and manipulate and lie, and we have almost no experience with how to build large-scale, robust systems of cooperation.”
Because complex general systems cannot be evaluated in a laboratory before deployment, Harari concluded that deliberate restraint is humanity’s most urgent safeguard.
In conclusion, Harari reiterated the need to buy time to ensure technology serves human welfare. In navigating that future, Harari maintained that preserving human agency is not an abstract ideal, but the essential condition for survival.

articles.title: Clipto enables ChatGPT and Claude to search and analyze years of people's meetings and video calls - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Clipto enables ChatGPT and Claude to search and analyze years of people’s meetings and video calls
Artificial intelligence assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude have become essential tools for millions of workers worldwide, helping them compose emails in seconds, generate complex code and draft reports by looking at whatever data that person has access to.
But there’s one thing that’s missing from those chatbots’ knowledge. Ask them what was discussed in the previous week’s team meeting or on yesterday’s call with a client, and it will be stumped.
It’s this shortcoming that a startup called Clipto Inc. is trying to solve with the launch of a new AI chatbot memory platform called Clipto Studio, which enables AI assistants to listen in on calls, presentations and meetings and search through them or analyze them upon request.
Clipto argues that this is going to be an important capability as AI becomes more pervasive in daily work. Though AI chatbots can sift through email inboxes and corporate databases in seconds, that’s not where many companies’ most valuable knowledge is actually stored. Rather, Clipto says the most important business insights are trapped in raw video and audio files.
Most of the big decisions are made during Zoom calls, customer interviews and team meetings, but the details of those discussions are stored in heavy, unstructured data formats that are incredibly expensive for AI to process. But AI can potentially provide much more meaningful help to workers if it has a way to access this knowledge.
That’s where Clipto Studio comes in. It’s a native skill set that integrates directly with ChatGPT, Claude and other AI assistants using the Model Context Protocol, powered by proprietary models that run locally on user’s Mac and Windows computers.
The software works by pre-indexing speech, individual speaker’s voices, facial expressions and other on-screen visuals before transforming the raw footage into a structured and easily searchable dataset that’s optimized for AI chatbots. Then, when the user asks a question about one of their recent conversations, or even one from two years ago, it can quickly find the answers it needs by searching through the metadata of those recordings.
Clipto founder and Chief Executive Henry Kang said AI knows basically everything that has been posted online, but has barely scratched the surface of the terabytes of audio and video data that’s sitting in people’s hard drives.
“The next generation of AI will need to understand the conversations, experiences and knowledge that never makes it into a text-based document,” he said. “That’s the future we’re building, giving AI the memory it needs to move beyond answering questions from the internet and start getting real world done with what we ourselves have seen and heard.”
Clipto Studio can be thought of as a kind of instant-replay service. For instance, a management consultant could ask ChatGPT to pinpoint the exact time when a project’s scope changed by looking at more than six month’s worth of calls and meetings, and it will surface the exact moment when that occurred. Alternatively, a researcher might prompt Claude to identify the most common problems with a particular product or service by looking at thousands of customer calls, and pull out direct quotes that illustrate the depth of those issues.
There are other use cases too. For instance, users could ask Clipto Studio to look at dozens of hours of event presentations they’ve attended and create a highlight reel that surfaces the most interesting or relevant moments from them.
Clipto Studio’s official launch is a big moment for the startup, which recently signaled its ambitions with the hiring of former Google LLC research scientist Dr. Mei Han as its new chief scientist. Han, who holds a doctorate in robotics from Carnegie Mellon University, has been tasked with leading the development of Clipto’s lightweight multimodal AI architecture.
Han said she believes in Clipto’s mission because it’s trying to help AI perceive the world in the same way as humans do, by seeing and listening to what’s going on around them.
“The challenge isn’t just recognizing speech or identifying what’s on screen,” she said. “It’s connecting that information across thousands of recordings so AI can understand the context and use it. We’re building the technology to make video and audio as accessible and as useful to AI as text, opening up an entirely new generation of applications.”

articles.title: UCIe Consortium Advances from Chiplet Connectivity to System-Level Integration with UCIe 4.0 Specification
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
UCIe Consortium Advances from Chiplet Connectivity to System-Level Integration with UCIe 4.0 Specification
Today, the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) Consortium, the open standards group for interconnects between chiplets within a package, announced the release of the UCIe 4.0 Specification, taking the UCIe architecture beyond chiplet-level interface design to address key requirements for integrating multiple chiplets into a cohesive on-package system.
As chiplet architecture grows more sophisticated, connectivity is only part of the challenge. Systems incorporating compute, accelerator, memory and other chiplets must also address how those components are managed, secured and monitored while efficiently using power, die area and package resources. The UCIe 4.0 Specification addresses these broader system-level requirements with new capabilities spanning manageability and security, efficiency, memory connectivity and reliability."UCIe is evolving from defining how individual chiplets connect to addressing what is required for multiple chiplets to function together as a system," said Cheolmin Park, UCIe Consortium President and Samsung Corporate VP and Head of Package Marketing team at Samsung Electro-Mechanics. "With UCIe 4.0, we are extending the architecture with system-level manageability and security while continuing to improve memory connectivity, efficiency, and reliability. These capabilities provide a stronger foundation for building increasingly sophisticated heterogeneous systems around an open, interoperable chiplet ecosystem."
Standardizing Memory and Increasing System Efficiency
The specification introduces a standardized on-package memory link between SoCs and memory logic chiplets, providing a power- and cost-efficient approach to scaling memory bandwidth using existing memory technologies. By leveraging the existing UCIe PHY and Adapter ecosystem, the UCIe.mem protocol simplifies memory integration while achieving data efficiency as high as 93.75% and die-edge bandwidth density of approximately 2.5 TB/s/mm. This combination delivers high throughput and enables memory bandwidth to scale with evolving system and workload requirements.
The newly released specification also gives designers new ways to improve system efficiency, including an optional power-optimized profile that delivers up to 30-80% greater energy efficiency at 64 GT/s and an enhanced bump map for UCIe-S 48 GT/s and 64 GT/s that increases bandwidth density while reducing the shoreline needed for high-speed die-to-die connectivity. The enhanced bump map provides approximately 20% greater shoreline bandwidth density and 10% greater area bandwidth density, letting designers achieve higher bandwidth in a given footprint or free package resources for other system needs.
Together, these enhancements give system designers additional flexibility to optimize bandwidth, power, area and memory resources across the package rather than treating each chiplet interface in isolation.
Advancing System-Level Security and Manageability
The UCIe 4.0 Specification introduces Trusted Reporting of Chiplet State (TRoCs) to support trusted reporting of chiplet state, helping the system establish confidence in information from individual chiplets, verify that they are operating as expected, and protect against spoofed or manipulated state information.
UCIe 4.0 introduces two-way integrity-protected management channels to help protect communication between chiplets from unauthorized modification and verify the integrity of management information. Together with enhanced reset management, these capabilities provide a more robust foundation for securely managing individual chiplets as part of a larger system.
UCIe 4.0 also introduces manageability and security capabilities for environments where multiple chiplets, potentially from different vendors and serving different functions, operate together within the same package.
Extending System-Level Reliability for Automotive Applications
The UCIe 4.0 Specification expands system-level capabilities with features supporting the growing adoption of chiplet architectures in automotive applications.
New optional error notifications and link-health monitoring provide greater visibility into interconnect integrity and potential failures, enabling systems to detect and respond to link issues. Standardized link-health information can also be incorporated into broader automotive reliability and functional-safety requirements, helping system designers monitor the health of chiplet interconnects as part of the overall vehicle system.
UCIe 4.0 Specification Highlights:
- Standardized connectivity between SoCs and memory logic dies simplifies memory integration, achieving up to 93.75% data efficiency and approximately 2.5 TB/s/mm die-edge bandwidth density for power- and cost-efficient scaling of on-package memory bandwidth as system and workload needs evolve.
- Co-Optimized link profiles deliver up to 30-80% greater energy efficiency, while the enhanced UCIe-S bump map for 48 GT/s and 64 GT/s provides ~20% greater shoreline and ~10% greater area bandwidth density to enable higher bandwidth, a smaller footprint, or more package resources for other system needs.
- Enhanced security capabilities introduce Trusted Reporting of Chiplet State (TRoCs) for trusted chiplet state reporting and integrity-protected management channels to secure communications from unauthorized modification.
- System-level manageability delivers enhanced reset management and greater chiplet-state visibility for reliable operation across integrated systems.
- Optional error notifications and link-health monitors provide greater visibility into interconnect integrity and potential failures for automotive reliability and functional-safety mechanisms.
- Fully backward compatible with all previous UCIe specifications for seamless integration and adoption.
The UCIe 4.0 Specification is available to the public by request at www.uciexpress.org/specifications.

Motorola Edge 70 (512 GB) com 14 cristais Swarovski e tela POLED de 120 Hz volta a atingir o 2.º menor preço que já vimos, com desconto de 54% no Pix na Amazon
O Edge 70 Crystals By Swarovski de 512 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 2.789 no Pix na Amazon. A edição especial do celular da Motorola, com 14 cristais na traseira e tela POLED de 120 Hz, volta a atingir no Black November 2026 o 2.º menor preço visto pelo Achados, com desconto de 54% sobre o original de R$ 5.999.
Esta versão do Edge 70 tem como destaque 14 cristais Swarovski incrustados na traseira, que conferem um ar sofisticado ao celular. Ele conta com as certificações IP68/IP69 e militar MIL-STD-810H, que conferem proteção contra poeira intensa, mergulhos acidentais e altas temperaturas.
Todas as câmeras são de 50 MP: há uma wide com OIS e uma ultrawide com ângulo de 120º, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e uma frontal que tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K, com as traseiras suportando 60 fps.
Sua tela POLED de 6,7″ possui taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 4.500 nits, entregando imagens com cores realistas, alta fluidez e visibilidade garantida. O vidro Gorilla Glass 7i protege-a contra arranhões e quedas.
O kit interno do Edge 70, formado pelo chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 e 12 GB de RAM física, suporta apps em multitarefa e soluções do Moto AI. Os 512 GB de espaço interno dão e sobram para guardar vídeos e fotos.
Sua bateria de 4.800 mAh resiste a até 38 horas de uso, segundo a Motorola, enquanto o carregamento rápido de 68 W via USB-C permite receber uma carga para o dia inteiro em apenas 15 minutos.
O Motorola Edge 70 Crystals By Swarovski de 512 GB (apenas R$ 2.789 no Pix) será atualizado até o Android 20 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.
A Black November 2026 é a campanha do varejo realizada durante o mês da Black Friday, que ocorre dia 27 de novembro. Nesse período, a Amazon e outras lojas trazem cupons e descontos antecipados com condições especiais.
Acompanhe o Achados no Telegram ou WhatsApp e aproveite todas as promoções.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: « Un problème au niveau d'iOS » : Binance alerte sur une faille de l’iPhone qui menace tous les portefeuilles crypto
articles.text:
Binance tire la sonnette d’alarme. Dans un message publié sur X, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies indique que la faille de l’iPhone permet à des « applications malveillantes de lire les fichiers locaux d’autres applications, mettant en danger les phrases de récupération, les clés privées et les identifiants de connexion dans l’ensemble de l’écosystème ». D’après la plateforme, les mises à jour iOS 26.7.1, iOS 27.0.1 et iOS 27.2 sont concernées.
 A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.…
— Binance (@binance) November 10, 2026
Binance souligne que le problème ne vient pas de son application iOS. Yi He, cofondatrice de la plateforme crypto, met bien en avant qu’il « s’agit d’un problème au niveau d’iOS ». En clair, tous les portefeuilles crypto installés sur un iPhone vulnérable sont potentiellement concernés. Notez que la faille d’iOS n’a rien à voir avec le piratage de Binance, dont le butin est toujours en cours de blanchiment sur les blockchains.
Une faille qui fait tomber les cloisons de l’iPhone
Sur iPhone, chaque application fonctionne normalement dans un espace isolé du reste de l’OS, appelé le « bac à sable » (sandbox). Une application ne peut donc pas fouiller dans les fichiers d’une autre application, pour des raisons évidentes de sécurité. La faille worse_query permet justement de contourner cette protection. Découverte par deux chercheurs, @0xjohnny et @forcequitOS, la faille a fait l’objet d’une démonstration sur GitHub. Il est bien possible d’exploiter la faille pour s’emparer de données confidentielles, ou supprimer les informations d’une app.
Sur le papier, des pirates pourraient se servir de la vulnérabilité pour pénétrer dans le portefeuille crypto des détenteurs d’iPhone, en subtilisant la phrase de récupération dans une application. Pour arriver à ses fins, l’attaquant doit mettre au point une application iOS malveillante, programmée pour exploiter la défaillance.
« Un attaquant devrait toujours parvenir à installer un logiciel malveillant sur l’iPhone ciblé, par exemple en convainquant son propriétaire d’installer une application provenant d’une source non fiable », explique Bitdefender dans un rapport consacré à l’incident.
Le risque concerne donc surtout les utilisateurs qui installent des applications en dehors de l’App Store. Par ailleurs, la faille « n’expose pas automatiquement tous les portefeuilles crypto ». Le risque « dépend de la façon dont chaque application stocke et protège ses informations sensibles », nuance l’éditeur d’antivirus.
Pour Charles Guillemet, directeur technique de Ledger, ce type de faille « était autrefois très coûteux et réservé à des attaquants disposant de moyens importants ». Son coût tend désormais « vers zéro, et elles sont désormais exploitées à grande échelle », vraisemblablement à cause de l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle. « Ne stockez simplement rien de précieux sur votre mobile, surtout pas vos phrases de récupération crypto », recommande le responsable.
 Unfortunately this kind of vulnerability used to be very expensive and reserved to high potential attackers. Their cost is trending towards zero and are now exploitee at scale.
Simply don’t store any valuable in your mobile, especially not your crypto seeds…
— Charles Guillemet (@P3b7_) November 10, 2026
Une faille toujours béante
Il y a quelques jours, Apple a déployé iOS 27.2.1, une mise à jour truffée de correctifs. Neanmoins, Apple n’a pas corrigé la faille pointée du doigt par Binance. Ni iOS 27.2.1 ni la première bêta d’iOS 27.3 ne corrigent la faille. Bonne nouvelle, aucun vol de cryptomonnaies exploitant la vulnérabilité n’a été signalé pour le moment.
En attendant un correctif, Binance recommande de supprimer toutes les applications installées depuis des sources non officielles. Si vous soupçonnez une intrusion, transférez vos fonds vers un nouveau portefeuille, créé au besoin sur un appareil sain, puis déconnectez toutes vos sessions actives. Évitez aussi de conserver votre phrase de récupération dans une capture d’écran ou une note sur votre téléphone. C’est la meilleure façon de se faire dépouiller.

Source : Bitdefender

articles.title: Premios Xataka Verisure 2026: todavía puedes conseguir tus entradas (y te adelantamos una novedad)
articles.text:
Los Premios Xataka Verisure 2027 están a la vuelta de la esquina. En apenas unos días, el 17 de noviembre, descubriremos en una gala llena de sorpresas los mejores productos tecnológicos del año, desde el mejor coche eléctrico al mejor móvil fotográfico, pasando por el mejor router, el mejor smartwatch o la mejor freidora de aire.
Es un año de muchos cambios, como salta a la vista, y uno de ellos tiene que ver con los presentadores. El tándem Joaquín Reyes y Ángela Blanco ha conducido la gala durante los últimos años, así que es el momento de darles un más que merecido descanso. Así que sí, xatakeros, este año estrenamos nuevo dúo de presentadores: Ana Brito (@elshowdebriten), humorista, comunicadora y copresentadora del pódcasts Poco se habla!; y servidor, Jose García, Responsable de Productos en Xataka.
Protege tu hogar frente a robos y ocupaciones con las cerraduras inteligentes de Verisure, disponibles como parte del sistema de alarma Verisure. Al margen de permitir abrir la puerta usando las llaves o desde el móvil, alertan ante cualquier intento de manipulación y transmiten la información a la unidad central de la compañía para generar un salto de alarma. Descubre la solución que mejor se ajusta a las necesidades de tu vivienda o negocio.
Cómo seguir la gala de los Premios Xataka Verisure 2026 en directo
Como todos los años, la gala tendrá lugar en los Cines Capitol de Madrid y la entrada será totalmente gratuita. Si ya tienes la tuya, ¡te esperamos el martes por allí!, y si no la tienes, todavía quedan unas poquitas (muy poquitas), así que todavía puedes pedir la tuya en este enlace. Sobra decir que puedes venir con un acompañante, solo marca la casilla correspondiente en el formulario. En pocas palabras:
- Cuándo: 17 de noviembre a las 20:00
- Dónde: Cines Capitol (Madrid) y xataka.com
- Entradas: Pide la tuya en este formulario (gratis y por orden de inscripción)
Si no puedes acompañarnos en persona, no hay problema. La gala se podrá seguir en vivo y en directo en streaming a través de nuestro canal de Twitch. Además, antes de la gala habrá una pregala presentada por Ana Boria y Ángela Blanco que, como no podría ser de otra manera, estará llena de sorteos.
En lo que respecta a la gala, tendremos que esperar para descubrir los ganadores, pero sí os podemos dar un breve adelanto: Jimmy Wales, fundador de Wikipedia, estará en el teatro y tendremos oportunidad de charlar con él. Y cuando termine, tendremos una fiesta en La Cartuja (C/ de la Cruz 10). Para acceder, tendrás que enseñar la pulsera que te daremos en la gala.

articles.title: Google comprará datos de una aerolínea en liquidación para entrenar IA: así cuidará la privacidad de empleados y usuarios
articles.text:
Google pagará USD 10 millones por los archivos digitales de Spirit Airlines, la aerolínea de bajo costo que dejó de operar en mayo, para entrenar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial. Los sindicatos retiraron sus objeciones después de que el acuerdo se modificara para excluir información sensible de los empleados.
Spirit está en liquidación y vende sus activos para pagar a los acreedores. Google ganó en agosto de 2026 la subasta por los datos, según la agencia Reuters.
Según el resumen que hizo el medio especializado en viajes Skift del expediente de 157 páginas, el lote incluye unos 1.900 millones de correos internos de 91.000 cuentas, 664 millones de elementos de Microsoft Teams, 91 millones de archivos y cerca de 30 millones de líneas de código. Hay datos comerciales, como tarifas y paquetes de vacaciones.
El sindicato Asociación de Auxiliares de Vuelo (AFA-CWA), que agrupa a 55.000 afiliados, había objetado la venta desde su anuncio en agosto de 2026. Su argumento era que las garantías de Google protegían a los clientes, pero no a los trabajadores, cuyos correos y mensajes llegan hasta 1986.
Lo que quedó fuera de la venta
Con el nuevo texto, quedan excluidos los historiales médicos, los registros de pruebas de alcohol y drogas, los expedientes disciplinarios, los documentos de identidad y los datos de programas de seguridad. Skift añade la nómina, los datos biométricos y los reclamos sindicales a esa lista.
Una empresa independiente, Tonic AI, deberá borrar de los archivos todo lo que permita identificar a una persona. El sindicato afirmó que el procedimiento seguirá una norma internacional (ISO 27559) más exigente que la estadounidense que Spirit pensaba usar, y que un verificador independiente revisará el resultado.
Google tiene prohibido intentar reidentificar a las personas y debe procesar los datos en un entorno seguro. La compañía puede retirarse del trato si la limpieza reduce el volumen de información comprada en más de 8 por ciento, según Wired.
Google dijo en octubre que no buscaba comprar información personal: los datos se excluirían o los anonimizaría un tercero independiente antes de recibirlos. Esta vez no respondió de inmediato a las consultas de la prensa.
Un reclamo que juntó a pilotos, mecánicos y legisladores
A la objeción de AFA se sumaron en septiembre los sindicatos de pilotos, mecánicos y otros gremios aéreos. En octubre, unos 120 legisladores, con la senadora Elizabeth Warren y el representante Steven Horsford al frente, pidieron garantías antes de que se entregaran los datos.
Según el sindicato, el Código de Quiebras y las leyes federales y estatales no ofrecen hoy protecciones de privacidad para los trabajadores. “Sin nuestro sindicato, nadie habría hablado por los trabajadores en esta venta de saldo de su información privada”, afirmó Sara Nelson, presidenta internacional de AFA.
Nelson dijo a Wired que el gremio exigirá cláusulas de protección de datos en los contratos con otras aerolíneas y que ya empezó a reunirse con políticos estatales para escribir leyes. “Esto es un problema incluso en trabajos que parecen los más protegidos frente a la IA”, señaló.
Ari Ezra Waldman, profesor de derecho en la Universidad de California en Irvine, calificó el arreglo de “un resultado bastante bueno” para los empleados. Añadió que los sindicatos sabrán desde ahora que deben negociar la privacidad cuando se vendan datos de una empresa. Waldman planteó una alternativa más simple: prohibir del todo la venta de datos.
Spirit dijo en un comunicado que agradece la colaboración de Google, del defensor de la privacidad del consumidor y de los sindicatos. Ese defensor había recomendado en octubre aprobar la venta si se excluía la información personal de 97 millones de clientes, según Reuters.
El tribunal de quiebras fijó una audiencia sobre la venta para el 17 de noviembre. Reuters dijo que se espera que el juez apruebe el trato esa semana. Asimismo, la AFA tiene otras cinco presentaciones activas en el caso de quiebra de Spirit.

articles.title: ServiceNow launches AI-powered engine to accelerate migrations from CRM rivals - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
ServiceNow launches AI-powered engine to accelerate migrations from CRM rivals
ServiceNow Inc. is bidding to steal business from other customer relationship management vendors with an artificial intelligence-powered engine that it says can reduce enterprise CRM implementations from months to weeks.
The new Autonomous CRM Engine uses AI to analyze existing CRM environments, recommend business process improvements and automate deployment of redesigned workflows on ServiceNow’s platform.
The offering represents a competitive challenge to established CRM providers such as Salesforce Inc. and Microsoft Corp. by potentially lowering the switching costs that help vendors retain customers. The initial rollout targets only Salesforce installations, and others are planned.
The announcement comes amid growing concern about the costs and limitations of aging CRM systems. Gartner Inc. last year warned that legacy CRM platforms can create hidden maintenance expenses, integration dependencies and security risks that impede modernization. The researcher predicts that by 2028, most enterprises will identify outdated CRM systems as an obstacle to effectively using AI.
Gartner recommends that organizations evaluate technical debt, integration dependencies, data quality and the full cost of maintaining legacy CRM systems before deciding whether to modernize or replace them.
The discovery process is one of the most time-consuming aspects of CRM modernization, said Terence Chesire, group vice president of CRM and industry workflows at ServiceNow. Organizations typically must interview employees across departments and geographies to understand how sales and service processes operate.
“We’re able to collapse that into literally days where we show them how all their sales processes occur by product line,” he said.
Autonomous CRM Engine uses metadata application programming interfaces to examine business objects, configuration settings, custom scripts and workflows. It organizes that information into a graph database and applies AI to reconstruct how activities such as sales approvals, customer escalations and service requests actually function.
ServiceNow claims the analysis can expose discrepancies between documented procedures and everyday practices, including approval steps employees routinely bypass.
More than migration
Beyond transferring existing processes to a new platform, ServiceNow uses the discovery information to recommend redesigned workflows based on industry practices. Business leaders can examine proposed changes in a visual workspace and modify processes to accommodate unique business characteristics. Once approved, changes can be deployed directly into ServiceNow’s CRM environment.
Chesire acknowledged that automation doesn’t eliminate difficult organizational decisions or integration challenges. “The parts that potentially get extended are all those linkages to other systems because we always land inside a heterogeneous environment,” he said.
ServiceNow addresses those dependencies through its Workflow Data Fabric, which provides access to external information without the need to move or copy it. Its integration capabilities also extend to older applications through robotic process automation.
Gartner cautions that CRM modernization projects must account for hidden application dependencies, regulatory data-retention requirements and business processes that may rely on retired systems. It also recommends establishing clear data ownership and governance policies before making changes.
The research firm suggests measuring modernization success through operational improvements rather than retired applications. It suggests performance targets such as annual operating cost reductions of at least 20%, retention of 95% of historical data in searchable archives and a 35% reduction in duplicate or inconsistent records.
Customer results
Chesire acknowledged that ServiceNow hasn’t conducted comparative productivity studies against competing CRM platforms, although the company demonstrates its technology to prospects using their own business processes and data. The firm cited several customer examples to demonstrate the potential benefits of consolidating customer operations.
Germany soccer league Bundesliga-Gruppe GmbH consolidated fan services from seven digital channels onto ServiceNow in about a month and now resolves 89% of fan inquiries on first contact, according to ServiceNow. Bell Canada connected 26 applications and 8,800 data silos to one platform to support 12,000 field employees, while Everpure Inc. eliminated 13 legacy systems and now resolves 72% of customer issues before they’re reported.
Chesire said AI adoption is increasing pressure to modernize systems whose business logic is buried in custom code. ServiceNow plans to extend Autonomous CRM Engine’s capabilities to continuously monitor configurations and eventually improve CRM operations autonomously.
The engine is available now, with additional capabilities planned for 2027.
ServiceNow said its CRM and Industry Workflows business has surpassed $2 billion in annual contract value. Its CRM net new annual contract value tripled both sequentially and year-over-year in the third quarter.

articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone à 238,00 €
L'aspirateur balai Dyson V8 Cyclone passe sous les 250 € chez Amazon.
L'innovation peut-elle se nicher dans la réinterprétation ? Ce qui apparaît comme un sujet de bac de philo trouvera peut-être une réponse après notre test du Dyson V8 Cyclone, la vision 2025 d'un aspirateur-balai sorti en 2016.

Points forts
- Belles performances d'aspiration.
- Entretien facile.
- Relativement discret, aussi bien visuellement qu'acoustiquement.
Points faibles
- Autonomie trop faible à la puissance turbo.
- Extraction de la brosse pénible.
- Manque d'astuces pratiques (pas d'indicateur d'autonomie, de rampe de leds…).
Dans les grandes lignes, le Dyson V8 Cyclone reste le même que le V8 “normal”. Pour le meilleur et pour le pire, serait-on tenté d'ajouter. Certes, il existe quelques menues différences au niveau de la prise en main, une amélioration de la gestion du bruit, et on ne peut que féliciter Dyson d'avoir enfin pris le virage de la batterie amovible. On regrette d'autant plus que cet aspirateur-balai n'ait pas pris celui de l'indicateur d'autonomie précis, ou encore de la rampe de leds sur la tête d'aspiration. Ceci étant, malgré une durée de vie en mode turbo famélique, le V8 Cyclone est un modèle efficace et très simple à entretenir.

Les performances d'aspiration du Tineco Pure One Station 5 n'en pâtissent pas (et c'est sans doute le principal), mais il est difficile de faire face à la concurrence sans un afficheur d'autonomie restante — même basique — ou encore un indicateur de puissance utilisée. Mais c'est avant tout l'autonomie minuscule du Pure One Station qui le handicape. Car avec quelques minutes d'utilisation supplémentaires, il aurait pu devenir une véritable référence.

articles.title: Pré-Black Friday Amazon : le chargeur Anker Nano II 65 W retrouve son prix du Prime Day !
articles.text:
Le pré-Black Friday d’Amazon ramène sous les 20 € un accessoire que nous avons déjà relayé plusieurs fois cette année, et qui peut remplacer deux ou trois blocs dans un sac. L’Anker Nano II 65 W est à 19,99 € chez Amazon, le prix déjà vu aux Jours Flash Prime d’octobre, à condition de lui fournir vos propres câbles USB-C.
Avec ses deux ports USB-C et son port USB-A, l’Anker Nano II 65 W, aussi vendu sous le nom d’Anker 735, vise ceux qui transportent un ordinateur portable et un smartphone sans vouloir deux chargeurs. Sa technologie GaN II, de seconde génération, lui permet de délivrer jusqu’à 65 W dans un bloc compact aux broches repliables.
En ce moment, Amazon le propose à 19,99 € au lieu de 39,99 € de prix conseillé, dans le cadre de ses offres de pré-Black Friday. Ce n’est pas un record : nous l’avions relayé à 17,99 € lors du Prime Day de juin, avec un coupon, puis à 22 € fin août. L’offre du jour égale celle des Jours Flash Prime d’octobre.
Deux USB-C, un USB-A et jusqu’à 65 W dans un bloc de poche : l’Anker Nano II 65 W passe à 19,99 € chez Amazon, contre 39,99 € de prix conseillé.
Pourquoi choisir l’Anker Nano II 65 W ?
- Un ordinateur portable en charge : Utilisé seul, un port USB-C fournit jusqu’à 65 W, de quoi alimenter un MacBook Air ou un Dell XPS 13. Le chargeur d’origine de votre ultraportable peut rester à la maison.
- Trois appareils à la fois : Anker annonce 45 W et 20 W quand les deux USB-C servent ensemble, puis 40 W, 12 W et 12 W avec les trois ports occupés. Le port principal garde la priorité, le smartphone et les écouteurs se partagent le reste.
- La charge rapide des smartphones : Le chargeur gère le PPS de l’USB Power Delivery 3.0 et le Quick Charge de Qualcomm. Les Galaxy et Pixel récents en profitent, dans les limites détaillées plus bas.
Du sac de voyage au bureau, ce qu’il change au quotidien
Le déplacement est son terrain le plus évident. Un ultraportable USB-C, un smartphone et une tablette ou une console portable se partagent une seule prise murale, ce qui compte dans une chambre d’hôtel ou un train où les prises se font rares. Anker cite parmi les appareils compatibles l’iPhone, l’iPad, le MacBook, le Steam Deck, les Galaxy, les Pixel et le Dell XPS 13. Les broches repliables, elles, évitent d’abîmer le reste du sac.
Au bureau, il peut aussi remplacer la grappe de chargeurs qui encombre souvent la multiprise. Il s’adresse d’abord à ceux qui ont déjà basculé vers l’USB-C pour l’essentiel de leurs appareils. Il est en revanche moins pertinent pour un PC portable gaming ou une station de travail mobile, qui réclament plus de 65 W. Même réserve pour les Galaxy compatibles avec la charge à 45 W : ce chargeur les plafonne à 25 W.
Entre le petit bloc 30 W et le chargeur de 140 W
Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs chargeurs USB, le choix le plus compact reste l’Anker PowerPort III mini, limité à 30 W : de quoi recharger vite un smartphone, pas d’alimenter un ordinateur portable. Le Nano II 65 W joue dans une autre catégorie, celle du chargeur unique pour toute une sacoche. Pour un portable qui demande davantage, il faut viser un bloc plus puissant, comme les chargeurs GaN de 140 W qu’Anker propose aussi. Entre les deux, ce modèle couvre les besoins de la plupart des ultraportables et des smartphones.
✅ Les points forts
- Jusqu’à 65 W sur un seul port USB-C, assez pour un ultraportable
- Deux USB-C et un USB-A pour trois appareils à la fois
- Format compact grâce au GaN II, avec des broches repliables
- PPS et Quick Charge pour la charge rapide des smartphones
- 19,99 €, au niveau des Jours Flash Prime d’octobre
❌ Les limites
- Aucun câble fourni dans la boîte
- Puissance partagée : 40 W au mieux sur le port principal avec trois appareils
- Les Galaxy compatibles 45 W plafonnent à 25 W
- Une chauffe sensible à pleine puissance, selon des retours d’utilisateurs
Si votre sac compte un portable USB-C et un smartphone, l’Anker Nano II 65 W est affiché à 19,99 € sur Amazon pour le pré-Black Friday.
À 19,99 €, l’Anker Nano II 65 W reste une offre solide pour qui veut un seul chargeur capable d’alimenter un ultraportable et un smartphone. Le prix conseillé de 39,99 € gonfle toutefois la remise affichée : nous l’avons déjà vu à 22 € en août et à 17,99 € avec coupon au Prime Day. La vraie référence est donc le prix des Jours Flash Prime d’octobre, que cette offre égale.
Prévoyez un câble USB-C compatible 65 W si vous n’en avez pas, sans quoi votre portable ne profitera pas de toute la puissance. Les possesseurs d’un PC gaming ou d’un Galaxy compatible 45 W ont intérêt à regarder un modèle plus puissant. Pour les autres, il a de bonnes chances de devenir le seul chargeur du sac, celui qu’on emporte partout sans y penser.

articles.title: Corsair Launches HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL PSU with Transparent Panels and PinProtect+
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Corsair Launches HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL PSU with Transparent Panels and PinProtect+
Corsair is proud to launch the HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL, its first power supply with active 12V-2x6 per-pin overcurrent protection via PinProtect+. The power supply also simplifies builds by powering up to 24 iCUE LINK devices directly from the integrated iCUE LINK System Hub, and delivers stunning visuals with the transparent side panels, an RGB-lit fan, and custom-made Japanese capacitors.
The HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL began as a prototype shown at COMPUTEX 2025, and the positive response led Corsair to bring it to market. Built on the current HXi SHIFT platform, it is the first Corsair power supply with PinProtect+ per-pin overcurrent protection (OCP) for the native 12V-2x6 GPU connection. Cybenetics Platinum-rated efficiency, ATX 3.1 certification, PCIe 5.1 compliance, and comprehensive Corsair iCUE software control deliver the performance, protection, and flexibility that demanding PCs need.[Editor's Note: Catch the TechPowerUp Review]
The HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL features transparent polycarbonate windows on three sides, offering an unobstructed view of its internal components, such as the custom 105°C-rated capacitors. Designed to make the engineering within as impressive as your finished build, the see-through enclosure transforms the power supply into a centerpiece for showcase PCs. An integrated 140 mm Magnetic Dome bearing fan features customizable RGB lighting that enhances system aesthetics and provides visual feedback on the status of the native 12V-2x6 overcurrent protection when PinProtect+ activates, combining customizable illumination with useful system information.
PinProtect+ GPU Protection
PinProtect+ per-pin OCP monitors each of the six 12 V pins on the native 12V-2x6 GPU connection in real time, with per-pin current readings displayed in iCUE. If current on any pin exceeds the set threshold for longer than the delay, iCUE displays a warning and the fan's RGB lighting turns red. If abnormal current continues, PinProtect+ reduces power to the GPU, causing it to shut down to help reduce the risk of damage, and the fan ramps to full speed. The default delay accounts for brief power excursions, a spike that resolves in time is recorded in the event log and no action is taken.
As an upgraded version of PinProtect, which is built into the RM1200e, PinProtect+ is customizable in iCUE. Users can set the current threshold from 7 A - 10 A (9.5 A by default), choose a delay of 10 to 180 seconds, review the event log of overcurrent events and their pin readings, and check connection status from a PinProtect+ tile in the Cooling tab. After a restart from a shutdown, iCUE notifies users to check the included 12V-2x6 cable's dual-tone connectors if the gray tips are visible, indicating that the cable is not fully seated. This makes a loose connection easy to spot. Although not recommended, PinProtect+ can be switched off in iCUE.The integrated iCUE LINK System Hub simplifies system building by allowing compatible iCUE LINK devices to connect directly to the power supply, eliminating the need for a separate System Hub and its associated PCIe power cable. The integrated hub's dual-channel design supports up to 24 connected iCUE LINK devices with 12 devices per channel, giving PC builders ample options when it comes to intelligent system cooling. Compatible devices daisy-chain together and are automatically detected by Corsair iCUE software, letting you customize fan speeds and RGB lighting per device.
Side-mounted connections provide convenient access to Corsair Type-5 cables, and the fully modular design lets builders connect only the cables they need for simpler installation, cleaner routing, and a tidy interior. Premium individually sleeved cables with low-profile cable combs keep everything organized and professional looking, complementing the power supply's unique design. 
HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL delivers up to 91% overall efficiency, reducing heat generation for reliable, low-noise operation. It's ATX 3.1 certified and PCIe 5.1 compliant, supporting power excursions of up to twice its rated output to maintain stability during demanding workloads and GPU power spikes. 
The fan uses an optimized fan curve to deliver effective cooling while minimizing noise, and Zero RPM Mode automatically stops the fan at low to medium loads for silent operation, with the fan spinning only when additional cooling is needed. The 3D Y-pattern fan grille is designed to maximize airflow with minimal obstruction.
Robust custom 105°C-rated capacitors contribute to reliable power delivery and long-term durability, helping deliver stable voltage, reduced ripple, and steady power to all components of the PC build. With 1000 W of rated output, the HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL provides ample power for high-performance gaming systems and demanding components. 
Pricing and Availability
The Corsair HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL is now available from the Corsair worldwide network of authorized retailers and distributors and on the Corsair webstore. 
The Corsair HX1000i SHIFT CRYSTAL is backed by a 10-year warranty, alongside the Corsair worldwide customer service and technical support network.
MSRP: USD $339.99, GBP £249.99, EUR €289.90.
For more information, visit the product page.

Hopefully the per-pin overcurrent protection becomes standard on PSUs from here on out. Really can't afford to replace a GPU these days.

articles.title: Amazon highlights EGP 29 billion GDP contribution as it expands Egyptian operations
articles.text:
Amazon highlights EGP 29 billion GDP contribution as it expands Egyptian operations
- US e-commerce and technology company Amazon announced that its investments contributed more than EGP 29 billion to Egypt's GDP over the past decade, according to an economic impact assessment conducted by consultancy Keystone Strategy.
- The company said its investments supported more than 60,000 direct, indirect, induced and seasonal jobs across Egypt during the period, spanning logistics, technology, operations and professional services.
- According to Keystone Strategy, the estimated GDP contribution reflects Amazon's cumulative investments in infrastructure, technology, logistics and employee compensation. Amazon expanded its presence in Egypt following its acquisition of Souq.com in 2017 and the launch of Amazon.eg in 2021.
- The findings were announced at the Global Entrepreneurship Festival in Cairo. Amazon said it would continue investing in local infrastructure, technology and small businesses.
Press release:
Amazon today announced that its investments have contributed more than EGP 29 billion to Egypt’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) over the past decade and supported more than 60,000 direct, indirect, induced and seasonal jobs across the country. According to analysis by the economic consultancy Keystone Strategy, the GDP contribution reflects Amazon’s cumulative investment in infrastructure, technology, logistics and employee compensation. The findings were unveiled at the Global Entrepreneurship Festival, the largest entrepreneurship event in Africa, held in Cairo under the auspices of the Prime Minister of Egypt, H.E. Dr. Mostafa Madbouly.
“Amazon’s presence in Egypt reflects our long-term confidence in this country and its people. Over the past decade, we have invested consistently in infrastructure, in technology, in logistics and in the tens of thousands of Egyptian businesses that grow and create jobs through Amazon. We have done so through periods of economic uncertainty because we believe in what Egypt can achieve. The figures we are sharing today are not just a measure of our investment. They reflect the ambition of Egyptian entrepreneurs, the resilience of local businesses and the talent of a workforce that continues to deliver. We are proud of what we have built here, and we intend to keep building,” said Omar Elsahy, General Manager, Amazon Egypt.
A decade of investment: Building a lasting economic footprint in Egypt
Since acquiring Souq.com in 2017 and launching Amazon.eg in 2021, Amazon has steadily deepened its presence in Egypt. According to estimates by Keystone Strategy, Amazon’s cumulative investment over the past decade has contributed more than EGP 29 billion to Egypt’s GDP spanning infrastructure, technology, logistics, and employee compensation.
Amazon’s presence has built a foundation of economic activity that reaches well beyond the company’s own operations. Investment at this level, maintained year after year, including through currency volatility and wider regional uncertainty, supports local supply chains, stimulates demand and creates the conditions for growth and employment across sectors such as logistics, technology and professional services.
More than 60,000 jobs supported across Egypt
Amazon’s impact extends well beyond its direct workforce. The more than 60,000 jobs supported over the past decade span direct, indirect, induced and seasonal roles across sectors including logistics, operations, technology and professional services from the teams in Amazon's fulfillment and logistics operations and its regional customer service center, to the suppliers, delivery partners and service providers that its presence sustains.
Beyond Amazon’s own operations, thousands of small and medium-sized Egyptian businesses sell and grow through Amazon, creating their own jobs, hiring their own teams and building livelihoods in communities across the country. Today, tens of thousands of Egyptian selling partners reach customers nationwide and around the world, and the jobs and economic activity they generate are a critical part of Amazon’s wider impact on the Egyptian economy.
Expanding services, deepening local investment
The company has also continued to expand its services for customers, including Amazon Now, which delivers groceries, fresh produce sourced from local farmers and everyday household essentials within minutes through micro-fulfillment centers across the country. This sustained investment in infrastructure, technology and local businesses reinforces Amazon’s role as a long-term partner in Egypt’s growth and job-creation agenda.
What is next for Amazon in Egypt
Amazon remains committed to empowering entrepreneurs, supporting small and medium-sized businesses, and investing in the people, technology and infrastructure that help the Egyptian economy grow. As Egypt continues to prioritize private-sector investment, entrepreneurship and job creation, Amazon will keep building for the long term.

articles.title: Robotáxis e motoristas estarão no mesmo app de corridas, diz dona da 99 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Robotáxis e motoristas estarão no mesmo app de corridas, diz dona da 99
Tecnoblog conversou com o vice-presidente sênior da DiDi. Executivo vê os carros autônomos como uma forma de reforçar a oferta nos horários de pico.
A gigante chinesa de mobilidade DiDi quer que os robotáxis e os motoristas humanos atendam passageiros no mesmo app de corridas. O responsável pela operação internacional da companhia, que inclui o app 99 no Brasil, disse que os veículos sem motorista teriam um papel complementar. Stephen Zhu falou num “modelo híbrido” que uniria robôs e humanos. Ele recebeu veículos de imprensa estrangeiros, inclusive o Tecnoblog, na sede da empresa em Pequim.
Zhu vê espaço para os robotáxis ajudarem nos horários de maior movimento. De acordo com ele, uma frota de carros com motoristas, dimensionada para o horário de pico, pode ficar ociosa no meio do dia. Se for dimensionada para os horários mais tranquilos, pode faltar carro no pico. “Se você só tem veículos suficientes para os horários de menor demanda, nunca vai ter veículos suficientes para os horários de pico”, disse.
Para Zhu, colocar milhares de carros autônomos nas ruas também exige a resolução de problemas que vão além da direção. “E se o passageiro anterior deixou um hambúrguer no carro? E se derramou uma bebida no banco? Quem vai limpar esses veículos? Como vamos fazer a manutenção?”, perguntou. O executivo também questionou quem teria capital para comprar e manter uma frota desse porte.
Para levar o serviço a outros mercados, Zhu citou a necessidade de testes locais e de autorizações dos reguladores. O executivo não indicou onde começaria a operação comercial fora da China. “Mesmo se lançarmos a direção autônoma, vamos fazer isso de forma relativamente gradual”, afirmou. Em abril, a DiDi anunciou os Emirados Árabes Unidos como seu primeiro mercado internacional para a tecnologia, com testes e iniciativas-piloto previstos para 2026.
A DiDi desenvolve uma tecnologia própria de carro autônomo desde 2016. Segundo Zhu, a empresa começou a rodar em Pequim sem motorista de segurança a bordo em 2024. Numa das garagens do projeto, é possível perceber o quanto o carro evoluiu da primeira para a quarta geração. O modelo mais recente, chamado R2, foi desenvolvido em parceria com a GAC Aion, braço de veículos elétricos da também chinesa GAC, que está no Brasil.
Eu tive a oportunidade de participar de uma demonstração do serviço. O embarque é tranquilo, num carro bastante confortável. Chama a atenção o fato de que o volante fica protegido por um invólucro de plástico, de modo que ninguém consegue acessá-lo. Segundo a DiDi, o R2 usa 33 sensores para compreender o ambiente, incluindo câmeras e radares. Entre eles está o LiDAR, sensor que usa pulsos de laser para mapear o entorno em 3D.
A viagem durou cerca de 20 minutos. Nesse período, o carro repetiu o mesmo trajeto algumas vezes. As duas telas no interior do carro trazem a representação gráfica do que ele está enxergando, com os carros na frente, atrás e dos lados. O sistema também identifica bicicletas (muito populares em Pequim), cones e sinais de trânsito, entre outros elementos comuns da vida de um motorista.
No teste, o carro manteve um ritmo conservador — alguns diriam que monótono. Chegou a trafegar a 30 km/h numa via com limite de 70 km/h. Na demonstração, eu não tinha como escolher um modo de condução mais ousado, digamos assim, caso estivesse atrasado para um compromisso.
Desde agosto de 2026, já dá para solicitar o R2 pelo app da DiDi em áreas de teste de Pequim e Guangzhou. A Waymo, por sua vez, já transporta passageiros em áreas delimitadas de 15 mercados nos Estados Unidos. Eu mesmo já circulei pelas ruas de San Francisco, na Califórnia, em um dos carros da empresa, com muito conforto.
Thássius Veloso viajou para a China a convite da DiDi

articles.title: « La prochaine version du smartphone » : Sam Altman dévoile sa vision du téléphone à l'ère de l'IA
articles.text:
Le 31 octobre dernier, Sam Altman, PDG d’OpenAI, a rencontré une cinquantaine de dirigeants de Samsung en Corée du Sud. Si nous savions que cette rencontre était centrée sur l’avenir de l’intelligence artificielle et de son intégration dans les entreprises, peu d’informations nous sont parvenues, les échanges étant restés relativement confidentiels. Cependant, plusieurs médias sud-coréens ont aujourd’hui rapporté des échanges qui ont eu lieu durant cette rencontre initiée par Samsung. Sam Altman a notamment partagé sa vision de l’avenir du smartphone.
Sam Altman imagine un appareil qui remplacera nos smartphones
Lors de la rencontre entre Sam Altman et une cinquantaine de dirigeants de Samsung qui a eu lieu en Corée du Sud, une session de questions-réponses a également été organisée. L’un des dirigeants de Samsung lui a posé la question suivante : « Quel type d’appareil deviendra, selon vous, un compagnon doté d’intelligence artificielle ? ». Sam Altman lui a alors répondu que cet appareil « sera la prochaine version du smartphone ». Il n’est donc pas ici question de smartphones de nouvelle génération intégrant l’intelligence artificielle qui viendraient remplacer les smartphones tels que nous les connaissons (plein d’applications), mais d’« un appareil ».
Mais quel type d’appareil ? Sam Altman précise : « Je souhaite un appareil aussi discret que possible, où l’IA, et non des applications, accède et gère proactivement nos vies physiques et virtuelles. […] Les appareils de nouvelle génération collecteront des informations provenant du monde physique ». Autant dire qu’à l’heure actuelle, ce sont les lunettes connectées qui correspondent le mieux à cette description. Nous pourrions aussi imaginer un pendentif ou un petit appareil à clipser sur soi, mais il faut rappeler que le Humane AI Pin a été un fiasco, tandis que le Muse Charm, le pendentif IA de Meta, ne s’annonce pas vraiment comme une révolution.
Pour l’instant, les lunettes connectées et les smartphones intégrant pleinement l’IA, comme le NaviX Ultra et le Cyclon, correspondent le mieux à la vision de Sam Altman : celle d’un appareil portable et discret, qui ne nécessite pas d’application.
Sam Altman annonce vouloir collaborer avec Samsung
Toujours dans le cadre de sa rencontre avec Samsung, Sam Altman a expliqué vouloir travailler avec le groupe sud-coréen afin de concevoir un appareil commun, soit un appareil Samsung intégrant pleinement ChatGPT. À l’heure actuelle, nous ne savons pas de quel type d’appareil il pourrait s’agir.
Pour rappel, OpenAI travaille depuis maintenant plusieurs mois sur un smartphone intégrant pleinement ChatGPT, et donc sans application. De son côté, Samsung lancera à la mi-décembre ses premières lunettes connectées qui intègrent Gemini (Google). Pour l’instant, aucune collaboration annoncée donc, mais cela pourrait changer prochainement.

articles.title: El Black Friday de Sihoo deja la Doro C300 Pro V2 a precio mínimo histórico: una silla ergonómica perfecta para casa u oficina
articles.text:
El Black Friday es uno de los momentos más importantes del año para hacer compras en todo tipo de dispositivos, especialmente de tecnología. No obstante, hace tiempo que todo tipo de tiendas y marcas se unieron a esta fecha. Una de ellas ha sido Sihoo, una marca que destaca especialmente por sus sillas ergonómicas. De hecho, la marca ahora mismo tiene en promoción la Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2. En este momento, la marca tiene disponible la silla por 484,99 euros. Pero la mejor opción está disponible en su tienda oficial, donde podemos encontrarla por 419,99 euros. Además, si usamos el cupón "SihooXAK", se nos queda por 394,79 euros.
SIHOO Doro C300V2 Silla de Oficina Ergonómica, Silla de Escritorio de Malla con Reposabrazos 8D, Soporte Lumbar, Silla de Ordenador con Reposacabezas 3D, Inclinación para la Oficina en Casa
El mejor precio para una silla que cuida al máximo de tu postura
El PVP de esta silla es de 519,99 euros, por lo que estamos hablando de un descuento bastante importante. Especialmente si aprovechamos el cupón de descuento de su tienda oficial. Eso sí, debemos tener presente que no es una promoción sin fecha de caducidad. Tanto el cupón como el descuento estarán disponibles hasta el 30 de noviembre. Por tanto, una vez que acabe el "mes del Black Friday", perderemos la oportunidad de conseguirla a este precio.
La pregunta que puede que algunos os estéis haciendo es: ¿qué hace tan especial a esta silla? Pues lo primero por lo que destaca es por contar con cuatro zonas coordinadas que siempre estarán en contacto con nuestro cuerpo. Esto es posible gracias al sistema DynaCore, que permite adaptar la silla a diferentes partes de nuestro cuerpo (cabeza, espalda, lumbar y brazos) incluso si reclinamos su respaldo.
Otro aspecto que la hace destacar por encima de otras sillas ergonómicas es la forma de su respaldo. Este se adapta a la forma de nuestra espalda, ajustándose a ella para ofrecer la mejor postura posible. Al hacerlo de forma automática, esto permite que, si compartimos silla con otra persona en casa, no tengamos que estar configurándola individualmente cada vez que la usemos.
Esta silla también cuenta con un sistema de reposabrazos que la marca denomina "reposabrazos 8D". Esto está muy por encima de los clásicos reposabrazos que encontramos en las sillas gaming, que permiten configurar la altura, posición, ángulo o lateralidad. Este sistema permite adaptarse incluso a nuestra posición. Si estamos utilizando el móvil y nos reclinamos, los reposabrazos nos permiten tener apoyados tanto los codos como los antebrazos.
Su reposacabezas también es digno de mención, especialmente porque ofrece un tamaño considerable con un diseño flexible. Esto permite que, al igual que ocurre con su respaldo, sea fácil de ajustar y cómodo de usar. Hablando del respaldo, cabe mencionar que este se puede ajustar en profundidad, y que es capaz de reclinarse hasta los 135º. Además, la silla cuenta con certificación IGR, lo que garantiza que se trata de un producto con una gran ergonomía.
Finalmente, cabe destacar que estamos hablando de una silla que cuenta con un diseño de malla transpirable. Esto no solo mejorará nuestra experiencia al usarlo en verano, ya que permite evitar que se nos pegue a la piel. También será ideal para el invierno, pues no estará tan frío como la piel sintética de otras sillas. Además, no podemos olvidar que Sihoo ofrece 30 días de prueba gratis y tres años de garantía, por lo que, si no nos convence, tenemos tiempo de sobra para devolverla.
