articles.title: Jensen Huang was having a third affair, Reuters reports | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang was having a separate affair with an employee that has not been previously reported, Reuters reported on Thursday.
Huang stepped down as CEO and board member for the company earlier today, in the wake of news of extramarital affairs with accused spy Alice Huang and Nvidia VP of Health Care Kimberly Powell. CFO Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO, but no permanent successor has been named.
Reuters is withholding the name of the new employee linked to Huang, but says she is an employee of Nvidia.
Huang has been called before Congress to testify about the national security implications of his relationship with Alice Huang in the coming weeks — but it’s unclear how much more will be revealed before the hearings take place. Already, his abrupt fall from grace is expected to have significant repercussions for the industry at large.

articles.title: The Jensen Huang saga isn’t just a tech-world soap opera — it could change the entire future of AI
articles.text:
The Jensen Huang saga isn’t just a tech-world soap opera — it could change the entire future of AI
The wrong relationship at the wrong time
Update: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO at 9:00 AM ET. The company's CFO, Colette Kress, is the interim CEO.
The Jensen Huang scandal is one of the most remarkable tech stories in recent memory, and, in my view, it’s less about the now ex-Nvidia CEO’s alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy than the tsunami-grade ripple effects of one man’s questionable choices.
We do not know, nor do we have proof, that Jensen Huang's (whose departure was confirmed by Nvidia on Thursday morning) alleged relationship with Alice Huang resulted in any kind of quid pro quo, or in state or industry secrets being leaked or traded. Even so, Huang is surely smart enough to know the perception: the incredible irresponsibility of an extramarital affair, allegedly with a woman who, even if she isn’t a spy, is an influential businesswoman in China, the biggest economic and strategic rival to the United States.
Nvidia chips are, according to a 2025 report by IOT Analytics, in 92% of all Data Centers. Ironically, virtually every AI-generated meme currently doing the rounds featuring Jensen Huang and Alice Huang (they’re not related) — and there are hundreds of them — has probably been generated using Nvidia hardware.
Nvidia is a publicly traded company, and its fortunes impact global markets — and right now everyone is nervous. Jensen Huang’s actions are the latest PR disaster for an industry that’s already struggling with major trust issues. Many people already worry that AI is not being developed or employed in our best interests, and that the companies creating these foundational models are chasing money, rather than dreams of heroic medical breakthroughs, climate change solutions, and occasionally finding previously unseen Mayan ruins. (I think they may be doing all of the above, but that’s just me.)
I get it if you think that one person's infidelity can't possibly have any bearing on an entire tech industry. I disagree. Huang’s fortunes are inextricably tied to those of AI. There might not be an AI industry without Nvidia and Huang (again, see Nvidia's AI market share numbers above), and so you have to question what the future of the industry looks like without his specific vision for AI hardware over the next few years.
What's love got to do with it? Not much
This is about much more than the fact that Jensen Huang had an affair. It's about who he had the affair with, when it happened, what information might have been shared, and how, if any of this is true, Jensen Huang might have been used to steer US chip policy in relation to AI, and reshape the global AI race to favor or assist China. The fallout from all that boggles the mind — and it may reshape our AI future.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Let’s make one thing clear: this is not about Jensen Huang’s matters of the heart. He’s not the first powerful business figure to have an affair. But Alice Huang — if indeed the two were romantically involved — is not just anyone. She is described in numerous reports as a high-powered executive at Megaspeed, an apparent Nvidia cloud partner since 2023 that, up until a few years ago, was part of a Chinese gaming company known as 7Road International.
When Megaspeed was spun off as a separate company, Alice Huang became the de facto boss (she had majority shares), but NBC reports that her role with the company is less clear; as of May, she was reportedly still ‘the boss’ and running operations.
Right now, the FBI is trying to figure out if Alice Huang is a Chinese spy. Whether she is one may not matter. After all, it’s widely accepted that some Chinese companies are only nominally independent of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), which reserves the right to set aside a company’s privacy and ensure that its goals, strategies, and operations align with the CCP’s goals.
Jensen Huang and Alice Huang may have known each other for a decade, but if their deepening relationship aligned with recent events, it’s a bad look, whether or not Alice Huang is in fact a spy.
You see, Jensen Huang spent part of 2025 lobbying the White House and, specifically, President Donald Trump to relax his Chinese export rules so Nvidia could keep selling its chips to China. Those conversations happened while Jensen and Alice were, if not in a relationship, seemingly business partners (Megaspeed reportedly became an Nvidia cloud partner in 2023).
It stands to reason that Megaspeed and Alice Huang would want Nvidia to continue selling the chips Nvidia custom-designed for the region to China.
Jensen Huang succeeded, but in doing so, may have put the White House in a difficult position. After all, Jensen would have had a duty to disclose any partnership with Megaspeed, if only because the White House is well aware that Chinese companies are not independent of the Chinese government, which is that administration’s stated reason for banning so many Chinese tech products from coming into the US market.
Did he? Who knows? That's one of the questions the FBI and others will be looking to answer.
A long tech history
I often think back to my first meeting with Jensen Huang some 30 years ago, when he still went by Jen-Hsun Huang. Back then he was focused on — checks meeting notes — “a graphics chip that incorporated graphics acceleration, sound (can play two WAV files at once) and 3D acceleration.” It was a simpler time, and Huang was scrappily competing with companies like Matrox and ATI. He was a smart guy, although at the time he left no lasting impression on me.
I was impressed and maybe a bit confounded, though, when Jensen Huang started focusing on the AI capabilities of his chips more than a decade ago. Initially, a lot of the work was going into supporting autonomous vehicles. It was the discovery by others that Nvidia GPUs and their native math-iness could power model training and generative operations that transformed his business — and which may have also transformed Jensen Huang, who has now resigned from the company he helped found.
I don’t recall a leather jacket in 1996 (it was firmly in place by 2015), but Jensen’s signature style seemed to coincide with his transformation into a high-profile industry rock star. He still seemed humble, but by 2024, as the AI boom was starting to take off, his customers, and the industry, knew he was effectively the most important tech CEO in the world.
And with that came great responsibility. Like it or not, the AI industry was hugely reliant on him. But he shirked that responsibility, and made, it seems, some very messy choices that may have unforeseen ramifications for all of us.
Crossing a rubicon
Become a TechRadar Insider by simply clicking 'Join Now' at the top of this page. Have a question? Please email membership@techradar.com
Regardless of what the FBI discovers, expect a chilling effect on further sales of AI chips to China. Huang argued to the White House that Nvidia losing access to the Chinese market might help Chinese AI competitors and thereby hurt the US in the AI race. He might be right, but Jensen Huang’s say in the future of the AI industry may now be diminishing by the minute.
Jensen’s admission and how he handles the next few days, weeks, and months will influence the stock market, the AI industry, and how tech companies conduct business on the global stage, as well as whoever will succeed him as Nvidia's CEO (Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, has been named as an interim boss for now).
Nvidia’s role as the AI chip leader may remain undiminished, but only if it figures out its leadership picture. As it stands, the company cannot make AI chips fast enough. A stumble here will alter the course of foundation model development, future AI capabilities, and even robotics. It might also hinder the potential good work that all those AI CEOs keep promising. Another company could pick up the slack, but it won't happen quickly enough for most people's tastes.
Let’s face it, while nothing else seemed capable of slowing the inexorable march of AI, I think this scandal might do the trick — and what comes next could have implications far beyond the tech world.

A 38-year industry veteran and award-winning journalist, Lance has covered technology since PCs were the size of suitcases and “on line” meant “waiting.” He’s a former Lifewire Editor-in-Chief, Mashable Editor-in-Chief, and, before that, Editor in Chief of PCMag.com and Senior Vice President of Content for Ziff Davis, Inc. He also wrote a popular, weekly tech column for Medium called The Upgrade.
Lance Ulanoff makes frequent appearances on national, international, and local news programs including Live with Kelly and Mark, the Today Show, Good Morning America, CNBC, CNN, and the BBC.

articles.title: Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years at Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years at Nvidia
Nvidia has appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive officer. The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has stepped down as president, chief executive officer and board member with immediate effect, ending his 33-year tenure as the company’s chief executive, following a turbulent week.
Nvidia has appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive officer. The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.
Kress said, “Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”
Kress will retain the finance role while serving as interim CEO. She joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft.
The board appointed former Synopsys chief executive and executive chairman Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chair.
Jones said Kress understood the business and its customers. He added, “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”
On November 8, Huang apologised in a company-published message for being unfaithful to his wife and pledged to co-operate with an independent board inquiry into reports that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
Reports say Huang had another extramarital affair with a senior executive of Nvidia, in addition to the relationship with a Chinese national Alice Huang, who was allegedly recruited as an intelligence asset by the Chinese government.
On November 10, independent directors appointed former acting US attorney Joon H. Kim and law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the inquiry. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company information had been compromised.
Nvidia faces a fast-growing, increasingly competitive AI-chip market. Founded in 1993 as a graphics-chip maker, it later adapted GPUs for parallel computing through software such as CUDA.
In its latest reported quarter, ended on July 26, it recorded revenue of $96.2 billion, including $89 billion from data centres. Its next results are due on November 17.

articles.title: La batterie solaire murale Samduo Nex E6000 à 1 599 € pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Pour le Black Friday, la batterie solaire murale Samduo Nex E6000 passe à 1 599 € au lieu de 1 999 €, soit 400 € d’économie. Le compteur intelligent Samduo Smart Meter, d’une valeur de 129 €, est également offert avec chaque commande. On vous explique le pourquoi du comment de cette solution de stockage domestique qui mise autant sur sa compacité que sur sa simplicité d’installation.
Produire sa propre électricité grâce à des panneaux photovoltaïques, voilà une perspective qui séduit de plus en plus de particuliers. Pouvoir en profiter une fois le soleil couché, c’est encore mieux. C'est précisément la promesse de la Samduo Nex E6000, une batterie domestique de 6 kWh conçue pour stocker le surplus d’énergie solaire afin de le restituer lorsque le foyer en a besoin.
Mais plutôt que de s’imposer comme un équipement encombrant dans le garage ou le cellier, elle adopte un format mural particulièrement fin. Et à l’occasion du Black Friday, son tarif devient nettement plus intéressant.
Une batterie solaire de 6 kWh qui sait se faire discrète
C’est probablement le premier élément qui distingue la Samduo Nex E6000 : son format. Avec seulement 11,9 cm d’épaisseur, pour 84,25 cm de hauteur et 50 cm de largeur, cette batterie de 59 kg peut être fixée directement au mur grâce au kit de montage fourni. Un choix esthétique et pratique, qui permet de limiter l’encombrement au sol. Un vrai plus dans les espaces où chaque mètre carré compte. Elle a d'ailleurs reçu le Red Dot Design Award 2026, l'European Product Design Award 2026 et le German Design Award 2027.
Un autre détail appréciable au quotidien, c’est son fonctionnement, annoncé à moins de 25 dB, ce qui permet de l’installer sans transformer la pièce en local technique particulièrement bruyant.
Derrière cette silhouette relativement discrète, on retrouve une capacité de stockage de 6 kWh, extensible jusqu’à 90 kWh en associant plusieurs unités. De quoi envisager une installation évolutive à moyen ou long terme, en fonction des besoins énergétiques du foyer.
Une installation Plug & Play et un pilotage intelligent de l’énergie
La Nex E6000 entend également simplifier l’installation. Pas besoin de faire intervenir un électricien pour la raccorder : l’onduleur est directement intégré et la batterie se branche sur une prise secteur classique, en trois étapes, sans recâblage de l’installation électrique existante. Sa puissance bidirectionnelle atteint 2 600 W, avec une injection réseau certifiée de 800 W.
Concrètement, la batterie va se charger d’emmagasiner pendant la journée le surplus d’électricité produit par les panneaux solaires, pour le restituer en soirée, lorsque les besoins du foyer augmentent au même rythme que la production photovoltaïque diminue.
L’application Samduo prend ensuite le relais avec un plan de charge sur 24 heures, qui tient compte des habitudes de consommation et des tarifs de l’électricité. Que l’on dispose d’un contrat à prix fixe ou d’une offre à tarification dynamique, le système adapte son fonctionnement sans imposer de changer de fournisseur.
Le compteur intelligent (offert avec la batterie) joue ici un rôle important, puisqu’il mesure les flux d’électricité entrants et sortants du logement. Ces données permettent à la Nex E6000 d’affiner progressivement son pilotage et de mieux gérer l’autoconsommation. Les amateurs de domotique apprécieront également la compatibilité avec Home Assistant et Homey.
Une batterie pensée pour durer, avec une offre Black Friday à la clé
Côté fiabilité, Samduo mise sur des cellules LiFePO4, annoncées pour au moins 10 000 cycles de charge et de décharge. La batterie bénéficie d’une garantie de 10 ans et d'une certification IP65, pour une protection contre la poussière et les projections d’eau. Elle dispose également de deux prises de secours pour alimenter certains équipements en cas de coupure de courant.
Reste la question du prix. Pour le Black Friday, la Samduo Nex E6000 est proposée à 1 599 € au lieu de 1 999 €, soit 400 € de remise. Le compteur Samduo Smart Meter, habituellement vendu 129 €, est également offert pour l’occasion. L’offre est valable sur le site français de Samduo jusqu’au 30 novembre, sans cumul possible avec d’autres codes promotionnels.
Enfin, chaque commande donne également accès à un concours organisé le 21 décembre prochain, avec 12 iPhone à gagner (pour autant de gagnants) : 3 iPhone Duo 256 Go et 9 iPhone 18 Pro 256 Go. Attention, l’inscription n’est pas automatique, et il est impératif de s’inscrire avec son adresse e-mail et son numéro de commande.

articles.title: NVIDIA Co-Founder and CEO Jensen Huang Officially Resigns
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
NVIDIA Co-Founder and CEO Jensen Huang Officially Resigns
NVIDIA's co-founder, chief executive officer, and president has officially signed a letter of resignation, stepping down from the role he has held since 1993. Following a series of controversies, NVIDIA announced on Sunday that the company's board of directors is launching a full-scale independent investigation into recent reports of founder and CEO Jensen Huang having a relationship with a woman the U.S. intelligence community believes is an agent of the Chinese state. Another allegation has since emerged, claiming that Jensen had an inappropriate relationship with one of his direct reports. As a result, Jensen Huang has resigned from all his positions, including President, Chief Executive Officer, and member of the Board, effective immediately.
The company board has begun the search for a new CEO and, in the meantime, has named Colette Kress, currently serving as vice president and chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. According to the official statement, NVIDIA's board is looking for a permanent CEO and is open to considering both internal and external candidates for the position. Who exactly will take on the role is unknown, as the board must find a suitable successor. During the transition, CFO Colette Kress will continue to perform CEO duties and manage the company.Additionally, NVIDIA's board has appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chairman, bringing more changes to the executive structure. Jones brings more than three decades of experience as an entrepreneur, technology executive, and venture investor, having previously served as CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys. The company's earnings schedule remains unchanged, with third-quarter fiscal 2027 results due on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, followed by an earnings call at 2 p.m. PT. During the earnings call, we will likely gain more insights, as analysts are expected to follow up with extensive questioning.

articles.title: Cómo bloquear chats de WhatsApp y configurar otras cuatro funciones de privacidad paso a paso
articles.text:
WhatsApp permite bloquear cualquier chat, individual o de grupo, para que desaparezca de la lista principal y quede en una carpeta que solo se abre con la huella, datos biométricos o el código del teléfono. Así lo indica el Centro de ayuda oficial de la aplicación, que reúne además otras opciones de privacidad poco usadas.
El tema volvió a escena porque la plataforma de mensajería prueba un ajuste para decidir quién ve el número de teléfono de quienes tienen nombre de usuario, una función aún en desarrollo según WABetaInfo. Mientras llega, la aplicación ya ofrece herramientas disponibles hoy, que se activan en pocos pasos.
Cómo bloquear un chat y ocultarlo de la lista
En Android y iPhone, hay que deslizar el chat hacia la izquierda, o mantenerlo presionado, tocar “más opciones” y elegir “Bloquear chat”. En WhatsApp Web y Windows, se hace clic derecho sobre la conversación y se elige la misma opción. Para desbloquear, el camino es igual pero con “Desbloquear chat”.
Las otras personas del chat no reciben ningún aviso. Según la ayuda oficial, el chat bloqueado se cierra solo cuando el usuario bloquea el dispositivo, y las notificaciones no muestran el contenido ni el nombre del contacto: aparece “WhatsApp” o “WhatsApp: 1 mensaje nuevo”.
Si el usuario aún no creó un código secreto en su teléfono principal, la aplicación le pedirá crearlo antes de bloquear chats. Ese código es independiente de la clave del teléfono y permite esconder la carpeta de chats bloqueados: entonces solo aparece al escribir el código en el buscador.
Hay dos advertencias. Las llamadas de los contactos con chats bloqueados no se bloquean. Y quien olvide el código puede recuperar los chats ocultos con la opción de desbloquear y borrar, pero esa acción elimina los mensajes, fotos y videos de esos chats. Se pueden restaurar si hay una copia de seguridad anterior.
Otras funciones para ajustar en Privacidad
Los mensajes temporales se borran a las 24 horas, a los 7 días o a los 90 días. La duración solo afecta a los mensajes nuevos. Para aplicarla a todos los chats nuevos, se entra en Ajustes > Privacidad > Duración predeterminada de los mensajes. WhatsApp advierte que un mensaje reenviado a un chat sin esta función no desaparece, y que una copia de seguridad hecha antes puede conservarlo.
La foto de perfil, la última conexión, la información y las personas que pueden añadirte a grupos se controlan en Ajustes > Privacidad, con cuatro opciones: Todos, Mis contactos, Mis contactos excepto o Nadie. Por defecto, cualquier usuario ve la foto de perfil, las confirmaciones de lectura y cuándo estás en línea.
El bloqueo de la aplicación exige huella, rostro o contraseña, aunque se puede seguir respondiendo desde las notificaciones y atendiendo llamadas. Los mensajes de “ver una vez” desaparecen tras abrirse y no se guardan en la galería del destinatario, que tampoco puede hacer capturas de pantalla de ese contenido, según la ayuda.
Para estados, el usuario elige quién los ve: por defecto se comparten con todos los contactos, y la ayuda aclara que no se puede fijar la audiencia en “Todos”. Las personas mencionadas en un estado pueden volver a compartirlo con su propio público.
Una revisión guiada y los límites del número de teléfono
La “Revisión de privacidad” reúne los ajustes principales en un solo lugar. Se abre en Ajustes > Privacidad > Revisión de privacidad, y guía por cuatro secciones: quién puede contactarte, qué información personal se muestra, cuánta privacidad tienen los chats y qué protección extra tiene la cuenta, con verificación en dos pasos, llaves de acceso y correo de recuperación.
La ayuda también describe el “Chat restringido”, que puede activarse en chats individuales o de grupo y limita el uso de clientes no oficiales o agentes de IA. Su nombre anterior era “Privacidad avanzada del chat”.
Sobre el número de teléfono, la página de ayuda sobre privacidad indica que no hay manera de ocultarlo con los ajustes generales, y que tampoco se pueden esconder los números de los miembros de un grupo. La excepción son los nombres de usuario, que WhatsApp despliega de forma gradual. El ajuste con cuatro opciones que reportó WABetaInfo sigue en desarrollo y no tiene fecha de lanzamiento confirmada.

articles.title: ByteDance estaria trabalhando em IA rival do Muse • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ByteDance estaria trabalhando em IA rival do Muse
Agente pessoal pode chegar “nas próximas semanas” com proposta bastante semelhante à nova inteligência artificial da empresa estadunidense.
A empresa chinesa ByteDance, criadora do TikTok, estaria trabalhando no lançamento de um novo agente pessoal de IA nos moldes do Muse, da Meta. A ideia seria alcançar as principais companhias estadunidenses do setor em termos de tecnologia. A expectativa é pelo lançamento “nas próximas semanas”, mas ainda não há informações sobre seu funcionamento.
Em uma reunião fechada, o co-fundador da empresa, Zhang Yiming conversou com o time responsável sobre prioridades no desenvolvimento da nova inteligência artificial. Segundo ele, a dona do TikTok teria potencial de competir diretamente com nomes como Anthropic, OpenAI e a própria Meta por volta de 2029 ou 2030. As informações foram divulgadas pela Bloomberg.
A ideia da empresa seria bater de frente com os principais nomes do mercado nos próximos três anos, sobretudo as companhias estadunidenses. Ainda não há informações sobre a aplicação da IA em si. A expectativa é por um modelo bem parecido com o Muse, agente pessoal da Meta anunciado por Mark Zuckerberg no início de setembro.
Isso significa acesso a serviços de e-mail, agendas e até contas de bancos. Agentes como o Muse podem responder mensagens, fazer pedidos online, realizar transações, entre outras atividades automatizadas. Outro uso está relacionado a hardware como os Meta Glasses e até o “tamagochi” Charm. Ainda não está claro se a ideia da ByteDance também passa por oferecer os serviços em dispositivos.
Vale lembrar que o Muse está disponível apenas nos Estados Unidos e já apareceu envolvido em diferentes polêmicas. Nas primeiras semanas de funcionamento, a Meta contou com atendentes humanos terceirizados para realizar as tarefas de chamadas telefônicas, o que levou à suspensão dos testes da recurso.
Já em outubro, uma pesquisa da empresa de segurança Claroc identificou cerca de 7 mil conversas do agente expostas para qualquer um ler online. Segundo o site Engadget, a entrada da ByteDance no mercado de agentes pessoais de IA levantaria dúvidas relacionadas à privacidade.
O governo dos Estados Unidos, por exemplo, tem combatido a entrada de tecnologias chinesas no país para evitar o acesso a dados de cidadãos. As políticas vão desde a proibição de chips até o bloqueio de chamadas telefônicas a partir de telefonias chinesas.

articles.title: Merak Capital leads $1.3 million investment in Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios
articles.text:
Merak Capital leads $1.3 million investment in Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios
- Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios has raised $1.3 million in a funding round led by Merak Capital, a Riyadh-based investment firm. The round's stage and other participating investors were not disclosed.
- Founded in 2024 by Sari and Firas AlSaedi, Lambda Studios develops and publishes video games. The business originated as a project the founders started in Makkah nearly a decade before formally establishing the company.
- The studio initially developed games for Roblox, where it has reached millions of players, according to Merak Capital. It is now expanding to other gaming platforms, including Steam, to reach new audiences with its own intellectual property.
- The investment will support Lambda Studios' expansion beyond Roblox. It follows Merak Capital's $1 million investment in Floaty Studio in July 2026 and its participation in a $1.45 million round for Majestic Mind Games in August.
Press release:
Saudi gaming startup Lambda Studios has raised $1.3 million in a funding round led by Merak Capital, as it seeks to expand its game development and publishing operations beyond Roblox to additional platforms, including Steam.
Founded in 2024 by Sari and Firas AlSaedi, Lambda Studios began as a personal project nearly a decade ago in Makkah before evolving into a game development and publishing business.
The company initially focused on Roblox, where its games have attracted millions of players, according to Merak Capital. It is now looking to extend its reach to new platforms and audiences while retaining ownership of its intellectual property.
The new funding will support the studio's expansion across gaming platforms, including Steam, as it works to bring its games to a broader international audience.
Merak Capital said its investment was driven by Lambda Studios' ownership of its intellectual property and its approach to growth, which the firm believes will help the studio replicate its success across different gaming platforms.
The deal follows a series of investments by Merak Capital in Saudi gaming startups. In July 2026, the firm invested $1 million in Floaty Studio through its Merak Gaming Fund. It subsequently co-led a $1.45 million funding round in Majestic Mind Games alongside Impact46 in August.
The latest investment adds to Merak Capital's portfolio of Saudi gaming companies developing original intellectual property for international markets.

articles.title: Square takes Squaremates AI agent out of beta and opens up to sellers' own AI software - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Square takes Squaremates AI agent out of beta and opens up to sellers’ own AI software
Block Inc.-owned commerce platform Square today made its Squaremates artificial intelligence business agent generally available to sellers in the U.S., after the agent entered open beta in April under the name Managerbot.
For sellers who would rather stay in the AI software they already use, Square is also offering a new command-line tool and an updated Model Context Protocol server.
Running a business is “an endless string of judgment calls that are all on the owner,” said Willem Avé, global head of intelligence at Square. “We built Squaremates to help share that load,” he said.
Each seller’s agent now runs in its own secure workspace with access to cloud compute. Square said that gives it room for longer jobs. A seller could ask it to find customers who’ve lapsed over a given stretch of sales, for instance, and have it draft a discount to win them back.
A beta feature lets Squaremates build restocking orders directly on a supplier’s website, and the seller places them from there. Email access for its daily briefing is coming soon.
Fraser Thompson, who leads strategy and operations at Los Angeles-based Burgers Never Say Die LLC, put Squaremates to work on the restaurant’s house-made cheese sauce. “I dip my fries in it, I dunk my burger in it,” he said. “So I’m thinking, how are we not selling more of this stuff?”
Digging into attachment rates and customer segments showed that “our OGs, the regulars who’ve been with us since day one, love it.” The restaurant started promoting it on social media with what Thompson called “silly posts,” and he said that a few months later “we’d 12x’d our cheese sauce.”
“A lot of sellers already have an AI tool they like working in,” Avé said. The updated server, Square MCP, lets a third-party assistant answer questions about the business and make changes once the account is connected. Square CLI is aimed at sellers and developers who want to script or build on top of their accounts, and it gives their own tools and agents access to Square’s application programming interfaces.
Squaremates Apps are custom applications a seller writes with an AI coding tool and the CLI, which Square then hosts with a live connection to the seller’s business. Splitting cash tips by hours worked is one of the uses Square suggests.
Donnie McClanahan, who has four cafes around Knoxville, Tennessee, built a labor board app with the CLI and an AI coding agent. It pulls schedules and timecards from every location onto one screen. A lot of his mornings used to go to “playing catch-up just figuring out who’s where,” he said.
Sellers can try the tools at the Squaremates Tour, a run of in-person events Square kicked off recently. Apart from the features still in beta or coming soon, everything announced today is available to U.S. sellers at no additional cost. Squaremates itself is not yet available to sellers on Square’s Multi-Account Suite.

articles.title: Neutronenstern oder Schwarzes Loch? Dieses Objekt dürfte es eigentlich nicht geben
articles.text:
Wissenschaftler entdecken unsichtbares Objekt im Weltall, das es eigentlich nicht geben dürfte
Ein Team von Wissenschaftler:innen hat im Sternbild Fische ein Doppelsternsystem mit einem Roten Riesen als Hauptstern entdeckt. So weit, so unspektakulär. Schließlich sind etwa 50 bis 70 Prozent aller Sterne der Milchstraße Teil eines Doppel- oder Mehrfachsystems.
Klein, unsichtbar und ungewöhnlich massereich
Doch der Begleiter des Roten Riesen gibt den Forschenden Rätsel auf. Er ist sehr klein und außergewöhnlich massereich.
Das mysteriöse Objekt ist außerdem unsichtbar. Es lässt sich also nicht direkt optisch wahrnehmen, sondern nur durch die Auswirkungen seiner Schwerkraft auf die Umlaufbahn des Roten Riesen.
Ist das unsichtbare Objekt ein Neutronenstern?
Um welche Art von Himmelskörper handelt es sich bei dem seltsamen Begleiter? Die Autor:innen der Studie, die in der Zeitschrift Science Advances erschienen ist, tippten zunächst auf einen Neutronenstern.
Da Neutronensterne sehr klein sind, ist ihr Licht mit gängigen Instrumenten meist nicht messbar. Diese extrem dichten Objekte entstehen, wenn ein massiver Stern als Supernova explodiert.
Neutronensterne besitzen typischerweise eine Sonnenmasse von 1,4. Sie sind also 1,4 Mal so massereich wie unsere Sonne.
Zu schwer für einen Neutronenstern – zu leicht für Schwarzes Loch
Der mutmaßliche Neutronenstern im neuentdeckten Doppelsystem weist laut den Forschenden jedoch eine Sonnenmasse zwischen 1,8 und 2,8 auf. Die wahrscheinlichste Schätzung liegt bei 2,2 Sonnenmassen.
Für einen Neutronenstern ist das Objekt also zu massiv. Für ein Schwarzes Loch ist es aber wiederum nicht massereich genug. Dieser Typ entsteht, wenn noch massereichere Sterne als bei den Neutronensternen explodieren.
Leichte Schwarze Löcher sind mindestens drei Mal so massig wie unsere Sonne. Supermassive Schwarze Löcher können bis zu mehreren Milliarden Sonnenmassen entsprechen. Schwarze Löcher sind unsichtbar, da das Licht ihrer starken Anziehungskraft nicht entkommen kann.
Gigantischer Neutronenstern oder schwaches Schwarzes Loch?
„Damit befindet sich der unsichtbare Begleiter potenziell in der Masselücke zwischen Neutronensternen und Schwarzen Löchern“, heißt es in der Studie. Es handelt sich also entweder um einen besonders massiven Neutronenstern oder ein extrem massearmes Schwarzes Loch.
Am wahrscheinlichsten ist es laut der Studie, dass der mysteriöse Kompagnon ein supermassiver Neutronenstern ist. Diese Objekte sind ziemlich selten, da sie sich von ihrer Masse her an der Grenze bewegen, an der ein Stern normalerweise zu einem Schwarzen Loch kollabiert.
So könnte der supermassive Neutronenstern entstanden sein
Auf die Frage, wie dieser mutmaßliche supermassive Neutronenstern entstanden ist, haben die Forschenden noch keine Antwort. Supermassive Neutronensterne können in Doppelsystemen entstehen, wenn Neutronensterne Materie vom anderen Stern absorbieren.
Doch in diesem Fall liegen die Umlaufbahnen des Roten Riesen und seines Begleiters so weit auseinander, dass ein direkter Austausch von Materie unmöglich scheint.
Entdeckung stellt Stand der Forschung infrage
Stattdessen könnte das System ursprünglich aus drei Sternen bestanden haben. Aus zwei Neutronensternen oder einem Neutronen- und einem normalen Stern könnte sich ein einziges, supermassives Exemplar geformt haben.
Die Forschenden schließen auch nicht die Möglichkeit aus, dass supermassive Neutronensterne aus ganz normalen Supernovae entstehen können. Und unser bisheriges Wissen über extrem massive Himmelskörper noch große Lücken aufweist.

articles.title: Uber, DoorDash, and Airbnb say AI agents aren't taking off — reports reveal near-zero use as consumers reject bots
articles.text:
Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb say AI agents aren't taking off — as users rebel against being 'hyper-efficient at fun'
Sometimes, driving manually is just more fun
- Several firms say almost no one is using AI agents to access their services
- Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb all say the numbers are comically low
- Users have pushed back against AI agents and questioned their necessity
The whole point of using an AI agent, whether that’s Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots, is that it will save you time, change the way you work and perform the tedious drudgery that you’d rather not do. But several firms, including Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb, have admitted that almost no one is using AI agents to access their services, suggesting that the agentic revolution we were all promised might not be materializing — for now, at least.
The three firms said (via TechSpot) that AI agents had only been used to perform a small handful of transactions in recent weeks, compared to the millions carried out by real people. Uber, for example, had 320 million car rides booked by humans during the week of Halloween. The amount placed by AI agents? Just four, an almost comically low number.
DoorDash CEO Tony Xu shared a similar experience, saying that AI agents were responsible for several hundred orders on the platform. While the numbers aren’t as low as on Uber, TechSpot noted that DoorDash receives billions of orders every year.
And Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky argued that only a negligible portion of bookings on the app are made using AI agents. Chesky surmised that this might be because many people like to research trips themselves rather than hand everything over to an AI that can’t gauge the quality of a rental or the attractiveness of things to do nearby.
The AI agent backlash?
Part of the problem could be that AI agents are, in some cases, a solution in search of a problem. For instance, Uber’s chief financial officer Balaji Krishnamurthy stated that it takes people around 50 seconds to book a ride on the service, so it’s not exactly a longwinded process that AI agents can dramatically simplify.
There’s been something of a backlash on social media, too. On Reddit, one highly-upvoted comment noted that "thinking about what you feel like doing or eating is fun" and that few people are looking to become "hyper-efficient at having fun". An AI agent, they argued, sucks the joy out of life’s seemingly-mundane pursuits.
Another user put it this way: “So instead of opening the DoorDash app to order a pizza, I have to open my AI Agent and tell them I’m hungry and want to eat pizza and it has to be less than $30? Seems like more work to me to use [an] AI Agent.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Indeed, a recent report found that far from saving you time, AI tools are forcing many people to work an extra 90 minutes a day, while a separate study noted that workers are spending more time correcting AI content than doing actual work. Combined with the latest news from Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb, there's a growing sense that AI isn't always the time-saving solution it might appear on the surface.
Several companies and governments have already had enough of AI agents. The Wall Street Journal reports that United Airlines is banning AI bots from booking flights, while Alibaba has stopped its workers from using Claude Code and the Swedish government has blocked both Claude and ChatGPT over security concerns.
Perhaps one day AI agents will take off and everyone will be using them to streamline mundane tasks. But on the latest evidence, that day is a long way off — and there's a feeling that not every task is necessarily ripe for automation.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir : on sait enfin qui se cache derrière le mystérieux Magicien sombre
articles.text:
Les Anneaux de pouvoir : la saison 3 révèle enfin l'identité du Magicien sombre, et les fans peuvent se réjouir
La troisième saison des Anneaux de pouvoir vient enfin de dévoiler l'identité de l'enigmatique Magicien sombre, pour le plus grand plaisir des fans. Attention, spoilers droit devant.
Ça y est ! La saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir a enfin débuté sa diffusion sur la plateforme de streaming Prime Video, avec la sortie de ses quatre premiers épisodes.
Et au-delà de la belle qualité de cette saison, celle-ci apporte enfin quelques lumières sur l'univers de Tolkien, éclairant notamment le mystère autour du mage de Rhûn... Attention, la suite de ce papier contient des spoilers sur Les Anneaux de pouvoir.
Qui est Pallando, l'un des Mages Bleus ?
C'est l'une des grandes révélations de cette saison 3 : on connaît enfin l'identité de l'étrange Magicien sombre régnant sur la région Rhûn, apparu dans la saison 2 et incarné par l'acteur Ciarán Hinds.
Celui-ci est n'est autre que Pallando, l'un des cinq Istari, ces magiciens envoyés par les Valar (les dieux de l'univers de Tolkien) pour sauver la Terre du Milieu. Si les spectateurs connaissent bien Gandalf, Saroumane et même Radagast (apparu dans la trilogie Le Hobbit), les deux derniers étaient jusqu'à présent restés très énigmatiques.
Les Mages Bleus Alatar et Pallando ne sont en effet cités qu'indirectement dans les livres Le Seigneur des Anneaux, et Tolkien ne les a jamais développé plus que cela. Il s'est contenté de préciser "qu'ils sont partis en émissaires dans des régions éloignées vers l'Est et le Sud", des zones de la Terre du Milieu peu explorées par l'auteur.
Dans l'épisode 3 de la saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir, les spectateurs apprennent donc qu'Allatar et Pallando ont bien été envoyés pour protéger les terres de l'Est. Mais avide de pouvoir, Pallando a trahi et assassiné Allatar, provoquant la dévastation de Rhûn.
Ainsi, tout un pan de l'univers de Tolkien s'ouvre en grand, et ce qui était jusqu'à présent dans l'esprit et les fantasmes des adeptes de Tolkien se voit offrir une représentation, une réalité un peu plus concrète avec laquelle jouer et imaginer. Avec la mise en lumière de ce personnage méconnu, c'est tout un champ des possibles qui apparaît en Terre du Milieu, et c'est forcément réjouissant pour les fans.
Maintenant qu'Alatar et Pallandao ont eu le droit à leur naissance officielle à l'image, tout semble possible au niveau de l'œuvre de Tolkien et qui sait, cela permettra peut-être de voir demain des personnages issus des Enfants de Húrin, de Beren et Lúthien ou La Chute de Gondolin, soit des romans moins célèbres de l'auteur britannique.
Dans ce même épisode, le Feu Secret - pouvoir de création d'Eru Ilúvatar, être suprême de l'univers de Tolkien - donne pour mission à Gandalf de faire revenir son confrère Istar dans le droit chemin, afin de contrer l'ascension de Sauron.
Pour rappel, cette troisième saison des Anneaux de pouvoir se déroule cinq ans après les événements de la deuxième, alors que la guerre entre les Elfes et Sauron bat son plein. Le Seigneur des Ténèbres cherche à forger l'Anneau Unique, l'arme qui lui donnera l'avantage décisif pour remporter la guerre, asservir tous les peuples à sa volonté — et régner enfin sur la Terre du Milieu tout entière.
Pour l'heure, Rhûn est une région alliée du Mordor et il reste à voir si le magicien parviendra à inverser la tendance afin de donner plus de chances à l'alliance des Elfes et des Hommes à l'Ouest. Une tâche qui s'annonce particulièrement ardue, et que va tenter d'accomplir le magicien dans la suite de cette saison 3, voire même dans une potentielle saison 4.
Les quatres premiers épisodes de cette troisième saison sont visibles depuis le 11 novembre sur Prime Video. Les épisodes 5 et 6 sortent le mercredi 18 novembre, puis les ultimes épisodes 7 et 8 seront eux disponibles à partir du 25 novembre.

articles.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
Generative AI spend is hard to attribute. Before an organization expands AI access, CFOs and CTOs usually want three answers: what do we spend per person or per team, can we cap it, and how much work does it take to get there.
In our previous post, Tokenomics at Scale: How Jamf Built Real-Time Spend Enforcement for Amazon Bedrock, we explained a custom enforcement loop built on AWS IAM Identity Center, Amazon Athena over Amazon Bedrock model invocation logs, and AWS Lambda. This approach gives near-real-time control, but it requires code you then own and operate.
This post shows how to get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code to write for the common case. The approach relies on three things: IAM principal attribution, which Amazon Bedrock records automatically; AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) 2.0 or AWS Cost Explorer for reporting; and AWS Budgets with budget actions for enforcement. By the end, you will have per-identity cost reporting and an automatic guardrail that restricts Amazon Bedrock access when a threshold is crossed.
Solution overview
The solution has three parts: attribute, report, and enforce.
Attribute. Amazon Bedrock captures the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) principal identity, the IAM user or role, for every inference request. This happens automatically, with no change to your Amazon Bedrock model inference calls. If several people share one role, you add per-user detail with session tags passed at role assumption time. If each person or application has its own role, principal tags on the role are enough.
Report. Activate those tags as cost allocation tags, then read the data either in Cost Explorer for a console-only view, or in a CUR 2.0 data export for detailed line-item analysis and SQL queries.
Enforce. Create an AWS Budget scoped to Amazon Bedrock and filtered to one identity or tag value, then attach a budget action that applies a Deny IAM policy when the threshold is crossed.
The following sections show each part in more detail, alongside the implementation steps.
Prerequisites
To deploy this solution, you need:
- An AWS account with Amazon Bedrock model access enabled.
- Permissions to tag IAM principal, activate cost allocation tags, create data exports, and create budgets and budget actions.
- Amazon Bedrock accessed through IAM roles or IAM users.
- AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) configured with appropriate credentials.
- A CUR 2.0 data export and an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket to receive it. (optional, for detailed line-item analysis).
- Amazon Athena. (optional, for querying the export).
AWS Billing Console access is managed separately from most IAM permissions. Confirm you have it before starting.
Walkthrough
Before configuring anything, check what you already have. Amazon Bedrock records caller identity for every inference request automatically. Open Cost Explorer, filter Service to Amazon Bedrock, and group by the available identity or tag dimension. For accounts where each application or person already uses a distinct IAM role, this may be all the visibility you need.
To configure additional visibility:
- Step 1 gives you identity-level visibility.
- Steps 2 through 4 add tag dimensions and detailed reporting.
- Step 5 adds enforcement.
Step 1: Decide how identity maps to your users
How you tag depends on how your IAM principals are organized.
One role per person or per application. Attach principal tags directly to each IAM role or user. These are static and apply to every request from that principal. Use the IAM console, or the AWS CLI:
A shared role used by several people, or a gateway. Principal tags cannot distinguish users on a shared role, because every session carries the same tags. Use session tags instead, passed when the role is assumed. Session tags are dynamic and can vary per session. If a session tag and a principal tag share a key, the session tag wins for that session.
The role’s trust policy must allow sts:TagSession. Session tags can be passed three ways:
- sts:AssumeRole with --tags, for a gateway assuming a role per user or tenant.
- AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, with tags in the https://aws.amazon.com/tags claim of the OpenID Connect (OIDC) ID token (this is a claim name, not a URL you browse to).
- AssumeRoleWithSAML, by mapping PrincipalTag:* attributes in the identity provider’s Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) assertion.
If your organization already captures a claim like saml:sub for other purposes, that alone does not make it available here. Your identity provider must separately map that attribute to a PrincipalTag:* SAML attribute statement, and the role’s trust policy must allow sts:TagSession, before it flows through as a session tag. The two integrations draw from the same SAML assertion but are configured independently. Common tag keys are user, team, Department, CostCenter, and Environment. You can apply up to 50 principal or session tags per IAM user or role.
Step 2: Activate cost allocation tags
Tags do not appear in billing data until you activate them.
- Open the AWS Billing and Cost Management Console.
- Choose Cost allocation tags.
- Filter by type IAM principal.
- Select your tag keys and choose Activate.
In an AWS Organization, activate IAM principal cost allocation tags in the management account (payer). Member accounts cannot activate them independently.
Two things to expect:
- A tag key only appears in this list after the principal has made at least one Amazon Bedrock call, so make a test call first if the list looks empty.
- It might take up to 24 hours for a newly applied tag key to appear for activation, then up to another 24 hours after you activate it before it begins populating billing data.
Activation does not apply retroactively by default, so activate tags before you need the data.
Step 3: Create a CUR 2.0 data export that includes caller identity
Skip this step if Cost Explorer is enough for your reporting.
- In the Billing and Cost Management console, choose Data Exports.
- Choose Create and create a CUR 2.0 (Standard) export.
- Under Additional export content, select Include caller identity (IAM principal) allocation data.
- Under Time granularity, select Hourly.
- Under Report data integration, select Amazon Athena. This sets the file format to Parquet and, importantly, delivers a setup script to your S3 bucket alongside the export data.
- Choose the destination Amazon S3 bucket.
- Run the delivered setup script (or the Glue crawler/DDL it defines) once. This is what actually creates the Glue Data Catalog table you’ll query in Step 4. The preceding console flow does not create it for you automatically.
If you already have a CUR 2.0 export created before enabling identity attribution, it will not include identity data retroactively. Create a new export with the caller identity option selected. In the export, principal and session tags appear as columns prefixed iamPrincipal/, and resource tags as resourceTags/. For example, a tag key team appears as iamPrincipal/team. AWS publishes a ready-made query set for this exact pattern in aws-samples/sample-cur-iam-principal-bedrock-tracking.
Step 4: Read the data
The following diagram compares the two ways to read the data: a console-only path through Cost Explorer, and a SQL path over the CUR 2.0 export with Amazon Athena.
Console path, no custom code. Cost Explorer, filtered to Amazon Bedrock and grouped by your tag key, gives per-team or per-user spend as a chart and table. This covers most recurring reporting needs and requires no query authoring.
SQL path, low code. Point Amazon Athena at the CUR 2.0 export to group spend by iamPrincipal/team and usage type:
Things to note:
- Service code: Amazon Bedrock spend can be recorded under more than one product_servicecode value, for example, AmazonBedrock and AmazonBedrockService.
- Table name: The table name (cur2_view) is whatever the setup script from Step 3 named it when it created the Glue table. Check the script or your Glue catalog if it differs. Column names match the CUR 2.0 Parquet schema regardless of table name.
- Billing-period column. Confirm how your export exposes the period. Some exports use billing_period (YYYY-MM). Others partition on a start-date or year/month column.
Two notes worth carrying into any query you write.
- Count all token types: Amazon Bedrock bills four token types, each at a different rate: input, output, cache read, and cache write. Each is a separate line item with its own usage type and unit price, so summing only input and output undercounts. The gap is largest for workloads that use prompt caching heavily. Refer to the AWS document Understanding Amazon Bedrock pricing in CUR for the latest information.
- Match the rate to the line item, not the model: Amazon Bedrock pricing in CUR is determined by three things: the token type, the service tier, and whether the request was routed through cross-Region inference. In-Region and cross-Region requests are priced differently, and service tier is reflected in the usage type as well. The usage type carries a suffix indicating cross-Region routing and service tier, so if your workloads mix these, match the rate to each line item rather than applying one rate per model. Refer to the CUR usage type examples for examples.
Step 5: Add enforcement with AWS Budgets and budget actions
AWS Budgets performs the attach, so there is no custom code for this workflow. Budget actions attach to a specific IAM user, group, or role. This isolates one person’s access only if that person already has their own role. If your Amazon Bedrock traffic runs through a role that many people share, a Deny action attached to that role blocks everyone on it, not only the person who crossed the threshold. The following diagram explains the enforcement workflow.
AWS Budgets can run an action when a threshold is crossed. Available actions include applying a custom IAM policy, applying a service control policy (SCP), and targeting Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) or Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) instances. For this use case, the IAM policy action is the relevant one.
First, create the Deny policy the action will attach. This example denies the higher-cost models while leaving a lower-cost model available, so the user can keep working:
Replace [HIGHER-COST-MODEL-ID] with the model ID you want to deny in your environment.
Then set up permissions and the budget itself.
There are two distinct roles here, and the AWS managed policy only covers one of them:
Your own user or role (the one configuring the budget) needs the AWS managed policy AWSBudgetsActionsWithAWSResourceControlAccess. It grants budgets permissions plus the conditioned iam:PassRole needed to hand your budget action role to AWS Budgets.
The IAM role AWS Budgets assumes to perform the action is not covered by a single named managed policy for this use case. Create it with a trust policy that allows the principal budgets.amazonaws.com to assume it (scoped with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions), and a permissions policy granting iam:AttachRolePolicy and iam:DetachRolePolicy (and organizations:AttachPolicy and organizations:DetachPolicy if you are also using SCPs). Refer to Setting up a role for AWS Budgets to run budget actions for the grantable permissions.
- Create the budget action role described earlier.
- Create a cost budget scoped to Amazon Bedrock, filtered to the identity or tag value you want to cap.
- In Configure alerts, add an alert threshold. Choose Actual for realized spend or Forecasted to act before the spend lands.
- Under Attach actions, choose Add Action, select the budget actions role, and choose the IAM policy action. Select the Deny policy and the IAM user, group, or role to attach it to.
- For automatic enforcement, choose Yes to run the action automatically. Choose No to require a human to approve each action from the Alert details page.
- Configure at least one notification so the affected user is told why access changed.
You can attach multiple actions to a single threshold, and multiple thresholds to one budget. That is how you build tiers: for example, deny the premium model at 80 percent and the mid-tier model at 100 percent, while never denying the low-cost model.
Only the management account can apply SCPs, and from the management account you can apply an SCP to another account.
Considerations
AWS Budgets is not near-real-time: Budget data refreshes up to three times a day, so spend can overshoot a threshold before the action runs.
Cost allocation tags are not retroactive: Expect up to 24 hours for a newly applied tag key to appear, then up to another 24 hours after you activate it before it begins populating billing data.
CUR does not contain per-request line items: Both classic CUR and CUR 2.0 aggregate Amazon Bedrock cost by usage type, operation, and pricing/resource attributes over an hour or a day.
IAM principal fields require CUR 2.0: The legacy CUR format does not include them. Per-token cost breakdowns are available in both formats.
Session tags are bound at AssumeRole time, not per request. Their values are constant for every call made with that session’s credentials, and they surface only as aggregated billing data. Session tags are not written to model invocation logs. Logs capture the caller’s identity.arn. To distinguish users on a shared session at the request level, use a per-user RoleSessionName, or set the user in request metadata on each call.
Budget actions attach to IAM users, groups, and roles. If your users are federated and have no standing IAM identity, the action needs a role to target. This is why the pattern works best when each person or application has its own role. If your users share a role or are federated without their own role, see our previous post for a per-user enforcement approach.
A shared gateway role collapses attribution by default. With a large language model (LLM) gateway, the identity captured is the gateway’s execution role.
New models need attention. Usage types are model-specific. When you enable a new model, confirm it appears in your queries and budget filters as expected rather than assuming it is covered.
Decision framework
| Requirement | Recommended path | 
| Quick reporting | Cost Explorer grouped by identity | 
| Per-team reporting | Cost Explorer with activated tags (Steps 1, 2, and 4) | 
| Detailed line-item analysis | CUR 2.0 export (Steps 1 through 4) | 
| Enforcement | AWS Budgets with budget actions (Steps 1 and 5) | 
Cleanup
To avoid ongoing charges, delete all the resources you created.
Conclusion
In this post, you learned how to get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code to write for the common case. As generative AI adoption scales, the organizations that win will be the ones that can answer the tokenomics question with confidence: what do we spend per person or per team, can we cap it, and how much work does it take to get there.
Now, it’s your turn to start exploring. We are here to help, and if you need further assistance, reach out to AWS Support and your AWS account team.

articles.title: Google's latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”
While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.
The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at its default high thinking level.
In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.
In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.
Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.
The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.
Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.
The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.
On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out.
In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform.
Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.

articles.title: Lunettes connectées Apple : un fournisseur chinois nous met sur la piste de plusieurs projets
articles.text:
Les rumeurs se font de plus en plus nombreuses autour des lunettes connectées d’Apple. Sans écran et voulant concurrencer les Ray-Ban Meta, elles arriveraient fin 2027. Désormais, ce sont des indices plus tangibles qui apparaissent : cette fois-ci, c’est un rapport financier d’un fournisseur d’Apple en Chine.
Ce fournisseur d’Apple a son carnet de commandes rempli
L’histoire nous vient du média chinois iFeng : l’entreprise TCB Devices, a indiqué dans son rapport financier du troisième trimestre 2026 participer aux projets d’« IA Glasses » et de « nouveaux écouteurs intelligents ». Son carnet de commandes est donc bien rempli, notamment pour l’année 2027 : ces deux projets devraient constituer une grande partie de son chiffre d’affaires. Et c’est là que tout se resserre : et si Apple était derrière ces grosses commandes ? L’industrialisation de lunettes connectées est en développement chez TCB Devices : cette collaboration porte sur de la soudure de précision et de l’inspection par vision machine.
Second produit évoqué, des AirPods dotés de caméras, qui pourraient eux aussi être lancés fin 2027. Les rumeurs à propos de ce produit vont déjà bon train : ces écouteurs auraient des capteurs photo basse résolution dans les tiges qui permettraient d’utiliser Siri avec Apple Intelligence. D’ailleurs, des informations sur ce produit auraient été repérées dans le code de macOS 26.7.
Ce qu’on sait des lunettes connectées d’Apple
Depuis des années, on sait qu’Apple travaille sur une première paire de lunettes connectées. Il ne s’agirait donc pas d’une nouvelle version du Vision Pro. Elles n’auraient pas d’écran et leur objectif serait de concurrencer les Ray-Ban Meta. Ces lunettes s’utiliseraient donc uniquement avec un micro et des haut-parleurs, pour communiquer avec Siri et Apple Intelligence. Elles également dotées de caméras pour prendre des photos et des vidéos, mais aussi pour que Siri/Apple Intelligence puisse analyser l’environnement : reconnaître des lieux, traduire du texte, aider à la navigation, etc.
Concernant le calendrier, il se serait décalé : d’abord prévues pour fin 2026, les lunettes auraient été repoussées pour le second semestre 2027, puis pour la fin de l’année 2027. Mais Apple pourrait décider de les présenter dans un premier temps lors de la WWDC 2027, sa conférence pour les développeurs prévue pour juin prochain. Face à la concurrence de Meta et à la myriade d’autres marques qui se lancent sur le secteur, Apple n’aurait plus le choix : il lui faut ses lunettes connectées. Et pour capter des parts de marché, Apple peut s’appuyer sur sa renommée, mais aussi son expérience utilisateur et logicielle et son intégration de Siri.

articles.title: Qvyon launches with $8M to improve safety for physical AI deployments - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Qvyon launches with $8M to improve safety for physical AI deployments
Physical AI validation infrastructure and software development company Qvyon Technologies Inc. launched today with $8 million in total funding to help companies validate autonomous vehicles and robots before deployment.
MaC Venture Capital led the funding, with participation from BDC Capital, BKR Capital and Spotlight VP.
Physical AI is artificial intelligence that moves from digital brains to the real world, allowing smart machines to perceive, reason about and act within physical environments. This can include factory floors, retail shopping aisles, the kitchen or the roadway.
Before companies can deploy smart machines, such as robots or self-driving cars, into the real world, they must understand how these systems will operate under both normal and abnormal conditions. Reproducing strange, unlikely and dangerous conditions in the field is difficult and risky. For example, a car might suddenly pull in front of a truck during a rainstorm or a sensor array on a robot might become blocked or damaged while working on a production line.
To address these examples, Qvyon released Mimic Core, a platform that takes real-world sensor recordings into simulated environments to produce varied test scenarios, allowing developers and engineers to access data and test physical AI models and robotics setups in virtual environments without repeatedly collecting field data.
A single recording can allow an engineer to create many test variations to tease out where systems make mistakes. This allows development teams to catch problems before putting robots to work in the real world.
“We spent years building AI for vehicles and saw how hard it was to prove those systems were ready for the road,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Frantz Saintellemy. “Companies need to test what happens in their own vehicles and factories by using their own recordings.”
Qvyon’s system ingests camera, lidar and radar data. It uses this to reconstruct environments in 3D and time-sequence snapshots, capturing scenes and how they change over time. It uses this to generate challenging conditions to test AI models against the hardware they will drive in simulation. The platform produces traceable datasets and validation evidence that engineers can use to evaluate smart machines’ performance before deployment.
Mimic Core works alongside the same virtual testing tools that companies already use and helps them better understand the scenarios and conditions robots and smart machines will face.
The company offers the product as software-as-a-service and as a self-hosted solution for companies that want to keep everything in-house. Qvyon stressed that when using its cloud product, customer data is kept separate and is never used to train AI models for other customers.
Mimic Core is available today via Qvyon Cloud with a 14-day guided evaluation, or for companies to run on their own systems.
The company said the funding will support Mimic Core and its rollout through the United States, Europe and Japan. Qvyon is also developing Mimic Validation OS, planned for the first half of 2027, to help companies measure and document test results, and Mimic Learn, planned for late 2027, to help improve AI using information from machines already in operation.

Premium Newegg combo takes the sting out of building an AM5-based gaming PC

articles.title: En plenos escándalos de Jensen Huang, hay una guerra abierta en el Gobierno de EEUU por seguir vendiendo GPUs a China
articles.text:
Nvidia tiene tres problemas enormes y eso significa que Estados Unidos... también. Uno es el tremebundo lío que está provocando Jensen Huang con sus aventuras extramatrimoniales. Otro es buscar sustituto para Huang, ya que acaba de dimitir. El otro es que el desvío de chips de inteligencia artificial de Nvidia hacia China, pese a las restricciones, sigue dando dolores de cabeza a Washington. Además, según un informe de Axios del que se hace eco Reuters, es algo que está ocasionando un frente interno.
Ni en el propio Gobierno liderado por Trump se ponen de acuerdo sobre cómo atajar el asunto. Y en el centro de la polémica está el protagonista de la semana, un Jensen Huang que, curiosamente, llevaba más de un año presionando para vender más GPU a China.
En corto. Howard Lutnick es el secretario de Comercio de Estados Unidos y, según ese reporte de Axios, habría frenado la ofensiva que el presidente Donald Trump ordenó contra las empresas sospechosas de desviar chips de Nvidia a China. Según Axios, Trump autorizó el jueves 5 de noviembre una tercera ofensiva este año, pero Lutnick se habría interpuesto.
Sala de Crisis. Aquí hay dos posturas claras: los que quieren evitar que las GPU sigan llegando y los que quieren aprovecharse de la situación. Ese mismo día, Lutnick se reunió en la Sala de Crisis de la Casa Blanca con Scott Bessent (secretario del Tesoro), Pete Hegseth (secretario de Defensa), Jamieson Greer (representante comercial) y Marco Rubio (secretario de Estado).
De nuevo, según Axios, Bessent reprochó a Lutnick que su departamento se esté resistiendo constantemente a aplicar los controles a la exportación y, aunque el secretario de Comercio pareció darle la razón, echó balones fuera argumentando que eso debía consultarlo con Trump.
Postura dura. Estos últimos meses, varios legisladores han pedido una postura más contundente de Washington al respecto, pidiendo una ley que endurezca las restricciones. Ahora vuelven a la carga tras la revelación de la relación que Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, ha tenido con una supuesta espía china que, además, es exejecutiva de una de las empresas de las que se sospecha que está implicada en ese contrabando de GPU que acaban en China.
Las GPU siguen llegando. Porque el lío comercial va a dos bandas. Por un lado, la vía legal y estrecha. Por otro, la ilícita. La mala suerte para Jensen es que está en el centro de ambas. El CEO de Nvidia lleva mucho tiempo queriendo dar un mordisco al jugoso y enorme pastel de la IA en China, convenciendo a Trump para que le dejara vender GPU avanzadas a las empresas chinas que las pidieran. Desde el punto de vista comercial, tiene sentido: son los reyes del sector y, además, alimentarían una industria con un potencial enorme en China.
Desde el estratégico, también, ya que harían que las empresas chinas dependieran de tecnología que no controlan, haciendo que si quieren seguir en esa carrera deban seguir comprando a Nvidia. A Trump le convenció la idea, ya que aceptó a vender ciertas GPU avanzadas previo recargo del 25%. Parecía un win-win, pero Pekín entró en juego poniendo impedimentos porque, precisamente, lo que no quiere es que sus empresas dependan de tecnología extranjera.
Pero luego está la otra vía: las empresas chinas no necesitan comprar a Nvidia legalmente porque las GPU ya están llegando, de algún modo. Llevamos meses informando sobre cómo este hardware aparece en China aunque nadie sepa muy bien cómo. Y, aunque llega con un sobreprecio fruto de que no deja de ser un producto de contrabando, llega. Como decía, Megaspeed es sospechosa de desviar al menos un pedido de más de 4.000 millones de dólares en equipo a China.
El agujero de Singapur. Y si te preguntas cómo eso es posible, la respuesta es que, al parecer, los que se encargan de certificar que se cumplan las restricciones son las propias empresas que venden. En medio están los reguladores y autoridades, pero en la práctica, parece que es Nvidia certificando que las GPU se facturan a quien tienen que facturarse, pero luego esas GPU pueden aparecer en otro sitio.
Con la propia Megaspeed, de Singapur, parece que ha ocurrido eso. Nvidia atribuyó a Singapur el 22% de sus ventas en un trimestre de 2024, pero el ministro de comercio del país explicó que la entrega física fue inferior al 1% y que ellos sólo facturaban. Como digo, la factura y el chip no tienen por qué ir juntos en este caso, y eso es lo que se querría cambiar para tener un mayor control.
Halcones. Relacionado con esto, hay un término en el que quizá no hemos entrado tanto por ser demasiado "estadounidensecentrista", y es el de los "halcones" o "China hawks". Es así como se conoce a quienes defienden esa línea dura con Pekín, los que piden restringir al máximo la venta de chips avanzados porque temen que refuercen tanto la IA como la tecnología militar del país. No son un sólo bloque de un partido y, como leemos en Quartz, es algo en lo que algunos republicanos y demócratas se dan la mano.
De hecho, ya protestaron cuando la Administración dio verde en enero a vender los chips H200 de Nvidia a China. Incluso hubo quien protestó cuando Nvidia tenía permiso únicamente para vender los H20, que son chips más recortados y muy lejos de la potencia de los de vanguardia que estaban usando en Estados Unidos. El argumento es que cada venta y cada chip enviado permitía recortar la distancia tecnológica entre los dos ejércitos.
Y ahí se toparon contra Jensen y Lutnick, que defendían que había que vender a los chinos lo suficiente como para que su industria se "enganchara" a la tecnología estadounidense. Veremos cómo termina todo porque el propio Lutnick ya se quitó crédito en estas operaciones, apuntando que él se encarga del resto del mundo y que quienes deciden sobre China son Greer, Bessent y el mismísimo Trump.
Ahora, el caso de Jensen y el lío morrocotudo de Nvidia seguro que da alas a los halcones para seguir oponiéndose.
