articles.title: Kutlerri.ai raises $4M to help US restaurants grow revenue and cut costs using AI agents
articles.text:
Kutlerri.ai
View Brand Publisher
Kutlerri.ai raises $4M to help US restaurants grow revenue and cut costs using AI agents
Founded by former HighRadius executives Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy, Kutlerri.ai charges restaurants a percentage of the revenue its AI agents generate or the costs they save.
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million from Houston-based Narahari Investments to scale its AI agents that help restaurants increase revenue and reduce operating costs.
Founded in December 2025 by former HighRadius executives Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy, the startup develops AI agents that handle specific revenue and cost-related tasks for restaurants. Unlike conventional software subscriptions, Kutlerri.ai charges operators based on the revenue generated or costs saved by its agents.
The company currently serves restaurants in the US and has more than 10 signed customers. Its product and engineering team is based in Bhubaneswar, Odisha; it also has an office in Houston, Texas. The core founding team includes Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav.
The funding will help scale its first commercial product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, bring three agents currently in beta to market, and develop a mobile-first self-service app.
Addressing restaurant profitability
According to the National Restaurant Association's 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry report, US restaurant and foodservice sales are projected to reach $1.55 trillion in 2026, although 42% of operators surveyed reported that they did not make a profit in 2025.
The association also noted in July 2026 that rising costs continued to put pressure on restaurant profitability. Even before the post-pandemic increase in costs, a typical restaurant retained only about five cents of every dollar earned.
With margins this narrow, even small improvements can make a difference. Kutlerri.ai focuses on increasing revenue and reducing costs through AI agents that take on tasks restaurants may not have dedicated staff to manage.
Restaurants already use software for point-of-sale operations, kitchen displays, inventory, online ordering, payroll, and accounting. However, these systems primarily record information rather than act on it.
For instance, catering enquiries may go unanswered, or delivery advertisements may continue running without producing results. Addressing such problems generally requires dedicated staff, which many independent restaurants cannot afford.
Kutlerri.ai’s agents are designed to handle these tasks. Its revenue agents work on catering, third-party delivery, and online ordering, while its cost agents focus on delivery advertising, food and labour costs, daily preparation, and waste.
Restaurants can use the agents through a fully managed service or, once launched, a mobile-first self-service app. In both models, Kutlerri.ai charges a percentage of the additional revenue generated or costs saved. If an agent does not deliver measurable results, the restaurant does not pay.
Catering agent generates $450,000 for RASA
Kutlerri.ai's first commercial product focuses on catering sales.
According to MONKEY's State of Catering 2026 report, 60% of catering orders came from just 5% of customers. The findings were based on transactional data from more than 8,000 restaurant locations and two million catering orders.
The figures highlight the importance of attracting new catering customers and reconnecting with previous ones, particularly for restaurants without dedicated sales teams.
The AI Catering Sales Agent identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius of a restaurant. It contacts businesses through email, text messages, and phone calls, reconnects with inactive customers, responds to incoming calls, chats, and emails, and closes orders. Restaurant operators approve decisions and retain their customer relationships.
Kutlerri.ai developed the agent with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group in the Washington, DC, area. The two companies worked together to develop the product around RASA’s catering sales requirements, with the restaurant group paying for the service throughout the development period.
According to Kutlerri.ai, the agent generated $450,000 in new catering revenue for RASA over 10 months, more than 10X the amount the restaurant group paid for the service, without requiring additional hires.
The catering agent is now live with operators in most major US cities, the company said.
From HighRadius to restaurant operations
Rana, CEO, and Tripathy, COO, previously worked at HighRadius, where business functions had clear ownership of financial performance.
Their interest in the restaurant sector began after observing the operations of a restaurant run by someone close to them. While the restaurant used several systems to track performance, there was no dedicated person to act on the information.
The founders subsequently spoke with other operators, including fast-casual restaurants and multi-location groups generating around $3 million annually.
They found similar challenges: scattered data, delayed identification of problems, decisions based on judgement rather than data, and margins that had remained unchanged for years.
These observations led them to build Kutlerri.ai around AI agents that could take responsibility for specific revenue and cost-related functions.
Expansion plans
Kutlerri.ai’s product & engineering, marketing, business development and customer success teams operate from India, with each function responsible for outcomes linked to restaurant profitability.
The company currently has one commercially available agent, three agents in beta testing inside restaurants, and two more under development.
It plans to expand its strategy, marketing, customer success and engineering teams as it develops and launches these products.
While Kutlerri.ai currently focuses on US restaurants, it is open to expanding into India and other markets in the future. As the company continues to grow, explore career opportunities with the team [email protected].

articles.title: IA : les nouveaux modèles deviennent obsolètes en seulement six semaines, selon Vercel
articles.text:
Une récente étude menée par Vercel montre que six semaines suffisent pour qu’un modèle ne soit plus à la mode. Des données qu’il faut toutefois tempérer.
Le marché de l’intelligence artificielle est en pleine ébullition. Pour rester dans la course, les géants du domaine multiplient les innovations : Google a dégainé l’IA de pointe Gemini 4 Argon le mois dernier avant de dévoilé Gemini 4 Carbon, Anthropic a lancé Claude Fable 5.2 et Mythos 5.2 ce lundi et GPT 6.2 ne devrait plus tarder à pointer le bout de son nez. La plateforme Vercel s’est intéressée à la vitesse à laquelle ces modèles sont adoptés. Le résultat donne le tournis.
Les modèles d’IA périment rapidement
Vercel a mis au point l’AI Gateway, un outil qui permet de relier les applications des développeurs à différents fournisseurs d’intelligence artificielle. Plus de 100 000 milliards de tokens y transitent chaque mois, ce qui permet à la société d’observer les habitudes de ces professionnels.
Dans un récent rapport, Vercel a partagé des conclusions pour le moins étonnantes : « Plus de la moitié des demandes de modèles de langage concernaient des modèles de moins de deux mois, contre moins de trois sur dix auparavant. Dans le mois qui suit le pic d’utilisation d’un modèle, trois équipes sur quatre qui l’utilisaient sont passées à un autre », peut-on notamment lire.
- Intégration native de Next.js
- Aucun serveur à configurer
- Déploiements depuis Git, CLI, API REST
Un modèle atteint donc son pic d’utilisation dans le mois qui suit sa sortie et sa « demi-vie » serait d’environ six semaines. La loyauté n’est pas de mise : « Les équipes changent fréquemment de modèle, généralement pour une version plus récente, et souvent pour un autre laboratoire. (…) Quatre sur cinq sont passées à une version plus récente, et six sur dix ont changé de laboratoire ».
Un fournisseur est toutefois plus prisé : Anthropic séduit deux fois plus qu’OpenAI. Paradoxalement, la firme de Sam Altman a vu sa part de revenus augmenter. Son concurrent n’a pas eu la même chance : « OpenAI perçoit désormais près de 15 centimes pour chaque dollar dépensé sur la plateforme, contre environ 9 en décembre, tandis que la part d’Anthropic a été divisée par deux pour atteindre environ 32 centimes sur la même période. »
Les modèles de décision ont le vent en poupe
Le rapport partage une autre constatation importante : les modèles de décision, qui « classent, évaluent ou choisissent parmi des options au lieu de générer du texte » sont de plus en plus appréciés : ils représentent actuellement quasiment un tiers des requêtes.
Les équipes font aussi de plus en plus appel aux modèles vocaux : 14 % des clients de Vercel s’en servent désormais contre 5 % auparavant. Même constat pour l’image et la vidéo qui signent leur meilleur mois. Le modèle Seedance 2.5 de ByteDance est premier du classement vidéo pour le troisième mois d’affilée, devant Google Veo et Kling.
Il faut toutefois prendre les données de ce rapport avec des pincettes : il ne concerne que les utilisateurs d’AI Gateway, qui ne représentent pas l’ensemble du marché. De plus, l’intérêt principal de l’outil est qu’il est possible de basculer facilement d’un modèle à l’autre. Il n’est donc pas étonnant que les équipes changent régulièrement de fournisseur. Malgré tout, ces éléments donnent un aperçu intéressant des tendances d'adoption actuelles et de la concurrence qui fait rage entre les modèles.

articles.title: Cómo cancelar una suscripción digital paso a paso y sin perderse entre métodos de pago
articles.text:
Dar de baja una suscripción digital se hace en un solo lugar, y ese lugar depende de quién cobra: la propia empresa, Apple o Google. Netflix, Spotify, YouTube Premium y las tiendas de aplicaciones publican en sus centros de ayuda pasos distintos, todos verificados para esta guía.
El tema volvió a la agenda el 11 de noviembre, cuando la Comisión Europea propuso la Ley de Equidad Digital. El texto busca que los contratos y suscripciones digitales sean más fáciles de cancelar y que terminen las renovaciones automáticas no deseadas y las pruebas gratuitas que se convierten en trampas de cobro.
Según la Comisión, alrededor del 60% de los europeos compra bienes o servicios en línea, y quienes lo hacen tienen más de 60% más probabilidades de sufrir problemas que quienes compran en tiendas físicas. La propuesta todavía no es ley, de modo que la protección depende por ahora de cada usuario.
Primero, averiguar quién cobra
Antes de buscar el botón de baja conviene saber quién emite el cargo. Apple recomienda buscar en el correo las palabras “receipt from Apple” o “invoice from Apple” (recibo de Apple). Si el recibo no aparece, la suscripción pudo contratarse con otra empresa, y el resumen del banco o de la tarjeta indica cuál.
Si la cuenta de Apple que figura en el recibo es la de un familiar, solo esa persona puede cancelar la suscripción. Netflix da una pauta similar: si en la cuenta no aparece la opción de cancelar, el servicio se paga a través de un tercero, como un operador de telefonía, y hay que darse de baja con ese socio de pago.
Spotify advierte lo mismo: si no hay opción para cambiar el plan, este está asociado a una empresa asociada, por ejemplo el proveedor móvil o de internet, y la baja se gestiona con ella.
Los pasos en cada servicio
En Netflix, hay que entrar en la página de gestión de la membresía, tocar “Cancelar” y confirmar con “Finalizar cancelación”. La plataforma aclara que cerrar sesión o borrar la aplicación no cancela la cuenta. Si queda tiempo del período pagado, se puede seguir viendo hasta que termine. También ofrece pausar la membresía un mes, hasta un máximo de tres, salvo en el plan Básico y en algunos medios de pago.
En Spotify, se entra en “Administrar tu plan” y se elige “Cancelar suscripción”. Premium sigue activo hasta la siguiente fecha de cobro y después la cuenta pasa al servicio gratuito, con las listas de reproducción y la música guardada. Si la baja ocurre durante una prueba gratuita, el cambio al servicio gratuito es inmediato y esa prueba no puede reactivarse.
En YouTube Premium, se toca la foto de perfil, luego “Membresías pagas”, la membresía que se quiere terminar y “Continuar para cancelar”. Después se elige un motivo y se confirma con “Sí, cancelar”. Si el cobro lo hace Apple o Google Play, la baja debe hacerse en esas cuentas. Los beneficios siguen hasta el final del período de facturación.
Cuando cobra Apple o Google
En un iPhone o iPad, se abre Ajustes, se toca el nombre del usuario, luego “Suscripciones”, la suscripción elegida y “Cancelar suscripción”. Si no hay botón de cancelar o aparece un aviso de vencimiento en rojo, la suscripción ya está cancelada. En una Mac, el camino empieza en la App Store, tocando el nombre en la barra lateral.
En Android, hay que entrar en las suscripciones de Google Play con la cuenta de Google que hizo la compra, elegir la suscripción y tocar “Cancelar suscripción”. Google aclara que desinstalar la aplicación no cancela el cobro. Al cancelar, el acceso continúa por el tiempo ya pagado. Algunas aplicaciones permiten pausar los pagos entre una semana y tres meses.
Google Play también distingue los planes de pago en cuotas: una vez cobrado, no se pueden cancelar los pagos restantes del plan, solo evitar la renovación siguiente. Las cuentas múltiples son otra fuente de confusión: si la suscripción no aparece, puede estar en otra cuenta de Google, y conviene alternar entre ellas.
La Comisión Europea calcula que sus medidas permitirán a los consumidores del bloque ahorrar hasta 13.700 millones de euros al año. Hasta que la propuesta se debata y, en su caso, se apruebe, los pasos de cada centro de ayuda siguen siendo la vía para dar de baja un servicio.

articles.title: Carro voador chinês deve entrar em operação nos próximos meses • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Carro voador chinês deve entrar em operação nos próximos meses
Montadora XPeng já fez demonstrações com protótipo e promete disponibilizar veículo em 2027.
A XPeng já tem uma previsão de quando seu “carro voador” chegará ao mercado. Com aprovação da aviação civil chinesa, o modelo poderá realizar voos recreativos em áreas rurais e voos de emergência já no verão de 2027 – nosso inverno aqui no Brasil, entre junho e agosto.
O veículo ainda não tem nome, mas seu protótipo já vem sendo demonstrado pelos últimos anos. Trata-se de um conjunto com duas partes: uma espécie de SUV que funciona como base e o próprio módulo de voo, que sai de dentro do carro principal e se “transforma” para levantar voo.
Segundo o The Guardian, o modelo custará US$ 300 mil, aproximadamente R$ 1,67 mi na cotação atual. No cockpit de voo, há espaço para duas pessoas, e o veículo funciona de forma autônoma. Também é possível pilotar o módulo de maneira simples.
O produto da XPeng é divido em um carro padrão, uma van de seis rodas, e um módulo de voo em si, menor e que “abre” as hélices para tomar sua forma definitiva. Segundo o CEO Deli Zhao, o modelo sai da SUV “exatamente como um Transformer”.
Em termos de design, o veículo não é muito diferente de outros carros voadores (ou eVTOLs, sigla em inglês para aeronaves elétricas de decolagem e pouso vertical, em inglês). A Embraer tem um protótipo com essa proposta, da mesma forma que a Uber divulgou seus primeiros conceitos de eVTOL quando ainda planejava lançar seu UberAir.
A diferença aqui fica por conta da SUV que “guarda” o módulo, permitindo aos usuários viajarem tanto por terra quanto em voo. Vale reforçar que o veículo tem permissão para altitudes baixas, além de operação limitada a áreas rurais em um primeiro momento.
Em uma conferência em Lisboa, Portugal, a XPeng demonstrou o veículo para o público. Segundo Zhao, as viagens correram bem, e “ninguém se machucou”. O modelo consegue voar por distâncias de até 30 quilômetros, o que deve aumentar com a evolução da bateria utilizada, prevista para chegar a 400 kW por quilo.
A aprovação dos voos passa pela chamada “economia de altitude baixa”, projeto econômico desenvolvido em Pequim para movimentar os céus da cidade com o transporte de cargas e pessoas. Zhao afirma que existem outros acordos encaminhados para levar a tecnologia para mais países asiáticos.
Ele foi questionado ainda sobre outra demonstração de “carro voador”: o da Tesla. Na ocasião, a empresa de Elon Musk exibiu um automóvel padrão com jatos de água que podem sustentar quedas e até virar o veículo no ar. De acordo com o executivo chinês, o protótipo da Tesla estava, na verdade, “pulando, e não voando”.

articles.title: 'Every company we’re talking to is asking the same thing': Leaders agree AI is vital for their workplace — but only 10% say they're doing anything about it
articles.text:
'Every company we’re talking to is asking the same thing': Leaders agree AI is vital for their workplace — but only 10% say they're doing anything about it
AI can’t adopt itself
- Research finds that 80% of IT leaders recognize AI needs a digital workplace
- But only 10% have led an AI transformation in their organization
- Lenovo report highlights the existence of an “AI readiness divide” where ambition is not matched by preparation
AI offers the promise of greater productivity, but if your business isn’t prepared, that promise is wasted, new research has claimed.
A survey from Lenovo show that while 80% of IT leaders understand the potential for AI needs in the workplace, only 10% of them have put in place the digital transformation to facilitate success.
The sixth volume of the Lenovo Work Reborn report provides the results of a 1,200-person survey, conducted with IT leaders across the UK, US, Canada, Australia, and eight other countries, some worrying implications for AI readiness - but also asserts that a divide is becoming apparent, various levels of unpreparedness potentially limiting opportunities for businesses and organizations that have fallen behind.
Scaling slow
The report highlights various surprises. First, it seems that while AI is scaled across business functions, just 10% of organizations have approached its implementation with a rethink on how work is produced. Similarly, just 10% of businesses have governance that covers AI tools, agents, and data access.
Elsewhere, businesses seem to be unable to measure AI’s value, with many adopting a “fire and forget” approach to its implementation. Just 10% responded saying that an ROI measurement is in place to understand AI’s impact in delivering results.
The Lenovo report presents the findings with a score on its AI Workplace Readiness Index. This is a metric that measures five dimensions of AI workplace readiness: architecture, operations, trust, workforce, and value. Organizations that score well in all five are considered to be ahead when it comes to AI implementation.
Organizations with AI fully in use across their core business functions are given an average score of 4.1 our of 5. At the other end of the scale, organizations that are still evaluating AI score 2.7.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Creating value with AI
Talk is cheap, and declaring a desire to embrace and implement AI is very different from actually doing so. Establishing an AI-ready digital workplace means more than positive words – leaders need to put in the groundwork and have the budget in place to make it happen.
Rakshit Ghura, Vice President and General Manager at Lenovo Digital Workplace Solutions, says “Every company we’re talking to is asking the same thing: what value are we actually getting from AI? That’s where workflow-level measurement matters. Are cycle times down? Are repeat incidents falling? Is the outcome better?” That is, says Ghura, “how you show where AI is creating value.”
Updating the workplace is a no-brainer. As Ghura also notes, “a workplace designed for the pre-AI era” prevents AI from being used effectively. “The opportunity is to redesign how people and AI work together, with the technology, support and governance around them built for how work is changing."

articles.title: Norwest closes $4B fund to back AI, healthcare and financial infra
articles.text:
Norwest closes $4B fund to back AI, healthcare and financial infra
Norwest’s $4 billion fund signals a long-term bet on AI, healthcare and technology, as the investment firm looks to back businesses across markets, stages and sectors.
Norwest, an investment firm focused on venture capital and growth equity, has closed a $4 billion fund, Norwest 18, the largest in its 65-year history. It will back companies in technology, healthcare and consumer markets across the US, India and Israel, from early-stage ventures to established businesses.
Founded in 1961, Norwest says it has invested in more than 750 companies and currently works with over 275 portfolio businesses. Its Indian investments include OfBusiness and Swiggy, and it has a Mumbai office. The firm notes its multi-stage approach is intended to support companies as they move from early development to expansion.
Norwest 18 follows Norwest 17, launched in April 2024. Since then, the firm says it has made more than 87 investments and worked with over 30 portfolio companies to achieve liquidity events, when investors can realise value from a holding. These include stock market listings by Amagi Media Labs and Swiggy, and acquisitions of businesses including Qualified by Salesforce and Veza by ServiceNow.
The firm believes its role extends beyond providing capital, particularly as businesses face more complicated growth decisions. Senior Managing Partner Jeff Crowe said companies are staying private for longer, expanding across markets and navigating increasingly complex decisions involving technology, talent and growth.
“Capital is only one part of what they need,” he said, emphasising the importance of long-term support, industry experience and networks.
Norwest expects AI to create opportunities across its established sectors and newer areas, including financial infrastructure, physical and voice AI, cybersecurity for AI agents, industrial technology, aerospace and healthcare. Norwest cites Beltic, Rain and Stablecore in payments and digital-currency infrastructure, and LlamaIndex and Generalist AI in intelligent systems.
The strategy comes as Indian technology investment becomes more concentrated. AI startups in the country raised $1.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $677 million a year earlier, but funding rounds fell 43%. Four large deals accounted for 72% of the total, indicating that capital is flowing disproportionately to infrastructure and model developers, while application businesses struggle to convert interest into paying customers.
Recent Indian fundraises show activity across related sectors. Bengaluru-based Even Healthcare raised $50 million in October from Khosla Ventures and Alpha Wave to expand its managed-care and hospital operations, while wealth technology startup PowerUp Money raised $10 million in November, led by Flourish Ventures, to develop AI-enabled wealth management.
Policy is also shaping the market. The IndiaAI Mission has expanded shared computing capacity to more than 45,000 graphics processing units, and selected 20 proposals for locally developed foundation AI models. In July, the Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0, with a Rs 1.275 trillion budget for semiconductor design and manufacturing.
Norwest is also strengthening support beyond funding by doubling its Senior Advisor Network, adding operating executives and launching the Norwest Operator Collective and Norwest Kinetic.
Managing Partner Jon Kossow said Norwest’s investment approach was built around maintaining long-term relationships with businesses as their requirements evolve. Its multi-stage strategy allows the firm to “meet companies where they are” and continue supporting them as they grow, he said.

articles.title: Le PDG de Nvidia vient de démissionner, c’est officiel
articles.text:
C’est officiel, Jensen Huang n’est plus le PDG de Nvidia. L’homme a remis sa démission ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, avec effet immédiat. Jensen Huang avait cofondé Nvidia en 1993. Une page se tourne dans le secteur de la tech.
Jensen Huang n’est plus le PDG de Nvidia
Ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, le conseil d’administration de Nvidia a tenu une réunion pour décider du sort de Jensen Huang. C’est finalement Jensen Huang lui-même qui a présenté sa démission avec effet immédiat. Colette Kress, directrice financière de Nvidia depuis 2013, a accepté d’occuper temporairement le poste de CEO de Nvidia jusqu’à la nomination d’un successeur permanent.
Une décision inévitable
Pour rappel, Jensen Huang a avoué avoir entretenu une relation extraconjugale avec Alice Huang, dirigeante de l’entreprise singapourienne Megaspeed. Outre les problèmes d’ordre personnel, les autorités américaines soupçonnent Alice Huang d’être une espionne au service de la Chine. Par la suite, Donald Trump a défendu Jensen Huang et le FBI a ouvert une enquête. Mais cela n’est pas tout puisque nous avons appris que le désormais ex-dirigeant de Nvidia a également entretenu une relation avec une employée de l’entreprise. La situation étant trop sensible, Jensen Huang a donc remis sa démission. Il reste à voir si cela résulte d’un accord avec le conseil d’administration ou si Jensen Huang a tout simplement pris les devants avant que le conseil d’administration de Nvidia ne décide de l’évincer. Jensen Huang a cofondé Nvidia en 1993. Une page importante se tourne donc pour l’entreprise.
Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia va maintenant devoir élire un nouveau CEO. Selon Bloomberg, Nvidia a d’ores et déjà fait appel à une entreprise externe pour identifier des candidats au poste de PDG.

articles.title: Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nectar, an AI-powered operating system for marketing, is launching a new AI agent designed to take a lot of the manual work out of influencer marketing, from finding the right creators to contacting them, managing partnerships, and tracking results.
Founded by sisters Misbah and Farah Uraizee, both former Meta employees, Nectar came out of stealth last year and uses AI agents to help brands manage social media, customer conversations, content moderation, creator partnerships, and competitor research.
Announced Thursday, its new “Creator Agent” can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations, and monitor how campaigns perform. Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.
Nectar joins other companies introducing agentic AI assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including Aspire and GRIN. The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. U.S. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau. As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.
Nectar says its Creator Agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.
Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds new matches as creators become more popular.
Once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.
“Brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and Nectar picks up the rest from their history,” CEO Misbah Uraizee tells TechCrunch. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. Nectar understands what is being said in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t.”
Another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a new baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.
Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.
The company plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.
This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.

articles.title: En reprenant Ardoiz, Archos "garantit la continuité des services pour les 22 000 abonnés" des tablettes pour seniors
articles.text:
Abandonnées par La Poste, les tablettes pour seniors Ardoiz sauvées par Archos
Bonne nouvelle pour les abonnés Ardoiz et les seniors qui voudraient tenter l'aventure de cette tablette à abonnement : l'activité, abandonnée par la Poste, est officiellement reprise par Archos.
En mai dernier, après dix ans de commercialisation, la Poste et sa filiale Tikeasy décidaient de jeter l'éponge avec Ardoiz, sa solution de tablette à abonnement à destination des seniors. Après un succès certain durant le Covid, l'activité depuis n'était plus assez suffisante pour la maintenir. Mais, en ce mois de novembre 2026, un nom qui s'est fait rare dans le monde de la tech grand public s'est manifesté pour annoncer la reprise de l'activité Ardoiz : Archos.
Avec Ardoiz, Archos souhaite "garantir la continuité et renforcer l'inclusion numérique"
Dans son communiqué de presse, Archos, partenaire de la solution depuis ses débuts, déclare "la réalisation effective de la reprise du fonds de commerce de la solution Ardoiz auprès de la société Tikeasy". Ainsi, la solution intègre pleinement une filiale du groupe Archos, renommée Ardoiz SAS.
L'objectif de cette acquisition est multiple pour Archos. La première est de garantir la continuité des services pour les 22 000 abonnés actuels. Pour rappel, Ardoiz est non seulement une tablette à l'interface ergonomique, simplifiée et sans publicité (229 €), mais aussi un abonnement obligatoire (11,99 €/mois) pour profiter de services adaptés et d'une assistance téléphonique.
"1 million de seniors en difficulté numérique"
En ajoutant cette corde à son arc, Archos compte, dans un contexte de vieillissement de la population et d'une digitalisation croissante de la société, "simplifier l'accès aux outils numériques pour les personnes âgées, leur permettre de communiquer aisément avec leurs proches (vidéos, partages de photos, messages) et de se divertir au quotidien."
Reste désormais à savoir si Archos apportera des changements à Ardoiz, tandis que la société dessine troix axes pour devenir "l'un des acteurs de référence du "bien vieillir" à domicile". Il est ainsi question d'une transition numérique douce via une prise en charge clé en main face à la fin des lignes fixes traditionnelles, d'un déploiement de services de proximité et d’entraide locale directement intégrés au cœur de l'application, et enfin l’intégration de dispositifs et capteurs connectés pour optimiser la sécurité et le confort des seniors à leur domicile.

articles.title: President Trump says Apple’s Tim Cook is the only man to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO — proposes ’A ‘legend replaces a legend’ in call for Apple’s executive chairman of its board
articles.text:
President Trump says Apple’s Tim Cook is the only man to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO — proposes ’A ‘legend replaces a legend’ in call for Apple’s executive chairman of its board
"There is only one man to take his place"
President Donald Trump has said that retired Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia, just hours after it was announced that the latter had resigned in the wake of a series of scandals. Taking to his Truth Social platform, the President said, "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President DONALD J. TRUMP."
Nvidia's board of directors announced on Wednesday that Huang had resigned following the revelation that he conducted an extramarital affair with a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, and a further affair with Nvidia Vice President of Health Care, Kimberly Powell.
Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, will serve as Interim CEO while the company looks for a replacement. Naturally, names have been floated as potential successor candidates, including Apple's Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.
With Nvidia at the center of the global explosion in AI, Huang and Trump have enjoyed a close relationship that routinely makes news headlines. Trump previously described Huang as 'utterly visionary' in regard to his views on tariffs and rescinding President Biden's AI Diffusion Rule.
President Trump's name has been mentioned in the ongoing Huang affair scandal. Notably, it is alleged that while U.S. intelligence believed that Huang had been the target of a Chinese honeypot operation, reports claim that President Trump was briefed on the matter but chose not to do anything with the information, so as not to affect Nvidia's sales or antagonize China.
Congress has summoned Jensen Huang to appear before the Select Committee on the CCP, with lawmakers threatening to issue Huang with a subpoena if he doesn't agree to attend a closed-door meeting voluntarily.
Tim Cook is currently the Executive Chair of Apple's board, having served as the company's CEO from 2011 to 2026. During his tenure, he oversaw the launch of a plethora of Apple services, including Apple Music and Apple TV, while expanding into new product categories such as Apple Watch and AirPods.

Nvidia's share price plunged more than 10 percentage points at the open on Wednesday, but recovered much of that ground as traders looked to take advantage of the dip in Nvidia's share price. The company will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results next week, on Tuesday, November 17.

articles.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock
Part 1 of this series built the operating model that controls Amazon Bedrock spend: attribution with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) principal tags and Cost and Usage Report 2.0, observability with model invocation logging, enforcement at three tiers, and a review cadence. That layer answers who spent it, and you can stop them. It can’t tell you whether the spend was well spent.
This post answers two questions that Part 1 deliberately left open. First: Why is this workflow expensive? The answer requires thinking in cost per task, not cost per token. Second: Is the agent better than the humans were? The answer requires baselines, controlled experiments, and a scorecard tied to decisions.
In this post, you learn a framework for calculating true model cost (including four hidden cost drivers that the pricing page doesn’t show), techniques for reducing cost per task through caching, routing, and output constraints, and a discipline for measuring agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard. This post is written for two audiences: the application and platform engineers who own the optimization levers, and the product owners and FinOps partners who need to justify agent spend to leadership.
Cost per task, not cost per token
Price per token invites quick comparison, but it doesn’t reflect what you actually pay. The published rate reflects the cost of a single token. Your bill reflects the cost of completing a task. A task is one complete unit of work your application asks a model to do: resolve one support email, extract fields from one invoice, or answer one user question. A task runs from the request through to a usable result, however many model calls it takes.
The lower-priced model might not be the cheaper one to run. A cheaper model might fragment your text into more tokens, pad responses with filler, misread your tool schema and loop through corrections, or burn thousands of reasoning tokens before answering. None of these costs appear on the Bedrock pricing page.
The four hidden cost drivers
Four model characteristics determine what that published rate actually costs you on your workload.
Tokenizer efficiency
A token isn’t a word, and it is not equal across models. Every model family uses a different tokenizer and vocabulary. The same text, code, or JSON payload splits into different token counts. If Model A’s list price is 15 percent lower but its tokenizer needs 40 percent more tokens for your data (common with structured schemas and numerical arrays), Model B is cheaper. The gap widens for non-English text: many tokenizers fragment non-Latin scripts into two to three times more tokens than the equivalent English.
Output alignment and verbosity
Output tokens commonly cost 3–5x more than input tokens (the ratio varies by family. Refer to the Bedrock pricing page). A model that ignores formatting constraints like “return only raw JSON” makes you pay that output premium for filler words. A model that follows formatting instructions closely saves money by generating fewer of these more expensive output tokens.
Agentic loop efficiency
Agentic workflows change the cost math entirely. Tool use (function calling) lets a model invoke external functions, requiring a multi-turn loop: analyze the prompt, decide to call a tool, wait for the observation, generate an answer. Each turn re-sends the full conversation history and tool results as input tokens. A model that takes four turns (each one re-sending a larger context payload) costs far more than one that finishes in a single pass.
Reasoning overhead
Many models support extended thinking, working through a chain of thought before the visible answer. Reasoning tokens bill as output tokens, so a model that thinks for 2,000 tokens before a 200-token answer bills you for 2,200. Some models redact the reasoning while still charging for it. Start with reasoning turned off and enable it only when benchmarks show a quality gap that justifies the cost.
Cost per task: A worked example
Consider an agentic workflow that reads a 750-word customer email, extracts entities, calls an API to verify account status, and outputs strict JSON. The following comparison uses illustrative prices (always benchmark against your own data and current Bedrock pricing):
| Metric | Model A (lower list price) | Model B (higher list price) | 
| Input list price | $0.50 / 1M tokens | $1.00 / 1M tokens | 
| Output list price | $1.50 / 1M tokens | $3.00 / 1M tokens | 
| Tokenizer efficiency (turn 1 input) | 1,500 tokens | 1,000 tokens | 
| Output verbosity (final response) | 450 tokens | 150 tokens | 
| Agentic loops required | 3 turns (error correction) | 1 turn (zero-shot) | 
| Cumulative input tokens, all turns | 6,150 | 1,000 | 
| Cumulative output tokens, all turns | 750 | 150 | 
| Total task cost | $0.0042 | $0.00145 | 
Model A: (6,150 x $0.50 + 750 x $1.50) / 1,000,000 = $0.0042
Model B: (1,000 x $1.00 + 150 x $3.00) / 1,000,000 = $0.00145
Why the 2x-priced model costs 65 percent less: three compounding factors. Model A’s tokenizer fragments the email into 50 percent more tokens, inflating every input payload. It pads its JSON with filler, tripling output tokens. And it misaligns with the tool schema, needing two correction turns that each re-send a growing history.
Cost per successful task
The preceding example assumes both models eventually succeed. In production they won’t, and a failure is rarely free. The formulas:
For retry-until-success workflows:
cost per successful task = cost per attempt / success rate
For escalate-on-failure workflows:
cost per successful task = cost per attempt + (1 - success rate) x escalation cost
Input further splits into three buckets when prompt caching is active: uncached input at base rate, cache reads below base rate, and cache writes above base rate.
Measuring it on your own workload
Which model is actually cheaper only shows up when you benchmark against your own data. Amazon Bedrock model evaluation is the managed feature for the quality half of that: define criteria, upload your prompt datasets, and get scored results with automatic metrics and optional human review, with no custom infrastructure required.
Quality scores alone don’t produce a bill, though. Three more Bedrock features supply the token and turn counts you price against them:
- CountTokens returns the input token count a given model would charge for a given payload without running inference. It’s the cheapest way to compare tokenizer efficiency (driver #1) across candidates before you spend anything on generation.
- Model invocation response carries a usage block with inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, and cacheWriteInputTokens. Accumulating those across the turns of a single task gives you the four terms of the preceding cost-per-attempt formula. One gotcha: when caching is enabled, inputTokens counts only the uncached tokens, so your total input volume is inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens. Sum them to know the footprint, but price them separately, since the three bill at different rates. Evaluate this multiple times throughout your journey and set the cache checkpoints based on what is the active current load. The drift in cache checkpoints happens as the application progresses and the tools become stale. This means that you will be writing more to the cache in 3 months from now when the drift has happened. Evaluating your data constantly for optimal cache usage becomes a primary lever to reduce cost.
- Model invocation logging writes per-invocation token counts to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) or Amazon CloudWatch Logs, so you can measure turns-to-completion against real production traffic instead of a sample. Tag calls with request metadata to slice those logged token counts by team, feature, or experiment. However, these are log fields, not cost allocation tags, and never appear in AWS Cost Explorer or your Cost and Usage Report. Application inference profiles do reach both, at a grain of one usage type per day. That grain is right for chargeback but too coarse for cost per task. Multiplying logged token counts by the published rates gives you a near real-time estimate rather than an invoice. It won’t reflect commitments, batch pricing, or provisioned throughput unless you model them. Reconcile against your Cost and Usage Report before you treat it as the bill.
Reducing cost per task: Four levers
Each of the four drivers has a lever, and each is documented in depth. Prompt caching cuts the re-sent context that made Model A expensive, which makes it the largest win on agentic paths. Intelligent prompt routing sends the easy requests to a cheaper model in the same family. A tool schema plus a maxTokens cap holds verbosity down more reliably than prose instructions do, and extended thinking stays off until a benchmark shows it earns its cost back. Batch inference halves the rate on bulk single-turn work, though it rules out tool calling and multi-turn exchange.
Proving agent ROI: Describe the human baseline
Efficient isn’t the same as valuable. An agent can be perfectly optimized and still not be worth running. The question that decides budgets is: is the agent better than the humans were?
Document the human process first
The biggest mistake in agent ROI is trying to prove value without first describing the human workflow. Before building or scaling an agent, write down the current process in operational terms: what triggers the work, which human roles are involved, where the handoffs sit, how completion is defined. This sounds like bureaucracy. It’s actually measurement design. Every instrumentation decision downstream (what counts as a run, what counts as success, where human time is spent) falls out of this description.
Measure the baseline before the agent ships
With the process described, measure the human baseline over a meaningful window: time to completion, queue time, active effort, reopen rate, escalation rate, cost per task, and outcome quality. Baselines must be measured before the agent goes live, not reconstructed from memory after the fact. Retrospective baselines are systematically flattering to the agent: people remember the average case and forget the fast ones.
Instrument the workflow as an experiment
After the baseline exists, instrument the agent workflow as an experiment from day one. Every run gets a trace ID, and every meaningful step is observable. A workflow-run record aggregates everything above the model call into a single analyzable unit:
Three fields deserve emphasis:
experiment block: Stamped at run creation and propagated into Bedrock request metadata, so model-level and workflow-level records join cleanly.
humanMinutes: What most teams omit and most need. Without it, “the agent did the work” silently excludes the 35 minutes a human spent reviewing it.
revenueEventId: The hook that makes revenue attribution possible later. It costs nothing to record and can’t be reconstructed afterward.
The rule: If the workflow telemetry can’t answer the business question, the instrumentation is incomplete.
Join cost to outcomes
With invocation logs landing in Amazon S3 (Part 1) and workflow-run records in your analytics store, one join produces the metrics that matter. Amazon Bedrock logs record tokens, not dollars, so first build a view that prices each invocation from token counts and your model rate sheet, aggregated by run ID. Then query with Amazon Athena:
        Note: Column names and join keys shown in the preceding query are illustrative. Verify against your invocation log schema and workflow telemetry store, which might vary by implementation.
Cost per successful outcome, retries per success, and human minutes per success are the three numbers that survive contact with a skeptical CFO. Cost per call flatters agents that loop. Cost per success doesn’t. Note the variant grouping: the same query, split by experiment arm, is the ROI comparison.
Compare agents and humans correctly
The most credible evaluation is an A/B or holdout test. Controlled treatment and control groups compare the agent-assisted workflow against the human baseline without confusing the result with market, seasonal, or organizational changes.
For customer-facing or revenue-linked workflows, randomize at the visitor, lead, account, or case level. For internal workflows (support operations, coding assistants), use matched cohorts: teams, repository groups, or pods.
The comparison covers four dimensions:
Efficiency: time to completion, hours recovered, queue-time reduction.
Quality: error rate, approval rate, reopen rate, escalation rate.
Cost: cost per task, cost per successful outcome, total cost to serve.
Business value: conversion lift, retention lift, expansion rate, revenue per rep or per workflow.
If the agent improves one dimension while meaningfully degrading another, the result is ambiguous and the deployment needs tuning.
Revenue: The hardest metric
Efficiency gains are the easiest part of the ROI story to prove. Revenue impact is harder, and it is the metric leadership funds against. In revenue-adjacent workflows, measure whether the agent improves conversion, time-to-response, deal progression, or revenue per rep. Holdout tests are the most reliable way to separate incremental revenue attributable to the agent from general business momentum.
When revenue lift is real, the conversation changes. The organization stops asking whether the Bedrock bill went up and starts asking whether the additional spend is buying a meaningful increase in business output.
The scorecard
Based on what we have observed working with customers, a strong operating model doesn’t require fifty metrics. What works is a small scorecard tied to decisions, reviewed on a regular cadence for every production agent.
The following thresholds are starting points, not prescriptions. Calibrate them against your own fleet data and organizational context.
| Dimension | Metric | Green | Yellow | Red | 
| Adoption | Active users / intended users | >70% | 40-70% | <40% | 
| Quality | Tasks completed without rework | >90% | 75-90% | <75% | 
| Efficiency | Hours recovered per week | >target | 50-100% of target | <50% of target | 
| Cost | Cost per successful outcome | ≤budget | 1-1.5x budget | >1.5x budget | 
| Business impact | KPI lift compared to baseline | Significant | Marginal | None or negative | 
Green means scale: the agent beats baseline while meeting cost and quality thresholds. Yellow means tune: promising but needs work. Red means retire or redesign: the agent consumes cost without enough measurable value. The willingness to actually retire a red agent is what makes the rest of the scorecard credible.
Conclusion
In this post, you learned how to calculate the true cost of a model by accounting for four hidden cost drivers (tokenizer efficiency, output alignment, agentic loop efficiency, and reasoning overhead), how to reduce cost per task through prompt caching, model routing, output constraints, and batch inference, and how to prove agent ROI by measuring human baselines, instrumenting workflows as experiments, joining cost to outcomes, and running holdout comparisons.
The cost optimization half answers “why is this expensive and how do I fix it.” The ROI half answers “is the agent better than the humans were.” Together with Part 1’s operating model (attribute, observe, enforce, optimize, operate), they form a complete framework: you can see who spent it, explain why, reduce the waste, and justify what remains.
To get started, benchmark your top model candidates against your own prompts using Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, capture tokens and turns from the usage block or your invocation logs, price them against current Bedrock pricing, and divide by success rate. For ROI measurement, consult the Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens for agent cost governance best practices.
If you have found other techniques for reducing cost per task or measuring agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock, let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Horizon3 launches Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab built on NodeZero attack data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Horizon3 launches Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab built on NodeZero attack data
Autonomous penetration testing company Horizon3 AI Inc. today launched its new Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab.
The lab will draw on data from NodeZero, Horizon3’s penetration testing service, which is used by more than 7,000 organizations including banks, federal agencies and hospitals.
Purdue University’s Z. Berkay Celik has been named the lab’s inaugural director. Celik is an associate professor of computer science at Purdue and co-director of the Purdue Security Laboratory. Much of his work deals with finding software vulnerabilities and building defenses for autonomous systems, and he has run joint projects with industry and government.
According to Horizon3, NodeZero tests now produce about 30 billion tokens of anonymized data a day. Gathered on customers’ live production networks, the data also shows how their defensive tools reacted to each NodeZero command.
Snehal Antani, Horizon3’s co-founder and chief executive and a former chief technology officer of Splunk Inc., said the company has “spent years collecting” the data. Putting it to use in research like this is the next step, he said.
The lab’s first projects include research on coordinated groups of AI agents used in attacks. Deception is another, building on a Horizon3 paper titled “Honeyquest for LLMs.” Also on the list, according to Horizon3, are “interruption and rollback mechanisms” for autonomous security agents.
Horizon3 published a paper on keeping such agents under control in May. Using Anthropic PBC’s Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Haiku 4.5 models, it tested a design that limited the AI to a fixed list of approved tools, and Horizon3 said the system never proposed an action outside that list across more than 420 deployments.
Trained separately for each customer, Horizon3’s cyber world models give its red and blue agents a shared memory, and the lab is expected to speed up their development. Horizon3’s Cyber Resilience Centers of Excellence, which focus on critical infrastructure, will also report to the lab.
Horizon3 said in October that it had passed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, with growth of 120% year over year. NodeZero has run more than 350,000 production-safe tests to date. Horizon3 said about 80% of its customers have moved from annual to monthly penetration testing.
Founded in 2019, Horizon3 raised $250 million in August at a valuation of more than $2 billion.

articles.title: Sony poursuit son ménage sur PC, et ferme un service PlayStation boudé par 99,6 % des abonnés
articles.text:
Discrètement, Sony vient d'annoncer la fermeture prochaine de son application PlayStation Plus sur PC. Un service (tout aussi discret) qui n'aura jamais vraiment trouvé son public, puisque moins de 0,4 % des abonnés Premium éligibles l'utilisaient.
Le ménage continue chez PlayStation, et après avoir progressivement revu sa stratégie concernant les jeux PC, Sony s'attaque cette fois à un service dont l'existence était probablement inconnue d'une bonne partie des joueurs. Le constructeur vient en effet d'annoncer la fermeture de son application PlayStation Plus sur PC, avec une échéance fixée au 10 décembre 2026 (soit dans un petit mois à peine).
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Moins de 0,4 % des abonnés Premium concernés
Derrière cette application se cachait notamment une fonctionnalité de cloud gaming permettant aux abonnés PlayStation Plus Premium de jouer à certains titres du catalogue PlayStation directement depuis leur ordinateur, sans posséder de console donc. Un héritage de l'ancien PlayStation Now, qui avait été intégré à l'offre PlayStation Plus lors de sa refonte.
Pour justifier cette décision, Sony avance un argument pour le moins imparable : la fréquentation du service. Ou plutôt, la non fréquentation du service. Dans son communiqué officiel, le géant nippon explique que « moins de 0,4 % des abonnés PlayStation Plus Premium éligibles » utilisaient l'application sur PC.
Un chiffre particulièrement faible, qui pousse donc le constructeur à revoir ses priorités. Sony explique notamment vouloir concentrer ses efforts sur les expériences réellement plébiscitées par ses membres, et à compter du 10 décembre, le streaming cloud via l'application PC ne sera donc plus disponible.
Bien sûr, cette fermeture à venir ne concerne en aucun cas les abonnements PlayStation Plus eux-mêmes, ni les avantages associés sur PS4 et PS5. Les abonnés pourront donc continuer à profiter normalement de leur formule sur leurs consoles.
PlayStation veut ramener ses exclusivités à la maison
Chez PlayStation, cette disparition intervient dans un contexte loin d'être anodin, puisque depuis plusieurs mois, Sony prend ses distances avec le marché PC, après avoir pourtant multiplié les portages de ses grandes exclusivités sur Steam et l'Epic Games Store.
Comme nous l'évoquions récemment, le constructeur entend désormais réserver ses grandes productions solo développées en interne à l'écosystème PlayStation. God of War, Spider-Man ou encore The Last of Us avaient pourtant ouvert la voie à une stratégie plus ouverte, mais qui touche désormais à sa fin.
La fermeture de l'application PlayStation Plus sur PC ne constituera pas, à elle seule, un quelconque bouleversement stratégique. Elle vient toutefois ajouter une nouvelle pièce à une tendance qui se dessine depuis plusieurs mois, avec un Sony qui souhaite avant tout valoriser ses consoles et leurs exclusivités, plutôt que multiplier les passerelles avec un écosystème concurrent.
- Une PS5 plus compacte, plus légère
- Le repositionnement du bouton Eject
- Un SSD de 1 To (822 Go d’espace disponible au déballage)

articles.title: Noctua Introduces NT-CP1 Carbice Carbon Nanotube Thermal Pad for AM5
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Noctua Introduces NT-CP1 Carbice Carbon Nanotube Thermal Pad for AM5
Noctua today introduced the new NT-CP1 AM5/4 carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM5 and AM4 processors. Leveraging Carbice's novel, space-grade carbon nanotube technology, the NT-CP1 is a premium-quality, easy-to-apply thermal pad that offers superior long-term stability for peace of mind. While thermal pastes and most other thermal pads gradually lose performance over time due to pump-out, delamination, cracking and other degradation effects, Carbice pads keep improving their performance over the first few hundred to a few thousand thermal cycles. This is possible thanks to the pad's robust mechanics, phase-change polymer coating and carbon nanotubes that incrementally conform to surface microstructures, enhancing the heat transfer rate with time and thermal cycling. Once this initial activation phase is completed, the NT-CP1 maintains stable, maintenance-free performance for years and years. As such, it is ideal for everyone who seeks to rule out thermal issues due to degradation and never wants to bother with reapply paste again.
Unlike other carbon or graphite-based thermal pads that can be brittle, slippery and highly electrically conductive, Carbice pads are sturdy, safe and easy to install using a straightforward "peel, press, peel" process. The NT-CP1's aluminium backbone makes it surprisingly robust and easy to remove. The slightly tacky polymer coating helps to keep the pad in place once pressed onto the CPU and ensures that the contact surfaces are electrically non-conductive before usage unless the polymer layer is penetrated.Whereas graphite and graphene-based pads tend to have a high carbon footprint due to energy-intensive mining or high-temperature growth processing, the NT-CP1 is manufactured by Carbice Corporation in the United States out of recycled aluminium and waste carbon gas that's used to grow carbon nanotube forests in an energy-efficient, low-temperature process. The NT-CP1 pad can be recycled through standard aluminium recycling and offers a complete path to waste circularity.
"Carbice pads offer a unique combination of ultimate performance stability and convenient installation. This makes the NT-CP1 the perfect choice for everyone who's looking for a thermal pad that's super easy to apply and never needs to be replaced," said Roland Mossig, CEO of Noctua. "Carbice's carbon nanotube thermal pads were first built for spacecraft. Now, with Noctua, every PC builder can put that same technology in their system. Noctua has spent two decades earning the trust of builders who care about every detail, and they share our belief that great engineering should last. The NT-CP1 is better for your hardware and better for people and our planet, and we couldn't ask for a better partner to deliver it," said Baratunde Cola, CEO and founder of Carbice.
The AM5/4 version has been carefully fine-tuned and validated for optimal performance on AMD Ryzen CPUs and APUs. With its ultra-thin 90µm profile and precut 33x33mm size, it fits both AM5 and AM4 socket processors.
Overall, the NT-CP1 Carbice pad is an innovative premium choice for users looking for a clean, convenient and environmentally friendly thermal interface material solution with reliable long-term performance, space-grade dependability and zero maintenance.
Suggested retail price
The manufacturer's suggested retail price is EUR 24.95 / USD 24.95.

articles.title: Xbox y Take-Two firman un acuerdo por 10 años: GTA 6 será el primer beneficiado a pocos días de su lanzamiento
articles.text:
Xbox y Take-Two Interactive, propietaria de Rockstar Games, anunciaron una alianza estratégica que se extenderá durante los próximos diez años y que tendrá a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) como uno de sus primeros protagonistas.
El acuerdo permitirá que el esperado videojuego llegue a más usuarios mediante Xbox Cloud Gaming desde el 19 de noviembre, fecha prevista para su lanzamiento mundial, incluso en consolas de la generación anterior como Xbox One.
La noticia fue confirmada por Asha Sharma, presidenta de Xbox, quien comunicó el inicio de esta colaboración a través de sus redes sociales. La directiva también reveló que GTA 6 ya se convirtió en el videojuego con más reservas de toda la historia de Microsoft Store, aunque no proporcionó cifras sobre la cantidad de copias adquiridas anticipadamente.
Por ahora, ambas compañías no han revelado todos los detalles del acuerdo ni las iniciativas que desarrollarán durante la próxima década. Sin embargo, la primera consecuencia concreta será ampliar las posibilidades de acceso a los videojuegos de Rockstar mediante la infraestructura de juego en la nube de Microsoft.
GTA 6 llegará a Xbox One mediante el juego en la nube
Uno de los aspectos más llamativos de esta alianza es que permitirá jugar GTA 6 en Xbox One, una consola que pertenece a la generación anterior y que no recibirá una versión nativa del videojuego.
La posibilidad será habilitada mediante Xbox Cloud Gaming, el servicio que transmite los videojuegos desde servidores remotos hacia diferentes dispositivos. En lugar de ejecutar directamente el título, la plataforma procesa el contenido en sus servidores y envía la imagen al equipo del usuario a través de internet.
Esto significa que quienes todavía tengan una Xbox One podrán acceder a la nueva aventura de Rockstar sin necesidad de comprar una Xbox Series X o Xbox Series S. La experiencia dependerá de la calidad de la conexión a internet, ya que el videojuego se ejecutará mediante transmisión en línea.
El servicio también estará disponible para los propietarios de Xbox Series X y Series S. Sin embargo, Microsoft aclaró que la versión transmitida utilizará los ajustes gráficos de Xbox Series S, por lo que no ofrecerá la misma calidad visual que ejecutar GTA 6 directamente en una Xbox Series X.
Otro detalle importante es que el videojuego no estará incluido en Xbox Game Pass. Para utilizar esta modalidad, los jugadores tendrán que adquirir previamente una copia de GTA 6 y contar con acceso al servicio de juego en la nube.
GTA 5 y Red Dead Redemption 2 también llegarán a Xbox Cloud Gaming
La colaboración entre Microsoft y Take-Two no estará limitada al lanzamiento de GTA 6. Las compañías también confirmaron que otros videojuegos importantes de Rockstar Games se incorporarán a Xbox Cloud Gaming durante los próximos meses.
Entre ellos se encuentran Grand Theft Auto V y Red Dead Redemption 2, dos de las producciones más exitosas del estudio. Su llegada permitirá que los usuarios accedan a estos títulos mediante transmisión en la nube, sin depender exclusivamente de una consola capaz de ejecutarlos de manera local.
La incorporación de ambos videojuegos ampliará el catálogo disponible en la plataforma de Microsoft y permitirá que más jugadores disfruten de las producciones de Rockstar desde diferentes dispositivos compatibles.
Aunque no se han especificado las fechas exactas de disponibilidad, la compañía adelantó que estos títulos formarán parte de las próximas incorporaciones al servicio.
Una alianza que durará una década
El acuerdo entre Xbox y Take-Two representa una colaboración a largo plazo entre dos compañías con una presencia importante en la industria de los videojuegos.
Take-Two Interactive es propietaria de Rockstar Games, responsable de franquicias como Grand Theft Auto y Red Dead Redemption. También controla 2K, compañía detrás de series como NBA 2K y Borderlands, además de Zynga, especializada en videojuegos para dispositivos móviles.
La alianza podría abrir nuevas oportunidades para que Microsoft incorpore más producciones de estas empresas a sus servicios digitales y amplíe el alcance de sus plataformas.
Por ahora, no se han anunciado otros videojuegos que formen parte del acuerdo ni se conocen sus condiciones comerciales. Tampoco se ha confirmado si habrá beneficios adicionales para los suscriptores de Xbox Game Pass.
La primera prueba de esta colaboración llegará el 19 de noviembre, cuando GTA 6 debute en el mercado y pueda jugarse mediante Xbox Cloud Gaming. La posibilidad de acceder al título desde una Xbox One representa uno de los movimientos más importantes de Microsoft para ampliar el alcance de su servicio de juego en la nube.

articles.title: Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer speaks out against AI, says ‘machines can never be artists as they aren’t human’ — ‘The entire purpose of art is to be a human form of communication. Full stop’
articles.text:
‘AI is not an artist’ — Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer shares his stance on AI replacement in video games, says ‘Machines can never be artists as they aren’t human’
"I think as long as it’s a creative tool to get you going, it’s fine"
- Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall shares his stance on AI in video games
- Wall believes the tech shouldn't replace human creativity, and "as long as it’s a creative tool to get you going, it’s fine"
- He adds that "Machines can never be artists as they aren’t humans"
Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 composer Jack Wall has shared his stance on AI music and the technology being used as a replacement in video games.
It's hard to ignore how rampant artificial intelligence has become in everyday life. It's become controversial and, as many continue to object to the tech, an unwelcome part of the entertainment business, dramatically changing the gaming landscape.
As AI becomes increasingly popular, some studios have been called out for their egregious use of AI, and tech companies like Nvidia have taken advantage of it to push AI-enhanced upscaling technology.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, the original Mass Effect composer shared his opinion on AI — something that wasn't around 20 years ago during the creation of BioWare's iconic sci-fi series — and believes the tech shouldn't replace human creativity, but only be a "creative tool" to help.
"I think as long as it’s a creative tool to get you going, it’s fine," Wall said. "I’m not a fan of AI music. AI music is just copying what’s been done before. But if you use it as a tool, and you’re still making the creative decisions, I think it’s fine."
The composer was firm on his stance that AI can never replace the work of real people, adding, "AI is not an artist."
"Machines can never be artists as they aren’t human," he said. "The entire purpose of art is to be a human form of communication. Full stop."

"Music is not just a bunch of notes strung together," Graves told TechRadar Gaming.
