articles.title: Google erweitert Android Auto mit Gemini – doch die meisten Smartphones gehen leer aus
articles.text:
Android Auto: Warum Googles neue Gemini-Funktion die meisten Smartphones ausschließt
Google erweitert sein System Android Auto, das Inhalte eines gekoppelten Smartphones auf dem eingebauten Bildschirm im Fahrzeug darstellt, um sogenannte proaktive Vorschläge. Wie Karthik Thirumalai, Product Director für Android-KI, im Firmenblog mitteilt, basiert die Erweiterung auf der Programmsammlung Gemini Intelligence und setzt ein kompatibles Pixel-Smartphone voraus.
Im Unterschied zur bisherigen Sprachsteuerung wartet die Software im Fahrzeug dabei nicht mehr darauf, dass Autofahrer:innen einen Befehl einsprechen, sondern verknüpft im Hintergrund selbstständig Daten aus verschiedenen Anwendungen. Fragt beispielsweise ein Kontakt per Textnachricht nach dem Treffpunkt für einen Pilates-Kurs, sucht das System die Adresse aus der zugehörigen Bestätigungs-E-Mail in Gmail heraus und blendet auf dem Autodisplay eine Schaltfläche ein, um die Ortsangabe mit einem Fingertipp zu versenden.
Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto: Exklusivität für Pixel 10 und Pixel 11
Mit dem aktuellen November-Update schaltet der Hersteller die Programmsammlung Gemini Intelligence, die lokale Berechnungen der künstlichen Intelligenz (KI) auf dem Gerät mit Cloud-Verarbeitung kombiniert, erstmals für die Hauptmodelle der Pixel-10-Reihe frei. Damit beschränkt sich die angekündigte Funktion für Android Auto laut Googles Support-Dokumentation auf diese Smartphones sowie auf die bereits im Sommer eingeführte Pixel-11-Generation.
Ausgenommen davon sind das Mittelklasse-Modell Pixel 10a sowie ältere Baureihen wie das Pixel 9, die aufgrund der Hardware-Anforderungen von mindestens zwölf Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher und einem entsprechenden Hauptprozessor außen vor bleiben.
Wie Android Authority berichtet, seien zudem Smartphones anderer Hersteller von der Funktion in Android Auto ausgeschlossen, obwohl Gemini Intelligence grundsätzlich auch auf Samsungs Galaxy-S26-Reihe, dem Galaxy Z Fold8 und Z Flip8 sowie künftig auf dem Modell Signature 27 von Motorola laufe.
Unterschied zu Personal Intelligence und Zugriff auf persönliche Daten
Die nun angekündigte „Proaktive Unterstützung“ geht über die im Oktober für Android Auto eingeführte Funktion „Personal Intelligence“ hinaus, über die wir bereits berichteten. Während „Personal Intelligence“ eine Schnittstelle bildet, über die der Assistent auf ausdrückliche Sprachabfrage hin Informationen aus Diensten wie Google Kalender, Google Maps oder Google Fotos abruft, analysiert die proaktive Variante laufend eingehende Benachrichtigungen und Bildschirminhalte ohne vorherige Aufforderung.
Für diesen automatisierten Abgleich benötigt die Software weitreichende Zugriffsrechte auf private Kommunikationsdaten wie E-Mails, Standortinformationen und Kurznachrichten in Google Messages. Google stuft die Funktion daher als Opt-in-Verfahren ein, das volljährige Kontoinhaber:innen erst manuell in den Einstellungen der Gemini-App aktivieren müssen, und gibt an, die Daten in isolierten Bereichen zu verarbeiten, auf die weder das Unternehmen selbst noch Drittanbieter-Apps Zugriff hätten, solange ein Vorschlag nicht angetippt wird.
Verfügbarkeit in Deutschland und Neuerungen im November-Update
Einen konkreten Termin für die Auslieferung der proaktiven Vorschläge in Android Auto nennt Google bislang nicht, zudem greifen geografische und sprachliche Einschränkungen. Laut der Support-Dokumentation steht die zugrunde liegende „Proaktive Unterstützung“ derzeit ausschließlich in den USA, Kanada, Australien, Indien, Malaysia und Singapur auf Englisch sowie in Japan auf Japanisch zur Verfügung, während Europa insgesamt und die deutsche Sprache noch nicht unterstützt werden.
Unabhängig davon bringt das aktuelle November-Update in Verbindung mit der Betriebssystemversion Android 17 QPR2 – einem vierteljährlichen Wartungs- und Funktionsupdate – andere KI-Erweiterungen nach Deutschland. Wie 9to5Google berichtet, sind die KI-gestützten Benachrichtigungszusammenfassungen ab dem Pixel 9 nun auch in Deutschland freigeschaltet, während der automatische Benachrichtigungs-Organizer ab sofort die deutsche Sprache unterstützt.

articles.title: Without Jensen Huang, is it game over for GeForce?
articles.text:
THE AFTERMATH: Jensen Huang's resignation this morning ends Nvidia's 33-year founder era, but it doesn't end the story. There's a search for a successor with no obvious candidate, an espionage case now touching four governments, a congressional hearing, and a growing roster of people offering their own picks for who should run the world's most important AI chipmaker.
Nvidia moved quickly to project continuity. In an internal memo, longtime director Harvey Jones told employees he would serve as the company's first-ever board chair. Jones, a former Synopsys CEO, has sat on Nvidia's board since its founding in 1993. The fact that Nvidia never had a separate chair until today says a lot about how much authority sat with one person.
CFO Colette Kress, at Nvidia since 2013, will run the company on an interim basis while keeping her finance role. CNBC reports she is gathering the executive team at the Santa Clara HQ to talk leadership and continuity. Her first real test: Nvidia is set to report quarterly results in just a few days, on November 17.
Meanwhile, investors are not waiting and the immediate reaction has been that Nvidia shares opened down more than 13%, briefly dropping the company below a $4 trillion market cap, before partially recovering by midday. Nvidia is still on track for six straight weekly losses, its longest losing streak since 2012. Apple has reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company. Wall Street and everyone else is split on what comes next.
No succession plan
Bloomberg reports that Nvidia has hired an outside firm to find candidates, but replacing Huang won't be easy. For three decades, Huang combined deep technical knowledge with tight operational control, running the company with a famously flat structure and dozens of direct reports.
Kress has become the obvious continuity pick, with the expectation that she will hold the seat for about a year before an outsider takes over. Among insiders, the name that comes up most is Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's hyperscale and HPC business and is closely tied to CUDA's origins.
Ben Bajarin called him the most logical choice, though Bloomberg notes he lacks the operating experience typically expected of a CEO. Analysts have also floated chief scientist Bill Dally, CTO Michael Kagan, and 32-year veteran Jeff Fisher. Huang's children, Madison and Spencer, both hold management roles at the company, but even observers who mention them question whether either is ready.
The outside list is a who's who of chip leadership: Arm CEO and former Nvidia executive Rene Haas, Intel's Lip-Bu Tan, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and AMD's Lisa Su, who happens to be Huang's first cousin once removed and runs Nvidia's most credible rival. Some analysts have even suggested a co-CEO setup, pairing a technical leader with an operator.
President Trump has also got a favorite. He declared that only Tim Cook could fill Huang's shoes, adding: "A Legend replaces a Legend!"
Elon Musk, meanwhile, is recruiting. Hours before the resignation, while reports of a possible ouster were circulating, a user on X asked Musk to hire Huang. Musk replied: "That would be an honor." He also endorsed a post arguing Nvidia's board should wait for its investigation to conclude before acting.
Is it also game over for GeForce?
That list should worry anyone who buys graphics cards. Look closely and you'll notice most of those names built their careers in data centers, finance, mobile chips, or CPUs. None of them co-founded a company in 1993 to make 3D graphics for PC games.
Huang did, and for all of Nvidia's pivot to AI, he never fully let go of that. Even after rebranding Nvidia as an AI infrastructure company, he kept reminding audiences that GeForce is what brought CUDA into the world, and that the AI boom wouldn't exist without it. At GTC in March, he called the modern Nvidia "the house that GeForce made."
Nvidia's gaming business hit a record $16 billion in the company's last fiscal year, but it was still a rounding error next to the data center. Then this year, Nvidia stopped reporting gaming separately and folded it into a new "Edge Computing" bucket alongside workstations, consoles, robotics, cars, and telecom gear. In the most recent quarter, that entire group brought in $7.2 billion, versus $89 billion from the data center. That's a mere 7.5% of revenue for everything Nvidia sells outside a data center and the earnings release didn't mention GeForce or gaming once.
Under Huang, GeForce arguably survived in part on sentiment, the founder's attachment to the business that built the company.
Gamers have been feeling the shift for a couple of years now. As AI swallowed the world's memory supply, Nvidia reportedly cut GeForce production by as much as 40% in the first half of the year. Kress herself (now interim CEO) warned investors that supply constraints would weigh on gaming going forward. It was widely known that no new gaming GPUs would come out this year, which would be the first such gap in roughly three decades.
Under Huang, GeForce arguably survived in part on sentiment, the founder's attachment to the business that built the company. A successor without that history will look at the same spreadsheet and see a comparatively unattractive consumer business competing with data center chips for the same scarce memory and TSMC wafers. From there, the options range from benign neglect to a spin-off or outright sale.
Then again, GeForce is still the entry point to CUDA for many developers and students. Consumer and data center GPUs share architectures, so much of the R&D carries over.
Nvidia also supplies the chip inside Nintendo's Switch 2. Untangling all of that would be messy. A more realistic risk isn't a sale but a slow fade: fewer launches, longer gaps between generations, and graphics card pricing dictated by how much memory is left after the data center business has taken its share. (If the AI bubble goes bust, that's an entirely different conversation.)
Whoever takes the job, how much attention Nvidia gives GeForce over the next couple of years will be telling.
The spy story keeps getting stranger
The Wall Street Journal is reporting a most surreal detail about the whole spy saga (yet): Huang was introduced to Alice Huang by Kang Wei, a Chinese businessman and former star fund manager he'd known for about a decade. Kang was also Alice Huang's husband, according to people who know the couple.
Huang and Kang reportedly first crossed paths in the 2010s, when Kang's firm Shanghai Hexi was investing in video game companies and Nvidia was mostly a gaming chip business. For roughly two years, Kang appeared to accept his wife's relationship with the Nvidia CEO, at times joking to associates that she worked as Huang's assistant.
The Journal describes the couple as serial dealmakers who moved from games to pharmaceuticals to cloud computing. In 2023, they renamed a Singapore company Megaspeed International, with Alice Huang as a director. Using Alibaba as a promised anchor customer, Megaspeed secured access to chips as an Nvidia partner.
According to the WSJ's sources, Alice Huang and Kang Wei pitched investors on new data center projects, promising to triple their money in three years and expressing confidence they could get Nvidia chips into China.
People familiar with the matter say most of the servers went to Malaysian data centers serving Alibaba, but some were shipped into China. Megaspeed says it followed all export control rules, but the WSJ has sources who say the couple pitched investors on new data center projects, promising to triple their money in three years and expressing confidence they could get Nvidia chips into China.
The New York Times is also reporting today that Singapore's government has just disclosed it held Alice Huang's passport from June 2025 to February over potential false declarations tied to Megaspeed. She was eventually released for lack of evidence, given a stern warning, and banned from re-entering the country.
What happens now with the "central bank of AI"
Beyond Nvidia's own stock, the GPU maker became more than a chip supplier under Jensen: it is an investor, financier, and loan guarantor to a huge slice of the AI industry, with obligations CNBC estimates at around $400 billion.
To name a few such data points: shares of Nvidia-backed neoclouds dropped today, with CoreWeave down about 8%. Big commitments include the $12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition, which is under review, and a $10 billion share purchase tied to Anthropic's IPO next week.
But none of this changes Nvidia's product roadmap. Vera Rubin is shipping, demand remains strong, and while AMD stock has climbed ~30% in the last few days, there's no way AMD could magically absorb Nvidia's customers even if they all switched tomorrow.
AMD isn't the only alternative, either. Google is now selling its TPUs to outside customers like Anthropic and Meta instead of only renting them through its cloud, and Amazon has signed up Anthropic and OpenAI for gigawatts of Trainium chips. Intel remains the question mark. Nvidia even owns a stake in it after a $5 billion investment last year, and its CEO is on some analysts' list to run Nvidia.
For 33 years, Nvidia's succession plan was essentially Jensen Huang. It now needs a real one.

articles.title: Microsoft's Outlook email hit by new outage | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Microsoft said its Outlook email service is currently experiencing an outage, preventing both business and consumer users from accessing their inboxes.
The issue was initially flagged as affecting the U.S. and the Americas, and later expanded to affect “any region.”
Microsoft hasn’t given a specific cause, but said that it was providing updates in its admin center, which wasn’t reachable at the time of publication. In a post on X for users who can’t access the admin center, Microsoft said some of its infrastructure was experiencing “elevated load,” and that it was “redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load.”
In its latest update, Microsoft attributed this incident to “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” for reasons it did not explain. Microsoft said it continues to investigate the outage.
Microsoft says its video conferencing tool Teams, file sharing platform SharePoint, and its AI tool Copilot are also unavailable. The company says its Defender XDR security system is also affected by the outage.
Consumers are also unable to access their OneDrive storage, Office (for the web), and several other Microsoft services during the ongoing outage.
TechCrunch will reach out to Microsoft for comment, as soon as our own email service has resumed.
The company’s last major incident was in September, when a days-long outage hit Microsoft 365, its online productivity suite that includes Outlook. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.

articles.title: Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — possible projects could include Terafab, SpaceX’s planned GPU manufacturing, or Tesla’s AI accelerators
articles.text:
Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — possible projects could include SpaceX’s planned GPU manufacturing, Terafab, or Tesla’s AI accelerators
Jensen Huang still possesses valuable knowledge despite his departure from Nvidia.
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known. But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him, Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X. A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.”
Despite the scandals that Jensen is currently facing, he still has the engineering know-how, deep knowledge of the industry and its inner workings, plus multiple connections across the world, which would be extremely valuable for any company looking to break into the semiconductor industry.
This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025. Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028. Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032. Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap, and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future.
We still don’t know what Jensen Huang’s plans are, but even though he’s no longer a part of the Nvidia board and its leadership, Jensen and his wife, Lori, still jointly own approximately 800 million Nvidia shares through various trusts and LLCs, while Huang himself personally owns around 70 million Nvidia shares.
Aside from that, he still has an outstanding invitation from Congress to discuss Nvidia’s security protocols, which could turn into a subpoena if he snubs them, although we don’t know how his resignation would affect the closed-door meeting. There’s also a reported FBI investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive who was allegedly instrumental in the import of $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI GPUs into China and is suspected of working with China’s Ministry of State Security.
Jensen Huang is just the latest in the long list of executives who resigned or were ousted from their leadership position because of a relationship or an affair with a subordinate. This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019. Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF.
It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang. But if the former Nvidia chief ever decides to work for Musk on his Terafab project, then Jensen could put his effort and expertise into turning it into a formidable competitor to Nvidia.

articles.title: Sony déclare forfait sur le streaming PC et renvoie les abonnés PlayStation Plus vers ses consoles
articles.text:
Sony retirera l’application PlayStation Plus pour PC le 10 décembre, un mois après une annonce glissée cette semaine en toute fin du billet mensuel consacré aux nouveautés du catalogue de jeux. Lancée avec la refonte de l’abonnement en juin 2022, elle permettait aux membres Premium de jouer en streaming aux titres PS4 du catalogue et à une sélection de classiques depuis un ordinateur. Moins de 0,4 % des abonnés éligibles s’en servaient encore.
Lire aussi : Sony dévoile un nouveau PlayStation Portal, avec plus de mémoire
Une application que ses propres abonnés avaient désertée
Le chiffre vient de Sony lui-même, qui l’avance pour justifier le retrait au détour du billet dévoilant les ajouts de novembre au catalogue. Le constructeur préfère, selon ses propres mots, se « concentrer sur l’amélioration d’expériences de haute qualité qu’un plus grand nombre de membres souhaitent utiliser ». Les abonnés concernés seront prévenus individuellement d’ici l’échéance.
Cantonnée au streaming des jeux PS4 du catalogue et d’une partie des classiques, l’application ne proposait ni téléchargement ni chat de groupe, et réclamait une manette compatible. Elle restait au passage interdite aux moins de 18 ans, exigeait une connexion d’au moins 5 Mbit/s et privait les joueurs des extensions achetées pour leurs jeux. À son lancement, elle n’embarquait pas même de moteur de recherche, et une centaine de titres manquaient à l’appel par rapport aux consoles, quand d’autres refusaient de se lancer. Sa configuration requise officielle en était restée à Windows 8.1 ou 10.
La page d’assistance qui hébergeait le lien de téléchargement renvoie déjà une erreur 404. Rien ne change en revanche sur PS5 et PS4, ni pour le streaming depuis une console ou un PlayStation Portal, toujours compris dans le palier Premium : la fermeture ne concerne que l’ordinateur.
Lire aussi : Sony donne des nouvelles de la PS6, mais un obstacle de taille se profile
Le PC, une parenthèse que PlayStation referme
Le streaming sur ordinateur avait déjà changé de statut en juin 2022, à l’absorption de PS Now dans le PlayStation Plus actuel. L’accès PC s’était retrouvé réservé au palier Premium, facturé aujourd’hui 151,99 euros par an en France, un ticket d’entrée qui avait alors quasiment doublé pour cet usage.
Le retrait de l’application prolonge surtout le mouvement entamé en mars, quand Sony a annulé les futurs portages PC de ses jeux solo, six ans après avoir entrouvert cette porte. La mention « PlayStation Exclusive » vient d’ailleurs de refaire son apparition sur les productions maison, et les portages déjà publiés restent seuls en rayon, sans nouvelle conversion au programme. Pour profiter du catalogue, il faudra désormais une PS4, une PS5 ou un PlayStation Portal, la console portable dédiée au jeu à distance.

articles.title: Black Friday : notre sélection des 7 des meilleurs aspirateurs à saisir chez Roborock, Ecovacs ou Tineco
articles.text:
Le Black Friday Amazon fait chuter le prix de sept aspirateurs laveurs, balais et robots confondus, avec des remises qui atteignent 250 € sur plusieurs modèles sortis cette année. Roborock, Ecovacs ou encore Tineco, Amazon casse les prix des grandes marques.
Le Black Friday tombe officiellement le vendredi 27 novembre, mais Amazon n'a pas attendu cette date pour baisser le prix d'une bonne partie de son rayon entretien des sols, où les aspirateurs laveurs figurent parmi les produits les plus remisés. Entre aspirateurs balais laveur ou aspirateurs robots, vous trouverez forcément votre bonheur.
Les meilleurs offres aspirateurs à saisir pour le Black Friday Amazon
- Le Roborock F25 Steam SET à 338 € au lieu de 599 €
- Le Tineco Floor One S7 Stretch Steam à 329,99 € au lieu de 549,99 €
- Le Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Pro à 599,99 € au lieu de 849 €
- Le Dreame T16 Pro Heat-A à 479,99 € au lieu de 629 €
- Le Ecovacs Deebot T90 Max Pro Omni à 399 € au lieu de 599 €
- Le Dreame L50s Pro Ultra-A à 499 € au lieu de 749 €
- Le Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni Care Kit à 549 € au lieu de 799 €
Le Roborock F25 Steam fait passer la vapeur sous les 350 €
Dernier arrivé dans la gamme F25 de Roborock, le F25 Steam ajoute un mode vapeur à la recette des balais laveurs de la marque et avait obtenu la note de 8/10 lors de notre test. À 338 € au lieu de 599 €, soit 250 € de remise, il devient le balai vapeur le plus abordable de cette sélection, ce qui en fait le point d'entrée le plus logique pour qui veut essayer le nettoyage à la vapeur sans dépasser les 400 €.
- Une vapeur pour les taches séchées : annoncée à 180 °C, une température relevée en sortie de chaudière et non au contact du sol, elle ramollit les salissures incrustées avant le passage du rouleau.
- Une prise en main facilitée : l'aspiration de 25 000 Pa s'accompagne de roues motorisées et d'une tête capable de se coucher à 180° pour passer sous les meuble…
- À savoir : l'autonomie mesurée par la rédaction tombe à 21 minutes en mode vapeur, contre une cinquantaine de minutes en mode Auto, et la vapeur consomme beaucoup d'eau, ce qui oblige à remplir plus souvent le réservoir d'un litre.
Tineco Floor One S7 Stretch Steam : la vapeur qui file sous les meubles
Lancé à 699 € à l'automne 2025, le S7 Stretch Steam réunit la mise à plat du S7 Stretch et la vapeur du S7 Steam dans un même appareil, une combinaison qui lui avait valu un 8/10 dans nos colonnes. Avec 220 € de remise sur le prix de référence affiché par Amazon, il se négocie aujourd'hui à un peu plus de la moitié de son prix de lancement.
- Une vapeur stable : la technologie HyperSteam produit une vapeur à 160 °C, avec une température qui reste constante tout au long du nettoyage.
- Une mise à plat bien pensée : l'appareil se couche entièrement pour filer sous les lits et les canapés sans perdre ses 22 000 Pa d'aspiration, et sa brosse nettoie le long des bords.
- À savoir : en mode vapeur, l'autonomie retombe autour de 25 minutes en usage réel.
Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Pro : le haut de gamme vapeur repasse sous les 600 €
Le S9 Artist Steam Pro occupe le sommet de la gamme vapeur de Tineco, avec un design plus travaillé que celui des S7 et plusieurs fonctions absentes du reste de la sélection. À 599,99 € au lieu de 849 €, il perd 249 € et repasse juste sous la barre des 600 €.
- Un mode ReverseScrub pour les taches collées : la brosse inverse son sens de rotation à la demande pour frotter une zone précise, en complément d'une vapeur HyperSteam annoncée à 160 °C.
- Une conduite assistée : la technologie SmoothDrive propulse l'appareil dans toutes les directions, ce qui allège nettement la manipulation malgré le gabarit, et le nettoyage des bords se fait lui aussi sur trois côtés.
- À savoir : les 90 minutes d'autonomie annoncées concernent le mode silencieux, alors qu'il faut plutôt compter une demi-heure en vapeur.
Dreame T16 Pro Heat-A : l'eau chaude à 90 °C dans un balai
Sorti cet été à 629 €, le T16 Pro Heat profite d'une remise de 149 € dans sa version Heat-A, qui ne se distingue du modèle standard que par son coloris gris foncé et sa distribution sur Amazon. Clubic l'a testé et noté 7/10, en saluant notamment son aspiration et son travail le long des plinthes.
- Un profil très bas : avec seulement 9,85 cm d'épaisseur une fois couché à plat, il se glisse sous les meubles bas.
- L'eau chaude plutôt que la vapeur : le lavage à l'eau chauffée jusqu'à 90 °C s'appuie sur une aspiration de 30 000 Pa et sur une brosse extensible qui va chercher la saleté jusqu'aux plinthes, avec un réservoir d'eau propre généreux de 900 ml.
- À savoir : la vapeur reste réservée au T16 Pro Steam, l'autonomie passe d'environ 70 minutes en mode Éco à 22 minutes avec l'eau chaude.
Ecovacs Deebot T90 Max Pro Omni : 40 000 Pa d'aspiration pour moins de 400 €
Présenté à l'IFA en septembre, le T90 Max Pro Omni reprend l'essentiel de la gamme T90 d'Ecovacs à un tarif plus contenu, et passe ici à 399 € au lieu de 599 €. Avec 200 € de remise, c'est le robot le moins cher de cette sélection.
- Une aspiration de haut de gamme : les 40 000 Pa annoncés grâce au système BLAST s'accompagnent d'une brosse ZeroTangle 4.0 conçue pour empêcher les cheveux et les poils de s'enrouler.
- Un rouleau lavé à l'eau chaude : le rouleau OZMO Roller 3.0 se nettoie en continu pendant le passage, puis la station OMNI le lave à 100 °C et vide le bac à poussière, tandis que le système TruEdge 3.0 le décale pour longer les plinthes.
- À savoir : la détection d'obstacles se passe de caméra, ce qui la rend moins fine que celle du T90S Pro Omni pour repérer câbles et chaussettes.
Dreame L50s Pro Ultra-A : le robot qui enjambe les seuils passe sous les 500 €
Successeur du L40s Pro Ultra, le L50s Pro Ultra a été lancé au printemps à 749 € et perd ici 250 €, ce qui le ramène sous la barre des 500 €. Contrairement aux deux Ecovacs de la sélection, il nettoie avec deux serpillières rotatives plutôt qu'avec un rouleau, et compense par une aspiration Vormax de 30 000 Pa et une double brosse HyperStream qui limite l'emmêlement des cheveux.
- Un double bras flexible : la brosse latérale et l'une des serpillières s'étendent pour aller chercher la poussière dans les angles et le long des plinthes.
- Une station qui gère presque tout : les serpillières y sont lavées à l'eau chauffée jusqu'à 100 °C puis séchées à l'air chaud, la poussière est aspirée automatiquement dans un sac prévu pour une centaine de jours et le réservoir du robot se remplit seul.
- À savoir : le robot donne le meilleur de lui-même sur les sols durs, et sur les tapis à poils longs il faut retirer les serpillières à la main.
Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni Care Kit : le plus autonome des trois robots
Lancé fin septembre à 799 €, le T90S Pro Omni est le modèle le plus complet de la famille T90, et cette version Care Kit ajoute un rouleau de rechange, une brosse latérale et un flacon de 260 ml de solution nettoyante. À 549 €, soit 250 € de remise, il conserve les 40 000 Pa du T90 Max Pro Omni en y ajoutant ce qui manque à ce dernier.
- Une navigation plus aboutie : la reconnaissance d'obstacles AIVI 3D 4.0 associe lumière structurée et caméra RGB, et la transmission à quatre roues TruePass l'aide à franchir des seuils de 2,5 cm sans s'immobiliser.
- Une station encore plus autonome : le rouleau et le bac d'eau sale sont lavés à 100 °C puis séchés à l'air chaud, la solution nettoyante est dosée automatiquement et la recharge PowerBoost récupère 10 % de batterie en trois minutes pendant le lavage du rouleau.
- À savoir : les 150 € d'écart avec le T90 Max Pro Omni ne se traduisent pas par une aspiration plus forte, et ne se justifient que si la caméra, le franchissement de seuils et le dosage automatique comptent dans le logement à équiper.

articles.title: Canonicus Capital raises Rs 192 Cr in its first close of Special Situations Fund
articles.text:
Canonicus Capital raises Rs 192 Cr in its first close of Special Situations Fund
The firm will focus on deploying capital into selected opportunities across the National Capital Region (NCR), while continuing to build towards its Rs 500 crore target.
Investment platform Canonicus Capital has announced the first close of its Special Situations Fund at Rs 192 crore, against a target corpus of Rs 500 crore.
Launched in 2025, the Special Situations Fund builds on the work of Canonicus Capital's Fund I through which it had raised and deployed Rs 311 crore. Together with Fund I, the first close takes Canonicus Capital's cumulative fundraising across its two funds to Rs 503 crore.
In a statement, the firm had said it will focus on deploying capital into selected opportunities across the National Capital Region (NCR), while continuing to build towards its Rs 500 crore target.
The fund will focus on situations where disciplined capital allocation, strong governance and active execution can help unlock value.
The firm's international fundraising programme, which included roadshows across the Middle East and Singapore, was temporarily paused due to the West Asia conflict. As conditions improve, Canonicus Capital plans to resume its international investor outreach and build on the momentum of the fundraise.
“Raising commitments is only half the job. The Rs 192 crore first close gives us the flexibility to approach the next stage with discipline, and our focus now is deploying capital prudently and delivering returns for our investors. We are not passive capital providers; we are execution partners," Rajan Gupta, Managing Director, Canonicus Capital, said.
“NCR is a competitive market, with significant capital competing for a limited pool of quality projects. Yet several fundamentally sound businesses and projects remain overlooked due to governance gaps, capital constraints and execution challenges,” he added.

articles.title: Widespread Microsoft outage takes down Outlook, Teams and more
articles.text:
A major Microsoft outage has left several of the company’s apps out of service.
On Downdetector, more than 140,000 North American users reported issues with Outlook alone, with many other users noting difficulties with other Microsoft services like Teams and Copilot.
In a threaed on X (Twitter), Microsoft’s official support page confirmed Microsoft 365 service may be disrupted “in any region” and said it’s “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact.” The company didn’t provide a timeline for when the outages may be resolved, but in a subsequent post in the thread, it noted that the “elevated load isn’t driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure.”
We’ll update this story once we get further updates from Microsoft. For now, though, just know that you’re far from alone in having any issues with with Microsoft services right now.

articles.title: Apple boude le Black Friday, mais ses iPhone et MacBook reconditionnés sont déjà remisés chez Back Market — Frandroid
articles.text:
C’est presque une tradition. Chaque année, le Black Friday promet des prix cassés, et chaque année, Apple se tient à l’écart de la fête. La marque à la pomme ne baisse presque jamais ses tarifs (elle a même tendance à les augmenter), et les promotions des revendeurs portent généralement sur des stocks limités qui fondent en quelques heures.
Back Market, de son côté, n’a pas attendu le Black Friday pour baisser les prix. La plateforme spécialisée dans le reconditionné affiche déjà des remises sur une partie de son catalogue Apple, en plus de prix inférieurs à ceux du neuf :
iPhone 15 Pro reconditionné à 577 € : un Pro au prix de l’entrée de gamme
L’iPhone 15 Pro reconditionné de 256 Go est affiché à 577 euros sur Back Market au lieu de 597 euros, soit 20 euros de remise. De quoi profiter de tout ce qui distingue la gamme Pro des iPhone classiques, avec deux fois plus de stockage que la version de base.
Son châssis en titane l’allège, son écran ProMotion à 120 Hz rend le défilement plus fluide et son téléobjectif ×3 permet de cadrer serré sans perdre en détail. Équipé de la puce A17 Pro, il est compatible avec certaines fonctionnalités d’Apple Intelligence. C’est aussi la première série d’iPhone à intégrer un port USB-C en lieu et place du Lightning.
Ce modèle est vendu en état correct : la coque peut porter des traces d’usure visibles mais sans conséquence sur le fonctionnement. D’autres iPhone 15 Pro avec de meilleurs grades sont aussi disponibles pour quelques euros de plus.
MacBook Air M1 à 549 € : le silence, batterie neuve en prime
Le MacBook Air M1 (13 pouces, 8 Go de RAM, 256 Go) passe à 549 euros. Cette offre inclut surtout une batterie neuve, qui garantit une excellente autonomie.
La puce M1 de ce MacBook Air est le premier processeur de l’ère Apple Silicon sur Mac : elle n’a pas besoin de ventilateur pour fonctionner, même à plein régime. Elle consomme aussi très peu d’énergie, ce qui permet au MacBook de tenir une journée de travail sans recharge.
Cette configuration convient à la bureautique, à la navigation et à la retouche photo légère. Pour stocker des projets vidéo plus lourds, un SSD externe complète facilement ses 256 Go.
MacBook Pro 14 pouces M1 Pro à 983 € : l’écran XDR sous les 1 000 €
Pour les usages plus exigeants, le MacBook Pro 14 pouces équipé de la puce M1 Pro, de 16 Go de RAM et de 512 Go de stockage est affiché à 983 euros au lieu de 1 070 euros. Soit 108 euros de remise. Il est vendu en très bon état, avec une batterie neuve.
Son principal atout est l’écran Liquid Retina XDR. Sa dalle Mini LED monte jusqu’à 1 600 nits en HDR et grimpe jusqu’à 120 Hz grâce à la technologie ProMotion. Vous obtenez ainsi des contrastes plus profonds pour la retouche photo et une image fluide au quotidien. La connectique évite aussi d’avoir toujours un hub avec soi, puisqu’il compte un port HDMI, un lecteur de cartes SD, trois ports Thunderbolt 4 et la recharge MagSafe.
iPad 11 à 428 € : la tablette connectée partout
Lancé en 2025, l’iPad 11 en version Wi-Fi + 5G et 128 Go est affiché à 428 euros au lieu de 476,99 euros, soit près de 50 euros de remise. Avec une carte SIM ou une eSIM data, il peut se connecter à Internet sans passer par le partage de connexion d’un smartphone. Pratique dans le train ou en déplacement.
Son écran Liquid Retina de 11 pouces et sa puce A16 suffisent largement pour le streaming, la prise de notes ou les jeux. Compatible avec l’Apple Pencil (USB-C) et le clavier Magic Keyboard Folio, il peut aussi servir de poste de travail d’appoint.
Apple Watch Series 10 à 355 € : le titane à prix réduit
Dernier produit de la sélection, l’Apple Watch Series 10 en 46 mm, titane ardoise et GPS + Cellular, est affichée à 355 euros au lieu de 452,32 euros, soit près de 90 euros de remise.
Plus fine que les modèles précédents, la Series 10 adopte un écran grand-angle plus lisible de biais et bien pratique pour consulter l’heure d’un coup d’œil. Ici proposée en version Cellular, elle permet de passer des appels ou d’écouter de la musique sans iPhone à proximité, à condition de souscrire l’option auprès de votre opérateur.
Côté santé, il s’agit toujours de la montre connectée avec l’un des meilleurs suivis du marché. Elle propose notamment l’ECG, la détection des chutes et les notifications d’apnée du sommeil.
Les garanties Back Market
Tous les appareils sont reconditionnés par des professionnels sélectionnés par Back Market. Ils bénéficient d’une garantie commerciale de 12 mois et d’un retour gratuit sous 30 jours si le produit ne convient pas. En cas de panne dans les six mois suivant la livraison, le Remplacement Express de Back Market expédie un appareil identique sous trois jours ouvrés, avant même le renvoi de l’original.
Enfin, quel que soit le grade choisi (état correct, très bon état, parfait état ou Premium), Back Market garantit un appareil 100 % fonctionnel, seul l’aspect change.

articles.title: Fracasa la segunda negociación sobre vivienda en Valencia y provoca la retirada de la acampada
articles.text:
La acampada por la vivienda de Valencia termina hoy. Después de 40 días, sus integrantes ya están retirando las tiendas de la plaza del Ayuntamiento. El motivo inmediato es que la segunda mesa con las administraciones, que exigían como condición para irse, no salió adelante. Entre tanto dime y direte, esta es la secuencia completa de hechos y las versiones enfrentadas.
Cómo empezó. Como ya documentamos, el 3 de octubre hubo manifestaciones por la vivienda en unas 50 ciudades. En Valencia la marcha acabó con cargas policiales ante el Palau de les Arts, donde se celebraba un congreso inmobiliario. Esa misma tarde, parte de los manifestantes montó tiendas en la plaza del Ayuntamiento. La idea copiaba la acampada de Sol, activa desde el 26 de septiembre y que finalizó el 3 de noviembre.
Cuántos eran. Depende de quién cuente y de qué día, como pasa siempre: en Puerta del Sol algunos decían que había 200 personas y otros que 2000. Según se estima, el 12 de octubre había más de 400 tiendas. Cuatro días después, el portavoz municipal hablaba de más de 700. El 3 de noviembre, otra cuenta daba más de 600. En este particular no existe un censo común y conviene recordar que una tienda no equivale a una persona. Puede ser una pareja y hasta un grupo de amigos o familiares.
Qué pedían. Dos cosas: que Valencia se declare zona tensionada, para poder limitar los alquileres de una vez por todas. Por otro otro lado, una mesa para que se sentaran los portavoces de Ayuntamiento, Generalitat y Delegación del Gobierno. La alcaldesa, María José Catalá, remitió lo primero al Pleno municipal. La Delegación, con Pilar Bernabé y después con Roger Llanes, descartó desalojar. Llanes justificó que en Valencia las “dinámicas” eran distintas a las de Sol.
Cinco fechas clave:
- 5 de noviembre: primera mesa, de carácter técnico. Duró más de tres horas. Los acampados habían citado a la alcaldesa, al delegado y a la consellera de Vivienda. Acudieron perfiles técnicos.
- 9 de noviembre: la acampada anunció una desescalada progresiva: menos espacio y fuera las tiendas vacías. Quería dejar sitio a la pista de hielo, el tiovivo y el árbol de Navidad. Ese mismo día, Ayuntamiento y Subdelegación del Gobierno mantuvieron una reunión técnica en la que concluyeron que la continuidad de la protesta era incompatible con la seguridad ciudadana y con el montaje de las instalaciones navideñas. La conclusión se apoyaba en informes de la Policía Local.
- 10 de noviembre: los acampados dijeron haber cumplido su parte y exigieron una segunda mesa para el jueves. Catalá respondió que “ya es momento de darle fin”. Llanes no fijó fecha límite para marcharse, aunque aseguró que las condiciones para la retirada avanzaban “a pasos agigantados”, si bien sonó especialmente jactancioso.
- 11 de noviembre: y llegamos a la huelga general por la vivienda. En la Comunitat Valenciana, el seguimiento fue aproximadamente del 60% según los sindicatos y del 2,5% según la patronal. Esa tarde, la policía cargó junto a la plaza contra varios viandantes, al final de una marcha de la CGT, si bien no hubo incidentes graves.
- 12 de noviembre. La segunda mesa no se celebró, así que la acampada anunció la retirada y comenzó a desmontar las tiendas durante la mañana.
Dos versiones del mismo final. Los acampados dicen que Delegación les trasladó el miércoles que no podía reunirse con ellos y que debían irse “inmediatamente”. Lograron retrasarlo un día para recoger de forma ordenada. Según su portavoz, la alternativa era la fuerza: “o desacampamos o nos enfrentamos a un desalojo forzoso”. La Delegación niega haber dado plazo alguno.
Catalá lo ve de otro modo: recuperar la plaza es, dijo, una buena noticia, y no hay negociación con quien presiona por la fuerza. El Ayuntamiento ya programó la limpieza y la retirada del vallado (están ahora en ello, de hecho). Ayer se escuchaba a más de un manifestante preguntar que desde cuándo la campaña de Navidad es más relevante que escuchar los derechos de la ciudadanía.
Limpieza responsable. Además, los acampados quieren dejar la plaza como la encontraron y donar los materiales que todavía puedan aprovechar otras personas. Hoy terminarán de desalojar, limpiar el espacio y devolverlo a su estado anterior. En su comunicado insisten en que la seguridad de quienes han participado y la no violencia han sido prioridades durante los 40 días de protesta. Su mensaje de despedida, según elDiario.es, es: “Nos levantamos, pero no renunciamos a nada”.
¿Y ahora? Es obvio que Valencia se desmarcó de Madrid a principios de noviembre. Allí, Sol acabó con el desalojo de 334 personas y el traslado de la protesta a los barrios. Valencia aguantó otra semana y termina sin bomberos, pero también sin la mesa que pedía. Serán en las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre donde se hablará mediante el voto. Entretanto, el Gobierno ya ha sacado adelante su decreto de vivienda a través de la Diputación Permanente.

articles.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM
Developers want AI coding assistants with minimal setup. With a large language model (LLM) gateway and LiteLLM, they can quickly access foundation models (FMs) available on Amazon Bedrock while you gain visibility and usage control. Platform teams need to monitor latency and errors, finance teams need to attribute inference costs to teams and projects, and security teams need consistent access controls. An LLM gateway can help address these needs by providing a centrally managed access point to the models that power coding assistants.
In this post, we show how to build a self-service LLM gateway using Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles with LiteLLM running on AWS Fargate to abstract Amazon Bedrock behind an OpenAI-compatible API. With this pattern, developers can access foundation models through a single API with a dedicated key while you gain per-user cost controls and model performance observability. By the end, you will understand the pattern well enough to build your own version from the illustrative snippets and AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) constructs. This post uses Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku models for example purposes. For a list of models and availability by AWS Region, see Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock.
This LLM gateway pattern follows a straightforward request flow from the developer, through the LiteLLM layer, to Amazon Bedrock and the underlying FM. The following diagram illustrates the production topology behind that flow. For simplicity, we don’t cover the addition of Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, such as content filtering and grounding, but you would normally include appropriate responsible AI controls before deploying to production.
A developer’s OpenAI-compatible client reaches the LLM gateway through Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, and an Application Load Balancer (ALB). It authenticates to LiteLLM on Fargate with a per-user API key. Behind that, the request draws on Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) (PostgreSQL) for virtual-key and spend state. It also interacts with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey as a cache, and AWS Secrets Manager for secrets. LiteLLM then ultimately invokes Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles using a scoped AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) task role. Amazon CloudWatch captures requests per minute (RPM) and tokens per minute (TPM) metrics and the quota alarm.
The architecture consists of these core components:
- LiteLLM on AWS Fargate: LiteLLM provides a proxy that exposes an OpenAI-compatible API. We run it on an AWS Fargate task with target-tracking Auto Scaling on CPU utilization. Developers point their tools at this endpoint and don’t interact with Amazon Bedrock directly.
- Self-service portal: LiteLLM includes a lightweight portal for admin and developer self-service. This web app can integrate with your corporate single sign-on (SSO). Using the portal, operations engineers set the spend policy while developers self-provision API keys within those parameters.
- Persistent and cache storage: LiteLLM uses Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey for non-persistent response caching. It also coordinates rate-limiting across AWS Fargate tasks. A separate Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) database is the database of record for persistent state such as API key metadata and spend tracking.
- Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles: Each model (such as Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku) gets its own inference profile, which you manage using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). With this, you get per-model quota isolation and a clean abstraction layer between LiteLLM’s configuration and the model versioning of Amazon Bedrock.
- Langfuse: Open source LLM observability for prompt-level telemetry, latency tracking, and debugging. It complements the infrastructure-level metrics of Amazon CloudWatch with application-level insight.
By using an OpenAI-compatible protocol, developers can configure their tools, such as Claude Code, Continue, and Cursor, with a single base URL and API key. Developers then operate at a level above the Amazon Bedrock backend and can swap models, add fallbacks, or migrate model providers without touching developer configurations.
Prerequisites
You will need an AWS account, Amazon Bedrock model access, and appropriate IAM permissions to deploy this project. You will also need LiteLLM. The LiteLLM AI Gateway component is open source and suitable for a small pilot with some limitations. LiteLLM documents the AI Gateway as free for up to five users with a license required beyond that. LiteLLM Enterprise is a scalable, production-minded licensed version that includes the open source gateway plus single sign-on, audit logs, delegated admin roles, and support. While the free tier supports virtual keys, the self-service key issuance described in this post requires the Enterprise version.
End-to-end configuration: Left to right
We walk through each configuration layer from the developer’s machine to the foundation model.
Step 1: Developer IDE configuration (for example, Claude Code)
Developers configure their coding assistant to point to the LLM gateway. This is the only configuration a developer needs to make to their tool:
With that configuration, each developer gets their own API key from the self-service portal and drops it into their tool configuration.
Step 2: LiteLLM gateway configuration
Deploy LiteLLM to a container service following the LiteLLM documentation. In this example we are using AWS Fargate. This will include the portal, which you can open at http://localhost:4000/ui during local testing.
The LiteLLM gateway is where you will map and enforce model names to Amazon Bedrock inference profile ARNs with per-key spend limits:
Set on the Fargate task from AWS Secrets Manager:
Note: Don’t hardcode the master_key or database credentials in config.yaml. LiteLLM resolves os.environ/VAR_NAME references at load time, so set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and DATABASE_URL as environment variables on the Fargate task, sourced from AWS Secrets Manager. Set the Langfuse credentials the same way in Step 5.
When a developer calls claude-sonnet-4-20250514, for example, LiteLLM resolves it to the inference profile ARN. It then authenticates to Amazon Bedrock using the AWS Fargate task’s IAM role and streams the response back in OpenAI format.
Step 3: Bedrock inference profiles (CDK)
With Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles you can create named endpoints for specific models, so you get quota isolation and fine-grained IAM control.
Choosing cross-Region inference (CRIS): Geographic or Global
Amazon Bedrock CRIS avoids the overhead of implementing cross-Region request routing yourself. Other benefits include:
- Access to a broader pool of Regional capacity.
- Automatic routing of requests to a supported Region with available capacity.
- Broader model selection, because some models are available only through an inference profile.
For this proxy pattern, we recommend Global cross-Region inference when the selected models support it and organizational policies permit inference processing across supported AWS commercial Regions worldwide. Geographic cross-Region inference keeps processing within a defined geography. For example, a US inference profile routes requests only to supported US Regions. Global cross-Region inference provides access to a broader pool of Regional capacity with potential pricing benefits compared with Geographic cross-Region inference. You can verify model availability, applicable service quotas, and model-specific pricing through current AWS documentation and AWS pricing pages.
CDK construct
Important: For Global CRIS, the copyFrom ARN must reference the system-defined inference profile prefixed with global., not the foundation-model ARN directly. Using a foundation-model ARN creates a single-Region profile without cross-Region routing. Additionally, the IAM policy must include the resource ARNs the invocation actually touches: the application inference profile and the underlying foundation model in any Region it might route to (Region-wildcarded). Scoping only to the application-inference-profile ARN returns not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource: arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/... at invoke time. This is scoped least-privilege: it names the exact models in use, not bedrock:* or *.
Step 4: Bedrock invokes the foundation model
The inference profile handles model resolution and cross-Region routing transparently without additional configuration. When LiteLLM calls the inference profile ARN, Amazon Bedrock routes to available capacity across configured AWS Regions and returns the response.
Step 5: Langfuse observability
LiteLLM integrates with Langfuse through logging callbacks, providing visibility into model invocations without requiring changes to developer tool configurations. To enable the integration, merge the following entries into the existing litellm_settings block from the Step 2 configuration, preserving existing callback entries:
Configure the Langfuse public key, secret key, and deployment endpoint as environment variables on the Fargate task. Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager:
The endpoint must match the selected Langfuse Cloud region or self-hosted deployment. Choose the hosting option based on data governance and operational requirements. Before enabling prompt and response logging, review the content captured by the integration and configure appropriate redaction, retention, and access controls.
Langfuse traces can include prompts, responses, model parameters, token usage, and latency, depending on the integration and logging configuration. This information helps investigate unexpected model responses and complements the operational metrics collected in Amazon CloudWatch.
Implementing cost controls
Cost controls are an important dimension to a successful AI strategy. Without cost controls, heavy usage of extended thinking features can lead to unexpectedly high charges, which we observed in our early pilots.
The spend limits configured in Step 2 (max_budget: 250, budget_duration: 7d) enforce a rolling 7-day window per API key, provided per-model model_info costs are set (refer to the Step 2 note). When a user reaches their limit, LiteLLM returns an HTTP 429 code with a clear message explaining that their budget has been exceeded. There’s no silent degradation or surprise bill. Developers and engineering teams can check current spend and reset timing through any of the following:
- Daily spend: Query GET /user/daily/activity with a start_date and end_date range to get per-day metrics: spend, prompt tokens, completion tokens, and API requests, broken down by model, provider, and API key.
- Per user spend: Query GET /user/info?user_id=… for a summary of a user’s total spend and the spend on each of their associated API keys.
- Portal dashboard: The Admin UI (at https://<proxy-host>/ui) includes a Usage tab where developers and admins can browse spend by model, user, and tag without hitting the API directly.
These same endpoints are how your finance team gets per-user attribution without you building custom metering infrastructure. A scheduled job hitting /user/daily/activity or /global/spend/report is enough to feed a cost dashboard or chargeback report.
Developer self-service portal
The self-service portal also handles key lifecycle processes. Developers authenticate with your corporate SSO to generate a key bound to their identity, which they can later regenerate if the key is exposed or to match a rotation policy. Platform engineers configure the budget policy once for individual developers to autonomously operate within their constraints. Two things developers use the portal for directly:
- Key generation: On the Admin UI’s Virtual Keys page (https://<proxy-host>/ui), developers authenticated through SSO choose Generate Key to create their own key, bound to their identity.
- Rate limit visibility: Each /chat/completions response includes x-litellm-key-remaining-requests-{model} and x-litellm-key-remaining-tokens-{model} headers, so developers can see their remaining RPM and TPM headroom for that model directly in their tool’s response. This is distinct from the dollar-based spend tracking earlier in this post.
Monitoring and observability
For an LLM gateway, traditional metrics like latency percentiles can be misleading, especially with extended thinking models, where a single request can take several minutes. Instead, we focus on requests per minute (RPM) and tokens per minute (TPM) as primary signals. Here, Amazon CloudWatch can help you monitor and alarm for these signals with the following configuration.
Amazon CloudWatch alarms for quota management
Note that the alarm configuration alerts at 60–70 percent quota utilization rather than waiting for throttling. This provides lead time to scale Amazon Bedrock quotas before users experience degradation.
Emitting the metric: LiteLLM has no built-in callback that publishes a metric named TokensPerMinute to a LiteLLM/Gateway namespace, so the alarm needs a source. A small custom-logger callback that calls CloudWatch PutMetricData on each request does the job. Register it through litellm_settings.success_callback (which is additive), not callbacks. The callbacks list replaces LiteLLM’s internal logger list, which includes the built-in spend-tracking logger, and will silently disable budget enforcement.
Here’s a minimal version of that callback, using LiteLLM’s CustomLogger class:
For prompt-level debugging, we run Langfuse alongside CloudWatch. When a developer reports “the model gave a bad response,” you can use Langfuse to inspect the exact prompt, token counts, and model parameters. For compliance-sensitive environments, Amazon Bedrock’s native invocation logging to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) provides an immutable audit trail.
Lessons learned at scale
We deployed this pattern end-to-end on a fresh AWS account to confirm the sample snippets work. In our own deployment, we scaled this LLM gateway to several hundred developers and learned several lessons.
Operational lessons
The main findings from running at scale:
- Extended thinking changes everything about latency. Requests using Claude’s extended thinking can take several minutes or longer, depending on the thinking budget. If your load balancer has a 60-second idle timeout, those requests will fail silently. To address that, you can set load balancer idle timeouts to at least 900 seconds and configure LiteLLM’s request timeout accordingly (timeout: 900 in the Step 2 configuration earlier in this post).
- When throttled, back off and retry on the same model before initiating a fallback. Our initial instinct was to fall back from Sonnet to Haiku upon throttling. But this is suboptimal for coding assistants because changing models breaks the consistent behavior developers rely on. Instead, retry the same model with exponential backoff at the proxy level (max_retries: 3 in Step 2). When a request cannot be served after retries, surface the error clearly rather than returning an alternate model’s completions.
- Separate automation tool invocations from developer traffic. continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines and automated code review tools should call Amazon Bedrock directly with their own inference profiles and quotas. Mixing automation traffic with interactive developer traffic leads to unpredictable latency and hinders meaningful cost attribution.
- Start with Global CRIS from day one, if feasible. We initially used Geographic (US) CRIS but ultimately migrated our inference profiles when we reached Regional quota limits. For our use case, we didn’t have data residency constraints so we could use Global CRIS. Global CRIS routes requests across Regions to draw on a broader capacity pool, simplifying management at scale.
Deployment considerations
Two configuration mistakes are common and hard to notice until spend or connectivity breaks:
Configuring per-model costs is mandatory for enforcing budgets. The model_info block on each model isn’t optional if you want to track per-user cost controls. When model points at an Amazon Bedrock inference-profile ARN, LiteLLM can’t look up the ARN in its built-in pricing table. It instead records $0 per token, so the max_budget and 429 throttle enforcement silently don’t trigger. Spend remains at $0 no matter how many tokens flow. Fix this by setting input_cost_per_token and output_cost_per_token (or input_cost_per_million_tokens).
Database compared to cache: The database_url must be PostgreSQL. LiteLLM’s virtual keys (/key/generate), store_model_in_db, and spend tracking are Postgres-backed.
A handful of smaller deployment details rounded out our checklist:
- Global CRIS IAM needs the foundation-model resources, not only the app-inference-profile ARN. Otherwise, invocation is denied at runtime.
- Give the Fargate task enough memory. LiteLLM’s gateway image runs out of memory and is killed at 512 MB (exit 137) before it can pass a health check. About 2 GB is a safe floor.
- Override the container entryPoint. The official image’s entrypoint is litellm. If you render a config at startup with a shell script, set entryPoint: ['/bin/sh','-c'] or your script is passed as arguments to litellm.
- IAM role and security-group descriptions must be ASCII. Em-dashes and -> arrows are rejected by IAM and Amazon EC2.
- Confirm model availability in your account and Region. Model IDs and CRIS profiles change. Verify with aws bedrock list-inference-profiles (for example, we used claude-haiku-4-5 because claude-haiku-3-5 was not available).
Clean up
This post walks through the pattern with illustrative snippets rather than a single deployable stack, there’s no one-command teardown. But the architecture relies on several resources that continue to bill while they run. These include the AWS Fargate service, Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL), Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, and the Application Load Balancer, along with supporting Secrets Manager secrets, CloudWatch alarms, and Amazon Bedrock application inference profiles. When you finish testing, remove them to avoid ongoing charges.
If you deployed the full solution using the Guidance for Multi-Provider Generative AI Gateway on AWS, follow that solution’s cleanup instructions to remove everything it created. For AWS CDK, run cdk destroy. For AWS CloudFormation, delete the stack.
If you built the pattern yourself from the snippets in this post, remove each resource:
- AWS Fargate service and cluster: Delete the Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service to stop and drain the tasks, then delete the cluster.
- Application Load Balancer: Delete the ALB along with its listeners and target groups.
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL): Delete the database instance. Take a final snapshot first only if you need to retain API key and spend data.
- Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey: Delete the replication group or cluster. It holds only cache data, so no snapshot is needed.
- Amazon Bedrock application inference profiles: Delete the profiles created in Step 3, either by removing the AWS CDK construct or by running aws bedrock delete-inference-profile.
- AWS Secrets Manager secrets: Schedule deletion of the proxy’s secrets, such as the master key and database credentials.
- Amazon CloudWatch alarms and log groups: Delete the TPM alarm and any LiteLLM log groups.
Delete the AWS Fargate service and ALB before the Amazon RDS and ElastiCache endpoints they depend on, so running tasks don’t error against removed backends during teardown.
Conclusion
In this post, we detailed a pattern for an LLM gateway that abstracts the multi-model architecture of Amazon Bedrock to provide your teams with scalable and observable self-service access. Because Amazon Bedrock routes across models through a single interface without changing infrastructure, your developers get instant access to foundation models through familiar APIs. Cost governance, observability, and a single control plane go to your engineering and security teams while finance gets per-user attribution without you building a custom metering infrastructure.
Start by working through the pattern and snippets in this post to understand how the pieces fit together. The AWS CDK snippets cover the Amazon Bedrock application inference profile, its IAM policy, and the CloudWatch alarm. The surrounding AWS Fargate service, Amazon RDS, Amazon ElastiCache, ALB, and AWS Secrets Manager resources follow standard AWS CDK patterns and aren’t shown.
When you’re ready for a complete, deployable implementation, the Guidance for Multi-Provider Generative AI Gateway on AWS closely aligns with this pattern. You can find the guide on the AWS Solutions Library with the accompanying blog post and GitHub projects. While this post stepped through the same core pattern, it focused on Amazon Bedrock for developer coding assistants. The larger solution architecture adds multi-provider support, Amazon ECS or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Amazon CloudFront and AWS WAF options, and an admin UI.
Explore the components of this architecture with additional documentation for Amazon Bedrock Inference Profiles, LiteLLM gateway, AWS Fargate, and Langfuse.
Try this pattern in your organization. Start with a pilot team, validate the cost controls, and scale from there.

articles.title: Hatz AI raises $24M to help small businesses go AI-native through their MSPs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Hatz AI raises $24M to help small businesses go AI-native through their MSPs
Large enterprises have emerged as the foremost adopters of artificial intelligence technology, and it’s giving them an unfair advantage over their smaller competitors.
Looking to change that is a startup called Hatz AI Inc., which has just raised $24 million in early-stage funding to empower managed services providers with the tools they need to keep AI simple for the smaller fish.
Today’s Series A round was led by Nadia Partners and saw backing from Vestigo Ventures and The Private Shares Fund. It will help Hatz AI scale up an MSP network that already spans all 50 U.S. states, nine Canadian provinces and nine other countries.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Jimmy Hatzell told SiliconANGLE that he sees small and medium-sized businesses as the lifeblood of the global economy, and he worries that they’re quickly being left behind by the AI revolution.
The challenge is that most smaller firms don’t have the in-house experts, such as the programmers and data scientists, nor the large budgets required to integrate AI into their business operations properly. For many, it’s simply impossible for them to make sense of an assortment of different third-party AI tools, chatbots and autonomous agents and absorb the unpredictable compute costs. And even if they do, they’ll almost certainly struggle to keep those systems and their data secure, Hatzell said.
Rather than go it alone, Hatzell believes that small businesses should instead look to the MSPs that already run much of their information technology systems. Many companies use an MSP to manage their cloud environments, day-to-day operations and keep everything secure, so they’re the most obvious partner to help them adopt AI too.
“AI transformation is existential for small and medium-sized businesses, but technology alone won’t make a business AI-native,” he said. “These SMBs need help from people they trust.”
However, those MSPs also need help if they’re going to be able to deliver AI services to those customers, and that’s where Hatz AI comes in. The startup has built an all-in-one AI operating system specifically for MSPs to offer AI securely to their customers. It operates as a multitenant AI control plane that comes complete with governance guardrails, spend tracking and automated routing tools to leading frontier models, so MSPs can package AI services under their own labels.
Instead of offering piecemeal AI tools, Hatz AI provides MSPs with access to a centralized team of customizable AI agents and workflows that are tailored to real-world business functions. For instance, there are purpose-built agents for automating internal ticket triage and technical operations, operational process automation, marketing content generation, sales lead qualification, financial bookkeeping and other standard business workflows. Hatzell said MSPs can use Hatz AI to offer these services to SMBs with simple deployment options and enterprise-grade security.
Nadia Partners’ Josh Schertzer said he’s backing Hatz AI because MSPs are the most logical partners to help smaller companies get to grips with AI. “By focusing exclusively on powering MSPs rather than trying to sell directly to end users, Hatz AI has built a true dominance in channel-delivered AI,” he said. “It’s setting the standard for how small businesses will adopt agentic workflows and next-generation AI tools securely.”
“By giving MSPs full control over governance, spend and deployment, we’re making it possible for every small business to become AI native,” Hatzell explained. “This capital accelerates our mission to put practical and secure AI within reach of every SMB in the world.”
Hatz AI’s decision to work with MSPs has already paid off, with its active MSP partner base tripling over the last year and its revenue growing at an even faster clip. To date, the company has issued more than 15,000 AI builder certifications globally. In the same timeframe, Hatz AI has grown its internal team from just 14 employees to more than 60, forcing it to open a new office in New York City to accommodate them all.
Going forward, the startup will use the funds from today’s round to build out its proprietary model-routing engines and internal software factory infrastructure and hire more staff to grow its forward-deployed engineering and AI research teams, Hatzell said.

articles.title: Apex Neural Rendering Beats NVIDIA DLSS in Both Image Quality and Performance
articles.text:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
Apex Neural Rendering Beats NVIDIA DLSS in Both Image Quality and Performance
According to a company called Apex Compute, there is a new player in neural rendering. The company has developed Apex Neural Rendering, which reportedly offers higher quality and performance than NVIDIA's DLSS implementations. It includes three key components: frame generation (ANR FG), super resolution upscaling (ANR SR), and ray reconstruction denoising for ray tracing (ANR RR). Running frame generation on NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5090 at 4K, the ANR FG achieves a latency of 1.01 ms per generated frame at a 2x setting, while NVIDIA's DLSS Frame Generation records 1.26 ms. We are not sure which version of DLSS FG was tested, but we can assume it was the latest version.
Regarding memory consumption, ANR FG uses only 214 MB of GPU memory, while DLSS FG requires more than double that, at 562 MB. Reportedly, the ANR FG neural network weights fit within just 0.17 MB, which is incredibly efficient. Based on samples on the company's website, the image quality that ANR delivers matches DLSS and even surpasses it in some cases. Apex Compute also managed to get Hogwarts Legacy and The Last of Us Part II Remastered working, showing the difference compared to DLSS, resulting in frame generation with more visual fidelity. ANR FG is a beta injector built around OptiScaler, which works in any game offering NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. You can view the results below.Supported GPUs include all of NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 20 series and newer, as well as the GeForce GTX 16 series. On the AMD side, support starts from the Radeon RX 5000 series and extends to the Steam Deck. Intel's Arc A-series and B-series are also supported, and surprisingly, Apple's M1 and later are compatible as well. The operating systems tested and supported include the now end-of-life Windows 10, Windows 11, Linux, SteamOS with Proton, and macOS 26 or later. Benchmarks comparing quality, image noise, and more are showcased below.Finally, Apex Compute will open-source this ANR framework with its components soon, which will be available on GitHub.

articles.title: Descargar la APK de XUPER TV en Android abre la puerta a robo de contraseñas y publicidad invasiva
articles.text:
Descargar la APK de XUPER TV, antes conocida como Magis TV, puede exponer a los teléfonos Android al robo de contraseñas, la instalación de malware y la recepción de publicidad invasiva.
La aplicación se distribuye fuera de las tiendas oficiales y promete acceso gratuito a películas, series y transmisiones deportivas, un atractivo que puede llevar a los usuarios a ignorar advertencias de seguridad.
Según un análisis de ESET, este tipo de aplicaciones puede solicitar accesos que exceden las funciones esperables para un servicio streaming. Esas autorizaciones pueden abrir el acceso a archivos personales, facilitar la descarga de software adicional y permitir campañas de spam o engaños que buscan obtener datos sensibles.
Por qué una app descargada fuera de Google Play Store implica más riesgos
Las aplicaciones disponibles en Google Play Store atraviesan controles de seguridad y calidad antes de llegar al público. Las tiendas oficiales establecen filtros destinados a detectar comportamientos irregulares, código malicioso y prácticas que vulneran la privacidad de los usuarios.
Las APK descargadas desde sitios alternativos no pasan por esas revisiones. El archivo puede haber sido modificado antes de su publicación o incluir componentes ajenos al servicio de video. En esos casos, el usuario instala una aplicación cuya procedencia y funcionamiento real no puede verificar con facilidad.
Qué puede pasar con las contraseñas y los datos personales
Una aplicación streaming no oficial puede convertirse en una vía para obtener información almacenada en el teléfono o para observar cómo se usan otras apps.
Ese acceso puede exponer datos que luego ayuden a realizar fraudes, suplantaciones de identidad o intentos de ingreso a cuentas de correo, redes sociales y servicios bancarios.
El riesgo crece si el teléfono contiene capturas de pantalla, documentos, fotos, audios o archivos con información laboral y personal. Expertos advierten que las apps potencialmente no deseadas pueden funcionar como puerta de entrada para programas de espionaje, troyanos y otras herramientas orientadas al robo de datos.
Cómo una app para ver películas puede instalar software adicional
Entre los comportamientos detectados figura la capacidad de promover la instalación de otros paquetes en el dispositivo. En la práctica, esto puede presentarse como una actualización, un reproductor necesario para ver un partido o una supuesta mejora de rendimiento.
Ese mecanismo puede llevar al usuario a incorporar aplicaciones que no buscó ni conoce. Algunas pueden mostrar anuncios de forma persistente; otras pueden recopilar datos o modificar el funcionamiento del celular.
Una actualización legítima suele llegar desde una tienda oficial o desde el desarrollador identificado, no desde ventanas emergentes o enlaces externos.
Por qué la publicidad trae varios problemas para la seguridad del dispositivo
La posibilidad de enviar notificaciones permite que una aplicación llene la pantalla con avisos, promociones o mensajes que imitan alertas del sistema. Algunos de esos mensajes pueden redirigir a páginas que piden credenciales, datos de tarjetas o la descarga de otros archivos.
La publicidad invasiva no siempre apunta al robo inmediato de información, pero puede crear un espacio propicio para el engaño. Un aviso que aparenta provenir de una empresa conocida, del propio teléfono o de una plataforma streaming puede llevar a que el usuario entregue sus datos sin advertir el origen real del mensaje.
Qué consecuencias legales hay por usar estas plataformas
El uso de servicios que retransmiten películas, series o eventos deportivos sin autorización plantea riesgos legales. Los titulares de los derechos pueden reclamar el retiro de contenidos y los proveedores de internet pueden bloquear el acceso a dominios vinculados con esas transmisiones.
Las consecuencias dependen de la legislación de cada país y de la forma en que actúen los titulares de derechos. Más allá de ese aspecto, la descarga de aplicaciones como XUPER TV combina dos factores: acceso a material sin licencias verificables y exposición a malware que compromete la seguridad digital.
