articles.title: Corsair HX1000i Shift Crystal power supply review: 1000W Platinum efficiency with an eye-catching transparent aesthetic
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Built by CWT, the HX1000i Shift Crystal is a showpiece that backs its looks with real substance. Efficiency is excellent, regulation and ripple are tight, and the fanless window covers half of its rated output at room temperature. Taiwanese capacitors, a noisy hot run and a 200 mm long chassis are the compromises, while the ten-year warranty and iCUE LINK integration add genuine value.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent overall efficiency
- + Cybenetics Platinum certified
- + Tight voltage regulation
- + Low ripple
- + Fanless up to 500W
- + Striking transparent design
- + Integrated iCUE LINK hub
- + Per-pin 12V-2x6 protection
- + 10-year warranty
Reasons to avoid
- - Taiwanese capacitors
- - Long 200 mm chassis
- - Loud when hot
- - Needs side clearance
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Corsair needs very little introduction to anyone who has built a PC over the past two decades. Founded in California in 1994 as a manufacturer of memory modules, the company has since grown into one of the largest brands in the PC component and peripheral market, with a catalog that covers cases, cooling, keyboards, mice, streaming gear, and of course, power supplies. Corsair entered the PSU market in the second half of the 2000s and built its reputation there by choosing its OEM partners carefully rather than manufacturing in-house. Channel Well Technology (CWT) has been one of the most important of these partners, producing a large portion of the RMx and HXi units over the years. The HXi series in particular has long been Corsair's high-end, digitally monitored family, positioned just below the flagship AX models.
We take a closer look at the HX1000i Shift Crystal to see if it deserves a spot in our best power supplies list. The HX1000i Shift Crystal is a bit of an odd bird, and Corsair is clearly fine with that. First shown at Computex 2026 and launching on November 12th, it combines the side-mounted connector layout of the SHIFT models with the digital HXi platform, and then wraps everything in a chassis with clear polycarbonate panels on three sides, turning the internals of the PSU into a part of the build's aesthetics. Beneath the show, the platform is built by CWT. It holds a Cybenetics Platinum certification at both 115 VAC and 230 VAC, and it is fully compliant with the ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 design guides. It also integrates an iCUE LINK System Hub and Corsair's PinProtect+ per-pin current monitoring for the native 12V-2x6 connector. The 1000W model that we are reviewing today is rated to deliver its full power output continuously at ambient temperatures up to 50°C and comes with a ten-year warranty.
Specifications and Design
| Corsair HX1000i Shift Crystal Power specifications ( Rated @ 50 °C ) |  |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAIL | +3.3V | +5V | +12V | +5Vsb | -12V | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAX OUTPUT | 25A | 25A | 83.3A | 3A | 0A | 
| Row 1 - Cell 0 | 150W | 150W | 1000W | 15W | 0W | 
| TOTAL | 1000W | Row 2 - Cell 2 | Row 2 - Cell 3 | Row 2 - Cell 4 | Row 2 - Cell 5 | 
| AC INPUT | 100 - 240 VAC, 50 - 60 Hz | Row 3 - Cell 2 | Row 3 - Cell 3 | Row 3 - Cell 4 | Row 3 - Cell 5 | 
| MSRP | $ unknown | Row 4 - Cell 2 | Row 4 - Cell 3 | Row 4 - Cell 4 | Row 4 - Cell 5 | 
In the Box
The HX1000i Shift Crystal ships in a very large and sturdy black cardboard box, with a large render of the unit on the front that does a good job of showing off the transparent panels and the lit fan. The model name is printed in big yellow and white letters across the bottom half, while the badges in the top right corner - ATX 3.1 with PCIe 5.1 and 12V-2x6 support, the Cybenetics certifications, and the iCUE LINK logo- tell you most of what you need to know before even opening the package.
The bundle is rather spartan for a product of this class. Inside the box, we found the AC power cord, four mounting screws, a handful of black cable ties, and a leaflet with safety and compliance information. There are no Velcro straps, no cable combs beyond those already on the cables, and no other accessories of any kind. It is not a deal breaker by any means, but a premium unit like this that is focused on aesthetics could have been a little more generous in this department.
All of the cables are fully modular and black, with individually sleeved wires and low-profile cable combs. There is a 24-pin ATX cable, two 4+4-pin EPS cables, three PCIe cables carrying four 6+2-pin connectors in total, and a native 12V-2x6 cable rated for 600W, alongside two SATA and two Molex cables with four connectors each. Eight Molex connectors on a modern 1000W unit is extremely generous, frankly more than any reasonable build will ever need. Corsair also supplies two iCUE LINK cables of different lengths and a USB cable that connects the PSU's monitoring interface to the motherboard.
| Corsair HX1000i Shift Crystal |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Connector type | Hardwired | Modular | 
| ATX 24 Pin | - | 1 | 
| EPS 4+4 Pin | - | 2 | 
| EPS 8 Pin | - | - | 
| PCI-E 5.1 | - | 1 | 
| PCI-E 8 Pin | - | 4 | 
| SATA | - | 8 | 
| Molex | - | 8 | 
| Floppy | - | - | 
External Appearance
With dimensions of 150 x 86 x 200 mm, the HX1000i Shift Crystal is a long ATX unit, which is a non-issue if you are getting the matching Corsair 4500X case anyway. In any other case, you will need to check your case's specifications before buying one. The side-mounted SHIFT connectors also require some free space next to the PSU, as the cables plug into the side of the unit instead of its face, which is great for cases with a hidden PSU compartment but not suitable for every chassis. The design is unlike anything else on the market. The steel frame is black, with Y-shaped cutouts forming the fan grille and a debossed pattern of the same shape on the opposite panel, while three of the sides are clear polycarbonate panels that reveal the white fan frame, the bulk capacitors, the coils, and the white PCBs. With the RGB fan lit, the unit very much looks like a piece of display hardware rather than a power supply.
The rear of the unit is a little more conventional, with the AC receptacle, a rocker on/off switch marked with the "HX1000i SHIFT" logo, and a large perforated area with the same Y-shaped cutouts for the exhaust. The modular connector bay is on the side, behind the clear panel. The face opposite the AC receptacle hosts the white control PCB, also visible through its clear panel, with two iCUE LINK ports, a USB Type-C port, and a small port marked "TACH". The hexagonal specifications sticker is on the solid steel top side of the unit and is an envelope-type that can be closed to hide the text.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The CRYSTAL is fully compatible with Corsair's iCUE software, which can be used to monitor the PSU, adjust its fan speed, and switch the 12V overcurrent protection between single- and multi-rail modes. Corsair also integrated an iCUE LINK System Hub that, according to the company, supports up to 24 iCUE LINK devices without the need for a separate hub. The most interesting addition, however, is PinProtect+, Corsair's per-pin current monitoring for the 12V-2x6 connector. If the current on a pin exceeds a user-customizable threshold, the PSU cuts power to the connector, and the RGB fan lighting turns red to signal the fault. Given the history of melting connectors, this is a genuinely useful feature rather than marketing fluff. We can confirm that it is working as intended, as we tried pulling 20A from a single wire of the 12V-2x6 connector and the PSU shut down instantly.
Internal Design
Cooling is handled by a 140 mm Corsair NR140HL-RGB fan. Corsair calls it a magnetic dome bearing design, and in practice it is a rifle-bearing fan with a half-domed shaft magnet, rated at 0.55A on 12V. The fan is white with addressable lighting, which also doubles as the visual alarm for PinProtect+. It is a decent fan, and the magnetic shaft should help with longevity, but it is worth mentioning that the regular HX1000i SHIFT uses a fluid dynamic bearing fan, which we would normally consider the better choice for a premium unit.
The OEM behind the HX1000i Shift Crystal is Channel Well Technology (CWT), Corsair's long-time partner for its HXi units. Almost every part inside the unit has been relabeled as "Corsair", including the capacitors and the magnetic components, so the OEM is not obvious at a glance, but the Cybenetics report confirms it. The layout is extremely clean and obviously optimized for aesthetics, which also explains the excessive length of the chassis. The bridge rectifiers have their own heatsink, the APFC components sit on another large heatsink, and the primary switchers have their own heatsink as well, while the secondary side components are on a vertical PCB right after the main transformer. All heatsinks are of good size and quality.
The transient filtering stage has four Y capacitors, three X capacitors, and two filtering inductors. Two bridge rectifiers sharing a large heatsink feed the APFC stage, which relies on two Infineon 60R099P6 MOSFETs and two fully encased filtering coils. The APFC stage also includes two bulk capacitors, one Corsair 560 μF / 420 V capacitor and one Corsair 470 μF / 420 V capacitor, for a combined capacity of 1030 μF. According to the Cybenetics report, these capacitors are supplied by Elite, a relatively reputable Taiwanese manufacturer, and they are rated for 105°C. They are not capacitors that we frequently encounter in anything above mid-tier, though, and we feel they are not a great match for a premium unit.
The primary inversion stage uses two more Infineon 60R099P6 MOSFETs in a half-bridge LLC resonant topology. On the secondary side, ten Infineon 014N04LS MOSFETs handle the synchronous rectification of the 12V rail, and the minor rails are derived from DC-to-DC converters. All of the capacitors on the secondary side are rebranded as Corsair, with black and white sleeves that match the color scheme of the unit, and are also made by Elite. These are mostly good parts, but it is a bit ironic that Corsair advertises 105°C Japanese electrolytic capacitors for the regular HX1000i SHIFT, while the version built to show its capacitors off uses Taiwanese ones.
Cold Test Results (25°C Ambient)
Cold Test Results (25°C Ambient)
For the testing of PSUs, we are using high-precision electronic loads with a maximum power draw of 2700 Watts, a Rigol DS5042M 40 MHz oscilloscope, an Extech 380803 power analyzer, two high-precision UNI-T UT-325 digital thermometers, an Extech HD600 SPL meter, a self-designed hotbox, and various other bits and parts.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At 25°C ambient, the HX1000i Shift Crystal is a very efficient power supply. It averaged 92.1% at 230 VAC and 90.5% at 115 VAC across the nominal load range, with the efficiency peaking at 93.6% (230 VAC) and 92.2% (115 VAC) at around 40% load. The curve is relatively flat after that, with the unit still achieving 91% at 230 VAC and 88.5% at 115 VAC while delivering its full 1000W. The efficiency at very low loads is good as well, at just over 88% with a 50W load on 230 VAC. These figures are in line with the unit's Cybenetics Platinum certification at both input voltages. There is no 80 PLUS certification for this unit.
The acoustics at room temperature are very good. The fan stays completely off up to 50% load, so a typical gaming system with a powerful graphics card will rarely ever wake it up. Once it starts, the unit registers 31.6 dB(A) at 500W, and the fan ramps up very gently, staying around 33 dB(A) at 700W and below 37 dB(A) at 900W. Only at full load does the noise climb to about 39 dB(A), which is still a low figure for a 1000W unit. Thermal performance gives no reason for concern at all, with the primary and secondary heatsinks reaching just 55°C and 58°C respectively at full load.
Hot Test Results (~45°C Ambient)
Hot Test Results (~45°C Ambient)
Inside our hotbox, at roughly 45°C ambient and still within the unit's 50°C rating, the HX1000i Shift Crystal hardly lost any efficiency at all. It averaged 91.7% at 230 VAC and 90.1% at 115 VAC, a drop of just 0.4 percentage points compared to the cold test. The peak efficiency dropped to 93.3% and 91.9%, respectively, and the full-load efficiency to 90.6% and 88.1%. That is a very strong result that shows how well the platform tolerates high ambient temperatures.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The fan is the part that changes its behavior the most in the heat. It starts spinning a bit earlier, at about 400W, registering 32.2 dB(A), and the noise climbs relatively fast to about 36 dB(A) at 600W and 39.5 dB(A) at 700W. Beyond 800W, the fan profile becomes much more aggressive, with the unit reaching 45.7 dB(A) at 900W and 46.8 dB(A) at its maximum output. That is definitely loud, though it takes very adverse conditions to get there. Internal temperatures rose considerably, with the primary heatsink reaching 84°C and the secondary heatsink 89°C at full load, figures that are high but comfortably within what the platform can handle.
PSU Quality and Bottom Line
Power Supply Quality
Voltage regulation is very good. Across the 20% to 100% load range, the 12V rail deviated by 1%, from 12.10V down to 11.98V; the 5V rail by 1% as well; and the 3.3V rail by just 0.7%. These are not the sub-0.5% figures of the very best digital platforms on the market, but all of the rails are well controlled, and the 12V rail stays very close to its nominal voltage across the whole load range. The ripple suppression is excellent. The 12V rail peaked at 48 mV under maximum load and 44 mV during the 12V cross-load test, while the 5V and 3.3V rails both topped out at 26 mV. Compared to the ATX design limits of 120 mV and 50 mV, that leaves a margin of 60% on the 12V rail and about 48% on the minor rails, which is very comfortable headroom for a 1000W unit.
During our thorough assessment, we evaluate the essential protection features of every power supply unit we review, including Over Current Protection (OCP), Over Voltage Protection (OVP), Over Power Protection (OPP), and Short Circuit Protection (SCP).
All protection mechanisms were verified and triggered correctly during testing. With the unit hot, OCP tripped at 148% (37A) on the 3.3V rail, 144% (36A) on the 5V rail, and 132% (110A) on the 12V rail, with OPP shutting the unit down at 130% of its rated output, or 1300W. These thresholds are on the high side, especially for the minor rails, but they are not unusual for an ATX 3.1 unit.

Bottom Line
The HX1000i Shift Crystal is a power supply designed to be looked at, and that is not something we often get to say. Corsair took a CWT-built HXi platform, cleaned up its layout to the point that it can be shown off, and placed it behind three polycarbonate panels with an RGB fan on top. The result is unique, and it is backed by a genuinely modern feature set, with ATX 3.1 compliance, full iCUE support, an integrated iCUE LINK System Hub, and a native 12V-2x6 connector with PinProtect+ per-pin current monitoring. The latter is more than a bullet point on the box, as the unit shut down instantly when we pulled 20A from a single wire of the 12V-2x6 connector.
Most importantly, the looks did not come at the expense of performance. The efficiency is excellent, with averages of 92.1% at 230 VAC and 90.5% at 115 VAC, and it barely moved when we raised the ambient temperature to 45°C. Voltage regulation is tight on every rail, and the ripple suppression is excellent, leaving a large margin against the ATX limits. At room temperature, the fan does not even spin up before the load reaches 500W and it stays quiet all the way up to the maximum output.
The compromises are few, but some of them are hard to ignore on a unit like this. The capacitors are all made by Elite and rebranded as Corsair. Elite is a relatively reputable Taiwanese manufacturer, but its capacitors are not something we frequently encounter above the mid-tier, and they are not a great match for a premium unit when the regular HX1000i SHIFT advertises Japanese capacitors. The fan uses a rifle bearing with a magnetic shaft instead of a fluid dynamic bearing, and it becomes loud under heavy load in a hot environment. The bundle is also spartan for an aesthetics-focused premium product. Finally, the 200 mm long chassis and the side-mounted connectors mean that not every case will accommodate the unit, although most buyers are likely to pair it with Corsair's matching 4500X case anyway. On the bright side, the ten-year warranty covers the unit for a period that very few users will ever need, and it makes the component choices easier to accept.
At the time of this review, Corsair had not made the price of the HX1000i Shift Crystal public, which makes a definitive value judgment impossible. The regular HX1000i SHIFT is the obvious comparison, as it offers the same side connector layout, iCUE integration, and iCUE LINK hub for $339.99 at Corsair's own store, along with a fluid dynamic bearing fan and Japanese capacitors. Compared to other showy high-end units, such as the Asus ROG Thor 1000W Platinum II or the Lian Li Edge 1000, the CRYSTAL is the only one that actually puts its internals on display, and its Cybenetics Platinum efficiency and tight electrical performance mean that it does not need its looks to justify itself. If it arrives at a reasonable premium over the regular HX1000i SHIFT, it is an easy recommendation for anyone building a showcase system, and a well-performing 1000W unit for everyone else who simply likes how it looks, as long as they can live with its parts selection.

While he has an extensive and broad engineering education, Dr. Fylladitakis specializes in electrical and energy engineering, with numerous articles published in scientific journals, some contributing to novel cooling technologies and power electronics. He has been a hardware reviewer at AnandTech for nearly a decade. Outside of his professional pursuits, he enjoys immersing himself in a good philosophy book and unwinding through PC games.
- quorm Are Taiwanese capacitors really still inferior in 2026? Is it still hard to make a reliable capacitor? Seriously asking.Reply
- EmmFyll quorm said:Are Taiwanese capacitors really still inferior in 2026? Is it still hard to make a reliable capacitor? Seriously asking.
Not inherently, no. Some Taiwanese makers are very good, and plenty of “Japanese” capacitors are actually made in China or Southeast Asia anyway. Making a reliable electrolytic capacitor is still hard though. It comes down to foil purity, electrolyte chemistry, sealing, and keeping it all consistent from batch to batch. The top brands have the longest track record of doing that over many years. Elite is a decent manufacturer and I do not expect these capacitors to fail early. My criticism is about positioning: on a premium unit that literally shows its capacitors off, and when Corsair advertises Japanese capacitors on the cheaper regular HX1000i SHIFT, buyers can reasonably expect better. articles.title: AI misuse in policing is a warning for any organization handling sensitive evidence
articles.text:
AI misuse in policing is a warning for any organization handling sensitive evidence
Secure, governed AI protects evidential integrity in sensitive investigations
An investigation into the alleged misuse of AI at Derbyshire Constabulary, arriving alongside wider scrutiny of generative tools across UK policing, has raised an uncomfortable question that extends far beyond the force.
What happens when powerful technology enters any organization where sensitive information is used to support decisions that may later need to be explained and defended?
The answer is not to keep AI out of investigations, intelligence or other high-stakes work, but to deploy it in ways that can withstand scrutiny. Within secure, auditable systems, with clear boundaries and human oversight, AI tools can help organizations connect information, manage growing caseloads and identify important patterns while ensuring that every insight can be traced, explained and defended.
The risk arises when employees turn to general-purpose tools that were never designed to meet those evidential and security standards.
Co Founder and Chief Strategy Officer at Clue Software.
The pressures that make AI appealing to teams handling high quantities of sensitive data will be familiar across public and private sectors. Caseloads grow, data sits across disconnected teams of investigators, analysts, HR professionals, safeguarding leads, legal, security and senior decision-makers, and a tool that can condense lengthy case reports in seconds is difficult to ignore.
The trouble begins when that tool has never been approved and sits outside the security perimeter, leaving no record of what it was asked or what it returned. A potentially more serious risk is that, in its pursuit of brevity or its interpretation of the facts, it may omit or overlook information that is vital to an investigation. When guilt, innocence and ultimately lives are at stake, such omissions are unacceptable.
At that point, the risk reaches into evidential integrity, regulatory compliance and, in policing, the administration of justice.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This is a governance problem that can surface anywhere sensitive and high-consequence information is being interpreted, summarized or used to support high-stakes decisions. The more useful AI becomes, the more important it is to define the conditions under which it can be safely used.
Any organization using AI to handle this type of information needs a policy that states which tools are sanctioned, what they may be used for, and where human judgement remains non-negotiable. Where those boundaries are left vague, people will draw their own, usually under deadline pressure.
Where generalist AI falls short of evidential standards
Intelligence and investigations are built on provenance and auditability. Every conclusion should be traceable to its source, and every step should withstand challenge months or years later.
Most generalist AI tools were never designed to carry that burden. Feeding sensitive intelligence into a third-party platform raises immediate questions about security, compliance and data sovereignty. Once material leaves a controlled environment, an organization loses sight of where it is held, who can reach it and whether it is being retained for model training.
Then there is the question of accuracy. Generative systems are constantly improving, but there is still margin for error. For example, the most sophisticated models are achieving hallucination rates as low as 4.2%, down from 12.2% by previous versions. This demonstrates that these tools are becoming more reliable with maturity, but there still needs to be scrutiny.
AI generated outputs cannot be fully trusted at face value, they need to be rechecked and validated. While presented as fact, information can be delivered outside of appropriate context or can occasionally be hallucinated analysis. These can pass into a report before anyone thinks to test it.
When AI-generated material is wrong or impossible to verify, the consequences run through everything that follows. Weak evidence undermines prosecutions, delays safeguarding decisions and hands opportunities back to the people we are trying to disrupt. None of this makes the case for keeping AI out of the process. It makes the case for keeping the wrong kind out.
What purpose-built investigative AI does differently
There is a place for AI within intelligence and investigation operations, however. Specialist platforms approach its use with auditability and evidential continuity designed into the foundations rather than bolted on later. AI accelerates the parts of the job that consume time, connecting the dots without adding judgement.
It can flag when the same entity – such as an individual, bank account or company - appears across intelligence reports, transaction records and internal correspondence, presenting those connections for an officer to assess. Patterns can surface in minutes, rather than through weeks of manual cross-referencing, and the decision about what it means stays where it belongs.
These platforms also operate inside secure environments, giving organizations control over how sensitive material is stored and processed. Queries, outputs and decisions can all be documented, which makes accountability far easier to demonstrate at the moment it is questioned.
Governance decides whether AI holds up
Trust depends on how a result was reached, just as much as the result itself. As AI becomes embedded in casework, organizations will be asked to show that it was used fairly, proportionately, and properly supervised. Technical controls alone will not answer that.
A governance framework is needed to effectively assign responsibility for AI-assisted decisions, set out how outputs are validated, and ensure the people using these tools understand where the limits sit.
It should also be explicit about where AI has no role. Some activities, particularly those bearing on legal proceedings, safeguarding or an individual’s rights, are not appropriate for automated assistance at all. Drawing that line matters as much as the choice of platform.
Innovation only works when it can be defended
Recent scrutiny of policing does not weaken the case for AI in intelligence and investigation operations. It shows where the failures originate, which is in unmanaged and unauthorized use, rather than in the technology itself.
The organizations that get the most from it will be those that deploy it inside secure, auditable environments where every insight can be traced, explained and defended. Integrity is what allows innovation to survive contact with a courtroom or a public inquiry.

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China.
Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models.
Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community.
Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source, whatever happens next.
Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology.
Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development.
Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab.
Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem.
Earlier this year, Huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China.
The impetus for that letter was Washington’s debate over how the U.S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections.
That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons.
Without Huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes.
Huang’s exit could also strengthen the arguments of those in Washington who are arguing for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies, particularly as the scandal surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and alleged spy, puts renewed scrutiny on his efforts to loosen chip export controls.
Restrictions on open-weight models from China could kneecap competition for American companies, the most powerful of which have kept their models closed.
Still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project Huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy.
As some of Nvidia’s biggest customers, including Google and OpenAI, develop their own chips, Nvidia has an incentive to cultivate a much broader ecosystem of AI developers and customers.
More players training, fine-tuning, and running models mean more GPUs sold, and less dependence on a handful of frontier labs.
Huang may be gone, but Nvidia still needs an open AI ecosystem. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority.
TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment.
This article has been updated with information from an Nvidia employee.

articles.title: Nvidia-Chef tritt nach Affären zurück - vorläufige Nachfolgerin steht schon fest
articles.text:
Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang tritt nach Affären zurück – vorläufige Nachfolgerin steht schon fest
Der langjährige Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang ist nach Affären zurückgetreten. Den Posten übernimmt kommissarisch Finanzchefin Colette Kress, wie der Chip-Konzern mitteilte. In der Zwischenzeit solle intern und extern nach einer dauerhaften Besetzung gesucht werden. Der 63-jährige Huang wurde zu einem Aushängeschild des KI-Booms und führte Nvidia zu Rekordzahlen.
Huang hatte am Wochenende zugegeben, seine Ehefrau betrogen zu haben. Zuvor war in Medienberichten die Rede von einem engen Verhältnis zu einer Frau gewesen, die von US-Sicherheitskreisen verdächtigt werde, vom chinesischen Geheimdienst angeworben worden zu sein. Mitte der Woche folgten Berichte über eine weitere Affäre, diesmal mit einer Top-Managerin von Nvidia. Bei Verhältnissen von Chefs mit ihnen untergeordneten Managern greifen US-Verwaltungsräte gewöhnlich hart durch.
Gesicht des KI-Wandels
Die Chips von Nvidia, einer der wertvollsten Firmen der Welt, dominieren in Rechenzentren beim Training und dem Betrieb Künstlicher Intelligenz. Huang profilierte sich als Gesicht des KI-Wandels: Bei Nvidia-Konferenzen und anderen öffentlichen Auftritten predigt er unermüdlich die weltverändernde Rolle Künstlicher Intelligenz in allen Lebensbereichen.
Eine Krise von Nvidia könnte auch viel weitere Kreise ziehen: Ihre Milliardengewinne investiert die Firma aus Santa Clara im Silicon Valley zum Teil in die Unterstützung von KI-Start-ups, die damit wiederum Chips des Konzerns kaufen. Huang baute in den vergangenen Jahren zudem ein enges Verhältnis zu US-Präsident Donald Trump auf.
Huang wurde noch vor kurzem beim Innovationsgipfel der Bundesregierung der rote Teppich ausgerollt. Die Bundesregierung vereinbarte eine Zusammenarbeit mit Nvidia.
Zunächst Dementis
Im Fall der Affäre mit einer möglichen chinesischen Spionin hatten Nvidia – und auch Huang selbst – zunächst von ganz gewöhnlichen Kontakten zur Managerin eines Kundenunternehmens gesprochen. Erst nachdem die «Financial Times» von einer Liebesbeziehung berichtete, gab der Nvidia-Chef die Affäre zu.
Der Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat leitete daraufhin eine Untersuchung ein. Zunächst hatte es geheißen, das Gremium habe weiterhin Vertrauen in Huang und dessen Führungsmannschaft.
«Ich war meiner Frau untreu»
Huang bestätigte am Sonntag in einer E-Mail an die Nvidia-Beschäftigten, dass er eine Affäre gehabt habe. «Ich schulde meiner Familie und Euch allen eine Entschuldigung», schrieb er. «Ich war meiner Frau untreu.» Das Ehepaar ist seit gut 40 Jahren verheiratet.
In der Milliardärs-Rangliste des Finanzdienstes Bloomberg steht Huang aktuell auf dem 13. Platz mit einem geschätzten Vermögen von 145 Milliarden Dollar, das hauptsächlich aus Nvidia-Aktien besteht. In der E-Mail schrieb Huang, dass er hoffe, das Vertrauen der Familie mit der Zeit zurückzugewinnen. Eine Tochter und ein Sohn des Paars arbeiten ebenfalls bei Nvidia.
Huang ist für Chipverkäufe nach China
Zwischen Huang und der US-Regierung gab es immer wieder Differenzen über Beschränkungen für die Lieferung moderner KI-Chips nach China. Der Nvidia-Chef argumentiert, Verbote schadeten der Dominanz von Nvidia und damit auch der Vorreiter-Rolle der USA, weil sie die Entwicklung eigener Technologie in China beschleunigen würden. Die US-Regierung versucht dagegen seit Jahren, chinesische Fortschritte bei Künstlicher Intelligenz durch die Blockade der Lieferungen von Hochleistungschips unter anderem von Nvidia zu bremsen.
Die aus China stammende Frau, mit der Huang eine Affäre gehabt haben soll, arbeitete zeitweise für die Firma Megaspeed. Das Unternehmen war verdächtigt worden, eine Hülle zu sein, über die Nvidia-Chips nach China geschleust werden könnten.

articles.title: Google corrige d'urgence une 8e faille Chrome exploitée par des pirates, installez vite la mise à jour
articles.text:
Début de semaine, Google a déployé une nouvelle mise à jour de Chrome sur Windows, macOS et Linux. Celle-ci corrige neuf failles de sécurité dans le code du navigateur, dont une vulnérabilité zero day. Il s’agit d’une faille qui a été exploitée par des pirates avant que Google ne puisse réagir et lancer un correctif.
Dans son bulletin de sécurité, Google indique avoir pris « connaissance de l’existence » d’une tactique d’exploitation qui permet de lancer des attaques « dans la nature ». En clair, des cybercriminels se servent déjà de cette brèche pour attaquer des internautes.
À lire aussi : Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d’internautes pendant 10 ans
Une faille dans la mémoire de Chrome
La vulnérabilité se situe dans le composant de Chrome chargé de lire le XML, le format de fichier texte qui sert à ranger et échanger des informations entre logiciels. Google précise qu’il s’agit d’une faille de type « use after free », une erreur de gestion de la mémoire très fréquente dans les navigateurs. Concrètement, Chrome libère une zone de la mémoire, mais continue ensuite de s’en servir. Un attaquant peut alors en profiter pour glisser ses propres données dans la mémoire.
Pour exploiter cette faille, les pirates doivent mettre au point une page web piégée, taillée pour déclencher la cyberattaque sans que l’internaute ne se rende compte de rien. Google a jugé la faille de sévérité « élevée ». Comme d’habitude, Google ne donne pas beaucoup de détails sur les cyberattaques en cours, « tant que la majorité des utilisateurs n’aura pas installé le correctif ».
Dans la foulée, Google a aussi colmaté cinq autres failles de sévérité élevée. Les défaillances concernent le système de fichiers WebGL, le moteur d’affichage, le processeur graphique et V8, le moteur qui exécute le code JavaScript des sites web. Deux failles de sévérité moyenne, liées au processeur graphique, ont aussi été corrigées par Google.
À lire aussi : DeepSeek aurait réussi à contourner les défenses de Chrome en 12 heures
Une huitième faille zero day en 2026
C’est la huitième faille zero day corrigée dans Chrome depuis le début de l’année 2026. La première, découverte en février, touchait la gestion des polices d’écriture. En mars, le géant a colmaté deux brèches dans Skia, la bibliothèque graphique du navigateur, et dans le moteur V8.
Une faille dans WebGPU a suivi en avril, puis une nouvelle brèche de V8 en juin. En septembre, Google a même dû corriger deux autres failles zero day dans le moteur V8, à quelques jours d’intervalle. Avec cette nouvelle brèche, Google a déjà corrigé autant de failles exploitées par des hackers en 2026 que l’an dernier.
Mettez vite à jour Google Chrome
Pour vous protéger des pirates, il est vivement conseillé d’installer la mise à jour 157.0.8103.50 ou .51 sur Windows et macOS, et 157.0.8103.50 sur Linux, au plus vite. Pour l’installer, cliquez sur les trois points en haut à droite de Chrome, puis allez dans « Aide » puis dans « À propos de Google Chrome ». Le navigateur télécharge alors tout seul la dernière version disponible. Cliquez ensuite sur « Relancer » pour installer les correctifs.

articles.title: Après les frigos des supermarchés, l’Europe s'inquiète des cyberattaques contre « les appareils ménagers »
articles.text:
En réaction aux cyberattaques visant les frigos de supermarchés en Europe, Juhan Lepassaar, directeur exécutif de l’Enisa, l’agence européenne de cybersécurité, tire la sonnette d’alarme. Selon lui, les appareils ménagers qu’on trouve dans les foyers risquent de se retrouver dans le viseur des cybercriminels.
« Aujourd’hui c’étaient les frigos, demain ce pourrait être les routeurs, et après-demain les appareils ménagers domestiques, et ainsi de suite », explique Juhan Lepassaar dans un entretien accordé à l’AFP.
Désormais connectés à Internet, les lave-linges, les fours, les aspirateurs robots ou les thermostats sont potentiellement exposés à des tentatives de prise de contrôle. Chaque service dont « vous dépendez en tant que citoyen, en tant qu’être humain, comporte une couche dans laquelle intervient un élément numérique, un morceau de code qui, s’il n’est pas protégé, peut être piraté », analyse le directeur exécutif de l’Enisa.
Quelques jours plus tôt, Christophe Bianco, responsable cyber chez Thales, abondait dans le même sens lors d’un point presse. Comme nous l’expliquions déjà en octobre en marge de la cyberattaque nationale, les frigos ne sont que « la partie émergée d’un iceberg ».
« Chez moi, j’ai un robot tondeur qui est connecté. Tous ces équipements qui peuplent de plus en plus nos environnements, dès qu’ils sont connectés, représentent une extension du périmètre à surveiller. Malheureusement, tous ne sont pas passés à travers une activité qui a permis de vérifier leur niveau de sécurité », souligne l’expert de Thales.
Des services essentiels en danger
Pour le responsable de l’Enisa, des cyberattaques pourraient un jour paralyser des services essentiels, comme « l’arrivée des policiers, l’intervention des pompiers, le fonctionnement de l’hôpital, le transport qui vous emmène du point A au point B […] ». Si ces services clés « ne fonctionnent pas, nous subirons un impact immédiat ».
En France, les autorités attribuent officiellement les cyberattaques à Shahid Kaveh, une unité cyber des Gardiens de la Révolution iraniens. Interrogé par l’AFP, Juhan Lepassaar s’est refusé à commenter cette attribution. Le patron de l’Enisa souligne toutefois que l’Europe est dans le viseur de plusieurs puissances étrangères.
« Que ce soit sur la Chine, l’Iran, la République populaire de Corée du Nord, il existe de nombreux acteurs alignés sur des États qui ciblent l’Europe, les entreprises européennes et les intérêts européens », estime le dirigeant.
Outre-Atlantique, le FBI alerte sur des « systèmes ciblés dans le monde entier ». Selon la police fédérale américaine, les cyberattaques ne se limitent pas aux frontières de l’Europe, et visent « les systèmes de réfrigération industrielle et de surveillance de la chaîne du froid » à travers le globe.
À lire aussi : « Une partie » de l’argent récupérée – le Crédit Mutuel Arkéa limite la casse après la cyberattaque
La « cybersécurité n’est pas bon marché »
Pour limiter les risques d’attaque, l’Europe mise sur le Cyber Resilience Act, un cadre qui impose des obligations de sécurité aux fabricants d’objets connectés, en vigueur dès l’année prochaine. Pour Juhan Lepassaar, « tous les incidents peuvent être évités », mais « la question est de savoir si nous sommes prêts à investir pour cela ». La « cybersécurité n’est pas bon marché », résume le responsable.

articles.title: OpenAI anunció el fin de los modos de voz Advanced y Standard de ChatGPT
articles.text:
OpenAI anunció que retirará los modos de voz Advanced y Standard de ChatGPT el 11 de diciembre de 2026 y los sustituirá por GPT-Live, su sistema de conversación por voz más reciente.
La empresa liderada por Sam Altman busca concentrar el desarrollo de estas funciones en un único modelo después de que el uso de la voz casi se duplicara desde julio de 2026.
Los usuarios recibirán una notificación sobre el cambio en noviembre de 2026. Durante el período de transición podrán continuar con las opciones anteriores, pero luego dejarán de aparecer en el selector ubicado en Ajustes > Voz.
Quienes hubiesen elegido alguno de los dos modos retirados pasarán automáticamente a GPT-Live. Las conversaciones mantenidas con esas alternativas permanecerán guardadas en el historial de ChatGPT y podrán continuarse por texto o mediante la nueva modalidad de audio.
Qué novedades trae el GPT-Live en la interfaz de ChatGPT
GPT-Live funciona con un sistema dúplex completo, capaz de escuchar y hablar de manera simultánea. Esto le permite dar señales de atención durante el diálogo, con expresiones como “mhmm” o “sí”, intervenir en intercambios rápidos o permanecer en silencio cuando la persona necesita tiempo para pensar.
Además, el modelo puede derivar preguntas complejas o tareas que requieren mayor atención a los sistemas de texto de la compañía. Mientras esas tareas se procesan en segundo plano, la conversación de voz puede mantenerse activa.
La versión Advanced utilizaba el modelo de voz anterior de OpenAI, que procesaba y generaba audio de forma nativa. Sin embargo, debía esperar a que el usuario terminara de hablar antes de responder, una limitación que volvía la interacción más rígida y repetitiva.
El modo Standard combinaba tres componentes: un sistema de conversión de voz a texto para transcribir lo dicho, un modelo de lenguaje para elaborar la respuesta y una tecnología de texto a voz para reproducirla. Ese esquema permitió el funcionamiento original de ChatGPT Voice, aunque generaba respuestas más lentas y podía perder información tanto en audio como en texto.
Cuáles funciones se conservarán de la tecnología anterior
La compañía incorporará a GPT-Live aprendizajes obtenidos del uso de los dos sistemas que serán eliminados. Las áreas previstas para mejoras incluyen la profundidad y el detalle de las respuestas, la continuidad de las conversaciones y una personalización más precisa.
OpenAI reconoció que algunos usuarios están habituados al estilo de interacción de los modelos anteriores y que el cambio puede resultar complejo. Por ese motivo, su Centro de Ayuda incluye orientaciones para adaptarse a las transiciones entre modelos.
Asimismo, los GPT personalizados conservarán la voz Advanced hasta que esa tecnología deje de estar disponible. La modificación afectará a quienes usen asistentes configurados para tareas específicas dentro de ChatGPT.
La reproducción de video en directo y la función para compartir pantalla seguirán operando con la tecnología de voz Advanced hasta que GPT-Live incorpore esas capacidades.
Qué impacto tendrá la unificación de los modelos de voz en ChatGPT
La decisión permite a OpenAI concentrar las actualizaciones, las correcciones y las nuevas funciones en una sola arquitectura. Hasta ahora, la coexistencia de varias opciones obligaba a mantener sistemas con capacidades y límites distintos dentro de la aplicación.
Para los usuarios, el resultado será una experiencia más homogénea entre dispositivos y tipos de conversación. Reducirá la necesidad de elegir una modalidad antes de iniciar un diálogo, aunque eliminará la posibilidad de optar por un sistema con un comportamiento específico según las preferencias de cada persona.
La centralización facilitará que OpenAI mida el rendimiento de la voz en situaciones reales y ajuste sus respuestas con mayor rapidez. La empresa podrá identificar fallas recurrentes sin dividir los datos entre modelos distintos.

articles.title: Google lanza Gemini 4 Hydrogen y lo integra con su buscador para dar respuestas más completas e inteligentes
articles.text:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen es la última adición a la familia de modelos de lenguaje insignia de Google. La firma de Mountain View lanzó su nueva IA este miércoles, sumándola a Gemini 4 Argon y Carbon, que debutaron en octubre.
De acuerdo con Google, Gemini 4 Hydrogen no está pensado para tareas que requieran de razonamiento profundo y extendido como las otras dos variantes. Por el contrario, la inteligencia artificial fue especialmente preparada para la ejecución rápida de tareas en flujos de trabajo destinados a agentes.
Más allá de los benchmarks y las capacidades que desbloquea Gemini 4 Hydrogen, la novedad realmente interesante que trae este modelo es su integración con el buscador de Google. Esto le permite a la plataforma brindar respuestas más rápidas e inteligentes, ampliando drásticamente la experiencia de búsqueda actual.
Los de Mountain View afirman que la llegada de Gemini 4 Hydrogen implica la actualización más importante que ha recibido el buscador web en materia de modelos de IA. El objetivo de la compañía no solo es enriquecer el contenido de las respuestas, sino también mejorar la comprensión de matices, intenciones y modismos incorporados en el lenguaje natural de los usuarios.
Gemini 4 Hydrogen ahora impulsa al buscador de Google
Entre las mejoras que llegan al buscador de Google de la mano de Gemini 4 Hydrogen, destaca la habilidad de la IA de entender consultas complejas o directamente mal escritas. Esto se debe a que el modelo de lenguaje puede detectar más fácil qué es lo que quiere decir el usuario, incluso aunque la pregunta tenga varias partes pero no esté dividida de forma apropiada o tenga errores de ortografía muy severos.
Por supuesto que esto es un arma de doble filo. Después de todo, Google le va a estar facilitando la vida a ese amigo o pariente que escribe con faltas ortográficas horribles porque sostiene que así "se entiende igual". Fuera de eso, puede ser una salvación si cometes errores involuntarios durante una búsqueda rápida.
Gemini 4 Hydrogen también promete mejoras en la ramificación de consultas, así como en el ofrecimiento de enlaces más útiles. Por otra parte, la inteligencia artificial incorpora más elementos gráficos en los resultados del buscador de Google. Esto no solo implica la inserción de imágenes o enlaces con vistas previas de multimedia, sino también de mapas, gráficos, tablas y más.
La integración de Gemini 4 Hydrogen con el buscador de Google se está desplegando desde hoy a los usuarios de todo el mundo. Para acceder al nuevo modelo cuando realices una búsqueda, tienes que pulsar el botón "+" que aparece bajo el recuadro de búsqueda y seleccionarlo desde allí. Si todavía no lo ves, es posible que se habilite en las próximas horas y/o días.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns as CEO in the wake of multiple affairs, Chinese spy allegations — Colette Kress appointed Interim CEO, board conducting search for permanent replacement
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in the wake of multiple affairs, Chinese spy allegations — Colette Kress appointed Interim CEO, board conducting search for permanent replacement
That didn’t take long
Nvidia’s board of directors has confirmed today that Jensen Huang has resigned as the company's CEO. The news follows revelations that Huang had been involved in not one but two extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and another with his direct report, Nvidia’s VP of health care, Kimberly Powell.
"NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."
In recent weeks, stories have come to light alleging that Huang was involved in an overly familiar relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect may be a Chinese intelligence asset. It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigation for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China.
Nvidia shares plunged more than 10 percent in early market trading following the news, and are now down more than 23% in the last month.
Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology. Separately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang’s entanglement may be a matter of national security, given his role in the global AI revolution.
Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft, among others.
Just a couple of days later, a second bombshell report emerged claiming that Jensen Huang was also romantically involved with Powell, one of his direct reports at the company. Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC. Security allegedly sequestered a bystander who filmed the interaction on camera and made the person an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

Nvidia also announced that Harvey C. Jones will serve as the company's first-ever Chair of the Board; he has previously served as CEO and Executive Chairman of Synopsys.

articles.title: Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime
AI agents have moved past one-off prompts. They now run multi-step workloads for hours at a time. The length of task that frontier agents can complete on their own doubles about every four months (METR), and 40 percent of large enterprises are scaling AI agents, up from 27 percent a year ago (McKinsey). As agents run longer and with more autonomy, the focus shifts from what agents can do to how securely, reliably, and economically they can operate at scale. Agents do more than traditional software: they execute code, navigate browsers, access sensitive data, and act on behalf of users. These capabilities introduce new security and infrastructure demands, making strong isolation essential for production deployments.
Every agent session needs a secure, isolated environment. But delivering that isolation at scale introduces a fundamental challenge: balancing performance, cost, and efficiency. Pre-provisioned environments consume resources even when idle, driving up costs. On-demand environments reduce wasted capacity but introduce cold-start latency, delaying agent execution. Neither approach scales efficiently without trade-offs. As organizations move from deploying a handful of agents to running thousands of concurrent sessions, building and managing custom sandboxes becomes increasingly complex, expensive, and unpredictable.
The challenge is evident. Only 15 percent of organizations have scaled orchestrated, multi-agent systems, and 70 percent say they can’t yet trust and govern their agents (Deloitte). Scaling agents shouldn’t mean choosing between security, speed, and cost. The next generation of agent infrastructure must deliver strong isolation with fast startup times, elastic scaling, and usage-based economics. Because as AI agents move into production, secure execution shouldn’t be the bottleneck. It should be the foundation that makes scale possible. The fastest path to production should also be the safest one.
The next generation AgentCore runtime
We built Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to help developers build, connect, and optimize agents securely at scale. AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is the managed compute layer. It gives developers a fully managed environment to deploy and run agents without building or maintaining infrastructure. Since launching, our customers have been pushing their agents into increasingly complex workloads. As those workloads grow, so do the demands on the execution environment: more compute, more flexible billing, and trust boundaries that extend to data, not only compute. Agents reach production at scale if the infrastructure underneath was built for both scale and speed.
Today we’re announcing updates to AgentCore runtime that meet those demands. The core guarantee stands: every session runs in its own hardware-isolated Firecracker micro virtual machine (MicroVM), with its own identity, policy, and audit trail. These updates expand what’s possible within that guarantee. Sessions now start up to 15x faster, scale to 4x more compute, and run up to 68% more efficiently, with the isolation boundary fully intact.
Here’s what’s new.
Run bigger workloads without waiting longer to start
Teams building increasingly advanced agents asked for more flexibility: the ability to scale memory and compute within the isolated session to match the demands of their workloads. From large codebase compilations to browser-driven workflows to local model inference, the execution environment needs to keep pace.
Sessions now scale 4x compared to the previous version, up to 8 vCPUs and 32 GB, with support for container images up to 10 GB. Sessions start in under 2 seconds, independent of image size and concurrency. You no longer need warm pools and pre-provisioned clusters to manage cold starts.
        “Migrating to the next generation of AgentCore runtime reduced our agent session cold starts from nearly a minute to under five seconds, even during peak traffic. It also eliminated startup delays longer than 30 seconds, all while our weekly agent volume more than doubled.”
— Siwei Shen, VP of Engineering, Coinbase
        “Mission is using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime to power a natural-language query agent that helps users retrieve property and sales insights without navigating complex data systems. In our initial comparison of both runtime versions, the same workload delivered 35% faster cold starts for inference requests and 77% faster starts for health checks, while reducing measured runtime cost per call by 17%. The new AgentCore runtime gives us a compelling combination of faster agent experiences and more efficient resource utilization as we bring enterprise agents into production.”
— Dr. Ryan Ries, Chief AI & Data Scientist, Mission Cloud
        “Our approach is to run Zuora’s cloud with automation and AI agents wherever we can, and that only works if the runtime is efficient and reliable. The next generation AgentCore runtime cut our memory footprint per invocation by around 60% in many use cases while handling more traffic at steady latency. That gives us a stronger cost profile as we expand agentic workloads across our platform.”
— Brad Ruppert, VP of Cloud and Security, Zuora
        “The Rescale platform helps R&D and engineering teams accelerate product development with agentic digital engineering. Our engineering-specific agents validate simulation inputs, troubleshoot jobs, select hardware, and generate reports, while engineers stay in control. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime allows us to deploy and scale those agents in production without building or operating the underlying agent infrastructure, so we can deliver new agents to customers faster.”
— Mark Whitney, VP Engineering, Rescale
Stop paying for idle agents
As teams move agents closer to production, they asked for billing that reflects how agents actually work. Agents spend much of their time waiting on a model response, a tool call, or a human decision. Agents should be billed for the work they do, not the time they spend waiting.
The runtime now reclaims memory within minutes of the agent releasing it, and an idle agent scales to zero. For multi-turn agents with natural pauses between interactions, this means up to 68 percent less memory consumed per session. For always-on agents, committed baseline pricing sets a memory baseline per session, billed as a minimum, with room to burst up to four times that baseline on demand. This gives steady workloads a predictable rate at AWS Lambda MicroVM rates. The runtime uses compute more efficiently, so you pay less for the same work. That makes the finance conversation that often gates production rollouts easier to close.
        “The next generation Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime helps us deliver more responsive AI experiences by starting agents faster and using memory more efficiently. Aligning consumption with actual usage gives our clients great confidence to scale agentic solutions while keeping costs connected to real demand.”
— Ashwin Patil, Principal, AI and Data Leader, Deloitte Consulting LLP
        “AgentCore runtime gives us a managed foundation for building agentic products and platforms around our customers’ data, tools, and business processes. The next generation Agentcore runtime makes that foundation more responsive and resource-efficient by restoring initialized environments and reclaiming unused memory. We’re beginning to build on the latest version because the cost and latency reductions make a significant difference in how our customers’ businesses operate.”
— Randall Hunt, CTO, Caylent
Isolation now extends to your data
Many enterprises face a persistent gap in their agent security model. The agent runs inside an isolated session, but the data it requires resides outside that boundary. Long-running agents pick up context as they go: files, credentials, tool outputs, and more. Teams end up building their own rules for how data moves in and out, adding complexity and risk with every new agent.
Isolation that stops at compute is only half a boundary. The next generation AgentCore runtime closes that gap. Each session still runs in its own hardware-isolated environment with its own identity, access policy, and audit trail. Agents can now dynamically mount and save their work to a filesystem, such as an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket with FUSE support. Your data stays inside the trust boundary for the entire job, governed by a single set of controls you define once.
        “At Okta, the combination of AgentCore runtime and Lambda MicroVMs provide the isolated execution environment and contextual memory our agents need to inspect code, run test suites, and open pull requests within ephemeral sandboxes. Paired with our identity-governed policy controls, AgentCore Runtime and Lambda MicroVMs demonstrate how we can safely scale autonomous engineering agents without risking workspace leakage or privilege escalation.”
— Monica Bajaj, SVP Engineering, Okta
        “From helping car shoppers value a trade-in to helping dealers book service appointments and structure deals, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore powers dozens of agentic solutions across Cox Automotive’s brands. Having a single, governed agent platform lets our teams across our business move from pilot to production with confidence.”
— Chris Dillon, VP, Product and Engineering, Cox Automotive
Our commitment
The agents that reach production are the ones you trust to act on your behalf, with real data, real stakes, and real accountability. Trust isn’t a feature you add later. It’s the runtime you build on. This release is a step toward that future: bigger sessions, efficient resource use, and storage inside the trust boundary, without loosening the isolation that makes the work trustworthy. By re:Invent, per-session scoping will bind each session to its own storage folder through session-labeled credentials, and we will keep building from there.
Get started
The next generation AgentCore runtime is available today in AWS Regions across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Visit Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to build on it or open the Amazon Bedrock console to start exploring.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir : voilà les Nazgnagôl (Nazgûl) déjà identifiés dans la saison 3
articles.text:
Dans les livres de J.R.R. Tolkien comme dans l’adaptation au cinéma de Peter Jackson, les Nazgûl ne sont plus que des spectres au corps invisible. Des silhouettes nimbées de ténèbres, qui furent autrefois neuf rois humains, asservies au pouvoir de l’Anneau unique. Ce sont les esclaves de Sauron.
Sur ces neuf serviteurs, l’auteur n’a identifié que deux membres. Plutôt que de se contenter de ces deux-là, la série Les Anneaux de pouvoir a choisi de remplir les cases vides avec ses propres personnages, pour étoffer le récit – qui se déroule au Deuxième Âge de la Terre du Milieu, des milliers d’années avant Le Seigneur des anneaux.
La saison 3, dont la moitié des épisodes est en ligne sur Prime Video depuis le 11 novembre, fait d’ailleurs la part belle à quatre de ces futurs spectres de l’Anneau, avant leur transformation finale. Sur ces quatre-là, un seul sort vraiment des textes de Tolkien. Les trois autres sont des créations de la série.
Attention, la suite de l’article dévoile des éléments de la saison 3.
Ce ne sont pas encore des Nazgûl, mais des Nazgnagôl
À l’époque où la série se passe, les Nazgûl n’existent pas encore. Comme ces rois humains viennent tout juste d’entrer en contact avec les anneaux maudits, leur déchéance démarre à peine. Les showrunners J.D. Payne et Patrick McKay ont donc créé un mot pour désigner cet état intermédiaire de pré-corruption : Nazgnagôl.
Ce terme a été bâti à partir du noir parler, la langue du Mordor imaginée par Tolkien : « nazg » y veut dire anneau, et les showrunners en ont déduit « nagôl », serviteur, un mot que Tolkien n’a jamais écrit mais qui suit sa logique. Des serviteurs de l’Anneau encore humains, donc, de chair et d’os, car, dans la chronologie de la série, Sauron n’a pas encore forgé l’Anneau unique qui fera d’eux des spectres. Chez Tolkien, c’est l’inverse : l’Unique existe déjà quand les Neuf apparaissent.
Dans le premier épisode, la série résume leur état en une phrase : quand il porte son anneau, un Nazgnagôl est à la fois de ce monde et d’un autre.
Le Roi-Sorcier et Khamûl, les deux seuls noms laissés par Tolkien
Le Roi-Sorcier d’Angmar
Tolkien n’a jamais dressé la liste exacte des Neuf. L’encyclopédie Tolkiendil, référence francophone sur son œuvre, résume ce qu’on en sait : ils étaient des seigneurs, dont trois Númenóréens et un Orientais, et sont apparus vers l’an 2250 du Deuxième Âge. Surtout, seuls le Roi-Sorcier d’Angmar et Khamûl l’Orientais ont droit à un nom, ou au moins à un titre.
Le Roi-Sorcier est le chef des Nazgûl et le plus célèbre des Neuf.
Vers l’an 1300 du Troisième Âge, il s’installe en Angmar, au nord, pour faire la guerre aux royaumes des Dúnedain, et prend la cité de Fornost en 1974. C’est lui qui poignarde Frodon au Mont Venteux, et c’est lui que tuent Éowyn et Merry à la bataille des Champs du Pelennor, le 15 mars 3019. Tolkien n’a jamais dit qui il était avant de porter l’anneau au doigt.
Pour le dire autrement, l’un des méchants les plus connus et marquants de la fantasy n’a ni nom ni visage, et la série n’a encore désigné personne pour ce rôle.
Khamûl l’Orientais
Khamûl est un peu mieux servi.
Dans les textes, il est le second du Roi-Sorcier, un ancien Orientais, que Sauron envoie en 2951 du Troisième Âge dans sa forteresse de Dol Guldur, située dans la Forêt Noire (Mirkwood). La série en fait le premier Nazgnagôl qu’on voit naître à l’écran. Joué par Zubin Varla, Khamûl y est un seigneur de guerre du Rhûn, à l’est, qui a perdu le pouvoir face au mage ténébreux.
Dans la saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir, Sauron fait s’affronter à mort des représentants de Rhûn, avec la promesse de confier un anneau au survivant. Khamûl tue ses anciens compagnons, soigne ses blessures grâce au pouvoir de l’anneau et promet en échange cent mille hommes au Seigneur des ténèbres.
Le roi des Lossoth, le roi des Haradrim et Theo, les ajouts de la série
Le roi des Lossoth
Le tout premier porteur d’anneau à apparaître dans la saison n’existe pas chez Tolkien.
Dès l’ouverture de l’épisode 1, un colosse en armure noire et en fourrures domine Galadriel au combat, au point qu’elle doit battre en retraite avec Arondir. De retour à Fondcombe, elle l’identifie devant Elrond : c’est le roi des Lossoth (joué par Paul Hickey), un peuple des terres gelées du Forodwaith, tout au nord du monde.
Il avait promis d’aider les Elfes avant que Sauron ne le retourne. Il a reçu son anneau avant le début de la saison, pendant l’ellipse de cinq ans qui la sépare de la précédente.
Le roi des Haradrim
Son homologue du Sud est présenté à partir de l’épisode 2.
Dans l’épisode 1, Gil-galad et Círdan constatent que Sauron s’est tourné vers les hommes pour grossir ses rangs, « les Lossoth au nord, les Haradrim au sud ». Les épisodes 1 et 2 citent un roi des Haradrim, peuple du Harad (ceux qui chargeront à dos d’oliphant au Pelennor, quelques millénaires plus tard), parmi les porteurs d’anneau.
Les deux Nazgnagôl (le roi des Haradrim et le roi des Lossoth) sont décrits un peu plus précisément dans l’épisode 2, lorsqu’ils se présentent à Durin IV. Ils ont même droit à des lignes de dialogue, et retirent leur masque pendant qu’ils tentent d’amadouer Durin IV avec de belles paroles. Une manœuvre qui ne prend pas, et la discussion finit par mal tourner.
Theo
Theo, lui, est le seul personnage déjà connu des spectateurs à rejoindre les Neuf.
Le fils de Bronwyn, joué par Tyroe Muhafidin et présent depuis la saison 1, coupe désormais du bois pour les navires des Númenóréens à Pelargir, où il prend douze coups de fouet. Il entend des officiers parler de l’offre de Sauron, se présente à l’épreuve à la fin de l’épisode 1 et reçoit son anneau dans l’épisode 2, avec « l’aide » de Sauron.
On apprend aussi qu’il est de lignée noble, fils de Fäldred, lui-même fils de Hammerthreg (les loyaux intendants du Mordor, selon Sauron), et qu’il aurait pu régner sur les terres du sud.
À la fin de l’épisode 4, Arondir, qui l’a presque élevé, se retrouve face à un Nazgnagôl masqué. C’est Theo qui le tue, sur ordre de Sauron. Ce dernier lui assure qu’il est né pour être un conquérant, un sorcier et un roi (il lui avait dit plus tôt qu’il avait accès à « certains pouvoirs »). Une piste vers le Roi-Sorcier ? Rien n’accrédite cette thèse pour l’instant.
Cinq anneaux donnés, quatre porteurs connus
Le site américain Nerdist a compté les anneaux. Dans l’épisode 1, le coffret de Sauron en contient six avant que Khamûl ne reçoive le sien. Dans l’épisode 2, il en reste cinq, dont celui de Theo, juste avant que Sauron ne le lui remette, puis quatre.
Sauron a donc déjà distribué cinq anneaux aux hommes, sur les neuf, alors qu’on ne connaît pour l’instant que quatre Nazgnagôl (les rois des Lossoth et des Haradrim, Khamûl et Theo). Un cinquième porteur manque donc à l’appel. Qui est-il ?
Nerdist mise sur Kemen, le fils de Pharazôn, l’actuel dirigeant de Númenor, l’une des principales puissances militaires du monde connu. Kemen balaie à deux reprises l’idée même d’anneau magique. Le site relève aussi que, malgré ses tenues couvertes de broches, il ne porte aucune bague. Mais peut-être y a-t-il anguille sous roche. Or, chez Tolkien, trois des Neuf étaient des seigneurs númenóréens.
Sur r/LOTR_on_Prime, le forum Reddit consacré à la série, les fans tiennent d’ailleurs un fil pour identifier les Neuf épisode après épisode.
Il reste donc quatre anneaux dans le coffret, et quatre épisodes à diffuser. Les épisodes 5 et 6 arrivent sur Prime Video le mercredi 18 novembre, et les deux derniers le 25 novembre.

articles.title: Le Pixel 11 aura bien le droit à GrapheneOS, et c'est grâce à Android 17 QPR2
articles.text:
GrapheneOS avait mis de côté ses travaux pour les Google Pixel 11 faute de MTE, une protection de la mémoire. Mais avec Android 17 QPR2 la donne change, et l’équipe confirme que tout fonctionne avec son système.
Le portage était presque terminé quand l’équipe a dû l’abandonner. Avec le MTE désormais disponible, il pourra sortir.
Pixel 11 : un portage quasi prêt, derrière QPR2 et le Signature 27
Nous rapportions le 31 août que l’équipe de GrapheneOS renonçait au Pixel 11. Elle déconseillait même de l’acheter. Le projet était pourtant bien avancé. D’après son message sur X, le portage était presque fini environ une semaine après la sortie des téléphones. Le blocage venait du MTE (Memory Tagging Extension), absent de ces modèles.
Le principe est simple. Chaque zone de mémoire reçoit une étiquette. Si un programme tente d’accéder à une zone qui n’est pas la sienne, les étiquettes ne correspondent plus et le processeur bloque l’accès. GrapheneOS estime que cela neutralise presque tous les exploits à distance. Les Pixel disposent de cette protection depuis le Pixel 8, et Graphene OS avait pour habitude de l’activer sur tout le système, y compris pour la plupart des applications, même sans l’accord de leurs développeurs. De son côté, Google ne l’a jamais activé par défaut sur Android.
Dans son message, l’équipe explique qu’Android 17 QPR2, une mise à jour intermédiaire d’Android 17, ajoute bien le MTE aux Pixel 11. Elle a vérifié que cette protection fonctionne avec sa propre version de GrapheneOS basée sur cette mise à jour, presque terminée. Cette version sera d’abord diffusée sur les appareils que GrapheneOS prend déjà en charge. Le support du Pixel 11 étant fini depuis longtemps, il pourra être livré lui aussi une fois cette version publiée. La priorité de l’équipe ira toutefois au Motorola Signature 27, dont la prise en charge reste à terminer. Aucune date n’est annoncée. Rappelons que jusqu’au partenariat avec Motorola, seuls les Pixel étaient officiellement pris en charge.
Reste la question des performances. Le MTE peut potentiellement ralentir l'appareil en vérifiant les étiquettes. GrapheneOS juge toutefois les performances du Pixel 11 acceptables, et même largement suffisantes, avec un impact comparable à celui des autres Pixel. Sur le Signature 27, elles seront nettement supérieures. Le site l’explique par un processeur bien plus puissant.

articles.title: 5 lessons to learn from the book Kaizen by Sarah Harvey
articles.text:
5 lessons to learn from the book Kaizen by Sarah Harvey
Discover five powerful lessons from Kaizen by Sarah Harvey on building better habits, overcoming resistance, and achieving lasting personal growth.
Have you ever decided to change your entire life, only to give up after a few days? Whether it is waking up early, exercising regularly, saving money, or learning a new skill, making major lifestyle changes can feel overwhelming. But what if you could transform your life without changing everything at once?
In Kaizen: The Japanese Method for Transforming Habits, One Small Step at a Time, Sarah Harvey introduces readers to the Japanese philosophy of Kaizen, which focuses on continuous improvement through small, manageable changes.
The book explains how this approach can be applied to different areas of life, including health, relationships, finances, career, and everyday habits. Instead of chasing overnight transformation, Harvey encourages readers to practise patience, understand their existing routines, and make gradual improvements that last.
5 Important lessons to learn from Kaizen by Sarah Harvey.
1. Small changes can lead to big results
One of the biggest lessons from the book is that you do not need to make dramatic changes to improve your life. Sometimes, the smallest actions can create meaningful progress when repeated consistently.
For example, if you want to develop a reading habit, start with just five pages a day instead of forcing yourself to finish an entire book in a week. Similarly, if you want to become physically active, begin with a short daily walk.
The idea is to make changes so manageable that you can continue them without feeling overwhelmed.
2. Understand your existing habits before changing them
Before introducing new habits, take some time to understand your current routine. Many people try to change their behaviour without identifying what is preventing them from making progress.
Harvey encourages readers to examine their everyday activities, identify areas that need improvement, and understand which habits are helping or holding them back.
For example, if you spend too much time scrolling through social media, observe when and why you reach for your phone. Once you understand the pattern, you can gradually replace that habit with something more productive.
3. Break big goals into smaller steps
Large goals can sometimes feel impossible because we focus too much on the final result rather than the actions required to achieve it.
The Kaizen approach encourages breaking ambitious goals into smaller, realistic tasks. Instead of worrying about writing an entire book, focus on writing one paragraph every day. If you want to save money, begin by setting aside a small amount regularly.
These manageable steps make it easier to stay motivated and track your progress.
4. Be patient and stop comparing your progress
Personal growth does not happen at the same speed for everyone. Some habits take weeks to develop, while others require months of consistent effort.
The book emphasises the importance of patience and creating solutions that suit your individual lifestyle. What works for someone else may not necessarily work for you.
Instead of comparing your progress with others, focus on becoming slightly better than you were yesterday. Remember that consistency matters more than perfection.
5. Track your progress and adjust your approach
Making changes is only one part of the process. You also need to understand whether those changes are working.
The book encourages readers to monitor their habits, review their progress, and make adjustments whenever necessary. Keeping a journal or maintaining a simple habit tracker can help you recognise improvements and identify areas that need more attention.
If a particular routine is not working, do not immediately consider it a failure. Find a more manageable approach and try again.
Final thoughts
Kaizen by Sarah Harvey offers a refreshing approach to personal development by reminding readers that meaningful transformation does not happen overnight. Instead of putting pressure on yourself to change everything at once, focus on making small improvements every day.
Whether you want to build healthier habits, improve your finances, strengthen relationships, or become more productive, the Kaizen philosophy encourages you to take one manageable step at a time.
The biggest takeaway is simple: you do not have to become a completely different person tomorrow. You just have to make a small effort to become better today.

articles.title: « Une légende remplace une légende » : Trump réclame Tim Cook pour diriger Nvidia — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le président américain s’est fendu sur Truth Social d’un message rédigé en lettres capitales dont il a le secret. Après avoir salué le « travail fantastique » de Jensen Huang, Donald Trump assure qu’il n’existe « qu’un seul homme » capable de lui succéder, « TIM COOK d’Apple », avant de lâcher : « Une légende remplace une légende ! ».
    Pour aller plus loin
Nvidia officialise le départ de Jensen Huang et confie les clés à sa directrice financière
            
Cette sortie survient quelques heures seulement après le départ du fondateur de Nvidia, remplacé en urgence par sa directrice financière Colette Kress le temps de dénicher un PDG permanent. Pour mesurer l’ampleur du séisme, nous avons retracé l’incroyable affaire Jensen Huang en vidéo.
Sur le fond, la suggestion n’a pourtant rien d’absurde. Le 1er septembre dernier, Tim Cook a cédé son fauteuil de directeur général d’Apple à John Ternus après quinze ans de règne, ne conservant que la présidence exécutive du conseil d’administration. Dans la Silicon Valley, il incarne surtout le modèle absolu d’une transition réussie derrière un fondateur tutélaire : dès mercredi, le professeur de gouvernance à Yale Jeffrey Sonnenfeld plaidait d’ailleurs dans les colonnes de Time pour que son nom figure en haut de la liste.
    Pour aller plus loin
Culte de la personnalité, zéro numéro deux : pourquoi Jensen Huang laisse Nvidia face à un vide vertigineux
            
Un candidat qui n’a rien demandé
Reste qu’aucun élément n’indique que Tim Cook ait été approché par Nvidia, ni même qu’il souhaite reprendre du service opérationnel à 66 ans. Le choix du futur dirigeant appartient exclusivement au conseil d’administration, désormais présidé par Harvey Jones, et nullement au Bureau ovale. Sans compter que le passif entre Cupertino et Santa Clara reste glacial, Apple ayant banni les puces graphiques de Nvidia de ses Mac depuis plus d’une décennie. En coulisses, un autre ponte de la pomme revient d’ailleurs avec beaucoup plus d’insistance : Johny Srouji, l’architecte des puces Apple Silicon.
    Pour aller plus loin
Qui pour remplacer Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia ? Voici les favoris pour lui succéder
            
Si Donald Trump adore distribuer les bons points et les postes clés de la tech américaine sur ses réseaux, cette incursion met surtout la pression sur les administrateurs de Nvidia.
Déjà épinglé pour sa passivité face à Jensen Huang, le conseil aurait tout intérêt à prouver son indépendance en évitant de suivre les consignes présidentielles. D’ici là, notre résumé vidéo de l’affaire permet de reprendre tout le feuilleton depuis le premier jour.
