articles.title: Nvidia busca CEO tras la salida de Jensen Huang: estos son los candidatos que suenan para el puesto
articles.text:
Nvidia ha perdido al único director ejecutivo que ha tenido jamás. Jensen Huang ha dimitido este jueves como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración, y la empresa ahora tiene que encontrar a alguien para dirigir al fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo. Por el momento, el puesto pertenece a alguien de la casa.
Qué ha pasado. Nvidia anunciaba que su directora financiera, Colette Kress, actuará como directora ejecutiva interina mientras mantiene su cargo financiero, y que el consejo buscará candidatos internos y externos para el puesto permanente. También ha nombrado a Harvey C. Jones, antiguo director ejecutivo de Synopsys, como presidente del consejo, siendo de hecho el primero en la historia de la empresa.
La salida de Huang se produce tras las investigaciones sobre sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, una de ellas presuntamente con Alice Huang, ejecutiva y directora de la empresa Megaspeed, sospechosa de ser espía china. Las acciones de Nvidia abrieron este jueves con una caída de más del 13 % tras la dimisión, borrando más de medio billón de dólares en valor.
La nueva CEO interina: Colette Kress. Ha sido directora financiera desde 2013, trabajó anteriormente en Cisco y Microsoft, y aparece junto a Huang en cada presentación de resultados. Josh Gilbert, analista de eToro, declaraba a Reuters que es “la opción obvia para mantener el rumbo” y una voz de confianza para los inversores. Ahora, que se quede de forma permanente es otra cosa. Para Gilbert la ventaja de Nvidia es la tecnología y el consejo probablemente querría a un ingeniero al mando.
Los ingenieros. Ian Buck, quien ayudó a desarrollar CUDA, el software que mantiene a los desarrolladores vinculados a los chips de Nvidia, y que ahora dirige los productos de IA a hiperescala, encabeza la lista para llevarse el puesto permanente. Shay Boloor, estratega jefe de mercado en Futurum Equities, contaba a Reuters que es el candidato interno más fuerte por ese motivo.
Otros miembros internos mencionados incluyen al cofundador Chris Malachowsky, el único ejecutivo al nivel de antigüedad de Huang, y a Andrew Bell, vicepresidente sénior de ingeniería de hardware, con una trayectoria destacada en el sector de los chips.
Los externos. Si el consejo mira más allá de Nvidia, que es algo que también plantean según el comunicado, el nombre que más suena es el del director ejecutivo de Arm, Rene Haas, antiguo ejecutivo de Nvidia. Tiene “sentido lógico”, según comparten en Reuters, pero tal y como comparte Charu Chanana, estratega de inversiones del banco Saxo, el modelo de negocio de Arm difiere considerablemente del de Nvidia.
Otras sugerencias son más especulativas:
- Bret Taylor: desde TechCrunch sugieren al fundador de Sierra y expresidente del consejo de OpenAI como una figura estable y bien conectada.
- Eric Schmidt: Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, de Yale, lo proponía como candidato, pero igual su propia aventura amorosa en el pasado complica las cosas.
- Tim Cook: pura especulación, pero según Jun Bei Liu, de Ten Cap, su experiencia en la cadena de suministro podría encajar. Ahora, que encaje y que pretenda dejar su puesto como presidente ejecutivo de la junta directiva de Apple es otra cosa muy distinta.
- Lisa Su y Lip-Bu Tan: respectivos directores ejecutivos de AMD e Intel. TechCrunch los incluye en su lista, pero tampoco son candidatos realistas pues son pocas las probabilidades de que dejen sus respectivos puestos de CEO. Y en el caso de Tan, es un reflejo del difícil momento por el que está pasando Intel, así que no se le espera demasiado.
¿Y la familia?. Los dos hijos de Huang ocupan cargos ejecutivos en Nvidia, aunque todavía son relativamente jóvenes e “inexpertos”, según relatan desde la BBC. Armina Rosenberg, de Minotaur Capital, ve plausible también una estructura de codirección ejecutiva, combinando a un líder financiero como Kress con un líder tecnológico como Buck.
Qué pasa ahora. De momento, y hasta conocer más noticias, tendremos que esperar al próximo martes 17 de noviembre, que es cuando Nvidia presenta sus resultados del tercer trimestre bajo el mando de Kress.

articles.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open source AI after Jensen Huang's exit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day.” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open source AI models in September for $12.9 billion, making it the second-largest acquisition in the company’s history, just behind that of chipmaker Groq’s assets for $20 billion in December 2025.
“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!,” Delangue wrote on X.
The post is interesting as it implies that Huang’s departure is potentially worrying to open source advocates, and he’s attempting to offer reassurance.
As Nvidia’s CEO, Huang was known as a strong advocate for open source AI and open-weight models, which is why there could be concerns about how a company that’s no longer under his leadership will now approach this space.
After Nvidia announced its plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market, Reuters reported in October. While Nvidia pledged that the platform would preserve open support, it would also allow the company to control a major distribution channel for AI models.
The Hugging Face deal is still scheduled to close in the first half of 2027. Requests for further comment on the deal status and whether Hugging Face has spoken yet with Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress were not returned.
Huang’s advocacy for open source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X. The letter, which was signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, Palantir, and others, urged the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models. It said models that “anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” are an important part of the AI ecosystem because they make AI “more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.”
Huang also wrote that open-weight models expand access to the AI economy, strengthen competition, and give customers greater control, as they know they won’t become locked into a single provider. “Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” his post on X stated.
In August, Nvidia also announced a $6 billion deal with the coding startup Poolside to help build out an open AI ecosystem in the U.S. to help the country compete against Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Kimi K3, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Last month, Nvidia expanded its Nemotron family of open-weight models with a large 120-billion-parameter model for agents used by the enterprise as well as with two new lightweight Bolt models that run on PCs.
Earlier this year, Huang promoted open source AI during his January keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, noting that open source models have “really revolutionized artificial intelligence.”

articles.title: Nvidia evalúa desplazar a Jensen Huang: quiénes son los favoritos para reemplazarlo
articles.text:
La junta directiva de Nvidia se reunió este miércoles para decidir si aparta a su cofundador y director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, según informó Reuters con base en una fuente cercana al proceso. La compañía, que se convirtió en el mayor proveedor mundial de procesadores para inteligencia artificial, enfrenta por primera vez en sus más de tres décadas de historia una discusión real sobre quién podría ocupar su conducción. Nvidia no respondió de inmediato a las consultas periodísticas sobre esa reunión.
La incertidumbre desató una fuerte reacción en los mercados. La acción de Nvidia acumuló una caída que borró unos USD 600.000 millones de su capitalización bursátil esta semana, según Reuters, lo que desplazó a la empresa del primer puesto entre las compañías más valiosas del mundo.
Entre los candidatos internos que concentran la atención de analistas e inversores aparecen dos nombres: la directora financiera Colette Kress y el ejecutivo técnico Ian Buck, ambos con más de una década de trayectoria en la empresa.
La junta de Nvidia evalúa el futuro de Jensen Huang
Huang cofundó Nvidia en 1993 y construyó la empresa sobre los procesadores para videojuegos antes de transformarla en el principal proveedor de chips para centros de datos y aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial. Su figura quedó tan asociada a la compañía que, según la analista Anna Wu, fundadora de Floodlines Research en Sídney, citada por Reuters, “Jensen Huang es una estrella de rock en la industria. Es la voz de Nvidia y un líder así es muy difícil de reemplazar”.
El directorio incluyó una investigación independiente dirigida por un exfiscal federal, según Financial Times. La junta cuenta con varios aliados de Huang que trabajan con él desde la década de 1990. Nvidia no emitió declaraciones públicas sobre el alcance ni el estado de ese proceso.
Colette Kress e Ian Buck, los perfiles que concentran la atención
Kress, de 59 años, ocupa la dirección financiera de Nvidia desde 2013. Antes trabajó en Microsoft, Cisco y Texas Instruments. Es uno de los cuatro ejecutivos que integran el círculo formal de oficiales de la empresa y acompaña a Huang en cada presentación de resultados trimestrales, lo que la convierte en una cara conocida para el mercado.
Según informó Semafor, algunos miembros del directorio la favorecen para asumir como directora ejecutiva interina. Josh Gilbert, analista principal de la plataforma eToro, recogido por Reuters, la describió como “la opción obvia para estabilizar la situación” dada su relación sostenida con inversores y su conocimiento de las finanzas de la compañía.
Buck, de alrededor de 49 años, presenta un perfil diferente. Se incorporó a Nvidia en 2004, participó en el lanzamiento de las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial sobre chips de la compañía y fue una figura central en el desarrollo del sistema de software CUDA, que mantiene a los desarrolladores vinculados al ecosistema de Nvidia.
Hoy dirige los productos de hardware y software de inteligencia artificial para los grandes centros de datos —el segmento más crítico del negocio— y cuenta con un doctorado de la Universidad de Stanford. Shay Boloor, estratega jefe de mercado de Futurum Equities, señaló a Reuters que Buck “es el candidato interno más sólido a largo plazo, dado su rol en la creación de CUDA y en la conducción del negocio hiperscala”.
El desafío de reemplazar a un CEO sin un sucesor público
Nvidia no cuenta con un plan formal y público de sucesión, según Financial Times, una situación que el propio Huang admitió al declarar que no cree en ese tipo de mecanismos. Su modelo de gestión es inusualmente horizontal: alrededor de 60 ejecutivos le reportan de forma directa, lo que le otorga una influencia extensa sobre cada área de la compañía, desde la estrategia de productos hasta las relaciones con legisladores y grandes inversores.
Esa arquitectura organizativa, construida alrededor de una figura singular, dificulta la identificación de un sucesor con capacidad para asumir de manera simultánea las funciones de estratega, tecnólogo, lobista y vocero ante los mercados. “No es intuitivamente obvio quién sería el sucesor”, afirmó Stacy Rasgon, analista de Bernstein, en declaraciones recogidas por Financial Times.
Algunos analistas sugirieron una solución intermedia: una estructura de co-dirección ejecutiva que combine el perfil financiero de Kress con el técnico de Buck. Armina Rosenberg, gestora de cartera y cofundadora de Minotaur Capital en Sídney —firma que tiene posiciones en Nvidia—, planteó esa posibilidad a Reuters: “La vía más realista es un líder interino del círculo interno de largo plazo, posiblemente como una co-CEO: alguien que estabilice el negocio y las finanzas, como Kress, junto a un líder de producto y tecnología, como Buck”.
En las especulaciones también surgió el nombre de René Haas, director ejecutivo de Arm y exejecutivo de Nvidia. Un banquero especializado en operaciones del sector de chips calificó a Haas ante Reuters como la opción externa más lógica por su perfil de alto nivel y su conocimiento de la industria de los semiconductores. Sin embargo, analistas e inversores le otorgan menos relevancia que a Kress y Buck en el debate sobre la conducción inmediata.
Qué puede pasar con Nvidia si cambia su liderazgo
La empresa dispone de una cartera de acuerdos y una hoja de ruta de productos que se extiende por varios años, según Financial Times, por lo que un eventual cambio en la conducción no implicaría una alteración inmediata de las operaciones ni del calendario de lanzamientos. El interrogante central que señalan analistas e inversores es si una nueva conducción podría sostener la visión estratégica de largo plazo que permitió a Nvidia anticiparse a la demanda de chips para inteligencia artificial.
En el sitio de apuestas Polymarket, las probabilidades de que Huang renuncie o sea destituido antes de fin de año se ubicaban en un 83%, con Buck como favorito entre los posibles sucesores y Kress en segundo lugar, aunque el volumen de operaciones en ese mercado es reducido.
La decisión que tome el directorio en las próximas horas o días definirá si Nvidia inicia una transición de liderazgo por primera vez en su historia, con consecuencias que trascienden a la empresa y alcanzan a toda la cadena de valor de la inteligencia artificial y los semiconductores a escala global.

articles.title: Data observability becomes a must as AI agents build databases - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agents that build their own databases are forcing a data foundation rethink
AI agents are changing how enterprises create, move and govern information, and data observability is turning into a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have. Models get most of the attention, but the data beneath them decides whether they hold up in production.
That pressure is now reaching the cloud-native community, where KubeCon organizers added a dedicated AI inference and agentic track this year. The industry has raced from chatbots to retrieval, fine-tuning and agents, yet every wave rests on the same groundwork, according to Sanjeev Mohan (pictured), principal at SanjMo, a data and AI advisory firm, and author of “Designing the AI-Driven Data Foundations.”
“AI can only be successful if it’s built on a solid foundation,” Mohan said. “You have no observability or transparency into it. No matter what you do on top of it, it will not be successful.”
Mohan spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed theCUBE’s second day of coverage at the event. (* Disclosure below.)
Why AI agents demand data observability at runtime
For decades, data was created once in an operational system and then pushed through brittle pipelines for extraction, transformation, cataloging and preparation. That model works when humans consume batch reports, Mohan explained. Thousands of agents change the math.
“They’re not going to wait for this pipeline to finish. They want access to the database directly,” Mohan said.
Agents are also doing something no earlier software did. They spin up short-lived databases, copy data and test different chains of thought before picking one action, according to Mohan. An agent reviewing a loan application might query census records and social media before rejecting it, which raises the question of how that decision gets audited.
“Governance becomes really important, and this is not like governance in the past where you would govern your data and then have a deterministic CFO report dashboard run on it,” Mohan said.
That makes data observability part of the architecture itself, not an afterthought bolted onto a warehouse. Mohan’s book, published in June 2026 by John Wiley & Sons Inc., examines how AI agents as first-class data consumers are redefining architectural principles that have stood for decades. Future platforms will need to blend structured and unstructured data in a single converged system, he noted.
“You have to save the state and you have to build the context, and this context is being built in runtime,” Mohan said. “The context for the same task could be very different for the three of us. So we’ll see new kinds of databases.”
Stay tuned for the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA.

articles.title: Neues Whatsapp-Feature: So kannst du bald Nachrichten geheimhalten
articles.text:
Neues Whatsapp-Feature: So kannst du bald Nachrichten mit sensiblen Inhalten geheimhalten
Schon seit 2021 bietet Whatsapp die Option, Fotos und Videos per Einmalansicht zu verschicken. Das bedeutet, dass Empfänger:innen die Medien nur ein einziges Mal öffnen und ansehen dürfen. Danach werden die Dateien wieder automatisch aus dem Chat gelöscht. Das Feature gibt es auch für Sprach-, aber nicht für Textnachrichten. Das soll sich aber künftig ändern, wie WABetaInfo berichtet.
Whatsapp: So verschwinden Textnachrichten bald schneller
Bisher hatten User:innen, die ihre Textnachrichten nicht dauerhaft in Whatsapp stehen lassen wollten, nur die Option, selbstlöschende Chats zu aktivieren. Künftig wird die Einmalansicht das automatische Löschen von Nachrichten deutlich schneller und einfacher machen. Sobald die Funktion freigeschaltet ist, können Whatsapp-Nutzer:innen wie gewohnt eine Nachricht eintippen. Im Anschluss müssen sie den Senden-Button gedrückt halten.
Dadurch öffnet sich das Menü, um die Nachricht entweder vorzuplanen oder per Einmalansicht abzuschicken. Sobald letztere Variante ausgewählt wird, schickt Whatsapp die Nachricht direkt ab. Die Empfänger:innen bekommen die selbstlöschende Nachricht nicht direkt angezeigt, wenn sie den Chat mit den Absender:innen öffnen. Stattdessen wird ihnen ein Hinweisblock angezeigt, auf den sie tippen müssen.
Durch das Auswählen öffnet sich ein separates Fenster in Whatsapp, das sich über den Chat legt und die Nachricht offenbart. Wird das Fenster wieder geschlossen, löscht Whatsapp die Nachricht sofort. Absender:innen bekommen dann auch noch einen Hinweis, dass ihre Nachricht geöffnet und gelesen wurde, falls sie Lesebestätigungen in den Whatsapp-Einstellungen aktiviert haben. Danach kann keine der beiden Parteien die Nachricht wieder öffnen.
Damit die Nachricht auch im neuen Fenster wirklich sicher ist, blockiert Whatsapp Screenshots und Bildschirmaufnahmen. Ebenso ist es unmöglich, den Text zu kopieren, zu speichern oder an andere weiterzuleiten. Dementsprechend lohnt sich das Feature immer dann, wenn du sensible Daten über Whatsapp verschicken musst. Aktuell startet Meta den Betatest für das neue Feature. Wann die Einmalansichten aus der Testphase in die Release-Version des Messengers überführt werden, ist nicht bekannt.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Raenest acquires UK-based payments company Remitise - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian fintech startup Raenest has completed the acquisition of Remitise, a UK-based payments company, for an undisclosed amount to expand its regulatory footprint and gain greater control over its global payments infrastructure.
Founded in 2022 by Victor Alade, Sodruldeen Mustapha, and Richard Oyome, Raenest initially operated as an Employer of Record (EOR) before evolving into a platform that redefines global banking for Africans, helping businesses and freelancers receive international payments, convert between currencies, operate a multi-currency wallet, while managing transactions seamlessly.
The platform also enables customers to open global bank accounts in their names, access physical and virtual dollar cards, and manage payments in USD, EUR, and GBP. To date, the company has amassed over one million individual customers across more than 50 countries, processed over US$2 billion in payments, and served over 300 businesses. It also offers a consumer-focused product, Geegpay, which provides Africa’s gig economy with efficient payment solutions.
Raenest raised US$11 million in Series A funding in February 2025 to expand its reach in existing and new markets, and its acquisition of Remitise is linked to that ambition.
“Acquiring Remitise is part of our long-term strategy to build a global financial company. We want to own more of the infrastructure behind our products, deepen our relationships with financial institutions and create a stronger foundation for the customers and businesses we serve,” said Victor Alade, Raenest’s CEO.
The acquisition builds on Raenest’s regulatory footprint and includes a money services business (MSB) and payment service provider (PSP) licence in Canada, as well as an international money transfer operator licence in Nigeria.

articles.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks | TechCrunch
articles.text:
United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.
The airline is the latest American corporate giant to prevent customers from using AI agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems. The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants. Sharing passwords with apps and assistants can create security risks if those credentials get leaked or exposed.
United warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles.”
The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances.
“As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants,” the airline said in a statement. “This work includes updates to our booking, ticketing and distribution policies.”
The airline’s move follows a warning from banks, including Bank of America, which last week urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants.

articles.title: Nintendo finally lets you gift games -- with some big limitations
articles.text:
Nintendo will finally allow digital game gifting on Nov. 16, albeit with some catches.
To start, this feature will be limited to Switch and Switch 2 users within the same family group. For context, a family group includes up to eight accounts and is naturally only intended for family members, making it difficult to gift most people unless they already happen to be in your group. There’s no option to send gifts to anyone on your Friends List.
Further, Nintendo says only “eligible” games, DLC, and upgrade packs will be available for gifting, although it’s unclear exactly which titles are excluded. Other restrictions include supervised accounts not being able to send digital gifts and the number of gifts being limited “in a given period.”
To send a gift, visit the Nintendo eShop page of the desired title and select the ‘Give as a Gift’ checkbox. From there, complete the purchase and select the gift recipient from the list of members of your family group. Note that gifts are sent immediately, so plan accordingly for when you want the recipient to get it.
All in all, these are the sorts of weird limitations you’d expect from Nintendo. If nothing else, though, you can still buy Nintendo eShop gift cards from most retailers as an alternative. It should also be noted that PlayStation doesn’t offer any digital game gifting at all, although Xbox and Steam do, and with far fewer restrictions than Nintendo.
In related news, Nintendo just announced its 2026 Black Friday deals for Canada, which include some decent savings on a Switch 2 bundle and various games.

articles.title: 'They don't want to sell you powerful cards, it's that simple': rumored RTX 5080 Super GPU is apparently canned, and gamers are getting angrier with Nvidia
articles.text:
Nvidia RTX 5080 Super GPU is canned, rumor claims — and I'm not surprised in the slightest
The frustrations of gamers are boiling over at this point
- Nvidia's rumored RTX 5080 Super has been cancelled we're told
- This GPU refresh was supposedly due to launch at the start of 2027
- It was canned due to the cost of the 24GB of video RAM, which makes sense – but PC gamers are getting increasingly frustrated with Nvidia at this point
Nvidia's RTX 5080 Super – an expected spin on the GPU with 24GB of VRAM – has been ditched according to the grapevine.
VideoCardz highlighted a post on the Board Channels (a common source of leaks over in China) which claims that the RTX 5080 Super was due for a launch in January 2027 (as previous rumors indicated), but it's now cancelled.
Seemingly Nvidia has informed graphics card manufacturers over in China that the launch is not happening, without providing any "clear subsequent launch schedule" (bear in mind that's a translation from Chinese), meaning that in theory this isn't just a delay – the Super GPU is apparently canned.
This is a different sentiment to a rumor from a week ago that the RTX 5080 Super was delayed by Nvidia, which didn't go as far as to suggest that the GPU refresh has been abandoned. Clearly, though, something's amiss with the heavily rumored RTX 5080 Super, and it makes sense that, as all this speculation points out, it's to do with the video RAM.
In reaching to hit 24GB of VRAM, the RTX 5080 Super would be using 3GB modules of GDDR7 – as opposed to the 2GB modules on the vanilla RTX 5080 – and those beefier memory chips are now so much more expensive that it's a big stumbling block.
Meanwhile, we're told that the plain RTX 5080 (16GB) will remain the flagship in China – the RTX 5090 isn't sold in the country, of course, and arguably, it effectively isn't sold anywhere else either, not at a sensible price anyway. Stock of the Blackwell flagship has become very thin on the ground everywhere, meaning you're looking at paying triple to quadruple the MSRP in many regions, or maybe even more than that (the GPU has tipped up towards 10 grand in the US).
It's got to the point where rather than buying a standalone graphics card, the best way to bag yourself an RTX 5090 is in a high-end PC with a deal.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Analysis: it's getting nasty out there
At this point, there have been so many rumors about the RTX 5080 Super (and other potential RTX 5000 Super GPUs in the past), that it seems likely Nvidia was intending on doing something with such a refresh – at some point, anyway. It's an expected part of every graphics card generation anyway, let's face it, but it isn't a surprise to hear that any such plans have been put on hold (possibly permanently).
Indeed, it always seemed a stretch to me that Nvidia was even considering an RTX 5080 Super at this stage in the game, with GPU price hikes hitting new levels of pain, and the broader RAM crisis predicted to get worse at the tail end of this year, and bleaker still in 2027.
The GPU market is just too difficult right now for Nvidia to entertain introducing a new consumer graphics card with 24GB of VRAM, especially given that it would have to use the much pricier 3GB modules. With Nvidia's priorities obviously lying with the data center and AI, letting the GeForce consumer GPU range stagnate in this way is only to be expected, really.
Meanwhile, tempers are flaring and gamers are getting even angrier about the way Nvidia is treating consumers. As one Redditor put it: "They don't want to sell you powerful cards, [it's] that simple. They are gatekeeping AI compute power for the big boys so you are forced to spend money on Altman [OpenAI]."
Another Redditor observed: "Nvidia aren't innocent bystanders here. They're the primary source of the demand that has shifted memory production from GDDR to HBM [for AI data center cards]."
There's a lot of bad feeling out there currently, and as one gamer complained of Nvidia: "I wish they'd just do something." Quite what, well, that isn't clear, but even though the RTX 5080 Super wouldn't have been a remotely affordable GPU, it'd still have provided another high-end option. And perhaps that might have taken some of the pressure off the rising price of the RTX 5080 (although probably not in all honesty – and indeed one rumor suggested that this card would be dropped in favor of the RTX 5080 Super).
In a way, this canning of a possible (but only rumored) graphics card, no matter how unobtainable this Super may have been, is just another signal that Nvidia doesn't care about the plight of consumers. With frustration continuing to boil over in the PC gaming community, and no let-up in the RAM crisis in sight, it's difficult to see matters going anywhere but further downhill from here.

articles.title: Impôts : le fisc a un nouvel outil dopé à l'IA pour repérer votre abri de jardin non déclaré
articles.text:
Déployée par la direction générale des finances publiques, cette technologie dopée à l’IA croise les images satellites avec le cadastre pour repérer les constructions non déclarées. Derrière cette chasse aux mètres carrés oubliés se cache une volonté de redresser les comptes publics et de traquer la moindre taxe foncière ou d’aménagement qui échappe encore aux radars de l’administration.
L’IA au service du fisc
Après Google Maps, c’est désormais l’IA qui permet de détecter les « erreurs » de déclarations foncières. Le dispositif baptisé « Foncier Innovant » permet de détecter des millions d’anomalies sur le territoire. Il s’appuie sur des algorithmes fournis par le groupe Capgemini et l’entreprise Esri France. En automatisant l’analyse des clichés aériens de l’Institut national de l’information géographique et forestière, le système identifie les piscines, les vérandas et les cabanons de jardin qui n’apparaissent pas sur les déclarations fiscales des contribuables.
Ayant déjà permis de dénicher plus de 140 000 piscines non déclarées lors de phases de test menées dans neuf départements, le programme est généralisé à l’ensemble du pays. Chaque direction départementale des finances publiques dispose désormais de ces données pour envoyer des avis de régularisation aux propriétaires épinglés, entraînant parfois des rappels de cotisations rétroactifs sur plusieurs années. Cela a permis aux communes de toucher 40 millions d’euros de recettes fiscales supplémentaires.
Quels risques pour les propriétaires ?
Concernant les sanctions financières, les contribuables épinglés s’exposent à des régularisations salées comprenant le paiement rétroactif des taxes dues, mais aussi des pénalités pour retard ou omission de déclaration. La taxe d’aménagement, due une seule fois lors de la construction, et la taxe foncière, calculée annuellement sur la base de la valeur locative cadastrale augmentée, viennent ainsi alourdir la note.
À lire : Test Ecovacs Goat A1600 LiDAR Pro : le robot tondeuse qui veut en finir avec les bordures
Pour rappel, tout abri de jardin entre 10 et 15 m2 qui peut servir de pièce annexe doit faire l’objet d’une déclaration préalable de travaux en mairie. L’oubli de cette formalité administrative, longtemps toléré par manque de moyens humains sur le terrain, se solde dorénavant par une facture. Les propriétaires sont donc plus que jamais dans le collimateur de l’État qui est prêt à tout pour augmenter ses recettes fiscales.

articles.title: « Les actes ont des conséquences » : le bras de fer qui secoue l'usine Volkswagen de la future Golf électrique - Numerama
articles.text:
La fin d’année s’annonce particulièrement tendue au siège historique de Volkswagen. Fin octobre 2026, une fuite révélait que le constructeur avait mis sur pause le développement de sa future Golf 100 % électrique (ou ID. Golf), alimentant les craintes sur les difficultés financières du groupe. Le 6 novembre dernier, lors d’une table ronde organisée à Xiamen (Chine) avec un groupe de journalistes français, dont Numerama, le patron de la marque Thomas Schäfer a confirmé ce gel temporaire et en a détaillé la cause.
Quelques jours plus tard, la réponse industrielle du site allemand se précise. Selon les informations publiées ce 11 novembre par Automotive News Europe, Volkswagen a décidé d’abandonner le programme industriel « Gamechanger » et son projet de gigacasting à Wolfsburg, préférant revenir à des méthodes d’assemblage plus conventionnelles pour sécuriser le lancement de ses prochains modèles électriques.
Un coup de pression nécessaire à l’usine de Wolfsburg
À Xiamen, le 6 novembre, Thomas Schäfer n’a pas cherché à enrober la situation pour expliquer pourquoi le programme ID. Golf a été figé : la sanction visait directement son usine mère. « Chaque usine a un objectif de réduction des coûts à respecter. Toutes les usines Volkswagen ont atteint leur objectif. Pas Wolfsburg. Ils ont raté leur cible d’environ 300 millions d’euros », a détaillé le dirigeant avec une franchise rare.
Face à ce dérapage budgétaire, Thomas Schäfer a choisi l’épreuve de force : le développement du véhicule resterait suspendu tant que la direction du site n’aurait pas présenté un plan d’économies à la hauteur du manque à gagner. Une réunion était prévue la semaine suivante, celle du 9 novembre. « Pour l’instant, c’est en pause, parce que 300 millions d’euros, c’est le coût de développement de la carrosserie d’une nouvelle voiture. Si vous gaspillez l’argent, vous ne pouvez pas avoir de nouvelle voiture. C’est aussi simple que cela », a-t-il tranché.
Thomas Schäfer nous a assuré que les futurs modèles restaient dans les temps. Le calendrier a pourtant déjà glissé, puisque l’ID. Golf, longtemps attendue en 2028, est désormais annoncée par Volkswagen pour le « début des années 2030 ». L’usine de Wolfsburg doit néanmoins rapidement améliorer ses résultats financiers.
Interrogé sur la portée psychologique d’un tel coup de frein au sein d’un groupe souvent critiqué pour son inertie, Thomas Schäfer a assumé la méthode forte : « L’équipe doit apprendre que les actes ont des conséquences. Nous sommes tous dans le même bateau, nous devons tenir nos chiffres pour nous défendre dans cet environnement ultra-concurrentiel. Si une équipe ne fait pas sa part du travail, il doit y avoir des conséquences. »
Wolfsburg renonce au gigacasting et revoit sa méthode de production
L’arbitrage tombe cinq jours après ce rappel à l’ordre, mais il dépasse le seul cas de Wolfsburg. Un porte-parole du groupe Volkswagen a confirmé ce mercredi 11 novembre que le programme « Gamechanger » ne sera pas déployé « sous sa forme initialement prévue ».
Concrètement, Volkswagen renonce à transformer Wolfsburg en usine vitrine équipée de presses géantes de gigacasting, une technique popularisée par Tesla qui consiste à mouler d’immenses sections de châssis en aluminium d’une seule pièce. Selon le Handelsblatt, le seul centre de fonderie aurait coûté plusieurs centaines de millions d’euros, et l’ensemble du programme quelques milliards. Un investissement qui a longtemps fait débat en interne.
Côté produits, ce renoncement permet toutefois de préserver l’essentiel. Le développement de la future plateforme SSP (Scalable Systems Platform) se poursuit, et les versions électriques du T-Roc, puis de la Golf, doivent toujours sortir de Wolfsburg, pour un volume annoncé de plus de 500 000 unités par an à elles deux. Côté direction, le transfert de la Golf thermique vers l’usine mexicaine de Puebla, prévu en 2027, reste au programme. Simplement, ces futures compactes électriques seront assemblées selon des procédés plus classiques, bien moins gourmands en investissements initiaux.
En une semaine, Wolfsburg a perdu son chèque en blanc, pour l’ID. Golf comme pour son usine vitrine. Sur le principe, c’est une bonne chose.
Volkswagen renonce à rattraper Tesla sur l’usine du futur. Sur le plan financier immédiat, la décision se défend, puisque le groupe évite d’engager quelques milliards d’euros au moment où ses comptes se tendent. Pour autant, Gamechanger devait justement faire baisser le coût de fabrication de l’ID. Golf et du T-Roc électrique. En revenant à des lignes classiques, Volkswagen économise sur l’investissement de départ, mais il lui faudra prouver que ses deux futures stars peuvent quand même sortir à un prix compétitif. Pourvu que le calcul tienne !

articles.title: Chez Logitech, la sortie de GTA VI mérite un jour de congé pour 7 000 salariés
articles.text:
Une journée manette en main, avec l’accord du patron : c’est le nouvel avantage proposé par Logitech. Chacun pourra choisir son jeu et utiliser cette journée jusqu’en novembre 2027.
À une semaine à peine de la sortie de GTA VI, certains joueurs regardent leur calendrier de congés avec insistance. Chez Logitech, une case supplémentaire vient de s’ouvrir. Le fabricant de périphériques a annoncé le 10 novembre son « Logi Game Day », une journée offerte à ses équipes pour jouer. L’entreprise présente cette initiative comme une première à l’échelle du groupe.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Chacun choisit son jour et son jeu
Le dispositif concernerait environ 7 000 employés dans le monde. Les stagiaires peuvent également en bénéficier, précise Tom’s Hardware. Chacun pourra choisir sa date au cours des douze prochains mois, sans obligation de forcément poser sa journée pour jouer à GTA VI. 
Logitech G organisera néanmoins un événement diffusé en direct ce jour-là, depuis son siège Amériques de San Jose. Robin Piispanen, directeur général de Logitech G et ancien joueur compétitif, animera les festivités. Dans le communiqué du fabricant, il cite GTA VI, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 et Forza parmi les jeux auxquels les équipes pourraient consacrer leur temps.
D’autres entreprises ont déjà adapté leur calendrier. Le préparateur automobile californien Burger Motorsports a ainsi annoncé une fermeture le 19 novembre, après plusieurs demandes de congés de ses employés, rapporte GTA BOOM. Une décision plus radicale que la journée laissée au choix des équipes de Logitech.
Logitech revendique les bénéfices du jeu vidéo
« Il est temps d’en finir avec le cliché selon lequel jouer est une perte de temps », estime Hanneke Faber, directrice générale de Logitech. Le fabricant défend l’idée que certaines compétences mobilisées en jeu peuvent aussi servir au travail.
Pour appuyer ce discours, le groupe cite son étude Ctrl Tomorrow, réalisée par Burson en mai et juin 2026 dans neuf pays, dont la France. Sa méthodologie distingue 8 168 adultes et un questionnaire séparé auprès de 1 350 décideurs IT. Selon le résumé qu’en donne Logitech, 81 % des joueurs interrogés associent le jeu à davantage de confiance, moins d’anxiété et de meilleures performances professionnelles au quotidien.
Une autre enquête publiée par Logitech, menée par Harris Poll auprès de 600 décideurs IT aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni et en Australie, avance que 98,8 % jugent leurs compétences de joueur liées à celles utilisées dans leur métier. Les répondants citent notamment la réflexion stratégique, la résolution de problèmes et la capacité à travailler sous pression.
Ce dernier panel est toutefois composé exclusivement de joueurs réguliers : tous déclarent jouer au moins cinq heures par semaine. Le résultat renseigne donc sur leur perception de leur propre pratique, sans permettre de comparer leurs performances à celles de non-joueurs.
Ces études commandées par le fabricant ne démontrent pas qu’offrir une journée pour jouer améliore la productivité. Pour les employés, l’avantage est en revanche immédiat : du temps supplémentaire pour leur loisir. Logitech n’a pas précisé si cette journée serait reconduite chaque année.

articles.title: Switch-Bastler aufgepasst: Nintendo lässt Modchip-Software sperren
articles.text:
Nintendo hat bei GitHub insgesamt 144 Repositories mit Firmware für Switch-Modchips sperren lassen. Im Mittelpunkt steht der quelloffene Modchip Picofly. Mit ihm lassen sich auch Switch-Konsolen öffnen, die gegen reine Software-Hacks abgesichert sind. Damit ist dann eigene Software („Homebrew“) möglich, aber auch der Verstoß gegen Urheberrechte, so der Vorwurf von Nintendo.
Nintendos Argumente
Den Antrag nach dem US-Urheberrechtsgesetz DMCA – es erlaubt Rechteinhabern, Inhalte schnell sperren zu lassen – hat Nintendo of America auf den 6. November datiert. GitHub hat ihn am Dienstag in seinem öffentlichen DMCA-Archiv veröffentlicht. Formal richtet er sich nur gegen das Repository Ansem-SoD/Picofly. Weil das Netzwerk aus Forks – also Kopien und Abwandlungen des Projekts – mehr als 100 Repositories umfasst und Nintendo alle davon als rechtsverletzend einstuft, sperrte GitHub gleich das gesamte Netzwerk, berichtet TorrentFreak.
Nintendo argumentiert, die Firmware umgehe die technischen Schutzmaßnahmen der Konsole, damit sie illegale Spielekopien ausführen kann. Konkret geht es um die Bootsequenz der Switch. Diese prüft Nintendo mit eigenen kryptografischen Schlüsseln ab, der Modchip hebelt die Prüfung aus. Neben Picofly nennt Nintendo auch die Firmware der Modchips SX Core, SX Lite und HWFLY.
So funktioniert der Modchip
Konsolen, die Nintendo seit Mitte 2018 produziert, sind gegen die Sicherheitslücke „Fusée Gelée“ abgesichert. Über diese Lücke ließen sich ältere Geräte per Software für eine eigene Firmware öffnen. Auf allen gepatchten Konsolen klappt das nur noch mit einem Modchip. Bastler löten den Chip in die Konsole ein. Beim Start erzeugt er gezielte Spannungseinbrüche, ein sogenanntes Voltage Glitching. Dadurch überspringt die CPU die Firmware-Prüfung. Statt des Original-Bootvorgangs lädt die Switch dann eine Datei von der microSD-Karte.
Picofly basiert auf dem Mikrocontroller RP2040 von Raspberry Pi und ist laut Anleitung quelloffen. Die Autoren unterstützen ausschließlich diesen Chip. Bei kommerziellen Modchips wie HWFLY oder SX Core helfen sie nur beim Aufspielen neuer Firmware, nicht beim Einbau oder beim Kauf. Custom Firmware lässt sich für Schwarzkopien nutzen – aber eben auch für Homebrew, also selbst programmierte Software, die Nintendo offiziell nicht zulässt. Das geht nun schwerer.
Wie Nintendo das Vorgehen begründet
Zur Begründung seiner Forderung verweist Nintendo auf das US-Strafverfahren gegen mutmaßliche Mitglieder der Hackergruppe Team Xecuter. Sie verkaufte die Modchips SX Core und SX Lite, die auf allen damals erhältlichen Switch-Modellen funktionierten. Gegen Verkäufer dieser Hacks zog Nintendo 2020 vor Gericht. Der Betreiber der Seite UberChips stimmte schließlich einem Urteil über zwei Millionen US-Dollar Schadenersatz zu. Nach der Strafverfolgung stellte Team Xecuter den Betrieb faktisch ein. Die Chips lebten in kompatiblen Alternativen wie HWFLY und Picofly weiter.
Der Betreiber des Picofly-Repositories kann mit einer Gegendarstellung gegen die Sperre vorgehen. Im Archiv von GitHub ist laut TorrentFreak aber bisher keine verzeichnet.

articles.title: Keralam positions itself as a value-driven launchpad for deeptech startups
articles.text:
Keralam positions itself as a value-driven launchpad for deeptech startups
The Keralam government is keen to enhance the value of its startup ecosystem especially with the deeptech segment providing financial and other infrastructure support
Keralam wants to build its startup ecosystem and lead from the front, especially in deeptech and AI.
At the inaugural of Huddle Global 2026, a beachside startup festival of the Keralam government, Chief Minister V D Satheesan said, “Our next task is to take Kerala's companies to the world. Kerala does not need the most startups. It must be the place where startups grow stronger.”
The state which had about 300 startups in 2016 now has around 9,200 such young companies with a combined valuation of $1.7 billion. The startup segment of Keralam has attracted over Rs 8,500 crore of funding.
Huddle Global has been positioned by the Keralam government as a showcase of its startup ecosystem and the inaugural edition was held in 2018.
The chief minister said there will be a shift in its approach for its startup ecosystem where the first phase was all about a mission and the second phase is to scale this mission.
He also highlighted that the state government has been supporting the startups through a fund of funds programme and is looking to strengthen this initiative by increasing the limits of its innovation grants, R&D support and seed funding.
“Our aim is simple. In Kerala, a good idea should never fail for the lack of capital,” Satheesan remarked.
The Chief Minister also stressed on the role of future technologies coming into play and the State government is looking to strengthen its incubation network through stronger partnerships with academia.
P K Kunhalikutty, Minister for Industries, IT, Future Technology and Startups, Keralam said, “Our focus will also be on emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence.” He further added that the government will bring in more initiatives in this segment to attract investments.
“Kerala is entering an important phase of economic transformation. We are focusing on attracting domestic and international investment, promoting emerging industries and creating new opportunities for sustainable growth,” the minister said.
S Suhas, Special Secretary, Electronics and IT Department, government of Keralam, highlighted the progress made by the startup ecosystem in the State. This includes building an edge AI chip, a satellite launch along with SpaceX, a mechanical manhole cleaning machine that has bagged in contract in Singapore etc.
“In Keralam one no longer has to ask whether it can build startups. The question today is how big they can grow,” he remarked.
The official said the government has taken numerous steps to encourage the startups in the State, especially becoming the first customers for these young companies.
He also stressed the growth of innovation centres in Keralam with over 600 colleges having such facilities with 63 incubators and over 10 lakh square feet of startup space.
The target of the Keralam government is to have around 100 deeptech startups valued at Rs 100 core and above.

articles.title: Outlook en panne : des milliers d’utilisateurs privés de leurs mails ce jeudi soir — Frandroid
articles.text:
Sur notre smartphone, l’application Outlook affiche un triangle bleu, deux petits plots de chantier gris et une phrase laconique : « Erreur lors du chargement du message ».
On n’est visiblement pas seuls à contempler cette illustration. Sur Downdetector, le site qui agrège les signalements d’internautes, la courbe d’Outlook s’est envolée en fin de journée.
En France, la plateforme comptait 402 signalements peu après 19 heures, soit son pic sur les dernières 24 heures. Le phénomène est bien plus massif outre-Atlantique, où les signalements ont commencé à grimper vers midi, heure de New York (18 heures à Paris).
Les symptômes se ressemblent : application qui ne charge plus, Outlook sur le Web qui reste blanc, boîte affichée comme « déconnectée » sans envoi ni réception.
Microsoft n’a encore rien confirmé
Au début de la panne, la page de statut officielle de Microsoft n’affichait aucun incident. Rien d’inhabituel : l’entreprise met souvent un moment à reconnaître un problème, et le détaille d’abord aux administrateurs informatiques dans le centre d’administration de Microsoft 365.
Aucune cause n’est connue à ce stade. Le service en cause pourrait être Exchange Online, le serveur de messagerie en ligne de Microsoft qui fait tourner Outlook.com et les boîtes mail professionnelles. Quand il flanche, l’application n’est plus qu’une coquille vide, quel que soit l’appareil utilisé.
Ce n’est pas la première alerte de l’année, loin de là. Le 22 janvier, Outlook tombait avec d’autres services de Microsoft 365. Fin avril, une panne de plus de dix heures empêchait de se connecter à Outlook.com, à cause d’un changement de configuration que Microsoft avait dû annuler. Le 2 juin puis le 31 août, Exchange Online flanchait à nouveau, la seconde fois en raison d’un problème de configuration du système d’authentification, selon Microsoft.
Que faire en attendant
Inutile de réinstaller l’application ou de changer son mot de passe : si le problème vient des serveurs de Microsoft, ça ne changera rien. On peut ouvrir Outlook sur le Web dans un navigateur, ce qui permet au moins de savoir si c’est l’appli ou le service entier qui coince.

articles.title: Synology patches a critical NAS flaw that could let attackers in without logging in
articles.text:
A hot potato: Despite recent controversies over its corporate policies, Synology still holds a large slice of the increasingly popular NAS market. When its devices are hit by dangerous security flaws, customers should take note. Hackers and cyber-criminals certainly will.
A newly published security advisory discloses two serious vulnerabilities in DiskStation Manager (DSM), the Linux-based OS used in Synology NAS products, one of them rated critical. The storage maker warned that the flaws could be abused to remotely access and attack vulnerable devices, giving cyber-criminals – or rogue AI agents, for that matter – an easy avenue to wreak havoc on users' data and local IT infrastructure.
Synology rates the SQL injection flaw "critical," with a 9.8 out of 10 score – the flaw could be abused to remotely access and attack vulnerable devices.
The advisory focuses on two vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-76954 and CVE-2026-85101. The first is an SQL injection bug in DSM's Auth API that lets remote attackers read or write arbitrary files, or carry out denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.
The second was found in DSM's rsync tool and could let attackers bypass authentication entirely to read specific files, write arbitrary files, or launch "limited" DoS attacks.
Synology rates the SQL injection flaw "critical," with a 9.8 out of 10 score in the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). The rsync bug is classed as "important," with an 8.6 base CVSS score. Both can be exploited remotely, without logging in, to attack vulnerable devices. Synology disclosed them roughly a month after releasing the DSM updates that fix them, a common practice that gives users time to patch before the details go public.
The NAS maker shipped the fixed DSM versions in October 2026, and the company now considers the issue "resolved." Users with automatic updates may already have the patch, but those on manual update policies should definitely check for new DSM releases. Fixes are available for DSM 7.4, 7.3, 7.2.2, and 7.2.1.
Synology credited external researchers from Viettel Cyber Security and Aytio with discovering and reporting the two flaws. Some users are calling the SQL injection bug in the login process an embarrassment for Synology's software stack, while others are touting their "satisfaction" at having replaced Synology's devices with competing NAS products.
The Taiwanese manufacturer was also criticized for forcing customers to use only "certified" hard disk drives in its NAS systems. The backlash grew so intense that Synology was ultimately forced to reverse course and let users install any HDD brand and model they wanted.

articles.title: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent
With a customer-managed knowledge base on Amazon Bedrock, you provision and scale the vector store, tune the embedding model and index settings, and plan capacity for each new data source. The migration guide in the Agent Toolkit for AWS helps you migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base. Managed Knowledge Base takes over that work and adds new retrieval capabilities, and your team keeps control of the content and the application that uses it.
Moving a production knowledge base means your team maps its configuration, creates the replacement, ingests content, updates the application’s retrieval call, and validates retrieval before switching traffic. To help, we added a knowledge base migration guide to the amazon-bedrock skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS. The guide gives your coding agent the context to plan the migration with you, starting with read-only discovery and a plan you review line by line. On your approval, the agent creates the new knowledge base and its data sources alongside the original, or writes a migrated infrastructure as code (IaC) template for your pipeline. Ingestion and updating your application’s Retrieve calls stay with you, and your agent can walk you through both.
In this post, we explain why we recommend the move and how the migration guide works, review the prerequisites, install the skill, plan a migration, update the application’s retrieval call, and validate retrieval before cutover.
Why move to Managed Knowledge Base
We recommend Managed Knowledge Base because it balances ease of use, retrieval accuracy, and cost.
AWS runs the store
With a Managed Knowledge Base, Amazon Bedrock handles ingestion, storage, indexing, and retrieval, and the store scales automatically as your content grows. Hybrid search, which combines keyword and semantic matching, is always on, with no index to configure. The knowledge base includes a managed embedding model, a managed reranker, and a built-in parser for multimodal file types.
You can still bring your own Amazon Bedrock embedding model when you create the knowledge base. On each retrieval request, you choose the managed reranker, an Amazon Bedrock reranking model, or no reranking. The managed reranker requires the managed embedding model.
Built-in capabilities
Managed Knowledge Base includes capabilities you’d otherwise build yourself:
- Native connectors ingest content directly from sources such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Microsoft SharePoint, and Atlassian Confluence. For the current list, see supported connectors. After the first full sync, later syncs pick up only changes, on demand or on a schedule. The Managed Knowledge Base includes a deletion safeguard to help protect against accidental bulk removal of indexed content.
- Access control list (ACL) awareness ingests document permissions with the content, so retrieval returns only what the signed-in user can access. For connectors that support it, such as Microsoft SharePoint and Atlassian Confluence, a real-time check against the source also catches permission changes since the last sync. ACL awareness doesn’t authenticate users, so your application must verify and pass the user’s identity.
- Agentic retrieval answers questions that a single search can’t by handling multi-part questions and retrieving iteratively. It can search more than one knowledge base in a single request.
- Integration with AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, exposes your knowledge base as a target. Any client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can then query the knowledge base, and the gateway handles authentication.
- Resource-based policies let applications in other AWS accounts use one team’s knowledge base. Scope each policy to the specific roles that call the knowledge base, and grant only the actions they use, such as bedrock:Retrieve.
Agentic retrieval, AgentCore Gateway integration, and resource-based policies are not available on customer-managed knowledge bases. For the AWS Regions where managed knowledge bases are available, and the features that AWS GovCloud (US-West) doesn’t support, see Supported AWS Regions.
Higher quotas
As of this writing, higher default quotas change how you can organize content. With 200 data sources per knowledge base, you can group related content in one knowledge base. With 10,000 knowledge bases per account, per Region, each team or product line can use a separate knowledge base.
| Default quota | Customer-managed | Managed | 
| Knowledge bases per account, per Region | 100 | 10,000 | 
| Data sources per knowledge base | 5 | 200 | 
| Concurrent ingestion jobs per knowledge base | 1 | 50 | 
| Query input characters | 1,000 | 10,000 | 
For current values, see Amazon Bedrock endpoints and quotas and Service quotas for managed knowledge bases.
Pay for what you store and retrieve
Cost is one of three things teams weigh when they consider this move, alongside customizability and direct control of the vector store. On a customer-managed knowledge base, you choose, provision, scale, and update the vector and text stores, and pay separately for the infrastructure you select. On a Managed Knowledge Base, those stages are part of the service, and storage and retrieval are metered directly.
The pricing models can differ too. With a customer-managed knowledge base, storage and retrieval charges depend on the vector store you choose. Some stores charge for provisioned or minimum capacity, and others, such as Amazon S3 Vectors, a capability of Amazon S3, charge only for what you use. A Managed Knowledge Base is priced on what you store and retrieve, so cost follows real usage. Usage-based pricing can fit enterprise question-answering, policy, and support knowledge bases that run at low utilization. For current rates, see Amazon Bedrock pricing. For the parsers available on a customer-managed knowledge base and how each is billed, see Parsing options for your data source.
| Cost driver | Customer-managed knowledge base | Managed Knowledge Base | 
| Vector storage | Priced separately by your chosen store. A provisioned retrieval service can have a minimum idle cost even at low volume | Included in the base storage rate of $5 per GB per month | 
| Multimodal document parsing | Requires Amazon Bedrock Data Automation, billed by page or image, or a foundation model, billed by token. Text-only parsing is free. | Included | 
| Embedding generation | Billed separately at your embedding model’s rate | Included with the default model. Charges apply only if you choose a custom model | 
| Ingestion, sync, and re-sync compute | Re-embedding, orchestration code, and indexing compute spikes on each sync add recurring cost | Included, with incremental sync that processes only new and changed content | 
| Connectors | Building and running custom connectors can add compute cost | Native connectors are included | 
| Standard retrieval | No Amazon Bedrock charge per query. Your vector store can charge per query, as Amazon S3 Vectors does. | $1 per 1,000 retrieval requests | 
| Reranking | Amazon Rerank is charged at $1 per 1,000 queries. A custom reranking model is billed at its own rate | Included in the $1 per 1,000 retrieval requests | 
| Agentic retrieval | You build the agentic workflow on a Bedrock model, which can cost roughly $18 to $24 per 1,000 queries before development and maintenance. Because model usage is billed by token, the price per query varies. | Agentic retrieval costs an additional $4 per 1,000 queries on top of the underlying retrieval calls, including multi-shot retrieval, reranking, and answer generation. Depending on the number of underlying retrieval calls, the total can range from roughly $6 to $9 per 1,000 queries. | 
Rates are only part of the total cost of ownership. On a customer-managed knowledge base, your team provisions, scales, and operates each stage as a separate resource. A Managed Knowledge Base consolidates them into one resource, with a default embedding model, foundation model, and reranker, and with per-knowledge-base rate limits by default. You manage the content and the application that uses it, and Amazon Bedrock operates the managed storage, embedding model, foundation model, and reranker.
Solution overview
A customer-managed knowledge base uses the VECTOR type, with a vector store you configure. A Managed Knowledge Base uses the MANAGED type. The migration guide directs your agent to create a new MANAGED knowledge base alongside the original without modifying or deleting the original during migration. Using the guide’s map, your agent writes a plan that lists which settings remain unchanged, which Managed handles differently, and which application changes you need to make. As Figure 1 shows, the original keeps serving every request while your team ingests content, validates, and cuts over.
How the migration guide works
The guide separates planning from implementation. In Explore mode, your agent answers questions about Managed Knowledge Base and can inspect your configuration with read-only calls, so you can estimate the effort. In Migration mode, the guide takes your agent through checkpoints:
- Introduce and choose. Your agent explains what it will and won’t touch. Choose the mode, a live knowledge base or IaC source, and a plain (default) or technical explanation style.
- Identify. Confirm the account and AWS Region. Your agent flags over-broad credentials, asks whether you want a cost analysis, and creates an output directory.
- Discover. Your agent reads the knowledge base and data sources with read-only calls, or reads your template files.
- Plan. Review the plan and application changes. By default, your agent stops here.
- Implement, if requested. For a live build, approve the exact preview of the provisioning script, and approve again if it changes. For IaC, your agent writes a migrated template and reports which schema checks ran.
- Handoff. Review what was produced and your team’s remaining steps.
As Figure 2 shows, resource creation stays separate from ingestion and cutover.
Review the configuration mapping
The guide maps each setting to preserve your data sources, filters, and chunking behavior when the managed type uses a different configuration. The plan classifies each setting:
- 1:1. The new knowledge base uses the same setting.
- Adjusted. Managed uses a different setting for the same outcome, and the plan applies the substitution.
- Blocked. There is no managed path today. Your agent excludes that knowledge base from the build, explains why, and points you to AWS Support. Other knowledge bases in the same run can proceed.
Compare chunking on your own content when you validate.
Review the permissions and generated changes
Discovery, planning, and the entire IaC path need only read-only credentials. For a live build, the guide directs your agent to propose a scoped policy that explicitly denies changes to the original knowledge base, and to never ask for administrator or full-access permissions. It also directs your agent to change only resources it created, reference secrets by Amazon Resource Name (ARN), and ignore instructions found in the data it reads. Review the generated AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy and provisioning script before you approve the run. After the build, check what the agent did in AWS CloudTrail event history, which keeps 90 days of management events. Each event records the API call, such as CreateKnowledgeBase, and the identity that made it.
For the optional cost analysis, your agent compares current spend with a Managed Knowledge Base estimate using current AWS prices. It uses read-only inputs, including Amazon CloudWatch metrics, Amazon S3 object sizes, and AWS Cost Explorer. Each figure is labeled as measured, supplied by you, or estimated.
Prerequisites
Use separate credentials for planning and for any approved resource creation.
- A compatible development environment with the Agent Toolkit for AWS.
- The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), configured with a least-privilege, read-only profile.
- Access to the original knowledge base configuration or its IaC files.
- For the optional live build: 
         
  - A scoped build profile, using the policy the guide recommends.
  - An IAM service role for the new knowledge base. The guide gives your agent the trust policy and permissions to help you create it.
  - Python 3 with boto3 for the generated provisioning script.
The Agent Toolkit for AWS works with compatible development environments and its repository on GitHub lists the available skills. Examples in this post use AWS CLI 2.37 and boto3 1.43.32.
Install the skill
Follow the Agent Toolkit for AWS getting-started instructions for your coding agent. The add-skill command installs the amazon-bedrock skill to the coding agents it detects. Add --agent to target one, for example --agent kiro.
After installation, your agent loads the migration guide when you describe a migration task. The following prompts are illustrative inputs, not transcripts.
Plan the migration
Choose the path that matches how you maintain the source.
| Path | What your agent reads | What it produces | AWS changes | 
| Explore | Documentation, and optionally your knowledge base (read-only) | Answers in the conversation | None | 
| Live knowledge base | Your knowledge base and data sources (read-only) | A plan, and optionally a new Managed Knowledge Base alongside the original | Only after you approve the exact preview | 
| Infrastructure as code | Your AWS CloudFormation template, AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) synthesized template, or Terraform configuration | A migrated template in the same format | None. Your pipeline deploys it | 
To start in Explore mode, ask a question:
When you’re ready, choose the live or IaC path.
Migrate a live knowledge base
Ask for a plan before authorizing resource creation:
Confirm the account and Region, then review the plan’s mappings and application changes. By default, the new knowledge base takes the original’s name with a -managed suffix. To build it, confirm the service role exists, switch to the build profile, inspect the provisioning script and its preview, and approve. Your agent runs the script, which creates the knowledge base and data sources, and reports their status.
Migrate infrastructure as code
Point your agent at the source template or configuration:
Your agent writes the migrated file to the output directory, deploys nothing, and shows you the diff. To keep the diff, ask your agent to save it. Run terraform init -backend=false and terraform validate before deployment. Your agent can walk you through both commands, but the guide leaves these checks to you because terraform init downloads the large AWS provider. Before you apply the deployment plan, check that it keeps the original resources you need for rollback.
Example conversation
The migration runs as a conversation. Before reading anything, your agent states its scope and asks how to proceed:
The plan summary shows each mapping, the caller changes, and the decisions you need to make:
For a live build, your agent stops at a preview, and the approval command requires the plan’s hash:
Example exchanges are lightly edited, with identifiers replaced.
Update the application’s retrieval call
Your application uses the same Retrieve operation for both types. The managed request targets the new knowledge base ID and replaces vectorSearchConfiguration with managedSearchConfiguration. Passing vectorSearchConfiguration to a managed knowledge base returns a validation error. Managed retrieval always uses hybrid search, so the managed request shape has no overrideSearchType field. Metadata filters keep the same syntax, except that managed knowledge bases don’t support the startsWith and stringContains operators. For the full syntax, see the Retrieve API reference.
The example assumes both knowledge bases contain the locale metadata used by the filter.
Validate retrieval and cut over
Evaluate the new knowledge base while the application still uses the original.
- If using IaC, review and deploy the target configuration through your pipeline.
- Sync each data source and review any failures. See Sync your data.
- Grant your application’s runtime IAM role bedrock:Retrieve on the new knowledge base ARN, and keep its access to the original knowledge base so you can roll back.
- Run representative queries against both knowledge bases with Retrieve, using that role. The two types use different score scales. Managed scores also depend on rerankingModelType, which defaults to MANAGED with the managed embedding model and to NONE with a custom one. Tune thresholds per mode, and hold the mode constant while comparing.
- Test metadata filters and permission-aware retrieval where used, including content the signed-in user shouldn’t receive. On an ACL-enabled data source, requests without userContext.userId (the user’s email) return no results.
- After acceptance, deploy the new knowledge base ID and request shape. Keep the original knowledge base, with current content, and application configuration through your rollback period.
For each query, check whether both return the same top document and how much results overlap. A short script can report pass or fail against criteria such as a matching top document on at least 90 percent of queries and no zero-result queries on the managed knowledge base. Tune that threshold for your workload. For other retrieval quality measures, such as context relevance and context coverage, see Use metrics to understand RAG system performance.
Watch for these differences when you compare results:
- Normalize source locations before comparison. A customer-managed knowledge base can return s3://bucket/key in location.s3Location.uri, and a managed knowledge base can return an https:// URL. Compare by object key.
- Compare the top result instead of assuming equal result counts. The two knowledge base types can return different numbers of results, and numberOfResults sets a maximum rather than a guarantee. Compare the top document, and review each query where it changes. For details, see Configure and customize queries for managed knowledge bases.
- Map renamed system metadata keys. For example, replace x-amz-bedrock-kb-data-source-id with _data_source_id in comparison code. Your own metadata attributes keep their names. For details, see Configure and customize queries for managed knowledge bases.
Clean up
If you complete the migration, retire the original only after the rollback period and a dependency review. Keep the source documents and buckets the managed knowledge base ingests from, and storage that other workloads use. Clean up IaC-managed resources through their owning template.
If you end the evaluation instead, keep the original and delete what you created in this order:
- Delete each managed data source and wait until it’s gone.
- Delete the managed knowledge base and wait until it’s gone.
- If you created the service role only for this evaluation, delete its inline policy, then the role.
- With a customer managed key, check aws kms list-grants for grants Amazon Bedrock created, which can remain after the knowledge base is deleted.
- Keep any S3 bucket that another knowledge base still reads.
Deletion protection on a managed data source limits how much a sync can delete, not whether you can delete the data source. Deleting the original knowledge base doesn’t delete its vector store, which continues to incur charges until you remove it. See Delete an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.
Conclusion
With Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, your team no longer runs a vector store or manages the underlying retrieval infrastructure. With the migration guide in the amazon-bedrock skill, you ask your agent for a plan, review it, and approve only the resources you want built.
To get started, set up the Agent Toolkit for AWS and ask your agent for a read-only assessment of your knowledge base. After migration, explore agentic retrieval for multi-part questions. To learn more, see Build enterprise search for agents with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base on the AWS Machine Learning Blog.

articles.title: Rogers rolls out early Black Friday deals, save on Galaxy, Pixel
articles.text:
Rogers has launched its early Black Friday offers with some deals and discounts on phones and more. We’ve checked the hottest offers and listed them for you here.

Get a $100 bill credit for every line you add with a financed phone. Rogers Red credit card holders can get an extra $100 Rogers Bank statement credit.

articles.title: Nebuly wants to help enterprises understand exactly what their AI investments are worth after raising $21M - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nebuly wants to help enterprises understand exactly what their AI investments are worth after raising $21M
An Italian startup called Nebuly S.r.l. says it’s going to help organizations better understand the impact their investments in artificial intelligence have on their bottom lines after raising $21 million in funding today.
The round was led by Planven and saw participation from backers including Exor Ventures, Tenacity Capital, TGVG Capital, Fastweb, Vodafone and CDP Venture Capital’s Digital Transition Fund.
The world’s biggest companies have been spending millions of dollars on artificial intelligence, but very few can actually say how much value those investments have returned. Though some leaders might be able to point to a few vanity metrics, they’ll likely stumble if pressed to come up with concrete numbers.
This is a problem because enterprise leaders are increasingly feeling the pressure to justify their investments in AI. A recent Gartner Inc. survey of business leaders found that 85% of respondents plan to step up their AI spending in the next year, but at the same time, only 22% say they have managed to scale the technology across multiple business units.
Meanwhile, spending is spiraling out of control at many companies. Famously, Uber Technologies Inc. revealed earlier this year that it had eaten up the entire budget it set aside for AI in 2026 in just four months.
Nebuly co-founder and Chief Executive Franceso Signorato told SiliconANGLE that one of the main challenges when it comes to understanding AI’s return on investment is that many companies have deployed a jumbled patchwork of AI models and applications. They’re using tools from OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic PBC, Microsoft Corp., Google LLC and others, as well as developing in-house tools under their own steam.
That makes it harder to see which projects are actually paying off and generating real business revenue. Although companies can track superficial metrics like token consumption and prompt tallies, genuine productivity gains remain obscured.
“Every enterprise is about to face the same question from its board, if it hasn’t already: What is AI actually worth to us? Nebuly exists to answer that question,” Signorato said. “Until now companies have measured AI by counting users, prompts and responses, which has fueled the rise of tokenmaxxing, where usage itself becomes the goal.”
Though it can be useful to keep track of who is using AI the most, Signarato said it doesn’t reveal if the technology is actually providing a net benefit to the company. “It doesn’t tell you whether an employee got back an hour of work or if a customer got the answer they needed,” he explained.
The lack of real insights can be risky, because AI is already starting to influence how business strategies and how companies spend money in other areas. “Companies are making decisions about hiring and head counts based on assumptions about AI productivity, not evidence,” Signorato said. “Decisions of that weight need real data.”
So it’s just as well that Nebuly claims to have the solution for these organizations. It has created an AI measurement platform that connects directly to the AI agents operating within its customer’s information technology environments, so it can study their behavior through a unified control plane.
Nebuly seeks to evaluate agentic productivity across two dimensions. In the case of internal, employee-facing agents, it tracks operational efficiency metrics, such as the number of hours of work they save human employees and the amount of capacity they free up.
It also takes into account net-new work that human teams couldn’t previously do. In addition, it identifies the kinds of work staff are applying AI to – such as routine, mundane tasks or higher-level strategic work, in order to help companies understand where their agents are most useful.
The platform also tracks external, customer-facing agents. With them, it monitors how they influence revenue, their impact on customer churn and their ability to generate upsell opportunities.
Auditability is a key concern, and so Nebuly ensures flexibility in terms of the financial assumptions it makes. This means financial teams can dig in and inspect the math it has come up with, to verify the performance insights it generates. The platform can be deployed on-premises or in private cloud environments in order to keep sensitive business data secure.
Nebuly’s insights are especially appealing to larger organizations. Almost all of its customers pull in annual revenue of more than $100 million, with about half exceeding $1 billion per year. They include Carl Zeiss AG, Iveco Group N.V. and Oura Health Oy. Most of those customers are based in Europe, but the funds from today’s round should help to change that, with Signorato planning to increase go-to-market hiring in the U.S.
Planven’s Giovanni Canetta Roeder said he’s backing Nebuly because he’s convinced that every large organization is going to need a way to measure AI’s return on investment. “Nebuly is building the way to do it,” he said. “The team turns what AI agents actually do into evidence of business value. That capability and the traction Nebuly has built among major enterprises made this a compelling investment for us.”
