articles.title: Google Photos va s'inspirer d'Apple pour une édition non destructrice de vos clichés
articles.text:
Sur Android 11 et versions ultérieures, retoucher une photo dans Google Photos ne crée plus de copie à chaque fois. Les modifications s’appliquent à l’original et peuvent être réglées après coup, comme sur l’app Photos d’Apple.
Magic Eraser, Unblur, retouches sur fichiers Ultra HDR ou C2PA : jusqu’ici, ces outils vous forçaient à enregistrer une deuxième version de l’image. Google annonce que ce n’est plus le cas, et votre galerie devrait donc moins s’encombrer.
Une édition non destructrice… Enfin !
Jusqu’à présent, chaque retouche avancée donnait un second fichier à côté de l’original. Quelques essais sur la même image, et la galerie se remplissait de variantes presque identiques. Si vous ne supprimiez pas tout de suite la version ratée, la retrouver quelques jours plus tard devenait pénible.
Google cite aussi l’Ultra HDR et le C2PA, deux types de fichiers qui forçaient eux aussi la copie. L’Ultra HDR, c’est un JPEG avec une information de luminosité en plus. Sur un écran compatible HDR, les zones lumineuses (ciel, lumières d’une ville) ressortent davantage, et sur un écran classique, la photo s’affiche normalement. Inutile pourtant d’avoir une photo Ultra HDR pour profiter du changement ; il vaut pour vos retouches en général, sur Android 11 et plus. Quant au C2PA, il ajoute au fichier un historique signé numériquement (qui a créé l’image, avec quel outil, quelles modifications, y compris par IA). De quoi vérifier d’où vient une photo et comment elle a été éditée.
Google Photos n'est pas seulement un espace de stockage d'images. C'est aussi un petit studio de retouche photo qui ravira le grand public grâce à ses nombreuses options et des modes d'amélioration par IA.
Désormais, à partir d’Android 11, l’enregistrement modifie directement l’image d’origine, mais dans une forme non destructrice. Concrètement, quand vous rouvrez l’éditeur après coup, les outils restent réglés sur votre dernier choix (un filtre ou la luminosité, par exemple). Il est donc possible de continuer à les ajuster ou de revenir à la version initiale.
Google Photos reprend donc le fonctionnement de l’app Photos d’Apple sur iPhone ou Mac. L’application garde toutefois l’option « Enregistrer une copie » pour ceux qui veulent conserver les deux versions. Le déploiement de cette nouveauté a démarré, mais aucune date de disponibilité certaine n'a été annoncée. Le mois dernier, nous rapportions que la retouche rapide de Google Photos, jusque-là réservée aux photos, s’étendait aux vidéos.

articles.title: Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview
articles.text:
Microsoft has released a public preview of a local command-line interface for Azure Logic Apps Standard, shipped as the logicapp extension for the Azure CLI. It adds project creation, workflow authoring, a local runtime, connector and connection management, run inspection, and test scaffolding to a tool that until now only managed deployed apps, so that a Standard workflow can be created, run, and tested without Visual Studio Code.
The extension installs automatically the first time an az logicapp developer command runs on Azure CLI 2.67.0 or later, and adds 19 command groups with 64 commands beside the thirteen existing cloud-management commands, which it leaves untouched. On the authoring side, project create creates or adopts a local project; workflow create, set, export, and validate work on individual workflow.json files with offline validation by default, and runtime start, stop, and show manage a local host on port 7071, launching the Azurite storage emulator when the project is configured for development storage.
The remaining groups reach into running and deployed apps. connector and connection inspect built-in and managed connectors and wire connections into a project or a deployed app, run and trigger history start, wait on, cancel and resubmit executions and download an action’s recorded inputs and outputs, and deployment package produces what the documentation calls a deterministic deployment package. Named context shortcuts hold a target so later commands do not repeat it.
(Source: Microsoft Community Hub)
The doctor and test commands say the most about who the tool expects to be typing. runtime doctor only reads: project files, tool versions, cached bundle evidence, loopback ports. It "never installs, downloads, starts, stops, repairs, decrypts settings, changes context, or contacts cloud storage," and it exits 1 for a required failure and 2 when a required check comes back unknown. Testing is split into three steps for the same reason. test create scaffolds a native SDK test project and stops before restoring a package or running anything, test plan writes a preflight report without executing a test, and test run is the only command that builds and runs them, under a deadline. The announcement lists limitations on that last step. In the pull request that added the extension, author Riley Evans goes further: native SDK test code is trusted rather than sandboxed, and the agent bootstrap command does not exist yet.
Sagar Sharma, a Microsoft MVP, wrote on LinkedIn that this is deliberate. The CLI is "literally pitched as adding determinism to local AI-assisted coding": an agent validates, runs, inspects and tests, then repeats until the run is green, and secrets reach it through stdin rather than on the command line. Sharma had already called the CLI the sleeper hit of Microsoft's recent Logic Apps announcements in an earlier write-up, on the grounds that an agent without a deterministic way to validate and run a workflow is guessing. Named contexts, capability discovery and the handling of secrets were his evidence that someone had designed for that case.
Sonny Gillissen, also a Microsoft MVP, put the same point in terms of a team's week. A new hire clones a repository and has a local runtime up "in minutes, instead of hours." A coding assistant drafting a workflow from a business requirement works "with an authoritative shell instead of assumptions." Integration flows get tested from the CI/CD pipeline instead of by hand. He called the CLI a bridge from today's development process to a fully automated one and, in passing, said an agent could test a workflow locally "without ever touching Azure at all."
That passing remark is the one Christos Panagiotidis, a Microsoft MVP and certified trainer, would test first. His pilot plan is explicitly a proposal rather than a report of a run, and its two main cautions come straight from Microsoft's own walkthrough. That walkthrough uses live Azure and Microsoft 365 resources, and some of its commands change deployed connections, so a local run has remote effects, whatever the terminal suggests.
Microsoft itself notes that validation "does not establish authorization or business correctness." Panagiotidis adds a housekeeping point: CLI extensions do not update with the CLI, so anyone comparing results across runs needs the CLI, extension, runtime and project versions recorded next to each result.
Microsoft has said a broader command surface will follow soon. Until then, the designer stays in VS Code. The CLI edits workflow.json directly; it cannot change the state of a running local app, and the pull request's own limits section concedes that Linux CI results prove neither native SDK execution nor execution against live Azure.

articles.title: Pour illuminer vos soirées, le JBL PartyLight Stick est à -44 % pendant le Black Friday sur Amazon — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le JBL PartyLight Stick parle surtout à celles et ceux qui ont déjà une enceinte JBL PartyBox à la maison. L’idée est simple : ajouter une barre LED qui suit l’ambiance musicale, avec des couleurs RVB et des effets ajustables depuis l’application JBL PartyBox. Dans le cadre du Black Friday 2026 chez Amazon, ce genre d’accessoire devient plus facile à glisser dans le panier, surtout si votre installation audio est déjà prête pour les soirées. Pour compléter une PartyBox sans transformer le salon en budget mariage, il est actuellement à moins de 50 euros.
L’offre en cours sur le JBL PartyLight Stick
- Des couleurs RVB synchronisées avec les enceintes JBL PartyBox compatibles Auracast
- Une autonomie annoncée de 8 heures, recharge complète en moins de 3 heures
- Une résistance IPX4 pratique pour supporter les éclaboussures
Lancé à 99,99 euros en septembre 2024 et vendu 89,99 euros hors promotion, le JBL PartyLight Stick perd 40 euros chez Amazon, où il est disponible à 49,99 euros.
Une barre lumineuse pensée pour accompagner une PartyBox
Une fois posé dans la pièce, le PartyLight Stick sert avant tout à créer une ambiance visuelle autour de la musique. Il ne remplace évidemment pas une enceinte et ne produit pas de son, mais il complète une installation JBL PartyBox avec des jeux de lumière synchronisés. Pour une soirée à la maison, c’est typiquement le petit accessoire qui évite la lumière blanche de plafonnier. Pas très rock’n’roll, le plafonnier.
Les réglages permettent d’agir sur le mouvement, la vitesse, l’intensité et les couleurs. Vous pouvez donc rester sur une ambiance assez douce, ou pousser les effets si la playlist commence à sérieusement bouger. Le format bâton (1,08 mètre de haut pour 1,15 kilogramme) reste aussi plus simple à placer qu’un gros projecteur, même si l’effet dépendra beaucoup de la taille de la pièce et du nombre de sticks utilisés.
Application JBL PartyBox, autonomie et résistance aux éclaboussures
L’application JBL PartyBox sert de télécommande pour choisir les couleurs, les motifs et la vitesse des animations. Elle permet aussi de connecter plusieurs JBL PartyLight Stick, ce qui devient intéressant si vous voulez répartir les effets lumineux dans la pièce. L’accessoire prend surtout son sens dans l’écosystème JBL PartyBox. Sans enceinte compatible, il reste utilisable : son micro intégré repère la musique qui passe et cale les effets dessus, à condition de mettre le son assez fort.
JBL annonce jusqu’à 8 heures d’autonomie, avec une recharge complète en moins de 3 heures via USB-C (le câble est fourni, pas le chargeur). C’est cohérent pour couvrir une soirée sans devoir chercher une prise au milieu du morceau. La certification IPX4 ajoute une sécurité contre les éclaboussures, pratique près d’une piscine ou sur une terrasse, mais elle ne transforme pas le produit en lampe étanche à immerger.

articles.title: SA fintech startup Lumepay raises $6m pre-seed round - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African cross-border payments startup Lumepay has raised US$6 million in pre-seed funding, alongside US$10 million in capital float, as it builds institutional-grade payment infrastructure for African businesses.
Led by CEO Harry Huang, Lumepay provides cross-border payment solutions for SMEs, corporates and institutions. Its rail-agnostic platform combines traditional finance and stablecoins to enable fast, cost-effective and transparent B2B transfers within and across African jurisdictions.
The startup launched Lumetrade, its digital asset and stablecoin trading venue, in April, before rolling out its payments platform in June, and has now raised US$6 million in pre-seed funding. The round was backed by founder-led angels and South African fintech investors. The US$10 million capital float was secured to give clients access to deep, reliable liquidity.
“The future of cross-border payments isn’t traditional finance or stablecoins; it’s a combination of both, backed by the FX depth to make them work for real businesses,” said Huang. “Our integrated approach addresses the real drivers of friction: fragmentation, liquidity inefficiency and execution risk.”
Lumepay is now live in Nigeria, Ghana, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique and Kenya, as well as the West and Central African CFA franc zones, and is awaiting further regulatory approvals to expand its payment capabilities in these markets.
Last month, the startup received regulatory clearance from the Central Bank of Kenya, marking its entry into East Africa. Businesses in Kenya can now use Lumepay to pay international suppliers in currencies including Chinese yuan, US dollars and Indian rupees, and to move money across intra-African trade corridors.
“In the months since the raise, we’ve turned plans into working products: diversified and reliable liquidity; a platform that handles cross-border payments end to end; a growing network of partners and payment rails; and regulatory clearance in South Africa and Kenya,” said Luc Varejes, Lumepay’s COO.
In South Africa, Lumepay works with Nedbank as its Third-Party Payment Provider (TPPP) sponsoring bank, while sister business Lume Trade, an authorised financial services provider covering crypto asset intermediary services, banks with Standard Bank.
“Working with Nedbank and Standard Bank across our two businesses reflects the compliance standards we have built from day one,” said Tatenda Nhemachena, Lumepay’s chief legal and compliance officer.
The pre-seed funding has been used to build out Lumepay’s core infrastructure, including its payment rails, banking relationships, regulatory approvals and licensed partner network. The startup is now focused on expanding its regulatory footprint across Southern, West and Central Africa, with Malawi, Mozambique and the CFA franc regions key targets, as it lays the groundwork for a Series A round.

articles.title: New N-able "4EverAble2Shell" zero-day exploited hours after PoC released
articles.text:
Hackers are actively exploiting a newly disclosed N-able N-central zero-day vulnerability dubbed "4EverAble2Shell" to compromise servers and deploy cryptocurrency miners, with researchers reporting at least 21 affected systems, including 19 running the company's latest security update.
The attacks follow security researcher Sean Bales' release of two new zero-day exploits today, dubbed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, which he says allow attackers to gain root-level access to N-central appliances and SYSTEM-level access to Windows systems.
N-central is a remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform used by managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams to monitor, manage, and secure customer devices and networks remotely.
The new vulnerabilities were disclosed on November 12, just two days after N-able released emergency security updates to address critical N-central zero-day vulnerabilities that Bales had publicly disclosed earlier this week.
Bales published proof-of-concept exploits for both the 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell vulnerabilities, saying they were tested against N-central Appliance 2026.4.1.26 HF2, the security update N-able released on November 10.
The 4EverAble2Shell exploit allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands as root on vulnerable N-central servers. However, the researcher says exploitation requires the platform's Legacy API functionality to be enabled.
The attack combines an Apache Axis vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-90436, with a separate N-central privilege escalation weakness to gain root-level access.
The second exploit, Agent2Shell, targets N-central's agent functionality and is claimed to allow attackers to execute commands with SYSTEM privileges on Windows devices.
The disclosures came after N-able took its hosted N-central environments offline earlier this week and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers after Bales published more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities.
Bales has criticized N-able's handling of the vulnerability disclosures and the company's slow response to patching responsibly disclosed flaws.
"It's much much easier for me to just release the research I have and the vendor can decide what they want to do with it, what they do and don't want to fix, etc. :)," Bales told BleepingComputer.
Bales said N-able has not patched two unrelated RCE vulnerabilities in a different N-able product that he previously disclosed to the company in July.
In a November 12 security advisory, N-able said it was implementing additional protections in response to the new disclosures, including restricting certain N-central features and integrations while it develops further fixes.
"We are restricting certain N-central features and integrations," N-able said.
"These measures may affect some functionality, but we believe taking additional precautions while remediation is completed is the right action to protect our partners and their customers."
The company says it has disabled the Intune integration as a precaution and is urging on-premises customers to ensure Legacy API access is disabled, which is already the default.
The protections have already been applied to hosted environments, but customers are also advised to continue upgrading their Agents and Probes under the previous Hotfix 2 guidance.
In its advisory, N-able said it had seen no signs of compromise using the new flaws, although security researchers have since reported successful exploitation of the vulnerability against production N-central servers.
Hackers already exploiting 4EverAble2Shell
Cybersecurity company Previdian told BleepingComputer that attackers began probing for the 4EverAble2Shell vulnerability on November 12, shortly after the public release of the proof-of-concept exploit.
The company first observed suspicious requests targeting its N-central honeypot at approximately 08:30 UTC, using the same Java class referenced in the publicly released exploit.
While the initial requests were limited to probing for vulnerable servers, Previdian later confirmed that attackers were attempting to execute the complete exploit chain against its honeypot server.
The attacks initially exploit Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 to execute commands as the 'nable' service account, then exploit a separate N-central privilege escalation vulnerability to obtain root privileges.
This attack chain matches the POC Bales released on GitHub.
According to Previdian, the privilege escalation stage abuses N-central's privileged setLDFileOwner helper and a symbolic link to make a normally root-owned script writable.
The attacker then modifies the script and invokes N-central's serverControl functionality to execute commands as root, while attempting to restore the modified files afterward.
The payload attempted to download and execute an additional shell script from an attacker-controlled server at 157.20.241[.]16, while sending diagnostic information and command output back to the same IP address.
Previdian is tracking the N-central privilege escalation flaw as VULN-2026-0009 and has added it to its own Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
Cybersecurity company Huntback also reports that attackers have already successfully compromised at least 21 production N-central servers using Bales' publicly released exploit chain.
Huntback saw the same attacker IP address as Previdian probing its N-central honeypots at approximately 08:30 UTC on November 12, with the first attempts to execute the complete exploit chain beginning at 09:16 UTC.
The attacks seen by Huntback exploited the 4EverAble2Shell exploit chain to download a shell script that installed an XMRig Monero cryptocurrency miner.
The miner was configured to use about half of the available CPU cores, likely to make the mining harder to detect.
Huntback identified other compromised systems through the attacker's cryptocurrency mining pool statistics, where infected systems were assigned identifiers beginning with nc_ followed by the server's IP address.
At 12:50 UTC on November 12, the researchers found 21 active miners using this naming convention, all of which had submitted mining shares within the previous five minutes.
The researchers then checked the associated IP addresses and confirmed that all 21 hosted N-central installations, including 19 running version 2026.4.1.26, the latest Hotfix 2 release issued on November 10.
The compromised servers were located across multiple countries, including the United States, Canada, South Africa, the United Kingdom, Germany, France, and Sweden.
While the attacks observed so far have been primarily used for cryptojacking, attackers could use compromised N-central infrastructure for additional malicious activity targeting managed customer environments.
Organizations running N-central should ensure that Legacy APIs are disabled and investigate suspicious requests to /dms/services/ServerUI, especially those referencing jline.internal.TerminalLineSettings.
Huntback also recommends checking for unexpected xvd.service systemd services, cryptocurrency mining processes, and files created under /tmp/.xvd or /var/tmp/.xvd.
Because the 4EverAble2Shell attack grants full root access to exploited servers, organizations that detect these IOCs should treat the breach as a full compromise of the server.

articles.title: Karnataka open to subsidising GPU access for startups through AI hub
articles.text:
Karnataka may subsidise GPU access for startups through AI hub
The state could offer support beyond the Centre’s IndiaAI Mission. It is also considering shared manufacturing space for small companies near Bengaluru.
Karnataka is exploring whether it can subsidise access to graphics processing units (GPUs) for startups through its upcoming artificial intelligence hub at IIIT Bangalore. Karnataka IT and BT Secretary N. Manjula raised the possibility at a panel on how the state can support women in tech and entrepreneurship, after a founder building industrial smart cameras asked about cheaper computing power.
GPUs speed up AI model training and testing, and rental costs can limit how often early-stage startups experiment and refine their models.
When asked whether Karnataka could offer support on top of the Centre’s IndiaAI Mission, Manjula told YourStory after the panel, "We are open to looking at it.”
The central programme gives eligible startups access to subsidised cloud computing. Manjula gave no details on the budget, eligibility criteria, or the timeline for state support.
Rising hardware costs
IIIT Bangalore Director Debabrata Das said hardware costs, particularly for memory, had risen fourfold over the past year, with GPU prices seeing the next-biggest increase. He said the AI hub was looking at giving startups access to computing resources to test ideas and develop proofs of concept.
The Karnataka Cabinet approved the AI hub in September at an estimated cost of Rs 35 crore. The hub will offer AI training and startup support, and its planned AI Living Lab will provide computing infrastructure and a place to test applications. Das said more details were expected at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, which will be held from November 17 to 19.
Women-led startups account for 30–35% of ELEVATE winners
The panel provided women founders an opportunity to raise challenges they encounter at different stages of building and scaling their businesses.
Addressing the gathering, Manjula said, “Karnataka has consistently worked towards building a strong technology and startup ecosystem through policies and programmes that support the entire innovation journey, from skilling and research to incubation, funding and commercialisation. However, it is equally important for us to understand how these policies translate on the ground.
"This interaction is an opportunity to hear directly from women entrepreneurs, understand the challenges they face and identify areas where we can do better. The feedback shared today, particularly on access to funding, markets and infrastructure, will help us take these conversations forward and work towards more actionable solutions.”
Highlighting the state’s targeted interventions, she spoke about programmes such as Women@Work, WEscalate, BioWise and ELEVATE Shakti, which support women through skilling, incubation, mentoring, research exposure and financial assistance.
Under the latest edition of ELEVATE Shakti 2026, 63 women-led startups were selected, with grant support of Rs 23.19 crore committed. The broader ELEVATE Grant-in-Aid Programme has supported more than 400 women-led startups since 2017, with committed support of Rs 118.98 crore.
Women-led startups account for 30–35% of the winners of Karnataka’s ELEVATE programme each year, Manjula said. She added that the state had identified about 11 technology business incubators at academic institutions outside Bengaluru as part of its efforts to support founders beyond the city.
The cost of getting to proof of concept came up during the discussion. A biotech founder said she was using her savings to generate the early evidence she needed to qualify for a funding programme.
C-CAMP CEO Taslimarif Saiyed pointed to grants and incubators that can help founders at that stage and offered to discuss what support C-CAMP could provide.
Shared space for small manufacturers
Karnataka is also looking at a parcel of land roughly an hour from the Bengaluru airport where small companies could start manufacturing before they are able to afford premises of their own, Manjula said at the panel. She said discussions were at an early stage and raised the possibility of renting out space and setting up common facilities that companies in areas such as electronics and robotics could share.
Karnataka weighs how to deploy its Rs 300 Cr deeptech fund
A committee examining how Karnataka should deploy its Rs 300 crore deeptech fund of funds has drawn up recommendations and is expected to submit them to the government shortly, Manjula told YourStory. She gave no timeline for when investments could begin.
The Rs 300 crore figure matches the allocation for a fund of funds in Karnataka’s report on its LEAP initiative. Under this model, the state can channel public money through venture capital funds that invest in startups. That can help draw in private capital and leaves investment decisions to the fund managers.

articles.title: Kia India to invest $2B in second plant in Andhra Pradesh
articles.text:
Kia India to invest $2B in second plant in Andhra Pradesh
Spread across a combined 465 acres for Kia and its suppliers, the new facility is expected to generate around 12,000 direct and indirect job opportunities.
Kia India has committed a combined investment of $2 billion, along with its supplier partners, to set up its second manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh.
The carmaker signed a memorandum of understanding with the state government to formalise the plan.
The factory will be located in Anantapur, the same district that houses Kia's current plant. It will add 2 lakh units of annual manufacturing capacity, taking Kia India’s combined capacity across both plants to over 6 lakh units a year.
Kia India is targeting early 2030 for production to begin, with the plant carrying out stamping, welding, painting and assembly. This plant will manufacture new models across ICE and EV powertrains, the company said in a statement.
Kia and its suppliers will together occupy 465 acres on the new site. The company expects the facility to support roughly 12,000 jobs, both direct and indirect.
In comparison, the first plant, across 945 acres, employs 24,237 people through direct and indirect roles. Set up with an initial investment of $2.9 billion, the facility builds the Seltos, Syros, Sonet, Carens, Carens Clavis, Carnival and Sorento models, spanning ICE, EV, CNG and hybrid versions.
Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO, Kia India, said, “India is central to Kia’s long-term growth ambitions, and the trust our customers have placed in us since we began operations in Anantapur has been instrumental in our journey."
He continued, "Our second manufacturing plant marks a significant new chapter, strengthening our ability to respond to customer demand with greater speed and flexibility, while supporting the introduction of new models across ICE and EV powertrains.
"As we enter our next phase of growth, we remain committed to contributing to India’s automotive ecosystem and building on the strong foundation we have created here. This will further expand our Made-in-India footprint, strengthening our ability to serve both domestic and overseas markets.”
Kia said the project would also help build India's manufacturing base, generate employment, and support the wider auto industry.

articles.title: Au cœur du MacBook Pro PROLED XDR se cache une bonne nouvelle pour la réparabilité
articles.text:
Le tout nouveau MacBook tactile d’Apple ne se contente pas de faire mieux que ses prédécesseurs du côté des caractéristiques et de la fiche technique, il améliore aussi légèrement sa note de réparabilité iFixit.
Poussé par les différentes législations et le changement de mentalité qui les accompagne, Apple a fait des efforts sur la réparabilité de ces appareils ces dernières années. Cela s’observe d’ailleurs dans la conception de son tout dernier ordinateur tactile, le fort délicatement nommé MacBook Pro PROLED XDR.
Passé sur les bureaux d’iFixit, le tout nouvel ordinateur portable a décroché un 5/10 sur l’échelle de réparabilité de l’entreprise, en légère progression par rapport à l’année dernière.
Des cartes-mères interchangeables
Cette amélioration est surtout due au fait qu’Apple semble enfin avoir abandonné ses pratiques de sérialisation sur ses MacBook Pro. Pour rappel, la sérialisation est l’opération qui consiste à lier un composant à une machine spécifique grâce à son numéro de série. Développée sous prétexte d’améliorer la sécurité des appareils, cette méthode complique considérablement les réparations faites hors Apple-Store en raison de l’accès difficile au logiciel d’appariement.

L’année dernière, la carte mère d’un MacBook Pro M5 ne pouvait par exemple pas être changée par celle d’un autre MacBook Pro M5 sans perdre l’accès à la fonctionnalité TouchID. Cette année, rien de tel. D’après les tests d’iFixit, tout fonctionne même lors de l’échange de carte mère. Il est tout de même nécessaire de faire tourner l’outil de réparation de macOS prévu à cet effet, mais il semblerait que Apple ait arrêté de compliquer la vie des magasins indépendants et bricoleurs et bricoleuses du dimanche. Le droit européen à la réparation avait de toute façon interdit la sérialisation.
Des ports USB-C modulables
Sur la démontabilité de l’appareil en elle-même, pas grand-chose à dire de plus que l’année dernière, selon iFixit. Apple a légèrement simplifié les choses, mais les ports USB-C et les ventilateurs ne peuvent toujours pas être changés sans devoir démonter la carte mère. Heureusement, tout est tenu avec des vis ou presque. Seule la batterie est encore malheureusement collée, contrairement à celle du Neo, qui avait le bon goût de s’enlever en quelques coups de tournevis seulement.

Lors de notre exploration des entrailles de la machine, nous avons tout de même remarqué que beaucoup de vis différentes tenaient les différents composants et qu’extraire la batterie en six morceaux n’était pas à la portée du premier ou de la première venue. Le clavier ne peut pas non plus être changé sans remplacer tout le châssis.
Cette différence s’explique surtout par le critère du prix des pièces qui, relativement au prix de l’appareil, est moins élevé sur les modèles M5 Max que M5 Pro. Les modèles 14 pouces sont aussi un poil plus facile à démonter (7,3 contre 6,7 sur les modèles 16 pouces) si l’on en croit la note qu’Apple s’est auto-attribué.

articles.title: Nigerians can pay without cards or transfers, yet remain completely unaware
articles.text:
The next time a point-of-sale (PoS) agent asks for a bank card, inserting it may not be necessary. Some Nigerian cards can already complete transactions with a single tap.
TechCabal tested this at a local PoS merchant. Using a Verve debit card issued through ALAT, the digital banking platform of tier-2 Nigerian lender Wema Bank, the team held the card near the terminal instead of inserting it. The machine recognised the card, requested a PIN, and dispensed ₦1,500 ($1.11) from the ₦1,600 ($1.19) transaction, which included a ₦100 ($0.074) merchant fee. The cash withdrawal went through without the card being inserted into the machine.
It was a small transaction, but it demonstrated a payment capability already available on some Nigerian cards and PoS terminals, yet still unfamiliar to many consumers.
The feature is easier to spot than it may seem. Look for a small contactless symbol on the card or PoS terminal: four curved lines that resemble radio waves. The symbol is often mistaken for the Wi-Fi logo, but it signals something different. On a card, it means the card can make contactless payments; on a terminal, it means the machine can accept them. The tap works through Near Field Communication (NFC), a technology that lets devices exchange data when they are close to each other.
Contactless payments are not new to Nigeria. In May 2015, Unified Payments, a Nigerian payment processing company, introduced a Near Field Communication (NFC) payment solution.
In September 2022, global payments company Mastercard, Nigerian commercial bank Providus Bank, French digital security company Thales, and African payments technology company Interswitch launched tokenised tap-to-pay solutions for smartphones and wearables, following nine months of development.
Now, Google Pay’s October 2026 market entry and a growing number of homegrown fintech solutions are drawing renewed attention to a technology that has been in use in Nigeria for more than a decade.
These developments could expand how Nigerians pay and receive money. Customers can use compatible smartphones instead of physical cards, while merchants can turn NFC-enabled smartphones into payment terminals. Other companies are exploring contactless payments linked to bank accounts and digital wallets. But wider adoption will depend on whether banks, merchants, and consumers can make the technology work in everyday transactions.
From contactless cards to Google Pay
The most visible development in Nigeria’s contactless payments market came on October 28, when Mastercard and Interswitch announced that eligible Mastercard holders could use Google Pay to make contactless payments with compatible Android devices.
The launch, announced at the 2026 edition of Moonshot by TechCabal, lets customers add supported Mastercard cards to Google Wallet and pay at merchants with compatible contactless terminals using their phones. Instead of presenting a physical card, customers authenticate on their phone and hold it close to the PoS terminal.
The partnership brings together three different parts of the payment experience. Google provides the digital wallet through which customers store and access their payment credentials. Mastercard provides the card network and tokenisation infrastructure, while Interswitch connects participating card issuers to the processing and tokenisation capabilities required for the service to work.
The innovation lies in turning regular NFC-enabled smartphones into payment devices while existing card networks continue to handle the transactions.
Interswitch is working with five Nigerian banks—GTBank, Wema Bank, ProvidusUnity Bank, Zenith Bank, and FirstBank—to expand tokenised payments across digital wallets and banking apps. But the partnership does not give every customer of those banks immediate access to Google Pay. Google’s published list currently supports selected cards from FirstBank, GTBank, Providus Bank, UBA, and Zenith Bank.
Wema Bank, despite its involvement in Interswitch’s initiative, is absent from that list. So are Verve and AfriGO cards. Even customers with eligible cards still need NFC-enabled Android phones and merchants with compatible contactless terminals. The rollout exposes a gap between the institutions building Nigeria’s tap-to-pay infrastructure and the customers who can use it today.
Once users have added and verified an eligible card on an NFC-enabled smartphone, they can tap at a local PoS terminal to make payments. For merchants, however, accepting contactless payments requires more than an NFC-enabled terminal. Acquiring banks and payment processors must support the transaction, and the terminal must recognise the customer’s card network or digital wallet. A PoS machine can carry the contactless symbol and still reject certain payment methods.
Nigerian fintech companies are also working to expand where customers can tap and what they can tap with. CashAfrica, a payments startup, has introduced a contactless mobile payment service in partnership with the fast-food chain Chicken Republic. Nearpays, another Nigerian payments startup, is developing software that allows merchants to accept contactless payments directly on compatible smartphones.
Nearpays uses software-based point-of-sale technology (SoftPOS) to turn an NFC-enabled Android phone into a payment terminal. A merchant enters an amount in the Nearpays application, and the customer taps a contactless card or supported device against the phone. The software initiates the transaction through the payment processing system.
“We’ve built a product that sits as a mediator and can communicate easily to both parties,” Nearpays founder and chief executive officer Victor Daniyan told TechCabal.
According to Daniyan, Nearpays routes domestic card transactions through the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), the country’s payment switch, and international card transactions through Visa, with banking partners involved in processing.
The model could reduce one of the costs of accepting card payments: PoS hardware. Merchants with compatible smartphones may be able to accept payments without acquiring another device, although processing fees, security requirements, and settlement arrangements still apply. Its commercial appeal will depend on whether those savings outweigh the costs of using the service.
The approach has gained ground beyond Nigeria. In 2025, Visa, the global payments giant, said its Tap to Phone technology processed over $33 billion in payments, underscoring the scale of smartphone-based acceptance in other markets. But those figures offer no guarantee of similar adoption in Nigeria, where merchants and customers already have a familiar alternative in bank transfers.
Together, Google Pay, CashAfrica, and Nearpays show how companies are expanding contactless payments from both ends of a transaction. They are changing the devices customers use to pay, and the equipment merchants need to accept payment.
However, underneath those interactions, payment credentials still need to reach financial institutions securely, without unnecessarily exposing sensitive account or card information.
What tokenisation changes, and what it does not
A phone can imitate a payment card without storing or transmitting the card’s original number during each transaction. That is one of the advantages of tokenisation, the security technology underpinning services such as Google Pay, the newly launched product in Nigeria.
When a customer pays with Google Pay, the phone does not need to share the original card number with the merchant. Instead, it uses a digital stand-in for the card. That is essentially what tokenisation does.
Think of it as giving someone a spare key that works only under certain conditions, while keeping the original key safe. The token represents the customer’s card, but it cannot be used in all the same ways as the card number it replaces.
When a customer adds an eligible Mastercard to Google Wallet, the bank verifies the card, and Mastercard’s Digital Enablement Service (MDES) helps create a token linked to the phone. Each payment also carries a unique security code, called a “cryptogram,” which helps the payment network check that the transaction is authentic. The code changes with each transaction, making captured payment information harder to reuse.
If the phone goes missing, the bank or wallet provider can disable its token without necessarily cancelling the physical card.
Tokenisation works alongside NFC, but the two do different jobs. NFC lets the phone and PoS terminal exchange information when they are close together. Tokenisation helps keep the customer’s original card details out of that exchange. Banks and payment networks still check and approve the transaction before money moves.
Not every contactless card uses the same token system as Google Wallet. Tokenisation also protects online payments, where customers do not tap anything.
For Nigerian payment companies, the greater opportunity may lie in expanding contactless payments beyond card networks.
Bank transfers already dominate much of Nigeria’s digital payment activity. In its Payments System Vision 2028 (PSV 2028) strategy document released in June, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) said that web and Internet transfers accounted for 51.9% of retail non-cash transaction volumes as of June 2024, compared with 28.5% for PoS transactions.
Nigerians have become accustomed to paying directly from their accounts, creating a commercial challenge for any product that asks them to adopt another payment method.
CashAfrica is attempting to build on that behaviour by developing account-based tokenisation. Rather than requiring a customer to hold a physical card, the company said it can create a digital identifier (a token) linked to a bank or fintech account and use it to initiate contactless payments.
Malik Asamu, the company’s founder and chief executive officer, argued that the opportunity lies in adapting contactless infrastructure to a market where consumers are more accustomed to using accounts than cards.
“If we can build an innovation that allows us to tokenise accounts, like we do cards, that then means that you can tokenise an account in the same model that you tokenise a card,” Asamu told TechCabal.
CashAfrica’s approach differs from Mastercard’s card-tokenisation model. Mastercard substitutes a card credential that already operates on its payment network. The fintech aims to make account balances accessible via a contactless payment experience, which requires identifying the account, authenticating the customer, and initiating a transaction through participating financial institutions.
The payment journey Asamu described, however, still involves an intermediary wallet. Customers first transfer money in the CashAfrica Cash Mobile app, select “Tap to Pay,” authenticate with a PIN or biometrics, and tap a compatible merchant terminal.
That introduces a commercial hurdle. A customer who already has money in a bank account must move it into another wallet before paying. For someone accustomed to making an instant transfer from a banking app, the additional step could offset the convenience of tapping a phone.
CashAfrica’s longer-term ambition is to make contactless payments available through existing banking and fintech applications.
Tokenisation protects card details, but it cannot prevent all forms of payment fraud. EMVCo, the international body that sets payment technology standards, said the technology limits what criminals can do with stolen card information.
However, in Nigeria, fraud increasingly relies on tricking customers into revealing sensitive information or gaining unauthorised access to their accounts. According to NIBSS, financial institutions lost ₦25.85 billion ($19.2 million) to digital payment fraud in 2025, even as losses fell by 51% from the previous year.
NIBSS noted that social engineering, account compromise, SIM-swap fraud, and phishing are among the industry’s biggest threats. A token can protect a card number, but it cannot stop a customer from being tricked into approving a fraudulent payment.
Regulation introduces another constraint. Under the CBN’s June 2023 rules, contactless payments through accounts and wallets can proceed without additional verification up to ₦15,000 ($11.14) per transaction and ₦50,000 ($37.14) cumulatively per day. Higher-value transactions require appropriate verification and authorisation, with further restrictions applying above the daily threshold.
Tokenisation can make digital payment credentials safer to use across devices. But it cannot, on its own, make banks integrate with new payment services, persuade merchants to accept them, or convince customers to abandon payment methods they already know and trust.
Will more Nigerians tap?
Nigeria’s digital payments market continues to expand. In 2025, the CBN said that electronic payment transaction volumes rose by 2.6% to 47.88 billion, up from 46.65 billion the previous year. The value of these transactions increased by 26.1% to ₦4.36 quadrillion ($3.28 trillion), from ₦3.46 quadrillion ($2.6 trillion) in 2024.
Nigeria’s growing digital payments market gives contactless providers a large customer base to potentially convert, but not necessarily a ready market. Bank transfers already allow customers to pay merchants directly from their accounts, often without a card or PoS terminal. A tap—whether using smartphones, cards, or other wearables—must offer a noticeable advantage in speed, convenience, or reliability to change that behaviour.
The United Kingdom offers an example of how that shift can happen. Contactless payments accounted for just 3% of all UK transactions in 2015. A decade later, they accounted for 39% of payments, with 19.2 billion recorded in 2025, according to UK Finance.
Years of investment in everyday acceptance underpinned much of the growth that contactless payments experienced in the UK. In 2012, London’s transport authority introduced contactless bank card payments on buses and extended them to the Underground and rail network in 2014.
Commuters could pay fares using cards they already owned, without obtaining a separate travel card, and benefit from the same fares and daily caps available through the Oyster system. By 2017, passengers had made more than one billion contactless journeys across London’s public transport network.
The wider banking industry also made the technology easier to use. Banks issued more contactless cards, merchants installed compatible terminals, and payment limits increased to accommodate more purchases. By the end of 2024, 89% of cards in circulation in the UK supported contactless payments, according to UK Finance.
The UK example suggests that adoption depends on giving customers frequent opportunities to tap, without requiring them to change how they hold or access their money. Public transport helped establish the habit, while widespread card issuance and merchant acceptance brought the technology into everyday shopping.
Nigeria already has its own example of contactless payments becoming routine. In Lagos, commuters use Cowry cards to tap onto regulated buses, trains, and ferries. Touch and Pay, the fintech operating the system, said it had surpassed five million users by 2025 and reported processing over ₦20 billion ($14.9 million) in transactions in 2024.
But Cowry operates through a dedicated transport payment system: commuters either load funds onto a physical card and tap it at transport terminals, or fund their Cowry account and pay using the app’s quick response (QR) code scanner. Participating transport operators accept both methods.
Extending contactless payments across ordinary retail transactions presents a different challenge because banks, card networks, and merchants must support compatible payment methods.
Google Pay, CashAfrica, and Nearpays are attempting to bring contactless payments into everyday transactions, but wider acceptance alone may not be enough to persuade Nigerians to change how they pay.
Nearpays’ proposition is partly about the merchant. The fintech’s solution lets NFC-enabled smartphones accept contactless payments without a hardware PoS terminal, potentially lowering the barrier to entry for businesses that want to accept card payments.
But the benefit to customers is less clear-cut. In our ₦1,500 ($1.11) withdrawal test, tapping the Verve card eliminated the need to insert it into the terminal, but the transaction still required a PIN.
Yet, for tap-to-pay to gain ground beyond transport and become commonplace in retail payments, security cannot be compromised in pursuit of convenience, especially at its current early stage of adoption.
With the speed advantage potentially amounting to mere fractions of a second over existing digital payment methods, and authentication still required in some cases, tapping may struggle to offer Nigerians a compelling reason to change how they pay. Without a clearer advantage, it risks remaining just another cool way to make a payment.

articles.title: La inteligencia artificial resucita las cintas magnéticas, la tecnología de las VHS
articles.text:
La cinta magnética, la tecnología de los antiguos VHS, vuelve a crecer gracias a la inteligencia artificial. Si creciste entre los ochenta y los noventa, seguramente te acuerdas de rebobinar las VHS antes de devolverlas al videoclub, de las cintas que se enredaban dentro del vídeo o de meter un lápiz en una casete para recogerla. Y quizá pensabas que todo aquello había quedado enterrado por el CD, el DVD, la memoria flash, la nube y el streaming, pero resulta que están volviendo con fuerza, aunque no al ámbito doméstico..
Cinco veces más cinta. Fujifilm ha anunciado una inversión de unos 10.000 millones de yenes, 57 millones de euros al cambio, para multiplicar por cinco su capacidad de producción de cinta magnética para almacenar datos en el ejercicio fiscal 2028. Eso sí, no hay que esperar videocasetes para el salón, porque se trata de cartuchos profesionales cuyo uso, según el mismo comunicado, está creciendo sobre todo entre los grandes proveedores de servicios en la nube y los operadores de centros de datos.
Una VHS muy evolucionada. El principio físico, de hecho, es pariente del de las viejas cintas de vídeo y de audio, ya que la información se graba como estados magnéticos sobre una capa de partículas pegada a una cinta muy larga, aunque los sistemas LTO (Linear Tape-Open) actuales son muchísimo más sofisticados. Según el comunicado de la inversión, la compañía japonesa lanzó en 2025 la generación LTO Ultrium 10, con unas partículas magnéticas híbridas muy finas, y desde enero de 2026 vende la versión que llega a los 40 terabytes sin comprimir.
El viejo peaje del rebobinado. Pero la cinta arrastra el mismo problema que conocía cualquiera que haya utilizado una VHS: es un soporte secuencial. Vamos, que para llegar a un dato hay que hacer correr la cinta hasta el punto en el que está grabado, mientras que un disco duro accede en milisegundos a archivos repartidos en diferentes posiciones, tal y como explica la misma fuente. Por eso nadie se plantea instalar Windows o abrir documentos a diario desde un cartucho, aunque para datos que hay que guardar mucho tiempo y consultar pocas veces resulta ideal.
El hambre de datos de la IA. Y es que entrenar y utilizar grandes modelos implica acumular cantidades enormes de información, que se suman a las que genera la digitalización de las empresas y que, según Fujifilm, hay que poder guardar de forma segura y eficiente. Tenerlo todo disponible en discos duros obliga a mantener muchos equipos encendidos y refrigerados, porque los discos consumen energía de forma continua, según el fabricante de bibliotecas de cinta Spectra Logic. Un cartucho, en cambio, puede sacarse de la unidad una vez escrito y quedarse en una biblioteca automatizada, donde no necesita electricidad para conservar los datos hasta que vuelvan a hacer falta.
Barata y desconectada. Además, la compañía defiende en su comunicado que la cinta permite guardar grandes volúmenes de datos durante mucho tiempo a bajo coste. También hay una ventaja de seguridad, porque un cartucho separado físicamente de la red crea lo que se conoce como “air gap”, un aislamiento que, según Fujifilm, sirve para proteger los datos frente a amenazas como el ransomware, un tipo de software malicioso.
Se da así una curiosa vuelta en la historia de la tecnología. Fujifilm, que trabaja con cinta magnética desde 1954 y asegura tener la mayor cuota del mercado mundial, destinará la inversión, la mayor que ha hecho nunca en instalaciones dedicadas a LTO, sobre todo a la última generación. Las cintas VHS no van a volver, pero la IA ha acabado tirando de un soporte con décadas a sus espaldas.

articles.title: Perplexity peut désormais accéder à vos comptes en banque et gérer votre argent
articles.text:
Anthropic a récemment annoncé la possibilité pour ses utilisateurs de connecter Claude à leurs comptes en banque. C’est maintenant au tour de Perplexity de pouvoir avoir accès à vos comptes bancaires afin de se transformer en conseiller financier. Cette fonctionnalité est disponible dès à présent en France.
Perplexity peut dorénavant accéder à vos comptes bancaires
À partir d’aujourd’hui, il est possible de connecter Perplexity à ses comptes bancaires, via la plateforme Plaid. Une fois la connexion établie, l’assistant IA se transforme tout simplement en conseiller financier en fournissant des réponses basées sur les données bancaires de l’utilisateur. L’intelligence artificielle peut par exemple élaborer un suivi budgétaire ou un graphique des dépenses, qui se mettent à jour automatiquement à chaque nouvelle transaction. Les différentes transactions sont par ailleurs divisées par catégories (loyer, courses, abonnements, cafés, etc.).
L’utilisateur peut par exemple poser les questions suivantes : « Combien ai-je dépensé en plats à emporter le mois dernier ? », « Combien ai-je dépensé en café le mois dernier ? », « Est-ce que je paie encore des abonnements oubliés ? », « Est-ce qu’il me reste suffisamment d’argent pour payer le loyer ? », etc. L’IA fournira alors une réponse sur la base des données bancaires de l’utilisateur.
L’assistant IA ne peut pas effectuer d’actions sur vos comptes
L’accès de Perplexity à vos comptes bancaires est en lecture seule, c’est-à-dire que l’assistant IA ne peut pas effectuer d’actions, comme faire des virement, faire des investissements ou déplacer de l’argent. Il peut seulement lire les données des comptes bancaires dont vous lui avez donné l’autorisation d’accéder. Notons également que l’IA n’a pas accès à vos mots de passe bancaires.
Il est possible de connecter Perplexity à ses comptes bancaires via Plaid dès aujourd’hui dans 17 pays européens, dont la France, l’Allemagne, l’Espagne, l’Italie, l’Irlande, la Pologne et les Pays-Bas. À noter que l’entreprise Perplexity définit cette fonctionnalité comme une étape vers ce qu’elle appelle « la finance intelligente », c’est-à-dire l’intégration de l’intelligence artificielle directement dans les questions financières. Petit à petit, l’IA s’immisce dans la plupart des services que nous utilisons, et nos comptes bancaires ne font pas figure d’exception.

articles.title: 74 Millionen Geräte betroffen: Warum viele den Wechsel von Windows 10 hinauszögern
articles.text:
74 Millionen Geräte betroffen: Warum viele den Wechsel von Windows 10 hinauszögern
Der offizielle Support für Windows 10 hat im Oktober 2025 geendet. Geräte mit diesem veralteten Betriebssystem erhalten keine Updates mehr und sind somit anfälliger für Sicherheitsbedrohungen. Trotzdem haben viele Nutzer:innen den Wechsel zu Windows 11 lange aufgeschoben. Einer der Gründe ist, dass das Upgrade bei vielen aus technischen Gründen nicht möglich ist. Dadurch sind Millionen Computer praktisch unbrauchbar geworden, obwohl sie weiterhin einwandfrei funktionieren. Im Auftrag von Refurbed hat Fraunhofer Austria jetzt im Rahmen einer Studie ermittelt, wie viele Geräte das in Europa konkret betrifft.
Millionen Computer können nicht wechseln
Die aktuelle Windows-Version setzt bestimmte Hardwarevoraussetzungen voraus, darunter TPM 2.0, Secure Boot und eine unterstützte Prozessorgeneration. Laut der Fraunhofer-Analyse können im gewerblichen Bereich nur rund 2,8 Prozent der Windows-10-Geräte technisch nicht auf das neue Betriebssystem wechseln. Die Migration wird hier vor allem durch langsame Beschaffungszyklen, Testphasen und knappe IT-Ressourcen verzögert. Im privaten Bereich fällt der Anteil der technisch inkompatiblen Geräte dagegen deutlich höher aus.
Wer ein nicht kompatibles Gerät besitzt, muss für eine Neuanschaffung oft mehrere hundert Euro zahlen. Andere Nutzer:innen zögern den Wechsel bewusst heraus. Ein Grund dafür ist laut Analyse die fehlende Dringlichkeit durch die kostenlose ESU-Verlängerung bis Oktober 2027. Manche lehnen Windows 11 auch aus Datenschutzgründen oder wegen der stärkeren KI-Integration ab. Inzwischen hat Microsoft die KI-Funktionen in Windows 11 sogar wieder reduziert und damit auf den Frust der Nutzer:innen reagiert.
Millionen Tonnen an Elektroschrott
Insgesamt sind in den 27 EU-Staaten laut Analyse rund 74 Millionen Windows-10-Geräte betroffen. 41 Millionen davon werden voraussichtlich nicht auf das aktuelle Betriebssystem wechseln. Das entspricht etwa 55 Prozent des aktuellen Bestands. Allein in Deutschland betrifft das rund 5,8 Millionen Geräte, die über die ESU-Übergangsfrist hinaus mit Windows 10 weiterlaufen werden. Entdeckte Schwachstellen bleiben dann offen und gefährden potenziell Millionen von Privatnutzer:innen.
Refurbed sieht darin nicht nur ein Sicherheitsrisiko, sondern auch ein Problem der Nachhaltigkeit. Wenn alle Geräte, die noch mit Windows 10 laufen und technisch nicht mit dem Nachfolgesystem kompatibel sind, ein weiteres Jahr genutzt würden, gäbe es laut Analyse ein Einsparpotenzial von rund 0,32 Millionen Tonnen CO₂ und etwa 1.172 Tonnen Elektroschrott. Das entspricht der jährlichen CO₂-Speicherleistung von über 500 Quadratkilometern Wald – also etwa der Fläche des Bodensees.
Wie lassen sich knappe Ressourcen schonen?
„Das Windows-10-Support-Ende trifft in der [EU] auf einen Gerätebestand, der noch über Jahre hinweg in relevantem Umfang weiterbetrieben wird, mit entsprechenden Sicherheits- und Umweltimplikationen“, heißt es in dem Whitepaper von Refurbed und Fraunhofer Austria. Der verfrühte Austausch technisch funktionsfähiger Geräte stehe in einem „klaren Spannungsverhältnis zu Zielen der Ressourcenschonung und Kreislaufwirtschaft.” Als mögliche Lösung nennen die Forscher:innen unter anderem befristete Übergangslösungen für technisch nicht upgradefähige Geräte, zum Beispiel in Form eines abgesicherten Windows-10-Boot-Mediums.

articles.title: Demandan a Workday por presunta discriminación de su software de IA: la empresa busca frenar los reclamos colectivos
articles.text:
Workday enfrenta una demanda que acusa a su software de filtrado con inteligencia artificial de discriminar a postulantes por raza, sexo, edad y discapacidad. Los demandantes sostienen que las herramientas de la compañía para recursos humanos perjudicaron a candidatos durante procesos de contratación.
La empresa pidió a un juez federal de San Francisco que impida el avance de las demandas colectivas: solicitó rechazar la certificación de un grupo que podría reunir a millones de postulantes y anular otro integrado por más de 15.000 personas que reclaman discriminación por edad. La presentación se realizó el martes 10 de noviembre, según informó la agencia Reuters.
“La cuestión no es si los demandantes plantean preguntas comunes, sino si un proceso colectivo puede generar respuestas comunes”, dijo Workday en el escrito.
En un segundo documento, con argumentos similares, la empresa pidió a la jueza Rita Lin que anule el grupo de más de 15.000 personas que se sumaron a la demanda por discriminación por edad, según Reuters y MLex, un servicio de análisis legal.
La ley federal contra la discriminación por edad en el empleo permite una certificación provisional: los posibles afectados reciben una notificación y deciden si se suman. Lin autorizó ese paso en mayo de 2025, y una orden del 7 de octubre confirmó que más de 15.000 personas habían ingresado, según Forbes.
Workday sostiene ahora que esos postulantes no están en situaciones comparables. Argumenta que cada cliente configura y usa la plataforma de manera distinta, que los empleadores toman sus propias decisiones y que no se probó que sus herramientas evaluaran la mayoría de las solicitudes.
Si la jueza acepta, la empresa pide que las reclamaciones de quienes se sumaron se desestimen sin perjuicio, es decir, que queden en libertad de iniciar casos individuales, según MLex.
Un caso que probará el uso de algoritmos en la contratación
Según Reuters, la demanda es la primera que apunta de forma amplia a los algoritmos que sostienen los programas de filtrado con IA, hoy muy comunes en las grandes empresas. Workday informó en su escrito que más de 11.500 organizaciones usan su software para recursos humanos, nómina y compras.
El caso involucra tres funciones. Una compara las habilidades del currículum vitae con las de una oferta de empleo, y Workday dice que la mayoría de sus clientes nunca la usó. Otra califica cuánto se ajusta una solicitud a la oferta, y la tercera busca en la base de datos de la empresa candidatos anteriores para sugerirlos.
Derek Mobley, el demandante que da nombre al caso, afirma que lo rechazaron en más de 100 empleos de empresas que usaban estas herramientas, en varios casos a las pocas horas de postularse, según Reuters. Un grupo de postulantes pidió en septiembre a la jueza que certifique el caso como demanda colectiva.
Workday niega las acusaciones. Dice que su tecnología solo analiza las calificaciones para el puesto y no rasgos protegidos como la raza o la edad, y que sus productos se prueban para detectar sesgos.
Lin rechazó en 2024 los primeros intentos de la empresa de desestimar el caso y, en junio, rechazó en su mayor parte el pedido de excluir las ampliaciones de la demanda basadas en leyes de California. La jueza tiene prevista una audiencia sobre la certificación de la demanda colectiva en marzo. El tribunal aún no resolvió la solicitud de anular el grupo de más de 15.000 personas.

articles.title: Ukraine says it can’t stop Russian strikes because Starshield is limited again
articles.text:
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said today that Starshield has again been disabled on fast-moving drones in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russian forces, and that the US has provided “very little” information about the return of the restriction.
“We have detected speed restrictions on Starshield on our Ukrainian territory again, in the temporarily occupied parts of Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said in a speech at the 9th European Political Community Summit in Ireland. “The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour—that’s 100 miles per hour.”
Zelenskyy’s allegation is that Starshield—the military variant of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite service—stops working on Ukrainian military drones when they travel above 161 kilometers per hour.
SpaceX today denied Zelenskyy’s allegation. “This is false. There has been no change,” SpaceX’s media relations department told Ars today when asked if SpaceX has any response to Zelenskyy’s statement that Starshield is being restricted again.
“This means more Russian strikes get through”
SpaceX has received multiple Pentagon contracts to give Ukraine access to the military-focused Starshield. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said last month that any decisions on Starshield restrictions are made by the US government. The Pentagon inspector general’s office has since declined a request from US senators to investigate who ordered the restrictions.
Ukraine officials reportedly said today that they believe the limit was reinstated to put pressure on Ukraine in the latest round of peace talks with Russia. Zelenskyy said in today’s speech that without satellite connectivity on its drones, Ukraine cannot intercept Russian drones that fly in from the occupied parts of Ukraine.
