articles.title: From multi-lingual AI agents to the future of voice: Google Cloud’s Naren Kachroo at TechSparks 2026
articles.text:
From multi-lingual AI agents to the future of voice: Google Cloud’s Naren Kachroo at TechSparks 2026
At TechSparks 2026, Google Cloud’s Head of Sales & GTM AI showcased Gemini 3.8 Live and Live Avatar, and showed an AI sales agent negotiating a helmet order in Hindi on a weak mobile hotspot.
For Naren Kachroo, the most useful AI is the kind that finishes the job. “There is no value created without the task actually getting completed with AI,” said Kachroo, Head of Sales & GTM AI at Google Cloud. At TechSparks 2026, during a product showcase titled ‘Voice AI in action’, Kachroo walked through Google’s latest voice models, customer use cases, and a live demo built for small businesses. His argument was: voice is becoming the main way people will interact with AI, and in India, that shift will happen in local languages and accents.
Kachroo said the industry has moved past treating generative AI as a question-and-answer tool. “We have moved from thinking about generative AI as chatbots, as something that we ask questions of and we get answers from,” he said.
The focus now is AI that has access to tools, data, and capabilities, and can take actions on a person’s behalf.
“We are not building AI for the sake of AI,” he added. The goal, he said, is AI that improves how people live and work everyday.
Two voice models, two jobs
Google recently announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. Gemini 3.8 Live can detect and switch between 97 supported languages within the same conversation. Kachroo explained how businesses should choose between the two models.
Gemini 3.8 Live suits simpler conversational and agentic tasks, such as a live voice chat with basic tool calling. Extended Thinking suits conversations that need deeper reasoning, context switching, and multiple steps. Cost also matters, he noted: Extended Thinking costs more per token.
Both are voice-to-voice models, which handle speech as input and output in a single model. For developers who need only one part of that pipeline, Google also offers separate models for text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and live translation.
Kachroo said the latest Gemini text-to-speech model performed strongly in Google’s internal testing with Indian languages, accents, and tonality.
What the demos showed
Kachroo played a series of short demos to show the range of use cases.
In the first, Shopify’s assistant, Sidekick, guided a merchant step by step through connecting a domain in the Shopify admin. In the second, a voice agent booked a restaurant table for eight people. Midway, the caller asked whether a cake was allowed, shared a photo from Google reviews to ask whether a dish was vegetarian, and asked about other vegetarian options before confirming.
The second demo required the agent to track context across multiple turns, remember preferences, and make several tool calls. That kind of task, Kachroo said, is where Extended Thinking fits.
He also showed Live Avatar, which pairs Gemini’s live voice with real-time video generation and lip-syncing, so users see an animated face as well as hear a voice. Google made Live Avatar available to businesses through Gemini Enterprise recently, and marks the audio and video it generates with an invisible SynthID watermark. Citi was a pilot customer: its Citi Sky assistant, built with Google DeepMind’s real-time avatar technology and the Gemini Live API, walks US wealth clients through options, such as what to do with a maturing certificate of deposit.
Why the cost is lower
Kachroo said Gemini 3.8 Live has the lowest cost per turn of any comparable model, and that Extended Thinking tops industry benchmarks for speech-to-speech quality.
Google has said Extended Thinking scored 82.6 on Artificial Analysis’ speech-to-speech quality index, the highest overall score.
The low price is not a land grab, he said. Google runs the full stack itself, from its TPU chips and infrastructure to the models and applications, and passes the efficiency gains on to customers. That lets Google offer both a top-quality model and a lower-cost workhorse model.
He pointed to two customers as examples of voice AI in use: Autotrader, which uses the technology for buying and selling used cars, and Equal AI, an Indian startup whose assistant answers and handles phone calls before the user picks up.
A sales agent for small businesses
The centerpiece of the session was a live demo of an assistant for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), which Kachroo said his team built in about a day. It is a large potential market: more than 7.8 crore enterprises were registered on the government’s Udyam portal as of February 2026, according to the MSME ministry. Kachroo flagged one risk upfront: he was running it on a mobile hotspot after failing to connect to the hotel network.
The demo featured a fictional safety gear company and its owner, Rajesh, who had just received about 500 helmets. Speaking to the assistant, Rajesh asked how many leads he had for helmets. The assistant found two: a construction firm in Mumbai that needed 500 helmets, and a hardware store in Agra that needed 50.
Rajesh told the assistant to drop the smaller lead, send a quotation to the Mumbai buyer, and call them to close the deal. He set one condition: the price had to stay above Rs 400 per helmet, and the assistant could book the order without coming back for approval.
The assistant then called the buyer and negotiated in Hindi. Kachroo said it carried context from the internal conversation with Rajesh into the external call, negotiated on the company’s behalf, and closed the deal.
That end-to-end flow is where Google wants voice AI to go, he said. With the 3.8 Live models, he believes businesses can now build voice agents into their processes that complete tasks on their own.
Built for how India speaks
Kachroo said the assistant could have held the same conversation in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, and other languages. That matters, he argued, because the Indian consumer is moving voice-first. Gemini Live itself now supports more than 25 Indian languages and dialects. According to the IAMAI-Kantar Internet in India 2024 report, 98% of India’s 886 million active internet users accessed content in Indic languages, and one in five used voice commands to go online.
“I believe that voice is the future,” he said. Voice AI in India, he added, will need to be native to the languages people speak, the accents they use, and what they are most comfortable with.
Kachroo said Google DeepMind has a team in Bengaluru researching voice, focused on Indian accents and cultural nuances. Google also funds Project Vaani, run by the Indian Institute of Science and ARTPARK, which has open-sourced more than 31,000 hours of speech in 105 languages from 165 districts.
Kachroo closed with an invitation for founders and developers to try the models, use the experiences, and share feedback, including what does not work, so that Google’s research and product teams can improve them. His larger point was that voice AI is ready to move beyond conversation into execution, and that India, with its range of languages and its voice-first users, is one of the markets where that shift will be tested first.

articles.title: Jensen Huang ha salvado a NVIDIA seis veces. La séptima crisis es él
articles.text:
En dos semanas, el consejo de NVIDIA ha pasado de expresar su confianza en Jensen Huang a preparar su destitución. Según Bloomberg, ya está trabajando con una firma externa para encontrar candidatos y baraja nombrar a un CEO interino. Todavía no ha anunciado ninguna decisión. No tardará.
Huang lleva más de tres décadas dirigiendo NVIDIA y la ha sacado del borde de la quiebra en al menos seis ocasiones. Pero esta vez el problema no es externo, es él mismo, y la empresa no tiene a nadie preparado para relevarlo.
Qué ha ocurrido. El caso ha escalado en cuatro pasos:
- 29 de octubre. NVIDIA califica de “nada inusual” la relación de Huang con Alice Huang, ejecutiva de Megaspeed. La inteligencia estadounidense la había señalado como sospechosa de desviar chips e información sobre NVIDIA a China.
- 8 de noviembre. Huang admite una infidelidad con la mencionada en un correo enviado a su plantilla. El consejo abre una investigación independiente y lo respalda.
- 10 de noviembre. NVIDIA contrata al bufete Wachtell Lipton para la investigación independiente. La acción encadena dos caídas que suman un 10%.
- 11 de noviembre. The New York Times publica que Huang también tuvo una relación con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de Healthcare y subordinada directa suya. La acción cae más de un 7% tras el cierre del mercado.
Lo que más pesa contra él son los desmentidos iniciales, más que la infidelidad en sí. Gary Gensler, expresidente de la SEC, ha dicho a Semafor que Huang “parece haber engañado al público”. Ya hay demandas de accionistas en marcha.
El contexto. Durante años, Huang abría sus presentaciones internas con la misma frase: “Nuestra empresa está a 30 días de quebrar”. No exageraba. La acción se ha desplomado un 90% dos veces antes de llegar a empresa más valiosa del mundo.
- 1996. El NV1 apostó por cuadriláteros cuando DirectX impuso los triángulos, y Sega canceló el chip. Huang viajó a Japón a reconocer el error. Sega convirtió la deuda en 5 millones de dólares de capital, y Huang despidió a 60 de sus 100 empleados.
- 2002. El pinchazo de la burbuja puntocom, la pelea con Microsoft por la Xbox, las cuentas reexpresadas a petición de la SEC y un GeForce FX que llegó tarde y peor que la competencia.
- 2008. Cargo de unos 200 millones de dólares por chips de portátil defectuosos. La acción cayó un 76% durante el año en el contexto de la crisis de entonces.
- 2018. Resaca cripto tras la caída de Bitcoin y compañía. NVIDIA se quedó con los almacenes llenos de GPUs sin demanda y un 54% de caída de un trimestre para otro.
- 2022. Ethereum deja de minar con GPUs y Estados Unidos veta el A100 y el H100 en China.
- 2025. La licencia obligatoria para el H20 le cuesta un cargo de 4.500 millones de dólares y deja su cuota en China a cero.
Entre bambalinas. En cada crisis, Huang ha seguido el mismo guión:
- Reconocer el error pronto.
- Recortar donde duele
- Y no tocar la apuesta a largo plazo.
En 2008 despidió al 6,5% de la plantilla y en el mismo comunicado prometió seguir invirtiendo en CUDA. Fue algo que en su momento sonó contradictorio, casi suicida, porque ese software encarecía cada GPU sin que aparentemente nadie lo pidiera. Así que Huang estaba empeorando su eficiencia en época de vacas flacas. Hoy la IA moderna funciona sobre él y de hecho CUDA es el mejor foso que tiene NVIDIA.
Casi todo lo que es hoy NVIDIA fue decidido durante un mal momento para la empresa.
- En 2012 se lanzó a por las redes neuronales, que entonces eran cosa de laboratorios universitarios, con una dudosa rentabilidad.
- En 2019 pagó 6.900 millones de dólares por Mellanox porque intuyó que el cuello de botella acabaría estando en la red. Acertó de lleno.
Cuando Sequoia entró en 1993, la empresa valía 7 millones. Hoy vale más de 4 billones y llegaron a ser 5,7.
El rastro del dinero. Ahora será juzgado por un consejo al que él mismo ha hecho extremadamente rico. Según Bloomberg, Mark Stevens y Tench Coxe, dos de los consejeros, sumaban casi 15.000 millones de dólares en enero de 2025, con la acción bastante más baja que hoy. Otros dos, Harvey Jones y Brooke Seawell, tenían unos 1.000 y 750 millones. Los cuatro están en el consejo desde los años noventa. Ese consejo parecía que iba a ser indulgente con su affaire, pero el segundo caso, con una subordinada, es mucho más difícil de dejar pasar. Hay precedentes en grandes empresas estadounidenses que acabaron con el CEO fuera, como el de McDonald's en 2020 o el de Intel en 2018.
Hasta ahora, la gran lealtad del consejo tenía lógica porque cada vez que apostó por Huang contra el mercado, ganó.
El contraste. Apple, Microsoft, Google y Amazon han relevado a su fundador sin hundirse, pero llevaban años preparándolo. Tim Cook ya era director de operaciones antes de pasar a CEO en 2011. Y Andy Jassy es quien levantó el negociazo que es AWS para Amazon. El único relevo a la fuerza, el de Jobs en 1985, casi hace quebrar a la empresa.
NVIDIA no tiene a su Tim Cook. Huang ha montado una estructura sin número dos. No es habitual que sesenta personas reporten a un CEO cada día. Si se va, se lleva a quien decide dónde estará el cuello de botella dentro de cinco años. Y llega en mal momento porque la ley de Moore ya no da chips mejores cada año, y China avanza hacia sus propios semiconductores.
Sí, pero. El estilo que ha salvado a NVIDIA, con control total, un consejo leal y cero contrapesos, es también el que ha dejado que un asunto personal acabe salpicando a la empresa.
Aún falta tela por cortar. La investigación interna sigue abierta. Lo de que Alice Huang es una espía viene de la inteligencia estadounidense y no se ha probado en público. Trump ha dicho que Huang debería seguir, y Huang conserva cerca del 3,4% de la empresa gracias a sus 811 millones de acciones.
Y ahora qué. El 17 de noviembre NVIDIA presenta resultados. Y el 18, Huang se sienta a puerta cerrada con tres presidentes de comités de la Cámara de Representantes.
En mayo, contó en How I Built This que, sabiendo lo que le esperaba, no volvería a fundar NVIDIA. Pensaba en treinta años de sobresaltos. No contaba con la madre de todos los sustos.

articles.title: Support für veraltete Version von Windows 11 läuft aus: Was Nutzer jetzt tun sollten, um ihren PC abzusichern
articles.text:
Windows 11: Support für veraltete Version läuft aus – wie du deinen PC jetzt schützen kannst
Für die Version 23H2 von Windows 11 wird ab sofort kein Support mehr bereitgestellt. Wie Microsoft in einem Beitrag auf seiner offiziellen Wissens- und Dokumentationsplattform mitteilt, ist das Windows-Sicherheitsupdate vom November 2026 das letzte für die Enterprise- und Education-Editionen. Betroffene Geräte erhalten somit keine monatlichen Sicherheitsupdates mehr, die vor aktuellen und neuen Bedrohungen schützen. Der Support für die Editionen Home und Pro wurde schon im November 2025 eingestellt.
Diese PCs erhalten keine neuen Updates
Gewerblichen Kund:innen räumt Microsoft grundsätzlich einen Support-Zeitraum von 36 Monaten ein, Privatanwender:innen erhalten zwei Jahre lang Updates. Für Windows 11 23H2 ist diese Frist jetzt abgelaufen. Am 10. November 2026 veröffentlichte Microsoft mit dem Sicherheitsupdate KB5131087 den letzten Patch für diese Version. Eine Übergangsfrist gibt es nicht. Betroffene Computer funktionieren zwar weiterhin, sind künftig allerdings anfälliger für Sicherheitsbedrohungen. Entdeckte Schwachstellen bleiben offen und gefährden somit potenziell Unternehmen, Schulen und Behörden.
Microsoft empfiehlt deshalb, betroffene Geräte schnellstmöglich auf die Version 26H2 zu aktualisieren, um auch weiterhin monatliche Sicherheits- und Qualitätsupdates zu erhalten. Nutzer:innen, die nicht wissen, welche Version von Windows 11 sie aktuell nutzen, können dies in den Systeminformationen ihres Geräts prüfen. Laut Winfuture ist ein direktes Update von 23H2 auf die aktuelle Version 26H2 mittels eines Enablement Packages allerdings nicht möglich – stattdessen ist ein vollständiges Feature-Update nötig. Die entsprechenden ISO-Dateien stehen direkt bei Microsoft zum Download bereit.
Windows 11 bleibt weiterhin unbeliebt
Microsoft hat Windows 11 im Oktober 2021 eingeführt. Trotzdem nutzt laut Statcounter rund jeder vierte Windows-Computer weiterhin den veralteten Vorgänger, obwohl der reguläre Support für Windows 10 schon im Oktober 2025 geendet hat. Der zögerliche Wechsel hängt auch mit den vielen neuen KI-Funktionen zusammen. Zwar halten viele Nutzer:innen die Technologie für ein nützliches Werkzeug, aber bei Vertrauen und Datensicherheit bestehen weiterhin Bedenken. Microsoft stattete in der Zwischenzeit sogar den Texteditor Notepad mit KI aus, obwohl dieser gerade wegen seines minimalistischen Designs beliebt ist.
Inzwischen hat Microsoft die KI-Integrationen in Windows 11 wieder reduziert und damit auf den Widerstand der Nutzer:innen reagiert. Das Ziel sei es, sich auf KI-Funktionen zu konzentrieren, die „wirklich nützlich” sind. Anfang März berichtete Windows Central zudem, dass Microsoft den Plan, weitere KI-Funktionen unter dem Copilot-Label zu integrieren, stillschweigend auf Eis gelegt habe. Wer seinen Computer vor Schwachstellen schützen will, sollte in jedem Fall schnellstmöglich zu dem aktuellen System Windows 11 wechseln – Beliebtheit hin oder her. Denn nur so bleibt der Computer vor potenziellen Bedrohungen geschützt.

articles.title: Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations
articles.text:
Israeli-American cybersecurity startup Daylight has raised $80 million in a Series B funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $120 million.
The investment round was led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives’ Growth Equity, with additional support from Okta Ventures, Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital.
Founded in 2024, with headquarters in New York and Tel Aviv, Daylight has built Aura, an AI-native platform that hunts for, analyzes, and contains cyber threats in real time.
Combining AI automation with human expertise, the platform continuously builds, runs, and customizes agents that handle day-to-day operations based on customers’ workflows, risks, and priorities.
Daylight provides these capabilities as part of a flexible service model. Customers can select the service to be fully managed, co-managed, or supported by forward-deployed engineers.
As AI agents handle routine operations, customers can use Aura to investigate their security environments, access security data, and manage security operations.
Daylight also covers AI platforms that organizations use, offering protection against prompt injection, risky MCPs, and rogue AI-driven activity.
“As these agents become more capable, they’ll fundamentally change how threats are detected, investigated, and contained, with expert security engineers implementing, governing, and continuously improving their operations,” Daylight co-founder and CEO Hagai Shapira said.
“At Daylight, we’re already bringing this vision to life through an agent-native model that combines the speed and scale of AI with the judgment and oversight of human experts. We’re building the foundation for a new era of security operations,” Shapira added.
The company plans to use the fresh funding to accelerate its platform’s development, expand its security and technology teams, grow its presence in the US, and enter new markets in the EMEA and APAC regions.

articles.title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
articles.text:
One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet’s atmosphere.
Except when we can’t.
On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we’ve been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that’s due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane.
Big changes
TOI-2535 is one of the many stars with exoplanet candidates identified by TESS, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. It’s a K dwarf, meaning it’s somewhat smaller than the Sun. And TESS found signs of a Jupiter-sized planet orbiting it every eight days, an orbit close enough to make TOI-2535b a “hot Jupiter” exoplanet. At that point, there was nothing especially unusual about it.
But a closer look at the data showed two very strange things. First, the timing of when its transits occurred could shift by as much as six hours, a substantial variation for an orbit this brief. That’s typically a sign of gravitational interactions with another planet; depending on the details of that second planet’s orbit, it may slow the first one or accelerate it through a transit more quickly. Since the second planet doesn’t show up in TESS data, it appears to orbit in a slightly different plane, so it doesn’t pass between its host star and Earth.

articles.title: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access Notion customers' chat transcripts | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A cyberattack at Fireworks AI has exposed some of its customers’ data, the company has confirmed. Fireworks AI, a platform that developers use to access and use open AI models, said an attacker breached its cloud provider to gain access to a Fireworks development system, which allowed access to some of its customers’ data.
The company said in its latest security advisory that the cybercriminals took Fireworks’ customers’ billing information and some datasets. Fireworks touts tens of thousands of customers worldwide using its platform, including legal tech company Harvey and AI company Cursor.
At least one confirmed affected customer is online document editor and notetaker Notion, which said in a disclosure that the breach affected around 1% of its own customers.
Notion said that Fireworks alerted the company to a security incident and later confirmed that the hackers had stolen some Notion customer data. On November 3, Notion said it disconnected its systems from Fireworks, deleted the data stored in its systems, and stopped all connectivity between the two.
Notion confirmed this week that the hackers took chat transcripts of its Notion AI customers who used the “Insights” feature. The company said that the transcripts include “any input to or output from the model that was written to the chat,” but added that much of the data was unattributable and could not be determined from which customer it was obtained.
The breach at Fireworks AI shows how tech companies are reliant on other tech providers for their own offerings, and how cyberattacks can, as a result, spill over into other customers.
Fireworks said that it believes the hackers are financially motivated and that their goals are focused on selling tokens from breaching access to large language models, or LLMs. These schemes rely on selling to unauthorized third parties, who can burn through AI model usage without using their own resources.
This is the second breach affecting Fireworks in as many months, following a security incident in October.

articles.title: Una empresa frenó su centro de datos de IA en Australia tras quejas de los vecinos
articles.text:
Quantum DC, una desarrolladora de infraestructura tecnológica, suspendió su proyecto de un centro de datos de inteligencia artificial de 1.200 megavatios en Tungkillo, en las colinas de Adelaida, Australia. Su director ejecutivo, Alby Tomassi, dijo que la empresa “malinterpretó” el enojo de los vecinos y que no pedirá la aprobación este año, según recogió ABC News.
El proyecto, junto con infraestructura de energía propia, se ubicaría en Collins Road, unos 41 kilómetros al este del centro de Adelaida. La empresa recibió contactos de más de 350 personas y una lista conjunta de 432 preguntas de la comunidad.
Los temas planteados abarcan el agua, la energía, el ruido, la iluminación y el cielo nocturno, el tráfico, los incendios forestales, las tierras agrícolas, la ubicación y el entorno natural, según Tomassi.
“Subestimamos la fuerza del sentimiento sobre esta propuesta”, afirmó el ejecutivo en un comunicado citado por ABC News. La empresa se disculpó y anunció que formará un panel de expertos independientes para revisar los estudios especializados y publicar sus conclusiones.
Reuniones canceladas y protestas propias
Quantum DC había programado dos sesiones de consulta en octubre, pero las pospuso para noviembre por razones de seguridad. Mientras tanto, los vecinos organizaron sus propias reuniones de protesta, con la asistencia de unos cientos de personas.
Ahora la empresa canceló también las sesiones de noviembre. Tomassi explicó que no serviría de nada reunir a 500 personas para responder 432 preguntas en un foro cargado de emoción. No descartó retomar el proyecto más adelante.
Magdalene Lippett, vecina de Tungkillo, celebró la pausa: “Las colinas no son el lugar adecuado para su centro de datos”, dijo a la radio 891 ABC Adelaide. La alcaldesa del municipio de Mid Murray, Simone Bailey, señaló “grandes preocupaciones” por la cercanía de una reserva de cielo oscuro, la distancia al cuartel de bomberos rurales más próximo, los caminos sin pavimentar y el posible efecto sobre las napas de agua.
En otra zona de Australia Meridional, el concejal Hank Langes, del consejo de Northern Areas, dijo que propondría ofrecer su territorio al proyecto, por el empleo que generaría.
El gobierno regional promete una ley
El primer ministro de Australia Meridional, Peter Malinauskas, afirmó que el episodio demuestra la necesidad de legislar. Según dijo, el estado necesita un marco estricto para evitar que se construyan, o siquiera se propongan, centros de datos en lugares inadecuados, y para que el interés de la comunidad sea “representado” y “aplicado”.
El caso se suma a otros proyectos retirados en el país. El 8 de noviembre, Stockland retiró un centro de datos de su plan para el antiguo club de golf de Kogarah, en Sídney, donde 593 de las 665 presentaciones públicas se oponían. La empresa atribuyó la decisión a su prioridad por el polo logístico.
En septiembre, Goodman Group abandonó el proyecto Mars, de USD 1.200 millones, en Lane Cove, a unos 160 metros de una escuela pública. Citó cambios regulatorios y las opiniones de la comunidad.
En Melbourne, la distribuidora eléctrica Jemena suspendió a fines de septiembre las conexiones del centro de datos M3 de NextDC por la oposición vecinal. Según NextDC, el siguiente aumento de suministro no llegará hasta el ejercicio fiscal 2028.

articles.title: NVIDIA podría destituir a Jensen Huang como CEO tras el escándalo con la espía china
articles.text:
Jensen Huang podría perder su puesto como director ejecutivo de NVIDIA. De acuerdo con The Wall Street Journal, la junta directiva estaría preparando una reunión para decidir el futuro del fundador y CEO de la compañía. Las cosas se complicaron para Huang luego de que una investigación interna descubriera vínculos con una supuesta espía china.
Según el reporte, el consejo de administración considera destituir a Huang después de que salieran a la luz dos relaciones extramaritales. Hace unos días, el CEO reconoció que había sido infiel a su esposa y pidió disculpas por traicionar la confianza de su familia y de la organización. La figura en el centro de esa polémica es Alice Huang, una ejecutiva de la compañía Megaspeed y con vínculos con el gobierno de Xi Jinping.
Los primeros rumores apuntaban a que Megaspeed habría ayudado a desviar chips de IA hacia China. La compañía, con sede en Singapur, se convirtió en uno de los principales clientes de NVIDIA para la construcción de centros de datos de IA en el sudeste asiático. No obstante, las autoridades estadounidenses sospecharon que Huang ayudó a contrabandear tarjetas gráficas, por lo cual abrieron una investigación a finales de 2024.
La relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang comenzó en 2023 y permitió que la ejecutiva china desviara 240.000 placas gráficas H100, H200 y A100 hacia el gigante asiático. The Information reveló que Huang montó una red de empresas en China junto con su hermana y esposo, incluyendo una que le ayudó a convertirse en socio preferente de NVIDIA. Este movimiento le garantizó acceso prioritario a los chips y al CEO de la empresa.
Jensen Huang se metió con una espía china y con una empleada de NVIDIA
Hace unas semanas surgió un reporte de que Alice Huang estaba vinculada a los servicios de inteligencia chinos. El Departamento de Justicia abrió múltiples investigaciones relacionadas con ella y el mundo se le vino encima al jefe de NVIDIA. Según informó el New York Times, Alice Huang (también conocida como Huang Le) trabajaba para el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China mientras mantenía una relación romántica con el directivo de la empresa de tarjetas gráficas.
Los investigadores temen que pueda haber accedido a detalles técnicos sobre el hardware de IA de NVIDIA y las discusiones internas con la Casa Blanca. Hasta ahora, las autoridades se han centrado en su papel como ejecutiva de Megaspeed, donde aprovechó su cercanía con Jensen Huang para ayudar a eludir los controles de exportación estadounidenses.
Además de esta relación, el New York Times señaló que el jefe de NVIDIA mantuvo un romance con otra empleada de la compañía. Kimberly Powell, vicepresidente del área de atención médica de NVIDIA, fue captada en un vídeo con Jensen Huang mientras se encontraban en un hotel de San José, California. Las políticas internas de la compañía prohíben este tipo de acciones, sobre todo cuando se trata de una relación extramarital entre un jefe y su subordinada.
Hasta el momento de esta publicación, el futuro de Jensen Huang permanece en el aire. Si la junta decide apartarlo del cargo, NVIDIA perdería al hombre que transformó la compañía y la convirtió en una de las más valiosas del mundo. Huang ha sido el rostro visible de la empresa por más de tres décadas, primero en su etapa gamer y ahora en el desarrollo de chips para centros de datos, por lo que encontrar un sucesor será un trabajo complejo.

articles.title: BluWave-ai secures $8.1 million for energy grid software as data centres strain load | BetaKit
articles.text:
Heading into its 10th year as a company, energy grid management startup BluWave-ai has raised fresh funding as it anticipates a surge in demand thanks to an AI data centre build-out.
The Ottawa company announced on Thursday that it has secured $8.1 million in a mix of equity from several angel investors and family offices, non-dilutive federal government funding (though it did not disclose through which department), and debt from Royal Bank of Canada and Bank of Montreal. Founder and CEO Devashish Paul said the financing was 40 percent debt facilities but did not break down the split further.
Founded in 2017, BluWave-ai is a cleantech startup that uses AI to help utility companies add renewable energy sources to their electricity grids and to manage energy loads more broadly. The 40-person company is led by Paul, who was a longtime tech executive and Royal Canadian Air Force officer before founding BluWave. The company has raised more than $24 million since its founding.
Despite a difficult few years for the cleantech sector, BluWave sees a renewed opportunity to help utilities manage energy fluctuations with AI software.
“All the data centres that are coming on board around the world are adding strain to the grid,” Paul said in an interview. Despite a difficult few years for the cleantech sector, BluWave sees a renewed opportunity to help utilities manage energy fluctuations with AI software.
Nearly 10 years ago, BluWave bet on the need for technology to help utilities manage a green energy transition. The company built an app that tracks energy loads and optimizes renewable energy usage and electric vehicle (EVs) charging. This summer, it partnered with four electricity utilities in Ontario to provide a provincial regulation system for EV charging.
It has established a global presence, with operations in Japan and in Europe. BluWave has also amassed a broad portfolio of patents for its energy management technology, allowing it to build a business out of licensing the patents to customers who want to create their own tailored products.
Paul said that changes in US administration leadership have swayed the clean-energy market over the years. When former President Joe Biden was in power, companies similar to BluWave cropped up to meet demand for smart solutions to renewable energy management, raising money along the way. But since then, through President Donald Trump’s second term, as he has slashed environmental regulations, Paul said some of BluWave’s competition has thinned out.
Then came the generative AI era: projected demand has exploded for data centres to supply computing power for AI. Canada has been no exception; Québec’s provincial utility suggested that electricity demand could increase by more than 30 percent by 2041, in part due to new data centre demand. In last week’s federal budget, the government pledged to enable domestic access to 500 megawatts of “sovereign AI compute.” At the same time, US data centre builders are eyeing Canada as an attractive destination, with projects underway from Anthropic, Meta, and Microsoft.
RELATED: Cleantech startup BluWave-ai closes $3.9 million in seed funding
All of this will undoubtedly make balancing provincial electricity grids more tricky, something BluWave argues it was built to help with. “We’ve played a bit of a long game,” Paul said.
While its main customers are utilities, Paul said it’s also targeting data centre operators and tenants. BluWave has developed a product tailored to data centre operators it claims would allow them to shift compute-intensive workloads to periods of low demand on electrical grids and consume less electricity in the process.
Along with the round, which BluWave is describing as “Series A2,” the company has added two board members: Suzanne Grant, the executive director of the Capital Angels Network, and former board member Mario Montana, a former semiconductor company entrepreneur. Montana stepped away in 2023 due to his professional and family workload, but Paul said the opportunity has since arisen to bring him back on.
Feature image courtesy Unsplash. Photo by Matthew Henry.

articles.title: Google lança IA para programar que promete ser 2,5 vezes mais rápida
articles.text:
O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen, novo modelo de inteligência artificial (IA) desenvolvido para programação, tarefas multimodais e fluxos de trabalho com agentes. Segundo a empresa, a tecnologia consegue concluir tarefas até 2,5 vezes mais rápido que seu antecessor, o Gemini 3.8 Flash.
Apresentado nesta quinta-feira (12), o modelo foi desenvolvido para executar atividades com rapidez e eficiência, incluindo escrever códigos, identificar erros, testar soluções e navegar por grandes bases de dados e repositórios de software.
De acordo com o Google, o Hydrogen também apresenta melhorias na precisão das respostas e na execução de instruções. Em testes internos, a empresa afirma que o modelo reduziu em mais de cinco vezes a quantidade de afirmações inventadas em comparação com a versão anterior.
Outro destaque está no desempenho em programação. No benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.1, a pontuação passou de 18,2% no Gemini 3.8 Flash para 57% no novo modelo.
O Hydrogen também supera o Gemini 4 Argon no Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, com 51 pontos na configuração padrão de raciocínio avançado, contra 50 do outro modelo. Na configuração máxima, a pontuação chega a 54.
Gemini 4 Hydrogen trabalha com outros modelos do Google
- Uma das novidades do lançamento é a possibilidade de utilizar o Hydrogen em conjunto com outros modelos da família Gemini 4, como Carbon e Argon;
- A proposta é dividir atividades conforme a complexidade de cada etapa. Enquanto modelos mais avançados podem cuidar de decisões complexas e análises profundas, o Hydrogen fica responsável pela execução rápida de tarefas, como escrever códigos, rodar testes e verificar alterações;
- Para facilitar esse trabalho, o Google apresentou o Orchestrator, recurso da plataforma de desenvolvimento Antigravity que alterna automaticamente entre diferentes modelos durante uma mesma sessão;
- Em testes com o benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.0, a ferramenta alcançou resultados de sucesso próximos aos do Gemini 4 Carbon, mas consumiu, em média, 24% menos cota e concluiu as tarefas 19% mais rápido;
- O sistema também permite utilizar agentes em paralelo. Nesse cenário, o Carbon pode atuar como coordenador, enquanto o Hydrogen executa tarefas específicas e verifica alterações em ambientes de trabalho separados.
Nova IA também analisa documentos, vídeos e planilhas
Apesar do foco em programação, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen também foi desenvolvido para atividades multimodais. O modelo consegue trabalhar com documentos PDF, planilhas, gráficos, arquivos de áudio e vídeos.
Segundo o Google, a tecnologia pode reunir informações de diferentes formatos e produzir relatórios estruturados, com referências aos materiais utilizados.
O modelo também foi projetado para desenvolvimento de sites e aplicativos interativos. Entre as possibilidades estão a criação de interfaces, protótipos e experiências visuais a partir de instruções em linguagem natural.
Outra novidade é a oferta de quatro níveis de raciocínio: baixo, médio, alto e xhigh. A configuração permite ajustar o equilíbrio entre velocidade, capacidade de processamento e profundidade das respostas, de acordo com a complexidade da atividade.
Leia mais:
- Gemini 4 Argon finalmente chega ao app e à busca do Google; saiba mais
- Gemini agora permite editar PDFs, documentos e planilhas dentro do chat
- Gemini chega ao Apple CarPlay e permite conversar com IA enquanto dirige
Gemini 4 Hydrogen também chega à Busca do Google
A atualização não ficará restrita ao desenvolvimento de software. O Google também incorporou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen à Busca, com melhorias na compreensão de perguntas e na apresentação dos resultados.
A tecnologia permite interpretar pesquisas feitas em linguagem natural, mesmo quando o usuário apresenta várias perguntas em uma única consulta ou comete erros de digitação. As respostas também passam a ter mais elementos visuais e variedade maior de links e sites relevantes.
No aplicativo Gemini, o modelo também promete melhorar a execução de tarefas cotidianas, a produção de textos, pesquisas e a integração com serviços, como Gmail e Google Drive.
Quanto custa e onde usar o Gemini 4 Hydrogen?
O Gemini 4 Hydrogen está disponível globalmente para desenvolvedores, empresas e consumidores, mas as condições de acesso variam conforme a plataforma.
Desenvolvedores podem utilizar o modelo pela API Gemini, no Google AI Studio e no Android Studio. Empresas também podem acessá-lo por meio do Gemini para negócios.
No Google Antigravity, plataforma de desenvolvimento da companhia, o acesso está disponível para assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra.
No aplicativo Gemini, usuários gratuitos podem receber acesso ao Hydrogen por meio da seleção automática de modelos, quando o sistema considerar que ele é adequado à solicitação. O modelo também foi incorporado à Busca do Google.
Para desenvolvedores que utilizam a API, o preço anunciado é de US$ 1,50 (aproximadamente R$ 8,40) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 (cerca de R$ 42,10) por milhão de tokens de saída.
O modelo oferece suporte a até um milhão de tokens de entrada e um milhão de tokens de saída, permitindo trabalhar com grandes volumes de informação em uma mesma interação.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists have gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual UN climate talks. But this year’s negotiations are taking place against a particularly tense geopolitical backdrop, as the world falls further behind the Paris Agreement’s goals.
Energy prices are soaring, and there are big questions about how countries will tackle the climate crisis. Expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance, and whether negotiators can agree on meaningful action.
Here’s what you need to know about COP31.
—Casey Crownhart
This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.
Inside the quest for cognitive immortality
Far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going beyond death. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores their ideas, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud.

articles.title: No, AI agents did not discover a previously unknown Maya site
articles.text:
Armed with a team of AI agents, Google researcher Pietro Miotti claimed earlier this week to have discovered a potentially unmapped Maya site in Mexico. There was just one problem: The site had already been discovered and was published in an academic journal last year. The incident, which sparked criticism among archeologists online, underscores a growing tension in science as amateurs wielding increasingly powerful AI tools parachute into specialist fields, often without the expertise needed to understand what they are looking at.
No, AI agents did not discover a previously unknown Maya site
Scientists are getting tired of amateurs parachuting into their fields and making ‘discoveries’ with AI.
Local communities are often already well aware of sites in their area.
Miotti said the idea to use AI to search for archeological sites came to him while traveling in Peru, when he began wondering what historic explorers might do with access to modern technology. He settled on lidar, a laser-based mapping technology that can produce detailed three-dimensional images of the environment, and set a team of 48 AI agents to comb through NASA lidar data for signs of undocumented sites. As “Peru isn’t well covered” by public lidar data, Miotti wrote, he shifted his focus to the Maya region.
The agents flagged numerous promising locations, including “one major village [that] doesn’t seem to have been registered” in existing records. Miotti, who described the research to The Verge as a personal side project done without any Google compute or resources, said he then reached out to Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) to check whether the apparent discovery was already known, including through unpublished research. Using the agents to translate his correspondence into Spanish, Miotti said INAH told him it had no record of a registered site at that location.
“It took less than 72 hours to go from a random thought while traveling to an official reply from the Mexican government. This is by far the best time ever to be alive,” Miotti wrote on his blog.
Miotti stressed that he is not an archeologist and emphasized that the finding would need to be verified with fieldwork. Nevertheless, he hailed it as proof that “we’re on the brink of a revolution across every science” and called for the “entire planet” to be mapped with lidar so AI agents could “help us find the rest.” Had he been an archaeologist familiar with the region, however, Miotti might have spotted a problem: The site was already known, and had been documented in an academic journal more than a year earlier.
“I didn’t expect it to get this much attention.”
Archeologists were quick to point out the oversight on social media. In a series of posts on Bluesky, Sarah Parcak, an archeology professor at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, stressed the importance of carefully checking findings against existing research. “This is why we have peer review,” Parcak wrote, adding that just because the Mexican government doesn’t have something in its database doesn’t mean it is unknown or unmapped. Other archeologists echoed her criticism, slamming the project for spreading misinformation and taking credit away from archeologists, who have been using advanced digital tools in their work for decades.
“This was a personal project that I was excited to share,” Miotti told The Verge. “I didn’t expect it to get this much attention.” He added that as a non-archaeologist, he had not realized a site not being registered wasn’t the same as it not having been mapped, adding that expert knowledge “is needed to verify what the agents find.” He also addressed the limits of his AI tools: “My agents and I missed it. Archaeologists rightly don’t publish the coordinates of sites, so checking whether a site is already known means comparing images against figures in papers, not searching a database. That’s much harder for agents, and it’s something these tools need to get better at. When people pointed it out, I updated the post and the blog as soon as I could to credit their work.”
Nevertheless, Miotti said this was an example of how agents could be used to help experts sort through large amounts of data. He said he has been encouraged by the archaeologists and PhD students that he said were reaching out to him “excited about the workflow and wanting to know how it works and whether it could help with their own survey data.”
“Our ‘problem’ is not discovering new sites,” Elizabeth Graham, a professor of Mesoamerican archaeology at University College London, told The Verge. “Most of us working in the Maya area know about tons of sites not explored or excavated or mapped, most of these found on foot,” she said. Graham also critiqued the use of the word “discover,” noting that local communities are often already well aware of sites in their area.
While she credited Miotti with doing a decent job of using AI to map the mounds from lidar data — “the interpretation of lidar data can be tricky” — Graham argued the bigger obstacle is funding for research. “The fact is, there just isn’t the funding to excavate or map sites as there was in the past, so in a way it doesn’t matter how many more are ‘discovered.’”
“Just spotting something does not add much to our knowledge.”
The controversy reflects a broader problem with AI in science, perhaps most visible with OpenAI’s recent advances in mathematics. While AI tools are increasingly capable of producing genuinely impressive results, they don’t always engage with the existing research those findings build upon. The result can be claimed breakthroughs that have, as is the case here, already been made by someone else, or a general failure to credit earlier work. Even when the findings are actually new, they can lack context a specialist would bring. Ultimately, amateur use of AI tools often ends up shifting the burden of establishing what has actually been found and why it matters to actual experts, work that would ordinarily be part of making a scientific discovery in the first place.
Ivan Šprajc, a professor of archaeology at the Research Centre of the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts in Ljubljana and a coauthor of the paper documenting the site, told The Verge he wasn’t particularly impressed by the agents’ work. Archeologists have been using lidar and “other sophisticated remote sensing tools for quite some time,” he said, adding that “just spotting something does not add much to our knowledge.” He told The Verge that while it is commendable that Miotti checked in with INAH, doing so is “not sufficient” as the institution does not have access to all possible information. “The fact that INAH has no official knowledge of a particular cluster of archaeological features does not necessarily mean that it has not been spotted or even explored by archaeologists.”
Šprajc said that he worries the growing use of AI tools by amateurs could overwhelm archeologists with claims of new discoveries. “Just today I have received an email from another AI ‘discoverer,’ so I am a little bit concerned about being flooded by this kind of message,” he said. He also raised another potential risk of amateurs publicizing the locations of archeological sites: attracting looters. “But as long as these findings do not lead to looting, I don’t see a major problem,” he added.

articles.title: The Memory Challenge Of Physical AI
articles.text:
Right-size the memory hierarchy around the device’s data streams, reuse patterns, latency requirements, and operating constraints.
Most AI hardware conversations start with compute, which is understandable since accelerators are visible, easy to compare, and often tied to headline performance metrics. Physical AI broadens that conversation by placing greater emphasis on how compute, memory, and data movement work together under real-world operating constraints. For intelligent systems that must see, interpret, decide, and act in the physical world in real time, it’s critical that the right data reaches the right engine at the right time.
As a result, data movement has become an increasingly important consideration when architecting physical AI systems. A physical AI device may simultaneously handle sensor streams, model weights, activations, temporary buffers, control loops, and safety functions. If memory access becomes unpredictable, compute engines can stall. Power consumption rises when data is moved too often, and poorly planned buffering can cause latency accumulation that is hard to recover from later.
As physical AI workloads become more complex, architects must now consider how predictably the complete system performs when multiple real-world workloads are active simultaneously.
Physical AI systems rely on a memory hierarchy that coordinates on-chip memory with larger-capacity external memory. LPDDR or GDDR may hold model weights, sensor data, activations, and other working data, while on-chip SRAM and cache keep the portions currently needed by the NPU, CPU, DSP, ISP, or other processing engines close to compute.
As workloads move through the processing pipeline, required data is transferred from external memory into on-chip memory, where it can be accessed and reused with lower latency and energy. The more effectively the architecture reuses that local data, the fewer times it must retrieve the same information from external memory. However, because SRAM and cache consume silicon area, their capacity is limited. Data that does not fit on-chip, or is used less frequently, remains in LPDDR or GDDR until it is needed.
This coordination is important because every unnecessary transfer across the memory hierarchy consumes energy, adds latency, and uses external-memory bandwidth. Physical AI systems are also constrained by device size, package complexity, power delivery, and thermal headroom. The goal is therefore not to eliminate external memory access, but to keep the right data close to compute for as long as it is useful and avoid moving it more often than necessary.
A well-planned dataflow coordinates compute engines, on-chip SRAM and cache, external LPDDR or GDDR, buffering, and interconnect around the workload. This helps keep compute resources productive while using external-memory capacity and bandwidth efficiently.
Humanoid robots, drones, autonomous vehicles, smart cameras, inspection robots, industrial robots, and autonomous mobile robots may all run local intelligence, yet each stresses memory and interfaces differently. Their architectures must determine which data should remain close to compute for immediate access and which should reside in higher-capacity external memory.
Humanoids may combine cameras, depth sensing, audio, inertial data, balance control, object recognition, path planning, and actuator feedback within a limited power and thermal envelope. If perception data arrives late, control decisions may be delayed. In addition, sustained performance drops and power rises if model weights and intermediate data are reloaded too often. In this kind of system, memory efficiency affects how smoothly the robot can perceive, decide, and move, all of which are key to successful real-time operation.
A drone or autonomous mobile robot has a different set of constraints. It may need visual navigation, obstacle avoidance, stabilization, object tracking, wireless communication, and video processing, all while staying within a limited power and thermal budget. Unnecessary external memory accesses reduce operating time, add heat, or introduce latency into the control loop. For these physical AI systems, bandwidth per watt is as important as raw bandwidth.
Autonomous vehicles and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) present an even greater challenge. With cameras, radar, lidar, ultrasonic sensors, vehicle telemetry, map data, and control functions, competition for memory access is fierce. Some data streams need continuous throughput, while others need fusion across sensor domains. Retaining relevant data long enough to support planning and decision-making is also an important consideration. In this environment, memory behavior affects both throughput and response predictability.
When building a memory architecture, architects should begin with the behavior of the physical AI workload itself. The objective is not simply to select the fastest external memory technology or provision the greatest possible bandwidth. It is to right-size the complete memory hierarchy, including local storage, external memory capacity, bandwidth, power, buffering, and integration, around the device’s data streams, reuse patterns, latency requirements, and operating constraints.
LPDDR and GDDR address different architectural priorities. LPDDR is often a strong fit when bandwidth per watt and memory capacity are needed to sustain local inference performance. When continuous image or sensor-stream bandwidth is the primary requirement, GDDR may be a viable option because its high bandwidth can meet those performance needs with fewer DRAM devices.
Available solutions give architects considerable flexibility in making this tradeoff. For example, Cadence offers LPDDR6/LPDDR5X PHY and Controller IP supporting data rates up to 14.4Gbps, as well as GDDR7 PHY IP supporting data rates up to 36Gbps for high-bandwidth applications. These options allow the external memory interface to be aligned with the workload rather than treated as a one-size-fits-all design choice.
A humanoid robot may prioritize power-efficient access to model weights, perception data, and control information. A smart camera or autonomous-vehicle perception processor may place greater pressure on sustained vision-stream bandwidth. In each case, the architecture should keep frequently reused and latency-sensitive data close to compute while selecting an external memory interface sized for the remaining capacity and bandwidth requirements. This helps avoid both memory bottlenecks and unnecessary over-provisioning.
| Device context | Examples | Primary pressure | Likely memory fit | 
| Mobile physical AI devices | Humanoids, drones, autonomous mobile robots, robotic modules | Sustained local inference under size, capacity, bandwidth, and latency limits | LPDDR for bandwidth-per-watt and high DRAM capacity design; GDDR selectively for heavy vision streams | 
| Vision-heavy physical AI devices | Autonomous vehicles, smart cameras, inspection robots, industrial vision systems | Continuous image or sensor streams with predictable response | LPDDR where memory capacity matters; GDDR when stream bandwidth dominates | 
Before selecting an external memory interface, architects should evaluate how the device’s dataflow and operating constraints affect five key areas:
A balanced memory architecture aligns data locality, traffic management, external memory selection, buffering, and latency predictability with the device workload. Together, these decisions help reduce unnecessary data movement, keep compute resources productive, and maintain predictable performance when multiple workloads operate concurrently.
Physical AI places intelligence inside devices that operate continuously, interact with real-world signals, and respond under power, thermal, latency, and reliability constraints. Meeting these demands requires compute, memory, and data movement to function as a coordinated system. Predictable data movement is crucial for physical AI devices to operate effectively under real-world conditions, making memory architecture an important part of the overall design. Selecting the right memory requires a careful balance of latency, power efficiency, bandwidth, buffering, and workload requirements. Architects must keep frequently used data close to the engines that need it, use external bandwidth efficiently, keep compute resources productive, and maintain predictable system behavior as workloads operate concurrently.
Learn more about how to architect physical AI systems with design IP in Cadence’s “Designing Physical AI Systems Under Real-World Constraints” white paper.

articles.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach
articles.text:
Apify has rotated critical internal secrets and revoked some third-party OAuth connections after detecting unauthorized access to its internal systems.
The incident occurred between November 9 and 10 and was detected the next day at 12:13 UTC. The company reacted by cutting off the attacker's access and launching an investigation to determine the impact.
Apify's response involved invalidating internal credentials, rotating API tokens, and resetting all active sessions.
Apify is a Czech web scraping and browser automation platform for developers. Businesses use its services to collect data for websites, search results, and social media posts.
The platform grew significantly with the generative AI boom, and reports having 80,000 customers, including Microsoft, Samsung, T-Mobile, Accenture, Siemens, the European Commission, and Roche.
Rotating customer API tokens and passwords
“On 9 and 10 November 2026, an unauthorized third party gained access to parts of Apify’s internal systems,” Apify said in an update on the incident.
Apify said it also revoked OAuth connections to external integrations, including GitHub, out of an abundance of caution. Impacted users can expect to be informed via email when it’s safe to reconnect.
In one notification, Apify said it had found no indication that account data stored on its platform had been affected by the incident. A sample seen by BleepingComputer informs that impacted customers' Apify API tokens and Apify Proxy passwords have been rotated.
In another letter sent to affected customers, the company advises recipients to reset their two-factor authentication (2FA) through the Apify Console, warning that their 2FA codes may have been exposed while assuring them that their passwords remain safe.

articles.text:
Volvo poursuit le développement de sa gamme électrique pour obtenir le plus rapidement possible un portfolio aussi complet que pertinent. 2027 verra ainsi l’arrivée d’un modèle entièrement inédit qui viendra se glisser entre l’EX40 et l’EX60. Le futur EX50 ira tailler des croupières au Tesla Model Y avec son autonomie XXL et sa recharge ultra rapide. Son prix devrait démarrer aux alentours des 50 000 €. Une future menace en vue ?
Ce n’est en tout cas pas une menace surprise car l’EX50 devait initialement remplacer les vieillissants XC40 et EX40 en un seul et même modèle électrique. Mais ça, c’était à l’époque où Volvo voulait faire une croix sur le thermique. Les choses ont changé depuis, avec une demande toujours incertaine sur les modèles à batterie. Le récent revirement de l’Europe sur l’échéance de 2035 en est une preuve supplémentaire.
4,60 mètres et 50 000 € : le gabarit idéal pour faire plier le Model Y ?
Raison pour laquelle le duo XC40/EX40 survivra pour concurrencer les BMW iX1, Mercedes GLA et Audi Q4 e-tron, plus compacts. L’EX50, lui, jouera le rôle de modèle électrique mondial avec un gabarit idéal. Dans sa récente conférence sur les résultats financiers du troisième trimestre, le constructeur a confirmé à demi-mot l’arrivée de ce véhicule : 2027 verra « un nouveau modèle pour l’Europe et deux modèles spécifiques au marché chinois ».
Plus long que les 4,44 mètres de l’EX40, l’EX50 devrait mesurer 4,60 ou 4,70 mètres, ce qui lui permettra de mieux cibler les 4,79 mètres du Tesla Model Y. L’EX60 s’étendant sur 4,80 mètres est plus proche de l’américain, certes, mais il le surpasse complètement en termes de prix ! C’est bien là que l’EX50 aura sa carte à jouer. Il misera aussi sur une technique avancée, en reposant très probablement sur la plateforme SPA3 utilisée par l’EX60.
Recharge de 10 à 80 % en 16 minutes : la claque technique assénée à la concurrence
L’EX50 se permettra ainsi de reprendre les batteries de son grand frère. On aura alors le choix entre un pack de 80 ou 91 kWh offrant respectivement 600 et 650 km d’autonomie. L’accumulateur de 112 kWh donnant 810 km sur l’EX60 serait prometteur pour abattre la concurrence, mais il pourrait être trop encombrant pour les entrailles du futur EX50. Le rayon d’action maximal restera dans tous les cas supérieur à celui du Model Y.
Côté recharge rapide, le suédois ne chômera pas avec sa plateforme 800 V. La puissance de 400 kW en courant continu DC de l’EX60 sera ainsi de la partie pour un 10 à 80 % de batterie en environ 16 minutes. Le Model Y est là encore loin derrière. Il gardera en revanche la main côté prix. Sauf si Volvo fait un effort ? Probablement produit en Slovaquie, le suédois pourrait être éligible aux aides de l’État, si son tarif passe sous les 47 000 €. Un autre défi…

articles.title: Entró en vigor: los propietarios no están obligados a pagar las cuotas de la comunidad pendientes si han pasado 5 años
articles.text:
Si tienes cuotas de la comunidad pendientes desde hace años, debes saber que eso no significa que tengas que pagarlas. Así, si la comunidad no ha realizado reclamaciones dentro del plazo legal, puede perder el derecho a exigirlas, pero para ello hay que comprobar dos cosas: cuándo vencieron los recibos y si existió algún tipo de reclamación.
Como recoge El Español en su información sobre las cuotas comunitarias, el Tribunal Supremo confirmó en varias sentencias que el plazo pasa de 15 años a solo 5. De esta forma, el tiempo anterior baja una década y la clave está en que esas cuotas ahora tienen su propia regulación al considerarse pagos periódicos.
Así, el artículo 1966.3 del Código Civil establece 5 años para reclamar cantidades que se deban abonar anualmente o en periodos más cortos. El Supremo reiteró esta interpretación en varias resoluciones, pero hay un detalle importante: el plazo se puede interrumpir si la comunidad reclama la deuda judicial o extrajudicialmente, o si el propio propietario la reconoce. Por eso, no basta con que un recibo tenga más de 5 años para considerarlo prescrito.
A todo esto debemos sumar que la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal obliga a los propietarios a contribuir a los gastos generales del edificio entre los que se incluyen, por ejemplo, servicios y cargas comunes. Si se produce un impago, la comunidad puede acudir al procedimiento monitorio especial para recuperar el dinero, pero solo podrá hacerlo si se cumplen los requisitos de liquidación y notificación de la deuda. Por eso, antes de reclamar, conviene revisar qué cuotas siguen siendo exigibles y cuáles podrían haber prescrito.

articles.title: Proton répond à la polémique sur l’IA avec un billet sur la sécurité de ses données
articles.text:
Après l’enquête de 404 Media sur le virage IA de l’entreprise, Proton explique dans un billet de blog comment la société protège ses données et assure qu’un humain valide chaque modification de code.
Il y a quelques semaines, 404 Media partageait des informations ayant fuité par un employé de Proton sur le changement de stratégie en interne. L’entreprise suisse entend miser plus que jamais sur l’IA, au risque de soulever plusieurs craintes, tant en interne que chez les utilisateurs. Dans un billet de blog, l’éditeur explique comment il sécurise ses services tout en utilisant l’IA pour se défendre.
Un SIEM, des clés physiques et un humain à chaque validation
Proton s’appuie sur un SIEM (Security Information and Event Management). Cet outil enregistre toutes les actions réalisées dans le périmètre de sécurité, qu’elles viennent d’un salarié ou d’un agent IA, c’est-à-dire un programme capable d’agir seul. Des analystes humains traitent chaque alerte suspecte. Seuls les appareils autorisés accèdent aux systèmes internes, et l’autorisation passe par des jetons physiques (des clés de sécurité matérielles) qu’une IA ne peut pas manipuler seule. Les serveurs et les ordinateurs portables sont aussi surveillés pour repérer des indicateurs de compromission, c’est-à-dire des traces d’intrusion.
Pour Proton, l’IA est aussi un outil de défense, et le seul qui permette de tenir. Des attaques qui demandaient autrefois les moyens d’un État sont désormais à la portée de presque n’importe qui. Or un attaquant n’a besoin que d’une faille, alors qu’un défenseur doit toutes les fermer. Le billet cite trois usages.
- Des relecteurs automatiques repèrent des défauts avant qu’une modification soit fusionnée dans le code principal, en plus des relecteurs humains.
- Des analyses continues cherchent des vulnérabilités dans le code de Proton, avec des modèles maison et des modèles « cyber » non publics d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic. Ces modèles ne reçoivent que du code source et des informations sur les menaces, jamais de contenu client.
- Enfin, des outils internes aident une équipe d’analystes à surveiller une surface d’attaque devenue trop vaste pour des humains seuls. Ce sont ensuite eux qui enquêtent sur les signaux remontés.
À ce jour, chaque modification doit être approuvée par un humain. Proton admet qu’aucune entreprise ne peut supprimer tous les risques et promet qu’une personne restera responsable de chaque changement mis en production.
Proton freine son élan
Mais au-delà des mécanismes purement techniques, il y a bien sûr les équipes et leur adoption de l’IA en interne. Nous rapportions fin octobre que Proton avait prévenu ses salariés d’entretiens sur leur usage de l'IA, puis assuré sur Reddit que cette technologie n’était pas un prétexte à des licenciements. L’enquête reposait également sur des messages Slack, des enregistrements de réunions et les témoignages de huit salariés. En réunion, le directeur technique, Bart Butler, aurait déclaré que 90% du code de Proton était écrit par IA. Plusieurs salariés disent qu’une bonne partie vient de Claude, le modèle d’Anthropic.
Par ailleurs, le manifeste interne publié par le directeur technique Bart Butler expliquait vouloir qu’une grande partie du code soit relue par des IA et non plus par des humains. Plusieurs salariés auraient été encouragés à travailler plus rapidement et affirmaient aussi ne pas oser évoquer leurs inquiétudes sur le degré de sécurité, par crainte de représailles.
Les fuites internes semblent donc avoir freiné l’élan initial de Proton sur un développement presqu’entièrement géré par une IA, avec des garde-fous humains et une sécurité toujours sous contrôle. Il faut dire que la communauté, elle aussi, a largement fait savoir qu’elle n’appréciait pas ce changement stratégique, tant sur le plan technique que sur les décisions de la direction envers les employés. L’entreprise reconnaît une communication bâclée avec les équipes internes.
Reste à savoir si l’entreprise saura bel et bien prendre le virage de l’IA pour rester compétitive face aux Big Tech tout en accompagnant la masse salariale vers cette transition. Si l’affaire a été particulièrement médiatisée, ce n’est certainement pas la seule entreprise à se heurter au problème.

articles.title: Volkswagen rapatrie la technologie chinoise, pas les voitures : Thomas Schäfer explique pourquoi
articles.text:
À force de voir Volkswagen multiplier les modèles électriques connectés et abordables en Chine, la question finit par se poser : à quand la même chose en Europe ? Sur place, le constructeur allemand a profondément revu sa copie industrielle pour tenir le rythme face aux marques locales, notamment grâce à son centre de R&D de Hefei.
Lors d’une table ronde à Xiamen le vendredi 6 novembre, à laquelle Numerama a assisté, Thomas Schäfer a posé les limites de ce transfert technologique. Le patron de la marque se dit favorable à l’arrivée de l’architecture électronique chinoise chez nous, mais ferme la porte à l’importation de voitures ou de plateformes à bas coût.
L’architecture électronique CEA viendra en Europe… en cohabitation avec Rivian
Le constructeur a confirmé l’arrivée en Europe de la CEA (China Electronic Architecture), son architecture électronique zonale développée en Chine pour réduire drastiquement le nombre de calculateurs et déployer des mises à jour à distance (OTA) fluides. De même, les systèmes d’aide à la conduite avancés conçus localement seront intégrés aux futurs modèles européens reposant sur la plateforme MEB+.
Mais cette brique technologique et logicielle chinoise ne régnera pas seule en Europe. Elle devra partager l’affiche avec la technologie issue de la coentreprise américaine nouée avec Rivian (baptisée RVT). « À l’échelle mondiale, nous aurons deux architectures : la CEA et la RVT avec Rivian. C’est géopolitiquement nécessaire », a expliqué Thomas Schäfer à Xiamen, rappelant qu’il est impossible d’installer un logiciel conçu en Chine dans une voiture vendue aux États-Unis, et inversement.
Pour le marché européen, situé entre ces deux blocs, Volkswagen opte pour une approche pragmatique. « Ce sera probablement un mélange, non pas mélangé au sein d’un même véhicule, mais plutôt réparti selon les tailles de modèles et les marques », a précisé le dirigeant, laissant entendre que les modèles grand public et abordables pourraient privilégier l’architecture chinoise, moins coûteuse à développer, tandis que les véhicules plus statutaires pourraient s’appuyer sur la base Rivian. Rien n’est encore figé : « Nous examinons actuellement cette question pour voir ».
Pas de plateforme CMP ni de modèle chinois à prix cassé chez nous
En revanche, inutile d’espérer voir débarquer la nouvelle plateforme CMP (Compact Main Platform), conçue en Chine pour abaisser drastiquement les coûts de production. Si Volkswagen compte bien l’exporter sous le nom de GMP (Global Main Platform) vers les marchés émergents comme l’Inde ou le Brésil d’ici la fin de la décennie, l’Europe n’est pas concernée.
« En Europe, notre plateforme MQB est imbattable en termes d’échelle et de performances. Cela n’a pas de sens de la remplacer alors qu’elle est déjà amortie. Nous passerons directement de notre configuration actuelle vers la future plateforme SSP », a tranché Thomas Schäfer.
Le patron de Volkswagen acte au passage la fin d’un vieux rêve industriel : « C’est de moins en moins possible de faire une voiture mondiale. » Entre une Amérique du Nord qui revient vers le thermique, une Chine obsédée par les grands gabarits connectés (sans besoin de capacité de remorquage ni de transmission intégrale) et une Europe très hétérogène, exigeant de petites citadines comme des breaks familiaux, les cahiers des charges ont divergé.
Cette fracture explique aussi pourquoi Volkswagen refuse catégoriquement d’importer directement en Europe ses modèles électriques vendus à prix cassés en Chine (dommage pour la toute nouvelle Volkswagen ID. Era 5X qu’on a testée).
À l’exception de modèles pensés dès l’origine pour l’export, comme le Cupra Tavascan, les voitures chinoises de la marque utilisent des matériaux et des composants (pare-brise, électronique) non conformes aux normes d’homologation européennes. « En Chine, il faut faire des voitures taillées sur mesure pour la Chine. Si vous commencez à bricoler en vous disant “tiens, on va aussi les exporter”, vous rendez la voiture plus chère et vous devenez non compétitif sur place », résume Thomas Schäfer.
Plutôt que de chercher à importer des voitures chinoises qui perdraient leur avantage tarifaire une fois passées à la moulinette des normes européennes, Wolfsburg rapatrie l’essentiel : la méthode de travail et l’architecture logicielle CEA, déjà prête et éprouvée. Reste un défi de taille pour les ingénieurs allemands : faire cohabiter sans heurts deux architectures électroniques distinctes (Chine et Rivian) au sein d’un même groupe en Europe, sous peine de replonger dans les déboires logiciels qui ont plombé la marque ces dernières années.

articles.title: ValueQuest commits Rs 775 Cr to advance India’s defence, manufacturing push
articles.text:
ValueQuest commits Rs 775 Cr to advance India’s defence, manufacturing push
The Mumbai-based investment manager is backing three businesses operating in the areas of defence tech, precision engineering, and power infrastructure: Sagar Defence Engineering, TASE Global, and Rational Engineers.
ValueQuest Investment Advisors, a Mumbai-based investment manager, has made a total commitment of Rs 775 crore to three Indian businesses in defence technology, precision engineering, and power infrastructure.
The investment firm announced new investments in Sagar Defence Engineering and Rational Engineers and also added to its earlier investment in TASE Global. The Rs 775 crore is a portfolio commitment, not a single company’s fundraise.
Sagar Defence Engineering develops unmanned and autonomous systems for maritime and other defence applications. Rational Engineers makes specialised copper conductors and insulation products for power and distribution transformers. TASE Global operates in India and the United States, manufacturing precision components and assemblies for global original equipment manufacturers and Tier-I suppliers across medical technology, aerospace, defence and industrial markets.
ValueQuest says its private equity platform manages more than Rs 6,000 crore, including co-investments, and is building out SCALE Fund II.
The investment strategy reflects the wider shift in the manufacturing sector. Companies are diversifying supply chains and seeking to reduce dependence on overseas suppliers for strategically important technology and components.
Ravi Dharamshi, Founder and Chief Investment Officer of ValueQuest, said, “The opportunity is not simply for India to manufacture more, but for Indian companies to develop the technology, capabilities and customer relationships to become globally competitive enterprises.”
Defence policy and procurement are helping drive this shift. The government reported that domestic defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, with private firms accounting for 24%. Meanwhile, exports rose to Rs 38,424 crore.
The government is targeting annual production of Rs 3 lakh crore and exports of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029. It has also opened 25% of the defence research and development budget to industry, startups and academia.
Power infrastructure offers another source of demand. The National Electricity Plan envisages peak demand of 388 GW by 2032 and an increase in the transmission network from 5.09 lakh circuit kilometres in June 2026 to 6.48 lakh by 2032. This expansion should support demand for transformers and components, although actual orders will depend on project execution.
Aniket Dharamshi, Co-founder and Managing Partner, ValueQuest, said the firm was not rushing to deploy capital. “Our focus is not on the pace of capital deployment, but on identifying the right businesses,” he said.
Recently, ValueQuest’s Tristar Fund secured over Rs 2,100 crore in commitments within 15 months of its first close, exceeding its original target and greenshoe.

articles.title: /Plan und /Goal: Was bringen die Abkürzungen für KI?
articles.text:
/Plan oder /Goal? So nutzt du zwei KI-Modi sinnvoll im Büroalltag
Wenig eingeben, aber dennoch präzisere Ausgaben bekommen: Dafür gibt es bei KI sinnvolle Abkürzungen. Zwei davon bringen im Büro am meisten, findet Prompt Engineer Susanne Renate Schneider: Plan- und Zielmodus. Im Podcast t3n MeisterPrompter erklärt sie mit t3n-Redakteurin Stella-Sophie Wojtczak, wie sich beide unterscheiden.
/plan und /goal nutzen
Im Planmodus werden dir bei ChatGPT laut Renate gezielt Rückfragen gestellt. Darauf basierend entsteht dann ein Plan. Im Vergleich mit einem einfachen Prompt seien die Fragen im Planmodus laut Renate direkt fokussierter.
Aktivierst du den Zielmodus, beschreibst du ChatGPT oder Claude lediglich dein Ziel, inklusiv der beschreibenden Kriterien. Die KI arbeitet dann auf dieses Ergebniss hin, auch über mehrere Schritte. In ChatGPT waren die Modi wie /study zum lernen bisher auch über die Vorauswahl erreichbar, das gelingt allerdings aktuell nicht.
Am einfachsten ist es dabei, diese Chatvorgabe mit /plan und /goal anzufordern. Das funktioniert laut Renate Tool-übergreifend. Selbstläufer sind die Modi jedoch nicht. Du musst demzufolge Rückfragen beantworten und Zwischenschritte prüfen. Die Verantwortung für die KI-Ergebnisse trägst außerdem du. When will the best 2026 Black Friday coffee machine sales start?

What Black Friday 2026 coffee machine deals do we expect to see?

Do Nespresso machines go on sale on Black Friday?

Nespresso machines that went on sale during Black Friday and Cyber Monday last year, included Nespresso Vertuo Pop and Vertuo Next.
What's a good coffee machine for home use?
It depends on how you like your coffee, and how much time you want to spend making it. You can check out our guide to the best coffee machines, but here's a quick breakdown:
• Best Nespresso: Nespresso Vertuo Pop
• Best overall: Breville the Barista Touch Impress
• Best travel: Wacaco Nanopresso
Does the coffee maker really make a difference?
In short, yes, the price and quality of a coffee machine will make a big difference to how your coffee tastes. While there are a few different reasons for this, the main thing that more expensive machines do better than cheap ones, is regulate the water temperature. A high-quality water heater will ensure you coffee is brewed at the perfect temperature, making sure all the flavour comes out, without burning the beans and making it bitter.
Tips for buying a coffee machine during Black Friday
1. Look at individual specifications: When thinking about grabbing a new coffee machine and looking at Black Friday discounts, the number one tip to remember is to buy one that suits you, and the best way to do that is to check the specs of each machine you look at.
The features that a coffee maker offers – or doesn't offer – can be the difference between a purchase you love and one you return a week later. The main thing, even if you feel confident in your skills as a barista, is that you want your coffee machine to be easy and efficient to use.
