The perfect coffee machine is a personal decision. It depends on how you like to drink your coffee, how much time you are prepared to take to make yourself a tasty brew and how much room you have in your home, as well as the cost of whole beans, ground beans and pods. Whether you like to smash an espresso or slowly sip a cappuccino, there will be a perfect coffee machine deal out there for you this Cyber Monday – just be sure to check the specs as you shop so you get one that's right for you.
2. Don't be blinded by discounts: It's very easy, with so many deals to sort through, to just find the one with the biggest saving in dollars, or biggest percentage discount, and quickly buy it. I mean, they all make coffee, right? What difference does it make? Well, a lot – and just grabbing the best deal might not leave you with the best coffee machine for your needs.
For example, Nespresso pod machines are fantastic. However, there are two different styles of Nespresso machines – Vertuo and Original – and the pod sizes they use are wildly different. So, pairing a whole bunch of Starbucks Nespresso pods with a new Nespresso Vertuo Next as a gift is a lovely idea – but those pods will be completely unusable with that machine. Pods also cost quite a lot more than beans, ground or whole, though you have to weigh that up with the speed they provide.
Point being, just because a deal has sliced the price of a machine by 70% doesn't make it a deal for you. Be sure to look at all your options, and always follow step one even when looking at a mind-blowing Black Friday coffee machine deal.
3. Do your research in advance: The best way to make sure you end up with the right type of coffee machine on Black Friday is to do your research in advance. We advise reading our best coffee machine guide to narrow down the product you're interested in and the specifications you need. Once you have a good idea of what you’re looking for, you can approach the Black Friday coffee maker with a good understanding of whether the machine you're interested in is worth the money. This also helps you see what the regular price is without Black Friday, so you can know whether a deal is an actual deal or not. Or, you could just check out our Black Friday deals so you don't need to worry.

articles.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
articles.text:
Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days. Now, Google is ready to take another swing at “intelligent eyewear” for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they’re no impulse buy.
These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered.
Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn’t told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea.
Google says the frames all weigh about 41 grams, which is not terrible but is definitely near the top for glasses generally. They will, naturally, weigh much more when you account for lenses. That will also determine the final pricing. So far, we only have the starting prices for these devices, including non-prescription lenses.
The setup here is similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses we’ve seen for a few years. There are no screens in the lenses, but you can interact with the AI system via voice or by activating the integrated camera. The experience should be similar to using Gemini Live on your phone, but it will be a lot easier to fire up the AI. You can say “Hey Gemini” or tap a touch-sensitive area of the frame to start interacting with the robot.

articles.title: Los sindicatos australianos acusan a grandes empresas de usar la IA para justificar despidos
articles.text:
Sindicatos y expertos de Australia acusan a grandes empresas del país de usar la inteligencia artificial como justificación para recortar empleos y trasladar trabajo al exterior, según informó la agencia Reuters. La práctica tiene nombre en inglés, AI washing: atribuir despidos a la IA cuando la causa principal es el ahorro de costos.
El caso que encendió el debate es el de Qantas. La aerolínea nacional anunció el 10 de noviembre que eliminará 850 empleos y trasladará al exterior algunas funciones corporativas, como parte de una reorganización con la consultora Accenture que se apoya en la IA.
La aerolínea respondió que seguirá consultando a los sindicatos y que se concentra en ofrecer a los afectados otros puestos dentro de la empresa y apoyo. No contestó a la acusación de AI washing, según Reuters.
No es la única compañía señalada. Las empresas de software WiseTech y Atlassian recortaron personal este año y atribuyeron los despidos a la IA. La telefónica Telstra redujo puestos en una empresa conjunta de IA que formó con Accenture, y parte de ese trabajo pasó a India.
Reuters añade que otras firmas australianas también redujeron su plantilla local mientras amplían operaciones en India, Filipinas y Vietnam, aunque en sus anuncios no mencionaron la IA.
Los sindicatos sostienen que el trabajo se pierde
Los gremios sostienen que los trabajadores australianos no son reemplazados por software sino por empleados con salarios más bajos en otros países. Melissa Donnelly, secretaria del Consejo Australiano de Sindicatos, dijo que a los gremios les preocupa que las empresas usen la IA “simplemente como cobertura” para recortar empleos sin rendir cuentas.
El Sindicato de Servicios de Australia, que representa a los empleados afectados de Qantas, fue más duro. Lo acusó de usar la IA para “lavar” los recortes, según una declaración que recogió Reuters. Su secretario nacional adjunto, Scott Cowen, advirtió que verán más recortes de este tipo si el resto de las empresas copia la táctica.
La senadora Barbara Pocock, del partido Los Verdes, dijo que le preocupa que grandes compañías usen la tecnología como excusa. “La IA está transformando nuestros lugares de trabajo y nuestra economía, pero eso no justifica dejar que se desboque”, afirmó.
Un profesor pregunta por qué el trabajo cambia de manos primero
Uri Gal, profesor de la Escuela de Negocios de la Universidad de Sídney, dijo que hay incentivos reales para el AI washing. Una empresa que anuncia despidos para ahorrar puede recibir críticas, explicó, mientras que la que presenta la misma decisión como parte de una transformación con IA parece innovadora.
Gal opinó que la decisión de Qantas parece una tercerización convencional. Según el profesor, la empresa informó que las funciones irán a Accenture, sobre todo en India, y que después se transformarán con IA y automatización. “Si la IA vuelve innecesarios esos empleos, ¿por qué el trabajo debe transferirse primero a otro grupo de empleados?”, preguntó.
El Banco de la Reserva de Australia, la entidad monetaria central del país, dijo esta semana que la IA todavía no causó pérdidas de empleo generalizadas. Señaló “señales tentativas de ajuste”: menos avisos de trabajo en las ocupaciones más expuestas a la IA y mayor crecimiento del empleo en las menos expuestas.
El contexto político presiona al gobierno laborista de centroizquierda. El desempleo está en 4,7%, su nivel más alto en cinco años, y el banco central subió las tasas cinco veces este año hasta el nivel más alto en 18 años. Un portavoz del gobierno dijo que espera que los trabajadores vean los beneficios de las nuevas tecnologías y que los empleadores inviertan en capacitarlos.

articles.title: Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack
articles.text:
All-in-one collaborative workspace and productivity platform Notion is notifying a small set of customers that their information was compromised in a data breach involving Fireworks AI.
A cloud platform for running and fine-tuning open source AI models, Fireworks AI was hacked twice in October: once through compromised internal credentials, and once through a third-party cloud provider that was hosting Fireworks R&D machines.
The second incident, linked to a recent rise in LLMJacking activity, occurred on October 24, when the attackers executed an unauthorized workload leading to the compromise of customer data.
Fireworks contained the incident the same day and notified Notion on November 2 that Notion AI data had been accessed. Prior to the incident, Notion used Fireworks as a general inference provider for delivering open-weight models.
Notion’s investigation into the compromised data determined that the hackers accessed Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, which helps customers understand their AI usage.
Fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces were affected, and most of the transcripts were unattributable to a customer or the workspace they came from.
“Beyond what’s in the chat transcript itself, there’s no information tying the chat back to workspaces, users or companies,” Notion says.
The company has contacted the affected customers with instructions on how to securely retrieve and review the data in their workspaces, but did not disclose how many customers were affected.
“We recommend treating this data as exposed. If you pasted sensitive information, passwords, API keys, or other credentials into Notion AI during the incident, rotate any exposed credentials,” Notion tells customers.
SecurityWeek has emailed Notion for additional information on the data breach and will update this article if the company responds.

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder and (now former) CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.
U.S. officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang, and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO
Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: Northside Ventures aims to build “institutional angel investor” with $30-million USD second fund | BetaKit
articles.text:
Toronto-based Northside Ventures has officially launched its second venture capital (VC) fund geared towards Canadian technology founders at the earliest stages of company formation.
Northside aims to raise $30 million USD ($40 million CAD) for Fund II by early 2027. The firm is already more than halfway there, having secured $17 million USD ($24 million CAD) in total commitments to date across two closes, surpassing the size of its inaugural $11-million USD ($15 million CAD) fund.
“We’re taking the approach of being an institutional angel investor in the Canadian ecosystem.”
Northside founder and solo general partner (GP) Alex McIsaac revealed the news in an exclusive interview with BetaKit. While the firm’s overall strategy remains largely to continue its focus on pre-seed Canadian tech startups at or near inception, Northside hopes to cut bigger cheques and invest in companies with a larger second fund.
Through Fund II, Northside intends to deploy an average of $500,000 USD into each startup’s first round of financing, which is more than twice as much as the $225,000 it deployed via Fund I. It also plans to double its reserves for follow-on investments in top-performing firms to 20 percent, and invest in a total of 40 companies (10 more than its predecessor).
Northside aims to combine the reach and support of a larger VC firm with the decision-making speed and personal approach of an angel investor. The VC firm often invests in entrepreneurs before they have built products, let alone businesses, and McIsaac said Northside has sometimes had to wait for founders to incorporate and set up their bank accounts to invest.
“We’re taking the approach of being an institutional angel investor in the Canadian ecosystem,” McIsaac said.
First-time Northside limited partner (LP) CIBC Innovation Banking and returning investor Intact Private Capital are co-anchoring Fund II; new LP TD Innovation Partners and existing San Francisco-based backer Bain Capital Ventures have also contributed, alongside undisclosed family offices, high-net-worth individuals, and Canadian tech entrepreneurs.
RELATED: Northside Ventures closes first early-stage VC fund at $15 million CAD
“At the earliest stages, investors are often backing a founder and an idea before much else exists,” CIBC executive managing director and head of innovation banking Paul McKinlay told BetaKit over email. “That kind of conviction capital is vital to a thriving innovation ecosystem, and it is the role Northside is playing. We’re proud to support a fund with a clear focus on investing at the very start of the founder journey.”
While CIBC Innovation Banking aims to support Canada’s tech and VC ecosystem across every stage, McKinlay noted that “strong later-stage companies only exist when there is a healthy early-stage market behind them,” and said the bank’s Northside LP commitment reflects its intent to support “the next wave of ambitious Canadian founders.”
McIsaac, former Canadian partner at Germany’s Global Founders Capital, launched Northside in 2023 to focus on promising Canadian tech entrepreneurs building in Canada and the US at the pre-seed level, where domestic institutional capital is often scarce. The Northside GP argued that compared to the much deeper US VC market, Canada lacks enough funds focused specifically on pre-seed startups.
“When I started Northside in 2023, that gap was there,” McIsaac said. “I think it’s still there.”
RELATED: Canada Rocket Company wants to build a sovereign alternative to SpaceX’s Falcon 9
While Northside invests across a broad range of sectors, with Fund II the firm is particularly interested in AI applications, AI infrastructure, and frontier tech, including robotics and defence. At the moment, McIsaac said the latter is the fastest-growing category.
McIsaac believes some of the most important tech companies created over the next decade will be built by Canadians, and is happy to invest in founders wherever they are building. Through Fund I, Northside backed 30 companies over three years, equalling a pace he set previously with Global Founders Capital. McIsaac said the portfolio split between Canadian founders building in Canada versus the US worked out to approximately 50/50.
Since then, nine of those firms have raised priced rounds at higher valuations, and 12 have secured additional capital at larger simple agreements for future equity valuation caps. Those early results have stoked McIsaac’s confidence in Northside’s thesis. Some of Northside’s Fund I success stories include Canada Rocket Company, Datacurve, North Vector Dynamics, Solcoa Industries, and Terminal.
RELATED: Y Combinator grad Terminal raises $20-million USD Series A round
While Northside has been running an analyst internship program since it launched, the firm decided last year to roll out a scout program to stay connected with its graduates. That initiative has grown from four to nine members across schools like the University of British Columbia, the University of Waterloo, the University of Toronto, and McGill University, and into an important source of deal flow for Northside.
During this time, Northside has grown its team to six. Former analyst intern Naomi Walch is joining as a full-time investment team member for the firm’s second fund. Northside also has two analysts focused on finding and researching prospective investments and two engineers responsible for building and maintaining the internal AI sourcing product that helps Northside manage its pipeline and complete more than a deal per month.
Northside has already begun picking up its investment pace with Fund II: the firm has made a dozen investments since the start of 2026, backing Aron AI, PolarGrid, Solderable, Space, Vernius Systems, and Windkey, among others.
“We’ve spent the past three years building the track record, relationships, team, and infrastructure to become an enduring institutional venture firm, without compromising the speed, conviction and personal approach that got us here,” McIsaac said. “With 12 new investments already this year, I feel more confident than ever in our ability to identify and back exceptional Canadian founders at the earliest stages.”
Feature image courtesy Northside Ventures.

articles.title: Oh, Palantir is ‘progressive’ now, is it?
articles.text:
I had other things to do today, but Alex Karp’s pathetic attempt to pivot back to the left gave me no choice but to put them on hold.
Oh, Palantir is ‘progressive’ now, is it?
A children’s treasury of things Alex Karp has said in public over the last three years.
Last week’s elections were a bloodbath for the right, a problem for all the wannabe fash founders who had tied their political fortunes to a “vibe shift” that enabled a glorious 100-year Trumpenreich. That freed up a lot of assholes to say what they actually thought. Except Donald Trump’s victory was, in fact, narrow, and two years of his corrupt policies have enraged Americans.
“I’ve been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir— all of our products are essentially progressive,” Karp told Politico.
Is that so, baby doll? Let’s run it back.
- August 2024: “I’m not going to apologize for defending the U.S. government on the border, defending the Special Ops, bringing the people home,” he told Maureen Dowd.
- February 2025: Karp wrote in a letter to shareholders that “As Samuel Huntington has written, the rise of the West was not made possible ‘by the superiority of its ideas or values or religion . . . but rather by its superiority in applying organized violence.’”
- February 2025: “Palantir is ‘making America more lethal’ by analyzing troves of data for the U.S. armed forces and allies to help them anticipate enemies’ moves, locate their coordinates ‘and, on occasion, kill them.’” I am quoting the WSJ here. The WSJ is quoting an earnings call.
- November 2025: Palantir is “the first company to be completely anti-woke,” Karp declared on an earnings call.
- November 2025: “I spend a lot of time talking to Nazis. Like, real Nazis.”
- November 2025: “Democrats just completely neglect males. ... It’s admirable to be a ... high-testosterone male. And ... you have the general vibe in the Democratic Party that there’s something wrong. ... I don’t find it very appealing as a dude.” Also, from the same interview, referring to his Democratic friends: “You have to grow a spine because a lot of these people actually agree with me in private.”
- November 2025: “Our competition is political. The woke left and the woke right wake up every day, figuring out how they can hurt Palantir. If they get into power, they’ll hurt Palantir. And by the way, it’s global. I view Democrats as my party, but if the Mamdani wing of the party takes over? If that’s my party, I’m not in it. Or the right woke wing, which is like, everything is a conspiracy, any use of technology is actually going to only be used to eviscerate and attack us?” Also, on progressivism: “Universities and elite institutions have played a corrosive role here. People are teaching pagan religion views — a new religion with sacrifices. Who’s the sacrifice? Me, I’m the sacrifice.”
- December 2025: In response to The New York Times’ reporting on his company (unclear which article, maybe this one?): “That article about us being a surveillance thing — is like, where it’s all implied what we do — yeah, but the problem is you lose credibility with anyone who goes on the thing and then — and that’s damaging for our democracy.” Later, in the same interview: “The one thing I would say to people in the audience — you know you, a lot of you think I’m right. And you know your spouse, your relative, your child, the person at work would be horrified if they knew it. You better speak up. Because everyone who thinks I’m a ridiculous fascist, they’re speaking up. They write about it every day. If you do not speak up, the people who are disagreeing with me or think I’m stupid — well, I disagree with myself. So, you have to speak up. And you cannot blame the far left, far right idiots when they speak up for their views. Do you speak up for your views? Where?”
- April 2026: That manifesto, which was previously published as a book. “The postwar neutering of Germany and Japan must be undone. The defanging of Germany was an overcorrection for which Europe is now paying a heavy price.” Also, well after Elon Musk did his little uhhh hand gesture and DOGE ran rampant across the US government: “We should applaud those who attempt to build where the market has failed to act. The culture almost snickers at Musk’s interest in grand narrative.” And maybe most notably: “Some cultures have produced vital advances; others remain dysfunctional and regressive. All cultures are now equal. Criticism and value judgments are forbidden.”
- July 2026: On CNBC, referring to frontier models: “This is the voice of American business that is being channeled through me.”
Anyway, for any other tech bros who want to do a less clumsy pivot than Karp, I have a suggestion. First, go to rehab, ideally for 90 days. Then come out and apologize for whatever it was you said between, I don’t know, 2020 and now. You feel very bad about what you’ve said, but it was the cocaine (or the amphetamines, or hell, blame it on ketamine, since the average person has no idea what a ketamine high looks like) speaking. You have dried out and sobered up. It was a challenge, but it was rewarding. You are now chastened. You want to work for public accountability. You are sorry about the dumb things you said while you were high.
This won’t work for Karp, who’s been absolutely adamant that he does not do drugs. But you, the savvy tech CEO and/or VC, you can’t skip the rehab part. You can’t blame the drugs if you don’t at least pretend to sober up.

articles.title: Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch
articles.text:
“Fifty-seven channels, and nothin’ on.”
Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.
Within a few years, there would be hundreds of TV channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch.”
The advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.
According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.
Gracenote, a Nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the UK who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 State of Play: Amid fragmentation frustrations, UX is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.
For example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch.”
Further, 19.2 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either “always” or “often” don’t know what to watch, can’t find anything, and then decide to do something else. And 27.4 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either always or often try to watch a specific program but end up not watching it because they couldn’t find it on streaming.
“Through the lens of catalogue size and streaming usage, connecting the 83.4 percent who don’t always know what they want to watch should be fairly straightforward, especially as companies increasingly use customer data to create personalized experiences that foster long-term engagement and loyalty. Audiences, however, aren’t finding what they’re looking for, and content discovery challenges are mounting,” the report reads.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned
articles.text:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis.
The 63-year-old will be replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim chief executive.
His exit comes after he admitted to having a relationship with a woman that US authorities believe was a Chinese spy. It also emerged on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive.
Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in pre-market trading, extending earlier losses after the announcement of Huang’s resignation.
Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, led it to become what was until recently the world’s most valuable company.
Huang’s departure marks a startling end to his more than 33-year tenure, during which Nvidia evolved from a small video-game chip company into the linchpin of the global AI infrastructure boom.
Huang has become one of the most recognizable figures in tech, as Nvidia’s semiconductors became integral to training and running AI systems such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude.
Nvidia stock extended its pre-market decline after the company announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive.
Shares were down 10.2 percent in pre-market trading, a move that would wipe off more than $400 billion in market capitalization.
This story was updated on November 12 with news of Huang’s resignation.

articles.title: Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones
Penlink’s Webloc is an application that locates people using information from the weather, gaming, email, and religious apps on their phone. It’s sold to the police.
The tool collects vast quantities of location data from smartphones via commonly used weather, gaming, email and religious apps. It can build a detailed picture of where a smartphone has been over the past 12 months, and update the data hourly, showing the movements of people on a near real-time basis. Law enforcement officers can use Webloc to zero in on a map and look at all phones that were present at a specific place and time, analyzing “billions of location data points,” according to company documents reviewed by Bloomberg.
There’s a nice infographic that explains how the system works at the link.
Rontea • November 12, 2026 9:20 AM
Freedom is not a gift one receives; it is the breath of the spirit. And when the spirit sleeps, even the weather app becomes a confessor, and the marketplace of data becomes the new confessional where the merchants of the world whisper to Leviathan, “Here is man, naked and numbered.”

articles.title: Pinceau 3D, vidéo retouchée en direct… Les 10 démos IA bluffantes de l'Adobe Max 2026
articles.text:
À Miami, Adobe a profité de la dernière grande keynote de son événement Max 2026 pour montrer comment ses chercheurs comptent simplifier le travail sur l’image et le son. Parmi les dix prototypes présentés, deux sont d’ores et déjà disponibles pour le grand public.
Changer la veste d’une actrice dans un plan, c’est une chose. La retrouver dans la même tenue après chaque scène en est une autre. Lors des Sneaks d’Adobe Max 2026, Scene Sweep a illustré ce que l’IA pourrait épargner aux monteurs : dans une séquence de plus de 40 secondes comptant neuf plans, la veste prune choisie sur une image suit le personnage dans les sept plans où il apparaît. C’est l’une des dix pistes qu’Adobe explore pour faire évoluer ses outils de création.
Une vidéo que l’on peut diriger en cours de génération
Scene Sweep commence par analyser le montage pour retrouver les personnages et les lieux d’un plan à l’autre, puis y reporter les corrections. Sur scène, Adobe ne s’est pas contenté de changer la veste de l’actrice. Un autre personnage a hérité d’une nouvelle coiffure pendant qu’un tableau était remplacé jusque dans les plans où il apparaissait sous un autre angle. Le résultat est bluffant, et l’on peut même comparer les variantes en mouvement grâce à des aperçus animés en basse définition, avant de lancer le rendu final.
Avec Project Live Set, on peut infléchir le cours d’une vidéo pendant sa génération. Pour le montrer, le démonstrateur est parti d’une photo de son chat, qu’il a demandé à l’IA de faire boxer. La séquence se déroule à l’écran alors que le logiciel génère les images suivantes, en gardant de l’avance sur la tête de lecture. Il suffit alors de nouvelles consignes pour changer les actions de l’animal ou les mouvements de caméra, le tout sans interrompre la lecture.
Avec On Cue, Adobe cherche à mieux maîtriser le rythme des vidéos générées par IA. Le principe repose sur une courbe d’événements, un signal de contrôle à une dimension dont les pics indiquent quand une action doit se produire. Sur scène, un chien sautait ainsi aux instants définis par la courbe. En réutilisant celle-ci avec d’autres consignes, on pouvait faire sauter plusieurs animaux en cadence ou synchroniser l’éclairage de différents immeubles. Cette courbe se dessine et se retouche à la main, mais peut aussi être extraite d’une vidéo ou d’un morceau de musique pour en reprendre le rythme et, par exemple, faire clignoter des ampoules sur les temps forts.
Sound Bender apporte ce contrôle au son. Un bruit d’impact mêlé à la musique est extrait sur une piste séparée à partir de sa description textuelle. Il sert ensuite de référence à un sound canvas, une surface dont les quatre coins portent des idées sonores. En s’y déplaçant, on explore leurs combinaisons ; le parcours peut être enregistré pour faire évoluer le bruitage en synchronisation avec la vidéo. Screen Test intervient pour sa part plus en amont : l’auteur définit un personnage fictif, voix comprise, puis dialogue avec lui pour explorer ses réactions et émotions.
- Suite créative très complète
- Logiciels Adobe professionnels
- Intégration entre les applications
Photoshop apprend à reprendre nos gestes
Pour montrer ce que Deep Brush a dans le pinceau, le chercheur à l’origine du projet choisit une photo de parkour et se met à peindre sur les murs en béton, comme le ferait un tagueur dans la vraie vie. Les couleurs changent, mais l’éclairage d’origine est préservé, tandis que des masques empêchent le trait de déborder sur la personne au premier plan. Le prototype analyse la géométrie, les couleurs et la lumière de la scène pour que le coup de pinceau épouse les surfaces, même courbes. On peut ainsi repeindre ce que l’on photographie, mais aussi y ajouter de la lumière au fil du geste.
Hands On prolonge cette approche en faisant apparaître, directement dans l’image, des commandes adaptées à son contenu (comme dans l’outil Edit Object de Firefly, l’IA reconnaît automatiquement les objets et personnes dans l’image). Quelques clics suffisent alors pour redimensionner un objet ou remodeler ses formes. Réduisez la largeur d’un canapé et il devient un fauteuil qui en conserve le style. Ailleurs, un verre se remplit de bière à la demande et un hamburger double de volume sous les yeux ébahis de son consommateur. Même le flacon de parfum rectangulaire se laisse changer de forme en manipulant simplement ses contours.
Avec Rinse Repeat, une retouche réussie peut servir de modèle aux suivantes. Sur scène, la présentatrice ajoute une ombre sous un flacon de parfum, puis confie au prototype le soin de faire de même pour cinq autres produits. Chacun reçoit une ombre adaptée à sa forme, le logiciel reprenant la méthode de l’utilisateur plutôt que de recopier les pixels. Il s’appuie pour cela sur les mêmes outils, calques et masques de Photoshop, que l’on peut ensuite reprendre à la main pour affiner le résultat.
- Génération multimédia centralisée
- Retouche générative intégrée
- Applications web et mobiles
Modéliser une image en 3D pour changer son angle de prise de vue
Dans une illustration vectorielle, Link Up adapte un élément au décor dans lequel on le déplace, en ajustant sa taille, sa perspective et son style. Le geste peut même suggérer une action. Sur scène, des animaux glissés d'un tobogan vers une piscine provoquaient des éclaboussures dont l’ampleur variait selon la vitesse du déplacement. Ces ajouts restent entièrement vectoriels et modifiables, pour permettre au graphiste de les retravailler à sa guise.
Sight Span donne, lui, envie de tourner autour des images. À partir d’un panda perché dans un arbre, du portrait d’un homme ou même d’un tableau, le prototype construit un environnement 3D dans lequel on se déplace à la recherche d’un autre cadrage. L’effet est spectaculaire, avec cette liberté de découvrir le sujet sous des angles que l’image d’origine ne montrait pas. La navigation se fait en basse définition ; une fois le point de vue choisi, un clic lance la génération du visuel en haute définition. L’IA recrée alors l’image, y compris les parties jusque-là invisibles, qu’elle doit donc inventer.
Et bonne nouvelle pour finir, Deep Brush et Hands On sont déjà proposés à l’essai dans le Playground d’Adobe Labs. On peut également y essayer Custom Filters, un projet distinct qui transforme une consigne écrite en filtre photo que l’on peut régler en direct et réutiliser sur d’autres images. Hier soir à Miami, l’IA générative a quitté le stade de la loterie par prompt pour commencer à devenir un outil de précision chirurgicale.

articles.title: Italie-France : où voir le match de foot en direct et en streaming ?
articles.text:
Zinédine Zidane a entamé sa campagne avec l’Équipe de France de fort belle manière. Son bilan est de trois victoires et un nul en quatre matchs. Pour cette deuxième trêve internationale de la saison 2026/2027, les Bleus se déplacent à Milan pour affronter l’Italie, nation avec laquelle ils ont partagé les points en octobre (1-1).
Le déplacement s’annonce périlleux, puisqu’il oppose les deux premiers du groupe 1 de la Ligue A de la Ligue des nations. D’autant que la France doit composer avec plusieurs forfaits majeurs : de Kylian Mbappé, dont Zidane a annoncé le forfait ce mercredi, à Ousmane Dembélé, en passant par William Saliba, Manu Koné et Jules Koundé. L’Italie, absente des trois dernières Coupes du monde (2018, 2022 et 2026), retrouve des couleurs sous la houlette de Roberto Mancini, revenu sur le banc de la Nazionale fin juillet.
Où suivre le match entre la France et l’Italie ?
Quand a lieu le match entre la France et l’Italie ?
Italie-France a lieu ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, à San Siro, stade mythique de Milan. Le coup d’envoi sera donné à 20h45.
Il s’agit de la cinquième journée du groupe 1 de la Ligue A de la Ligue des nations.
Italie-France est diffusé gratuitement sur TF1
Pas besoin d’abonnement : TF1 détient les droits des six matchs des Bleus dans cette phase de Ligue des nations et diffuse le match en clair sur le canal 1 de la TNT et sur les box des opérateurs. Les abonnés Netflix en France métropolitaine peuvent aussi le suivre dans l’application, mais uniquement sur téléviseur. La prise d’antenne est prévue à 20h35 avec Grégoire Margotton et Bixente Lizarazu aux commentaires.
À 22h50, TF1 enchaînera avec un après-match.
Comment regarder Italie-France en streaming ?
Le match est aussi disponible en direct sur TF1+, la plateforme gratuite du groupe TF1, sur ordinateur, smartphone, tablette ou TV connectée. Il suffit de créer un compte, gratuit, et de se rendre à cette adresse.
Les plateformes comme Canal+, Molotov, Free TV, Orange TV, SFR TV ou b.tv, si vos offres intègrent TF1, diffusent aussi la chaîne.
Le programme des Bleus en Ligue des nations
Zidane n’aura pas le temps de souffler : après Milan, les Bleus reçoivent la Turquie dès dimanche, à Bordeaux. Les six matchs de la phase de groupes sont tous diffusés sur TF1.
- Turquie-France le vendredi 25 septembre à 20h45 (victoire 1 à 0)
- Belgique-France le lundi 28 septembre à 20h45 (victoire 1 à 0)
- France-Italie le vendredi 2 octobre à 20h45 (nul 1 à 1)
- France-Belgique le lundi 5 octobre à 20h45 (victoire 4 à 1)
- Italie-France le jeudi 12 novembre à 20h45
- France-Turquie le dimanche 15 novembre à 20h45
Le classement du groupe 1 de la Ligue A de la Ligue des nations, avant la 5e journée :
| Équipe | Points | 
|---|---|
| France | 10 points (+5) | 
| Italie | 7 points (+3) | 
| Belgique | 6 points (+1) | 
| Turquie | 0 point (-9) | 
Les deux premiers du groupe se qualifient pour les quarts de finale, disputés en matchs aller-retour du 25 au 30 mars 2027. Les quatre vainqueurs se retrouveront pour la phase finale, en juin 2027.
À Milan, un match nul suffirait aux Bleus pour valider leur billet pour les quarts de finale. Une victoire leur assurerait la première place du groupe avant même la réception de la Turquie, dimanche.

articles.title: "Sentimentale Gründe": Warum Tesla den Cybertruck wohl doch länger bauen will
articles.text:
Sentimentale Gründe: Warum Tesla den Cybertruck wohl doch länger bauen will
Mit seiner Ankündigung, die Cybertruck-Produktion im Sommer 2027 auslaufen lassen zu wollen, hatte Tesla zuletzt für einige Aufregung gesorgt. Zunächst hatte Elon Musk erklärt, mit dem Produktionsaus des E-Pickup-Trucks Platz für die Herstellung des Cybercabs schaffen zu wollen.
Cybercab statt Cybertruck wegen Personalmangels?
Später schob der Tesla-Chef hinterher, dass die Produktion des Cybertrucks zu komplex sei, um sie neben der des Cybercabs weiterlaufen zu lassen. Letztlich ein Eingeständnis, dass es Tesla nach dem Weggang zahlreicher Manager:innen und Mitarbeiter:innen schlicht an Fachpersonal fehle, wie Electrek einordnet. Jetzt vollzieht Musk die nächste Kehrtwende.
Weil die Anzahl an Vorbestellungen die aktuelle Produktionsrate übersteige, wolle Tesla den Cybertruck jetzt statt wie zuvor angekündigt acht noch rund zehn Monate weiterbauen, wie Musk per X mitteilte. Zuvor hatte Tesla erklärt, die Anzahlungen von Käufer:innen, die aufgrund des Produktionsstopps leer ausgingen, zurückzahlen zu wollen.
Musk: Sentimentalität statt Gewinnmaximierung
Wie das damit zusammenpasst, dass die Gigafactory im US-Bundesstaat Texas auf eine jährliche Produktion von 125.000 Fahrzeugen ausgelegt ist, Tesla aber nur rund 30.000 Cybertrucks verkauft, erklärte Musk nicht. Vielmehr führte der Tesla-Chef für die Verlängerung der Produktion bis September 2027 sentimentale Gründe ins Rennen. Vom Standpunkt einer reinen Gewinnmaximierung sei das Ganze jedenfalls kein smarter Move, so Musk.
Laut eines Berichts von Inside-EVs könnte es sich dabei auch um eine Reaktion Musks auf den Aufschrei von Cybertruck-Fans handeln. Denn obwohl es sich bei dem E-Pickup-Truck um den wohl größten Flop der Autogeschichte handelt, hat sich der Cybertruck eine treue Fangemeinde erarbeitet. So haben über 5.000 Menschen eine Petition unterzeichnet, in der sie die Fortsetzung der Produktion fordern.
Unplugged Performance will Cybertruck bauen
Und tatsächlich könnten sie mit der Forderung Erfolg haben – allerdings könnte nicht Tesla, sondern der Zubehöranbieter Unplugged Performance die Herstellung übernehmen. Im Rücken hat das Unternehmen eigenen Angaben zufolge ein Konsortium an Investor:innen. Tesla soll dabei eine Lizenzgebühr pro gebauten Fahrzeug erhalten. Außerdem will Unplugged Performance die Fahrzeugpalette um einen Cyber-SUV und einen Cybercargo-Transporter erweitern.

articles.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
articles.text:
I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi.
The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.
The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.
Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out.
Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained?
Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad: business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.”
Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46.
Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China. But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.”
Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office a month ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished. The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address.
Megaspeed is only part of the story
Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing. The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun!
Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON, according to Bloomberg. Liang and Super Micro have not been charged.
But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists, and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times.
The question, of course, is how high this all goes
Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point, actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming.
More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed, which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him.
The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom. This is what gangster tech regulation looks like.
I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know?
Come January, Elizabeth Warren will be able to send subpoenas in her role as the chair of the Senate Banking Committee. And wouldn’t you know, she seems to be pretty interested. Democrats will control both the House and the Senate. Their voters have given them a mandate to root out corruption. And boy howdy, does Nvidia look like a sitting duck right now. If Huang knew chips were being diverted — or had reason to know that — and tried to ensure their sales anyway, he may have committed actual crimes (bribery, espionage, smuggling, whatever) and, under a functioning legal system, could actually go to jail. Nvidia dispensing with its indispensable CEO is the company reducing its risk of getting roped into Huang’s drama.
Will it be that easy for Nvidia? I wonder. The most interesting part of the second affair story, with Powell, the Nvidia vice president of healthcare, comes at the very end of the New York Times article. When someone took a video of Powell and Huang being “affectionate” in March, Huang’s security had nondisclosure agreements ready to go. CNBC reports that rumors of their affair have circulated “for years.” I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know? Especially since Huang had 60 direct reports, so every part of the company is covered in his fingerprints.
Over in the tech world, people still seem to be in denial. On X, the social network for Trumpist dead-enders, the account “zerohedge” posted, “Elon please hire Jensen.” Elon Musk replied, “That would be an honor.”

articles.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed that Windows updates released since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday are causing SQL Server performance and stability issues.
As detailed in a Windows release health dashboard update on Wednesday, this is caused by server queries that leave connections open after the queries complete. These connections accumulate instead of closing, degrading server performance over time.
"This issue affects SQL Server linked server queries that use OLE DB providers to connect to external databases. Oracle and PostgreSQL connections are among those known to be affected," Microsoft explained.
"In affected environments, administrators might observe an increasing number of open connections to external databases, even when the associated SQL Server linked server queries are no longer running."
It also added that admins may be able to manually close connections left open due to this bug or restart the SQL service to temporarily address stability and performance issues, but this can also kill active queries and may not fully address the issue, as it will resurface again after some time.
Microsoft says the issues impact both client (Windows 10 and Windows 11) and server (Windows Server 2012 and later) systems and will be fixed with an out-of-band Windows update to be released over the next few days.
While it works to resolve the bug, Microsoft said IT administrators can reach out to Microsoft Support for Business for a mitigation that can address the issue until a fix is available.
In September, Microsoft also shared a temporary workaround for SQL Server crashes on some Windows Server 2025 due to recent memory management changes.
The bug affects SQL Server when the Lock Pages in Memory (LPIM) Windows policy is enabled and may cause SQL Server crash dumps, SQL Server services to stop or restart unexpectedly, failures during database maintenance operations, memory corruption errors, and access violation exceptions (with 0xC0000005 error codes).
Yesterday, the company also confirmed reports that the November 2026 security updates are failing to deploy on Windows 11 systems where the October preview update has been installed, with affected users seeing 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993 error codes.

articles.title: Anthropic offre un reset gratuit des limites de Claude à ses abonnés, voici comment en profiter
articles.text:
Anthropic veut se faire pardonner pour les récents « désagréments ». L’entreprise américaine offre ainsi une réinitialisation des limites d’utilisation à ses abonnés payants. Attention, cette opération n’est valable que pendant une durée limitée. Voici comment en profiter.
Un reset pour toutes les limites des abonnements payants
Via son compte X ClaudeDevs, Anthropic a annoncé une réinitialisation complète et gratuite des limites d’utilisation pour les abonnés Pro, Max, Ultra et Team. Ce reset couvre tous les modèles et toutes les limites. À noter que les utilisateurs du forfait gratuit ne peuvent pas bénéficier de cette offre. Pour les abonnés payants, ce reset est activable jusqu’au 10 décembre 2026 à 23 h (heure de Paris).
Anthropic explique avoir décidé d’offrir ce reset des comptes payants pour deux raisons. Premièrement, l’entreprise américaine confie avoir corrigé récemment quelques « petits problèmes qui consommaient plus de limites que prévu », sans préciser lesquels. Deuxièmement, Anthropic reconnaît en quelque sorte que le reset offert le 9 novembre, à l’occasion du lancement de Claude Fable 5.2, n’a pas réellement profité aux abonnés qui avaient déjà atteint leurs limites hebdomadaires. Pour rappel, cette première réinitialisation ne restaurait que le quota hebdomadaire consommé sur les modèles Fable, en plus de recharger le quota de la session de cinq heures. L’entreprise de Dario Amodei veut donc maintenant se faire pardonner, même si ces problèmes n’ont « pas affecté tout le monde ».
Comment activer ce reset de Claude ?
Pour activer la réinitialisation de votre compte Pro, Max, Ultra ou Team, il suffit de vous rendre dans les paramètres, puis de cliquer sur « Utilisation ». Autre possibilité : accéder directement à l’adresse suivante : http://clau.de/reset.
Les personnes concernées peuvent réinitialiser leur compte jusqu’au 10 décembre. Bien entendu, le mieux à faire est de réinitialiser son compte à un moment où les limites d’utilisation sont atteintes. Pour rappel, Claude dispose de deux types de limites d’utilisation : un premier quota renouvelé toutes les cinq heures et un second, hebdomadaire, qui se réinitialise chaque semaine à une date et une heure définies pour chaque compte.

articles.title: Alfonso Muñoz: “Este requisito está dando lugar a la denegación de muchas jubilaciones anticipadas”
articles.text:
El funcionario de la Seguridad Social Alfonso Muñoz señala que hay un requisito económico que está provocando “la denegación de muchas jubilaciones anticipadas voluntarias”. Se trata del hecho de que la pensión calculada tenga que ser superior a la mínima a la que tendría derecho el solicitante a los 65 años de edad (teniendo en cuenta su situación familiar).
En esta modalidad se puede adelantar el retiro máximo hasta dos años antes de la edad ordinaria correspondiente. Además, hacen falta al menos 35 años de cotización efectiva. De estos, al menos dos tienen que estar dentro de los 15 anteriores a la jubilación o, en los casos previstos por la norma, al cese de la obligación de cotizar. Sin embargo, esto no es suficiente. Por otro lado, el artículo 208 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social indica que no se podrá acoger a esta modalidad si la pensión resultante no supera el umbral.
Ejemplo de cuantía para 2026
Por ejemplo, un trabajador de 63 años tiene 40 cotizados y tiene una pensión calculada de 1.058 € mensuales. Vive con su mujer, que no trabaja y no tiene pensión.
En el caso de nuestro ejemplo, veríamos que para un titular de 65 años la mínima es de 1.256,60 euros/mes (con cónyuge a cargo). Si no tuviera cónyuge, la mínima sería de 936,20 euros/mes. Por otro lado, si se diera la situación de que tuviera cónyuge no a cargo, esta mínima bajaría a 888,70 euros/mes. Las cantidades son en catorce pagas.
Para que tenga cónyuge a cargo, deben vivir juntos y haber dependencia económica. En 2026, la dependencia económica se consigue si el cónyuge no es titular de ninguna pensión pública (en los términos de la norma) y además tienen unos rendimientos computables (sin contar la pensión que queremos complementar) de menos de 11.013 euros/año entre los dos.
En nuestra situación, la mujer estaría a cargo si se cumple ese límite de rendimientos. Como nuestra pensión calculada es menor que la mínima, no podríamos optar a la jubilación anticipada voluntaria. Por otro lado, si nuestros rendimientos computables fueran superiores al límite, pasaríamos a estar en la categoría de cónyuge no a cargo.

articles.title: Cómo funciona la IA desarrollada por el MIT que logra imitar casi cualquier fenómeno del mundo real
articles.text:
Un estudio del Instituto de Tecnología de Massachusetts (MIT) y la Universidad de Columbia Británica presentó WorldParticle, un sistema de inteligencia artificial capaz de simular, con una sola arquitectura, fenómenos físicos tan distintos como el deslizamiento de arena y el plegamiento de proteínas. El modelo busca reemplazar los simuladores diseñados para tareas específicas y permitir el estudio conjunto de materiales, fuerzas y entornos que hasta ahora requerían herramientas separadas, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
La tecnología representó seis fenómenos físicos diferentes con mayor precisión que los métodos de simulación numérica; en el caso de las estructuras proteicas, lo hizo cerca de 100 veces más rápido que los simuladores convencionales.
El sistema, descrito en el servidor de prepublicación arXiv, podría utilizarse para analizar, por ejemplo, el impacto del petróleo en movimiento sobre una válvula elástica dentro de un tanque de almacenamiento. También permitiría estudiar dónde y de qué forma se desplaza la arena o el suelo cuando entran en contacto con un robot blando.
Un modelo para partículas, fluidos y proteínas
Los científicos suelen elegir un simulador distinto para cada proceso físico: uno para el flujo de agua, otro para el comportamiento de un objeto flexible y otro para modelar el plegamiento de proteínas. Cada herramienta se programa a partir de ecuaciones que describen el material o el fenómeno en cuestión.
WorldParticle reemplaza ese esquema mediante una red neuronal capaz de aprender, de forma general, a resolver las ecuaciones que gobiernan el comportamiento de la materia. El sistema no recibe una fórmula específica para cada caso, sino que identifica las dinámicas subyacentes y puede adaptarse a materiales, fuerzas y condiciones ambientales que no estuvieron presentes durante su entrenamiento.
Peter Yichen Chen, exinvestigador posdoctoral del MIT y actual profesor asistente de la Universidad de Columbia Británica, resumió la ambición del proyecto con una comparación: “Queremos tener un momento GPT para la simulación”, dijo, en referencia a un modelo de alcance universal, equivalente al que los grandes modelos de lenguaje tuvieron en el procesamiento de texto.
“Cada vez que las personas quieren construir un simulador para un fenómeno físico particular, necesitan programarlo desde cero”, afirmó Chen. “Nuestra visión es contar con un modelo fundacional que funcione directamente para cualquier escenario que se quiera simular. Este es un primer paso en esa dirección”.
De partículas a predicciones: así opera el modelo
El modelo descompone cada objeto, desde una duna de arena hasta una molécula proteica, en miles o millones de partículas tridimensionales. Luego rastrea su posición y velocidad a través del espacio y el tiempo para anticipar cómo evolucionará el material.
La red neuronal recibe como entrada las posiciones en tres dimensiones y las propiedades físicas de esas partículas. Después calcula su ubicación y sus características en el siguiente cuadro de la simulación, con predicciones en intervalos de un segundo.
“Es una arquitectura similar a ChatGPT, pero en lugar de predecir una palabra por vez para escribir un texto, predecimos cómo se moverán estas partículas, un paso a la vez”, explicó Chen.
Antes de cada paso, WorldParticle separa las fuerzas externas que inciden sobre el sistema físico. Entre ellas figuran las fuerzas de impulso que afectan a una ola del océano cuando golpea un rompeolas.
Una vez que calcula los estados iniciales de las partículas, el sistema reincorpora esas fuerzas a la simulación y corrige sus predicciones según el efecto que ejercen sobre el objeto. Ese mecanismo le permite generalizar sus resultados a materiales desconocidos, cambios en el ambiente y distintos tipos de fuerza.
Representar un objeto mediante millones de partículas puede, sin embargo, superar la capacidad de procesamiento del modelo. Para reducir esa demanda, el equipo aplicó una técnica de fusión y compresión de partículas que conserva detalles finos de su comportamiento.
“Necesitábamos realizar mucha ingeniería detallada y aplicar numerosos ajustes a la arquitectura para que fuera realmente generalizable y escalable”, indicó Guo.
Robots blandos, evolución del ARN y galaxias
Entre los seis fenómenos evaluados, las pruebas con materiales granulares mostraron con claridad las ventajas del sistema: mientras algunos métodos de referencia dejaban partículas de arena suspendidas en el aire, WorldParticle reprodujo correctamente su colapso hasta formar un montón.
El marco de propósito general podría aplicarse a tareas de manipulación con robots blandos, a la evolución del ARN y a fenómenos astrofísicos como la fusión de galaxias. Los investigadores pretenden adaptar la herramienta a esos sistemas y avanzar hacia una plataforma integral de simulación para el descubrimiento científico.
El investigador posdoctoral del MIT Minghao Guo, coautor principal del trabajo, señaló que unificar modelos puede permitir nuevas combinaciones entre fenómenos que antes se estudiaban por separado. “Si se estudian objetos deformables y fluidos, se necesitarían dos simuladores, uno para cada régimen físico. Pero si se los unifica en un solo modelo, quizá se pueda acoplar la física de estos dos procesos y obtener conocimientos sobre nuevos problemas”, sostuvo Guo.
“Vemos que la unificación de la computación y la ciencia puede darnos nuevos conocimientos y herramientas para descubrir fenómenos físicos o explicar fenómenos físicos que no tienen explicación”, afirmó Guo.

articles.title: Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk
articles.text:
The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month.
Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we’ve gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn’t want to make the Mac Pro anymore.
But the Apple Silicon iMac has always been more interested in looking backward. It’s the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. It’s a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. We’re long past the days when it was Apple’s primary workstation computer.
So I wanted to write about this new iMac from the perspective of that entry-level iMac buyer, who chooses the iMac because it’s simple and then uses it until it breaks. What does a new iMac get you if you’re stepping up from the M1 model or comparing it against an older refurbished M4 model? Without any real external updates, what makes this iMac iteration interesting?
Same friendly face
If you haven’t used an Apple Silicon-era iMac before, here’s a brief primer.
The new iMac is much thinner than the older aluminum Intel models. Its front is mostly one big 24-inch screen, surrounded on all sides by a relatively thick white bezel (I still wish black were at least an option, but Apple apparently doesn’t agree).
White bezel aside, it’s by far Apple’s most colorful computer. The iMacs ship with color-matched fronts, backs, stands, keyboards, mice, trackpads, and cables. Apple has tweaked the color offerings and changed the tints of each specific color a few times over the years, but the M6 iMac uses the same six color tints (plus silver) that the M4 iMac did.
The basic $1,499 iMac is essentially a MacBook Air in terms of ports—it has two Thunderbolt ports on the back and a headphone jack on the left side. Choosing this model also locks you into a lesser version of the Apple M6 with 10 CPU cores and 10 GPU cores instead of 12 of each, a maximum of 24GB of RAM, a minimum of 256GB of storage, and a maximum of 1TB. Its default keyboard doesn’t have Touch ID support, and the only way to get it is to buy the version with the built-in number pad, an $80 upsell.
The M6 iMac still comes with either two or four Thunderbolt 4 ports. The four-port version can run two external displays; the one-port version is limited to one. Ethernet is available on the power brick for an extra $30.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
The M6 iMac still comes with either two or four Thunderbolt 4 ports. The four-port version can run two external displays; the one-port version is limited to one. Ethernet is available on the power brick for an extra $30.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
The $1,699 version is the one to get if you still intend to use the iMac as a workstation. It includes the full-speed version of the M6 with all its CPU and GPU cores intact (though there are performance caveats here we’ll talk about later), plus options for 32GB of RAM and up to 2TB of storage. This version also includes four Thunderbolt ports on the back for connecting additional accessories. Both available keyboards on this version have Touch ID.
A 2.5 gigabit Ethernet port can be added to any iMac for $30. This port is located on the desktop’s power brick rather than the iMac itself, an elegant solution that keeps even a wired Internet connection hidden beneath your desk with the other cables. All iMacs also offer a VESA mount adapter option in place of the default stand at no extra charge.
I still really like the effect created by the color-matched keyboard, mouse/trackpad, and cables—even the white bezel complements the white keycaps and mouse. Just know you’re paying quite a lot for how the desktop looks. The $899 Mac mini is $800 cheaper than the iMac with the same chip, the same amount of RAM, and the same amount of storage. Sure, it would cost something to add a nice-looking 4K monitor, but not $800, even if you go for extra frills like a high refresh rate.
It’s fine that the iMac upcharges you for style and convenience. That’s the point of the computer. Just make sure that’s what you want to pay for.

Here are the basic specs for every entry-level iMac Apple has shipped, going all the way back to the last of the Intel models.
The iMac’s evolution has been slow and gradual during the Apple Silicon era. The computer has never gotten a base storage upgrade, and the base M4 and M6 models still only support a single external display (the upgraded models support two external displays, finally surpassing the old Intel model).
If you have any kind of Apple Silicon iMac and you’re happy with how it’s performing and you’re not hankering for more RAM or more displays, I don’t think the M6 model really adds anything worth upgrading for. It’s definitely faster, but even six years on, the Apple M1 remains perfectly serviceable for daily use, especially when it’s attached to 16GB of RAM.
And if you’re in the market for an iMac now, I think the M4 model still gets you the best bang for your buck if you can find one refurbished or on sale. That one still gets you a minimum of 16GB of RAM, Thunderbolt in all four ports for the four-port model, the 32GB RAM option, the nano-texture display option, and support for multiple external displays (again, in the four-port model).
The M6 iMac builds on that, and it comes with real performance benefits (more on that shortly). But the brightest dividing line in the Apple Silicon iMac model history is between the M3 and M4 model, not the M4 and M6 model. And that’s true despite the two-generation silicon upgrade.
