articles.title: Vapeur à 180 °C, nettoyage des bords : ce que promet le Roborock F25
articles.text:
Aspirer puis laver les sols, deux tâches historiques certes, mais que l’on aimerait parfois pouvoir confier à quelqu’un d’autre. Les aspirateurs laveurs promettent justement de simplifier cette routine. Voici sept bonnes raisons de s’y intéresser.
Le ménage a beau être incontournable, force est d’admettre qu’il est rarement enthousiasmant. Entre les miettes sous la table, les traces dans la cuisine, les cheveux dans la salle de bains et les poils d’animaux qui semblent se multiplier à chaque passage, conserver des sols propres demande du temps et de la régularité. C’est précisément là que les aspirateurs laveurs peuvent changer la donne, en combinant aspiration et lavage dans un même mouvement, sans avoir à sortir successivement l’aspirateur et la serpillière.
Un segment sur lequel on retrouve aujourd’hui de nombreuses marques, à l’instar de Roborock qui a développé sa gamme F25, avec plusieurs modèles pensés pour répondre aux petits tracas du quotidien. Mais quels sont réellement les avantages de ces appareils ?
1. Aspirer et laver en un seul passage
C’est évidemment le premier argument : pourquoi multiplier les opérations quand un seul appareil peut s’en charger ? Les aspirateurs laveurs aspirent les poussières, les débris et les liquides tout en nettoyant les sols.
Une approche particulièrement pratique après un repas, lorsqu’une boisson est renversée ou que les passages répétés dans la maison commencent à laisser des traces. Et bien sûr, via l’application mobile dédiée, il est tout à fait possible de programmer un nettoyage à distance, avant de rentrer le soir, pour retrouver un intérieur impeccable et qui « sent bon le propre » comme on dit.
2. Venir à bout des taches les plus tenaces grâce à la vapeur
Certaines salissures résistent davantage qu’un simple coup de serpillière. Pour y répondre, certains modèles, comme le Roborock F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2, intègrent une technologie (baptisée ici VaporFlow 2.0) qui diffuse une vapeur dense pouvant atteindre 180 °C.
Elle aide à décoller les résidus collants et les graisses sans avoir à multiplier les passages. Le système WaveFlow complète cette approche avec un nettoyage à l’eau chaude à 90 °C, soit un atout qui s’avère particulièrement intéressant dans une cuisine notamment.
3. Ne plus retrouver des cheveux coincés dans la brosse
C’est l’un des petits désagréments des appareils de nettoyage traditionnels : les cheveux et les poils finissent souvent par se multiplier autour du rouleau. Là encore, la technologie JawScrapers de Roborock repose sur un système de raclage et de séparation conçu spécifiquement pour limiter les enchevêtrements.
Elle contribue également à réduire les traces d’eau et les résidus laissés sur le sol. Un avantage appréciable dans les foyers avec animaux de compagnie ou cheveux longs.
4. Nettoyer même les recoins oubliés
Vous le savez forcément, les bordures et les angles sont souvent les grands oubliés du ménage. Là encore, certains robots disposent d’une technologie dédiée, visant à éradiquer ces “oublis”. Le F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 par exemple va particulièrement loin sur ce point avec son bras robotique IA SensEdg, qui permet un nettoyage à 0 mm sur trois côtés, pour longer les plinthes et les obstacles au plus près.
Les modèles F25 et F25 LT disposent également d’un système de nettoyage des bords, pour limiter les zones oubliées, avec une marge d’1 mm.
5. Ne plus avoir à nettoyer son aspirateur après chaque utilisation
Un aspirateur laveur doit aussi pouvoir s’entretenir facilement. Sur certains modèles, la station assure même un auto-nettoyage à haute température de 90 °C, afin de débarrasser le rouleau des saletés accumulées.
Elle prend ensuite en charge son séchage à l’air chaud, en grimpant jusqu’à 90 °C selon les modèles. De quoi limiter l’humidité résiduelle et les mauvaises odeurs, sans devoir laver manuellement la brosse après chaque session.
6. Passer sous les meubles sans être contorsionniste
Les espaces sous les canapés et les meubles bas sont rarement les plus faciles à atteindre. Grâce à la technologie FlatReach 2.0, les appareils compatibles de la gamme Roborock peuvent s’incliner à 180° pour nettoyer à plat.
Avec une hauteur de seulement 12,5 cm dans cette position, ils peuvent ainsi accéder à des zones habituellement difficiles à entretenir.
7. Un nettoyage plus confortable et efficace au quotidien
Enfin, un appareil efficace doit aussi rester agréable à utiliser. Certains robots haut de gamme misent notamment sur une maniabilité optimisée, avec des roues facilitant les déplacements et une conception pensée pour limiter les efforts.
L’autonomie et les capacités des réservoirs, qui diffèrent évidemment selon les modèles, permettent par ailleurs d’enchaîner les différentes pièces sans multiplier les interruptions. Un appareil qui aspire, qui lave, qui s’occupe des tâches difficiles et qui prend même soin de son propre rouleau, voilà de quoi revoir sérieusement quelques habitudes ménagères.
Avec sa gamme F25, Roborock décline plusieurs niveaux d’équipement, du nettoyage vapeur aux fonctions d’entretien automatisées. À l’approche du Black Friday, c’est sans doute l’occasion de retrouver un appareil adapté à son intérieur pour faciliter le ménage quotidien… Et retrouver au passage un peu de temps pour des activités autrement plus agréables que le passage de la serpillière.

articles.title: Pour rester en France, ChatGPT et Gemini pourraient devoir passer un examen
articles.text:
La commission « IA générative et vulnérabilités » a remis mardi 10 novembre à Emmanuel Macron un rapport de 177 pages, fruit de 55 auditions menées depuis février. Ses neuf experts, emmenés par la chercheuse en IA Serena Villata et les psychiatres Raphaël Gaillard et Amine Benyamina, y formulent 18 recommandations. Le document s’intitule « Protéger sans empêcher ».
Un examen d’entrée inspiré du médicament
La mesure la plus lourde conditionnerait la mise sur le marché des systèmes d’IA générative grand public, puis leur maintien, à une évaluation pluridisciplinaire préalable de leurs impacts. La mesure vise les seuls services destinés au grand public, ChatGPT et Gemini en tête ; les outils professionnels y échapperaient. Amine Benyamina assume la filiation pharmaceutique en défendant une véritable « autorisation de mise sur le marché ».
Le rapport réclame aussi un accès des autorités et de chercheurs agréés aux données d’entraînement, d’usage et de monétisation des modèles, ainsi qu’un « protocole national de réponse aux crises informationnelles liées à l’IA ». Les auteurs assurent ne pas « vouloir mettre un boulet au pied de l’économie française ni européenne » et pressent le chef de l’État de « prendre des décisions ». Celui-ci jugeait la veille, dans un entretien, qu’il fallait « interdire » l’IA partout où elle présente un risque pour les enfants.
« L’affaiblissement cognitif », première crainte des psychiatres
« Le premier enjeu est l’affaiblissement cognitif. C’est attractif, on y délègue des compétences. Puisqu’on y délègue des compétences, on ne les acquiert pas », résume Raphaël Gaillard, qui y voit un problème pour les jeunes comme pour le reste de la population. Son confrère Amine Benyamina parle d’une « dette cognitive », contractée à force de confier réflexion, décision et esprit critique à la machine.
La flagornerie des agents conversationnels, cette propension à flatter l’utilisateur au détriment de la vérité, figure parmi les mécanismes à encadrer dès la conception, au même titre que l’anthropomorphisme. « On crée un registre de relations émotionnelles qui peut avoir vocation à se substituer à l’interaction » humaine, décrit Raphaël Gaillard. Le psychiatre y voit « un système disponible en permanence, qui n’a pas d’autre intention que de vous garder en ligne ». Le rapport demande en parallèle des protections dédiées aux mineurs et un durcissement de la répression des contenus sexuels non consentis et pédocriminels générés par IA.
33 millions de personnes ont utilisé l’IA générative en France en début d’année, d’après le document, qui situe le pays au cinquième rang mondial des usages. Le rapport avancerait aussi que 73 % des Français s’informent désormais par ce biais, face à des contenus jugés 50 % plus persuasifs qu’un article de presse. Attendues pour mai dans la lettre de mission, ces conclusions auront mis six mois de plus à aboutir. « Si on ne prend pas ces décisions », prévient Raphaël Gaillard, l’externalisation cognitive, la dépendance affective et les dérives informationnelles, « on les subira ». Aucun arbitrage n’a été annoncé à ce stade.

articles.title: Why CommonFloor’s $200M exit felt like a loss to co-founder Vikas Malpani
articles.text:
Why CommonFloor’s $200M exit felt like a loss to co-founder Vikas Malpani
A decade after Quikr bought the real estate portal, Malpani reflects on leaving the startup he had spent years building and why he chose to start again.
Vikas Malpani thought he would feel like he had won when Quikr bought CommonFloor in 2016. He had spent several years co-building the startup, which began as a tool for apartment communities and grew into a property portal that reached millions of users. The company had been the focus of his working life. After the acquisition, Malpani missed the structure the company had given him. “I expected to feel like I had won. I felt like something had ended,” he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
The deal that brought CommonFloor into Quikr
Malpani founded CommonFloor in 2007 with Sumit Jain and Lalit Mangal. In January 2016, Quikr announced it was merging the portal with QuikrHomes, its real estate business. The companies did not disclose the financial terms. Business Standard reported the deal was worth $200 million, while Malpani put the figure at more than $200 million in his LinkedIn post. All three co-founders left CommonFloor about a year after the acquisition.
The acquisition came as investors were growing wary of startups burning through cash and Indian tech companies were buying smaller rivals to expand their businesses. Quikr struck two deals in 2015 and seven in 2016, according to VCCEdge data. CommonFloor gave it a bigger presence in online property listings, while another purchase that year, Grabhouse, helped it expand into managed rentals. Quikr also bought recruitment portal Hiree and folded it into QuikrJobs.
Starting over after CommonFloor
In an essay on his website, Malpani said he could have stayed in real estate, become a full-time investor or taken an advisory role. He went back to building companies, co-founding Leher, a social platform for live audio and video. The move took him into a business with very different economics from a property portal. Learning how that business worked, he wrote, came more easily than letting go of the identity he had built around CommonFloor. He also had to question whether the instincts he had developed there still applied.
Malpani is now co-founder and CEO of Garvik AI, which builds AI tools for businesses. Its ReBillion.ai platform helps employees find information across their company and lets businesses set up AI assistants. Malpani says the company has deployed those tools in banking, manufacturing, education technology and real estate. That last sector brings him back to a market he knows well, this time selling software to businesses after spending years building a portal for people looking for homes.

articles.title: Qui pour remplacer Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia ? Voici les favoris pour lui succéder — Frandroid
articles.text:
Début novembre, Jensen Huang a reconnu une liaison avec Alice Huang, ancienne dirigeante de Megaspeed, que le renseignement américain soupçonne d’espionner pour la Chine. Le conseil d’administration de Nvidia a aussitôt lancé une enquête interne, confiée à l’ancien procureur fédéral Joon Kim, pour savoir si son patron avait été la cible d’une opération d’espionnage. Puis le New York Times a publié ce mercredi 11 novembre de nouvelles révélations sur une liaison avec une salariée du groupe. Nvidia a officialisé ce jeudi 12 novembre la démission de son cofondateur, 33 ans après la création de l’entreprise. Le géant des puces pour l’IA doit maintenant se trouver un patron, alors que la succession n’a jamais été préparée.
Le communiqué de Nvidia ne donne aucune raison à ce départ et se contente de trois phrases d’hommage à Jensen Huang. Le conseil a accepté ce mercredi 11 novembre sa démission de ses postes de CEO et d’administrateur. Colette Kress, 59 ans, directrice financière depuis septembre 2013 après près de 25 ans chez Cisco et Microsoft, prend l’intérim sans lâcher la finance.
Ian Buck, l’ingénieur de CUDA en tête des pronostics
Le conseil dit qu’il étudiera des candidats internes comme externes, et il a engagé un cabinet de recrutement extérieur. Jensen Huang espérait que son successeur travaille déjà chez Nvidia, mais il refusait la planification de succession classique. Il n’a jamais désigné d’héritier, et plusieurs dizaines de dirigeants lui rendaient compte directement, dans une organisation très plate.
Ian Buck est arrivé chez Nvidia en 2004, après une thèse à Stanford sur Brook, un langage qui faisait déjà calculer aux cartes graphiques autre chose que des images. Il a ensuite mené le développement de CUDA, la plateforme logicielle qui permet aux développeurs de faire tourner leurs programmes d’IA sur les puces Nvidia, et qui les retient chez la marque.
Il dirige aujourd’hui les produits matériels et logiciels destinés aux hyperscalers, ces géants du cloud comme Microsoft ou Oracle qui remplissent leurs centres de données de cartes Nvidia. Sur Polymarket, un site où l’on parie sur l’actualité, il était donné ce jeudi à 38 % pour le poste permanent, devant Kress à 28 %. Mais il n’a jamais dirigé d’entreprise.
Trois autres vétérans du groupe ont moins de chances :
- Bryan Catanzaro, vice-président de la recherche appliquée en apprentissage profond, la technique qui sert à entraîner les IA actuelles. Il porte une grande partie des travaux d’IA de Nvidia et a une forte légitimité scientifique, mais il n’a jamais dirigé une structure commerciale de cette taille.
- Jeff Fisher, entré chez Nvidia en 1994, figure historique de l’activité grand public et des cartes graphiques GeForce.
- Jay Puri, patron des ventes et des partenariats mondiaux pendant plus de vingt ans, connu pour son carnet d’adresses chez les grands clients. Il a pris sa retraite en août 2026 et n’est plus que conseiller du groupe. Polymarket lui donnait 3 %.
Chez Apple et Arm, deux profils difficiles à débaucher
Hors de Nvidia, le premier nom vient d’Apple. Selon Semafor, qui s’appuie sur une seule source, Johny Srouji fait partie des personnes étudiées pour le poste. Cet ingénieur a dirigé la conception des puces A des iPhone et M des Mac, et il a piloté le passage des Mac des processeurs Intel aux puces maison Apple Silicon. Intel l’avait déjà envisagé comme CEO en 2019. Rien n’indique pourtant qu’il ait été approché. Apple l’a en outre nommé en avril 2026 directeur du matériel (Chief Hardware Officer), un poste créé pour lui quand John Ternus a été désigné CEO.
Donald Trump, jamais à l’abri d’une idée saugrenue, souhaite que Tim Cook, l’ancien CEO d’Apple devenu président exécutif de son conseil d’administration le 1er septembre, succède à Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia. Il a passé la direction d’Apple à John Ternus le 1er septembre, au terme d’une transition annoncée dès avril. On l’imagine mal reprendre un poste de CEO ailleurs.
Rene Haas connaît mieux la maison. Le CEO d’Arm, la société britannique qui conçoit l’architecture des processeurs de la quasi-totalité des smartphones, a travaillé sept ans chez Nvidia avant de partir chez Arm en 2013. Il dirige Arm depuis 2022, et un départ paraît compliqué : en mai 2026, Arm a proposé de lui accorder jusqu’à 800 millions de dollars (environ 690 millions d’euros) en options sur actions si l’entreprise vaut 2 000 milliards de dollars d’ici 2031. Les parieurs y croient d’ailleurs de moins en moins : sur Polymarket, sa cote est passée de 25 % à 5 %.
La piste familiale paraît exclue
Les enfants de Jensen Huang travaillent aussi chez Nvidia. Madison Huang est directrice du marketing produit, Spencer Huang directeur produit dans la robotique, et son gendre Nico Caprez, 35 ans, est vice-président chargé de l’infrastructure IA depuis son arrivée en 2024. Jensen Huang avait pourtant dit ne pas vouloir imposer le poste à ses enfants, qui devraient le mériter. Après un scandale né de la vie privée du fondateur, une nomination familiale paraît exclue, le conseil cherchant d’abord à rassurer les marchés.
Colette Kress parlera pour la première fois aux investisseurs en tant que patronne par intérim le mardi 17 novembre, avec les résultats trimestriels et une conférence prévue à 23 heures, heure de Paris. Nvidia n’a donné aucun calendrier pour la nomination de son CEO permanent.

articles.title: This is the Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter
articles.text:
At OCP Summit 2026, we saw Meta’s new MetaRoCE network adapter. This is Meta’s answer to providing an open RDMA transport layer that has features like packet spraying, congestion control, and more. This was a presentation we saw at OCP Summit, but Meta had a NIC on display.
Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter at OCP 2026
Here is the display from the Meta booth at OCP Summit 2026, where you can see an OCP NIC 3.0 card.
During its OCP 2026 presentation, Meta shared some of the big features of MetaRoCE:
- Per-path reliability and congestion control
- Receiver rate hints (RCN) for fast incast convergence
- Tolerates packet loss and reordering
- Single QP carries multiple streams over multiple network paths
- Runs on commodity Ethernet: ECN + ECMP, no switch (Source: Meta)
Before OCP Summit, Meta demonstrated this with the AMD Pensando NIC series. The programmability allowed it to implement the protocol without having dedicated hardware. That allows Meta to potentially source from multiple vendors.
Meta is trying to build a network protocol that can scale to million-GPU training, but also that can run on different network topologies and hardware.
As a quick aside, the NIC shown was an OCP NIC 3.0 with SFF pull tab design, which is our favorite form factor that we wish all server vendors used.
Final Words
Given Meta’s heritage of starting OCP Summit, they usually have super-cool hardware in the booth. Last year, we got the AMD Helios MI450 Rack at OCP Summit with a Different Version from Meta as an example. This year, the company brought some larger nodes, but also small items like this adapter. It is always neat to see what Meta is working on.
If you want to see what AWS is doing, for example, you can check out our Inside the Secretive AWS Networking Lab.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo. Original written by José Tadeu Arantes. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, Yugui Yao. Andreev qubit readout from dynamic interference supercurrent. Physical Review B, 2026; 114 (8) DOI: 10.1103/6gkt-hghj

articles.title: Microsoft podría pagar a los usuarios por alquilar su tarjeta gráfica en reposo para entrenar ia
articles.text:
Microsoft registró una patente que propone usar las tarjetas gráficas de millones de usuarios para entrenar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial mientras permanecen inactivas. El documento, titulado “Microentrenamiento oportunista en dispositivos periféricos mediante el aprovechamiento de la capacidad de GPU disponible”, plantea un sistema que distribuiría pequeñas tareas de entrenamiento entre los equipos de quienes se inscriban de forma voluntaria. La iniciativa busca sortear la falta de capacidad en centros de datos y se asemeja a la idea que planteó el jefe de OpenAI sobre aprovechar la memoria RAM disponible en los dispositivos de los usuarios.
El sistema evaluaría temperatura, consumo y disponibilidad de cada equipo
De acuerdo con el documento, la plataforma gestionaría variables como la utilización de la GPU, la memoria disponible, la temperatura y el consumo energético de cada dispositivo. Estos parámetros determinarían si la tarjeta gráfica cuenta con capacidad ociosa para ejecutar tareas de entrenamiento sin afectar la experiencia del usuario. Las cargas de trabajo se ajustarían según las características de cada equipo: una computadora orientada a videojuegos podría recibir tareas más complejas que un portátil con menor potencia.
Microsoft también analizaría el historial de uso de cada dispositivo para optimizar la asignación de recursos. Si una persona utiliza su computadora durante el horario laboral y la reserva para jugar por la tarde o la noche, el sistema priorizaría ejecutar las tareas de entrenamiento en las horas de oficina, siempre que no interfiera con el uso habitual del equipo.
La patente describe un mecanismo de verificación mediante el cual Microsoft asignaría tareas similares a distintos equipos para comparar resultados, detectar errores y descartar posibles manipulaciones. Una vez validados, los datos se combinarían e integrarían al entrenamiento general del modelo de IA.
Créditos canjeables
El documento contempla un esquema de compensación basado en créditos para quienes cedan el uso de su GPU. Microsoft no especificó montos, pero indicó que estos créditos podrían intercambiarse por software gratuito, acceso a modelos de IA o dinero en efectivo.
La empresa ya opera programas de fidelidad vinculados al uso de su software, por lo que podría aplicar una mecánica similar para recompensar a los usuarios que habiliten el acceso a su hardware.
Viabilidad del proyecto
La solicitud de patente fue registrada en abril de 2025 y se publicó el 5 de noviembre de 2026, según el portal especializado Wccftech. Se trata, por ahora, de un documento de patente sin confirmación de que vaya a implementarse en el corto o mediano plazo. La propuesta recuerda a SETI@home, el proyecto de la Universidad de California que utilizaba la capacidad ociosa de los procesadores domésticos para procesar datos astronómicos en busca de señales de origen extraterrestre.
La rentabilidad del esquema depende de múltiples variables, entre ellas el uso, la temperatura y la fiabilidad de cada equipo. Los usuarios que participen tendrían que asumir el costo adicional de electricidad que implica mantener la tarjeta gráfica en funcionamiento, además de lidiar con el calor generado durante la ejecución de las tareas de IA. Microsoft podría poner en marcha este sistema si la escasez de memoria y capacidad de cómputo se prolonga en el tiempo.
Lo que debes saber de las tarjetas gráficas
La tarjeta gráfica es el componente encargado de procesar los datos del procesador central para convertirlos en imágenes visibles en pantalla, y cuenta con su propio procesador —la GPU o Unidad de Procesamiento Gráfico— y memoria dedicada. Su vida útil puede extenderse de cinco a ocho años si recibe un cuidado adecuado, aunque ese plazo se reduce a tres o cuatro años en usuarios con demandas de alto rendimiento, como jugadores o profesionales de gráficos.
Entre los factores que pueden acortar su duración figuran el sobrecalentamiento por mala ventilación, el overclocking, la acumulación de polvo, el uso intensivo en tareas como la minería de criptomonedas y las fuentes de alimentación de baja calidad que generan variaciones de voltaje.

articles.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images
articles.text:
A critical vulnerability in Red Hat Quay could allow attackers to access private container images and replace content in repositories across an affected registry.
Red Hat Quay is an enterprise container registry used to store, manage and distribute container images. It allows organizations to control who can download or upload images used in application development and deployment.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123710, has a CVSS score of 9.8. It affects deployments where the service responsible for managing signing keys is accessible to untrusted clients.
“This Critical flaw in Red Hat Quay’s service key server allows an unauthenticated attacker to take over registry token signing,” Red Hat said in its advisory.
When anonymous access is enabled, an attacker without an account can obtain a registry token and exploit weaknesses in the key rotation mechanism to install their own trusted signing key.
The attacker can then generate tokens granting read and write access to any repository, bypassing normal access restrictions. This could expose private images and any credentials or other secrets stored in them, while also allowing attackers to overwrite images that other systems subsequently download.
The malicious signing key can be configured without an expiration date and survives registry restarts unless removed.
“Rotation also deletes the legitimate instance key as a side effect, and the attacker key can delete replacement instance keys,” Red Hat’s Bugzilla report explains.
This could interfere with normal registry operations, preventing legitimate users from uploading or downloading images.
“Turning off anonymous access doesn’t protect you, because any valid Quay account can still exploit the flaw,” Red Hat warns in additional guidance.
The company also notes that changing passwords or regenerating robot tokens does not invalidate an unauthorized signing key.
Red Hat recommends restricting access to the key-management service, reviewing logs for suspicious key changes, and removing unauthorized keys. However, the company warns that attackers could reinstall malicious keys until a fix is deployed.
The vulnerability was discovered by Red Hat’s Dave O’Connor.
Neither the advisory nor the Bugzilla report identifies a fixed version. However, fixes for this vulnerability and another Quay flaw tracked as CVE-2026-110697 were merged into the project’s GitHub repository on November 11.

articles.title: Preload von GTA 6: Datenverkehr steigt teilweise um das Zehnfache an – was das für den Release bedeutet
articles.text:
Preload von GTA 6: Datenverkehr steigt teilweise um das Zehnfache an – was das für den Release bedeutet
Am 19. November 2026 fällt der Startschuss für ein Spiel, auf das viele Zocker:innen schon seit Jahren warten. GTA 6 öffnet die Tore des neonbeleuchteten und chaotischen Vice City. Neu für die Reihe ist, dass das Spiel ausschließlich als Download angeboten wird. Damit im besten Fall niemand am Release-Tag enttäuscht wird, weil die Download-Server in die Knie gehen, lässt Rockstar den Preload von GTA 6 seit dem 10. November zu.
GTA 6 im Preload: Erste Vorzeichen für den Start?
Wie Golem berichtet, vermelden schon jetzt erste Internetanbieter, dass GTA 6 den Datenverkehr beachtlich erhöht. So verzeichnete etwa 1&1 in der Nacht vom 9. auf den 10. November einen Verbrauch, der etwa zehnmal so hoch lag, wie an normalen Tagen. Auch Vodafone berichtet von einem kurzzeitigen Anstieg. Wie uns ein Sprecher des Unternehmens mitteilte, lag der Datendurchsatz am Tag des Preloads etwa 60 Prozent über dem Niveau des Vortags.
Wie Vodafone weiter berichtet, geht der Großteil des Traffics aus Downloads über das Playstation Network zurück. Nach dem ersten Anstieg ging der Datenverkehr aber wieder etwas zurück. Er liegt zwar noch rund 20 Prozent über dem Normalwert, ist aber für das Netz keine besondere Belastung. Vodafone geht davon aus, dass der Preload dazu beiträgt, die Last über mehrere Tage gleichmäßiger verteilen. Marc Hölzer, Bereichsleiter Netzentwicklung bei Vodafone, sagt zum möglichen Anstieg zum Release: „Unser Netz ist auf solche Spitzen vorbereitet und verteilt die zusätzlichen Datenmengen so, dass die Downloads stabil bei den Kunden ankommen. Klar ist aber auch: Das Download-Tempo kann dabei von Nutzer zu Nutzer unterschiedlich sein und zeitweise schwanken.“
Und auch in den USA rüsten sich die Anbieter für den Release von GTA 6. Comcast bietet über seine Untermarke Xfinity etwa erhöhte Download-Raten für alle Kunden und das ohne Aufpreis. So sollen sich die mehr als 200 Gigabyte, die GTA 6 im Download beanspruchen wird, dank Verbindungen mit bis zu zwei Gigabyte pro Sekunde schnell abhandeln lassen.
Gegenüber Gamesindustry berichteten mehrere Branchenexpert:innen, dass der Release von GTA 6 zwar eine Herausforderung für den Datenverkehr sein wird, aber es aktuell keine Anzeichen dafür gäbe, von flächendeckenden Ausfällen auszugehen. Sie gehen davon aus, dass der Preload die Last vom Playstation Network und vom Xbox Store nimmt. Ohne eine neuntägige Vorlaufzeit hätten sonst alle Vorbesteller:innen direkt zum Launch den Download angeworfen und hätten die Server damit überfordert.
Neil McRae, Chief Technology and Innovation Officer beim britischen Internetanbieter Cityfibre, schlägt indes etwas vorsichtigere Töne an: „Es gibt keinen Weg daran vorbei, dass am Launch-Tag extrem viel los sein wird. Das liegt daran, dass viele Leute bis zum Launch mit dem Kauf warten.“ Doch in den vergangenen Jahren sind digitale Events und ausschließlich per Download angebotene Spiele immer mehr zum Standard geworden. Internetanbieter konnten sich laut McRae auf ein solches Großereignis also vorbereiten.
Er sagt dazu: „Egal, ob es der Launch von GTA 6 oder ein großes Update für Fortnite oder Call of Duty ist: Netzwerkspitzen sind mittlerweile ein normales Ereignis statt einer Anomalie. Die Anbieter sind in der Lage, sie zu handhaben.“ Gordon Thornton, der 17 Jahre bei Sony gearbeitet und dort das Playstation Network mit aufgebaut hat, findet ähnlich optimistische Worte für die Server der Playstation: „Sie wissen, wie viele Vorbestellungen es gab und welche Bandbreiten nötig sind, um die Vorbestellungen bereitzustellen […] Es ist der größte Titel und die größte Möglichkeit für die PS5, sie müssen es also hinbekommen.“

articles.title: Meta launches Muse AI agent for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS — so now you can talk to your fluffy life assistant anywhere
articles.text:
Meta launches Muse AI agent for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS — so now you can talk to your fluffy life assistant anywhere
Ever wanted to talk to an AI agent through your wrist? Now you can!
- Meta has announced Muse compatibility with Apple Watch and Wear OS
- Muse will now be able to help out with tasks through your smartwatch
- Your custom Muse agent will now show up on your wrist to answer questions and keep you on schedule
Meta has released Muse AI compatibility for Apple Watch and Android Wear OS allowing you to talk to your personal AI agent anywhere you go directly through your smartwatch.
As long as you can get past giving Muse total access to your personal life, you’ll find its ability to weigh in on your life really quite helpful, helping to keep you on task, on time, and in line with your life goals.
And now that you can interact with Muse’s AI persona Jolly through voice calls, text messages, or dictation on your smartwatch, you can cut out the crucial seconds it takes to pull your phone out of your pocket or log in to your laptop.
More ways to interact with Muse
Muse hit the AI agent market in September and surpassed 10 million US app store downloads within the first 40 days. The AI agent can help manage every facet of your life, from bills and your mortgage, to business meetings, client calls, and deadlines.
But it’s more than just a mundane task manager, Meta says Muse is also able to organize your social life and help achieve your life goals — and if you so desire, it can make purchases on your behalf.
In order to put a more likeable face on AI, Meta allows users to customize the look of their assistant who will pop up on your phone or watch screen whenever you need help.
Muse is quickly becoming a central focus of Meta’s consumer strategy, with the company teasing Muse Charm — essentially a Tamagotchi-sized device — that will allow you to see and communicate directly with your Muse from the palm of your hand.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
More recently, Meta announced that Muse would have access to Spaces, which gives users a way to create “custom experiences” with their Muse focused on particular tasks, topics, or goals.
If that wasn’t enough ways to communicate with your Muse, Meta also rolled out the ability to video call your AI assistant, with Jolly having the ability to convey “subtle expressions and gestures” to fit each conversation’s tone. Of course, Muse won’t be able to see you and will rely entirely on the tone of your voice and the topic of conversation to convey it’s ‘emotions’.
Of course, having this many ways to talk to your AI agent and giving it complete control over almost all of your data comes with a few downsides. Recent testing by Surfshark found that Meta’s Muse is the most data hungry consumer AI agent currently available, hoovering up double the types of data that its competitors do.
So if you’re on a phone plan with limited data, you might want to consider conducting your Muse conversations over Wi-Fi.

articles.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
articles.text:
Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found.
AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
A study testing Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT found that in as many as 15 percent of conversations, chatbots displayed ‘risky’ URLs.
The study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi and shared exclusively with The Verge prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of 151 brands. Questions included “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?”; “Where can I find [brand] online?”; and “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?” The test ran over the course of two testing periods in September and asked about 151 small and large companies like fashion brands Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, and Madhappy (a client of Podqi) and homeware brand Le Creuset. Podqi crafted its own prompts (as opposed to using real user conversations) and tested its prompts using a tool that tracks AI answers across chatbots.
Perplexity performed the worst, showing risky sites in 15 percent of answers
Over the course of 6,795 answers, Podqi found that all three AI engines cited and showed shoppers risky sites, defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, old brand domains that have been reregistered by someone else, or dead sites that aren’t active at all but that someone else could purchase and reuse. Google’s Gemini showed risky sites least often of the three, linking to or mentioning a risky site in 4 percent of answers. (Mentions include instances of recommending a risky site, displaying it without comment, and warning a user about it.) Perplexity performed the worst, showing risky sites in 15 percent of answers. ChatGPT fell somewhere in the middle at 8 percent. ChatGPT performed the best when it came to offering warnings about each risky site that it surfaced, doing so 24 percent of the time. Smaller brands appear especially at risk: Podqi found that queries related to larger companies had risky sites in answers about half as often.
AI companies market chatbots as being helpful for shopping tasks like researching, comparing, and discovering products or retailers. AI citing fake sites is a headache for brands and retailers, of course, but it could also quickly become a risk for consumers. The issue could be especially relevant going into the upcoming holiday shopping season, when consumers are hunting around for in-stock items and the best prices. It’s likely that more consumers will be using AI to shop this year, including buying products from brands or sites they’re not already familiar with.
“Part of this piece, too, is making sure that the consumers know, even though you are being fed a result in a particular chatbot, it is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information,” says Podqi CEO and cofounder Trevor West.
“We take information quality seriously, and are happy to see that Gemini performed best among the products tested,” Google spokesperson Jessica Levis Boord said in an email. “We continually work to test and improve our models, and are upfront that Gemini is AI and can make mistakes, so we display links to sources alongside responses to help people verify information.”
“Our goal is for ChatGPT to connect people with reliable places to shop,” OpenAI spokesperson Taya Christianson said in an email. “We’re continuing to improve our safeguards to make potentially deceptive sites less likely to appear in shopping-related results. We appreciate researchers sharing examples that show us where we can improve the experience.”
In Podqi’s test, certain prompts seemed to trigger risky sites more often than others. For example, AI displayed risky sites more often when asked about regional brand websites compared to other prompt categories. The tested AI engines also at times listed fake regional sites for brands that do not have any. In one conversation, Perplexity named the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website and called it “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.”
“Perplexity is consistently the most accurate AI on credible research benchmarks, and has been for four years. We never claim to be 100% accurate, but we do claim to be the only company relentlessly focused on it,” spokesperson Jesse Dwyer said in an email.

articles.title: Mangaluru’s Zupple Labs wins DRDO’s first-ever blockchain defence project
articles.text:
Mangaluru’s Zupple Labs wins DRDO’s first-ever blockchain defence project
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs is the first blockchain startup selected under DRDO’s Technology Development Fund. Over 30 months, it will build an indigenous security-audit framework for defence applications.
Mangaluru-based Zupple Labs has been selected by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) under its Technology Development Fund (TDF) programme. Its brief: build India's first indigenous framework for security auditing of blockchain applications in the defence sector.
The selection is rare by any measure. Fewer than 90 projects have made it through the TDF programme in its ten-year history, and this is the first in the blockchain domain.
What DRDO has asked Zupple Labs to build
Over the next 30 months, Zupple Labs will develop a platform that DRDO will use to standardise security audits of upcoming blockchain applications across the defence sector.
As defence agencies explore distributed ledgers for records, logistics and authentication, a common auditing standard matters. It gives every new application the same security bar before deployment, and keeps that capability built and owned in India.
Trust infrastructure for governments
Zupple Labs builds blockchain-powered trust infrastructure for governments and institutions, with a presence across four countries. Its systems secure and authenticate critical citizen records, making them tamper-evident and verifiable.
The records it handles include:
- Land records
- Educational credentials
- Identities
- Permits and work orders
A client list that spans continents
The DRDO mandate builds on an established public-sector track record. Zupple Labs has delivered solutions for:
- The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
- The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
- The Australian and New Zealand student immigration ecosystems
- The Governments of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra
- The Government of Kenya
Work with national ministries, a UN agency and foreign governments gives the startup experience in exactly the kind of high-stakes, compliance-heavy environments that defence demands.
From Mangaluru to the national stage
Zupple Labs was a winner of the Karnataka government's Elevate programme in 2019. Seven years on, its DRDO selection is a strong signal for the state's Beyond Bengaluru push to grow startup hubs outside the capital.
Congratulating Zupple Labs on securing a project under DRDO’s TDF programme, Capt Brijesh Chowta, Member of Parliament from Dakshina Kannada, said: “Glad to see Zupple Labs, one of the 10 start-ups in this year’s ‘Bolpu’ cohort, making strides in strengthening the security and resilience of blockchain technology and contributing to India’s growing cybersecurity capabilities.”
The point goes beyond one company. Deep-tech work of national significance is now coming out of Karnataka's tier-2 cities, and Mangaluru is proving it can build for governments, global institutions and the country's defence establishment.

articles.title: O que é a CoreWeave e por que sua infraestrutura importa para a IA
articles.text:
As ações da CoreWeave recuaram 6,3% antes da abertura do mercado, em meio à turbulência envolvendo Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, e à preocupação dos investidores com o financiamento da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.
A queda chama atenção porque a CoreWeave fornece a capacidade computacional usada em aplicações de IA. O desempenho da empresa ajuda a mostrar como as incertezas sobre o crescimento do setor também atingem companhias responsáveis por sustentar sua infraestrutura.
O que é a CoreWeave e por que ela importa para a IA?
A CoreWeave é uma provedora de computação em nuvem especializada em oferecer capacidade de processamento para aplicações de inteligência artificial. Seu negócio está ligado à expansão de empresas que precisam de grandes volumes de recursos computacionais para desenvolver e executar essas tecnologias.
A companhia faz parte do grupo conhecido como neoclouds. Diferentemente de gigantes como Alphabet, Amazon e Microsoft, essas empresas são mais jovens e concentram sua atuação no fornecimento de infraestrutura computacional. Elas não precisam desenvolver seus próprios modelos de IA para participar desse mercado: podem atender desenvolvedores e companhias que trabalham com essas tecnologias.
Nesse papel, a CoreWeave atua como parceira independente de empresas como Anthropic e OpenAI, além de competir com os grandes provedores de nuvem. Sua relevância está justamente em fornecer capacidade computacional para um setor cuja expansão exige cada vez mais processamento.
Esse modelo, porém, depende de investimentos elevados. Para ampliar a capacidade oferecida aos clientes, a CoreWeave precisa comprar chips e construir data centers. Como essas estruturas exigem financiamento, a disponibilidade de crédito e seu custo têm impacto direto sobre os planos de crescimento da companhia.
Endividamento coloca a expansão sob pressão
A preocupação dos investidores não se limita à queda das ações. Os títulos de dívida de alto rendimento da CoreWeave, classificados como junk bonds — papéis de maior risco que precisam oferecer juros mais altos para atrair compradores —, perderam valor.
Na segunda-feira, o título mais negociado da empresa, com juros de 9,625% e vencimento em 2032, oferecia rendimento próximo de 15%, segundo dados da MarketAxess. Quando o preço de um título cai, seu rendimento sobe, sinalizando que os investidores exigem uma remuneração maior para emprestar dinheiro à companhia.
As ações da CoreWeave também acumulavam queda de aproximadamente 40% no mês. Se o rendimento de 15% representar o custo de novas captações, financiar a compra de chips e a construção de data centers poderá se tornar economicamente inviável.
Há, contudo, alternativas de financiamento. Empréstimos e títulos garantidos por ativos, como data centers, ou por contratos de fornecimento de capacidade computacional a grandes clientes, como a Meta, tiveram desempenho melhor do que parte da dívida sem garantia. Isso indica que o acesso a recursos não está totalmente fechado, embora o custo e as condições de financiamento sejam pontos de atenção.
Por que a crise da Nvidia afeta a CoreWeave?
A turbulência envolvendo Huang acrescenta incerteza a um setor no qual empresas como a CoreWeave dependem da continuidade dos investimentos em infraestrutura. No mesmo pregão em que as ações da provedora de nuvem recuaram 6,3% no pré-mercado, os papéis da Nvidia caíram 6,8%.
O movimento conjunto não significa que a crise de liderança da Nvidia tenha provocado os problemas financeiros da CoreWeave. As duas companhias, porém, estão expostas às expectativas em torno do mercado de IA: a Nvidia fornece chips essenciais para essa infraestrutura, enquanto a CoreWeave vende capacidade computacional para empresas que utilizam essas tecnologias.
O mercado também avalia se a demanda por processamento será suficiente para sustentar os investimentos necessários à expansão do setor, sem elevar demais os custos de financiamento ou o preço dos serviços. Para empresas que dependem de dívida para crescer, crédito mais caro pode comprometer novos projetos.
A CoreWeave e a holandesa Nebius Group estavam entre as empresas que divulgariam resultados naquela semana. Os investidores aguardavam sinais de como as companhias pretendiam financiar a expansão e ampliar a capacidade computacional sem depender excessivamente de empréstimos caros.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: More game developers are starting to use generative AI
articles.text:
More video game developers are using generative AI tools in their jobs compared to last year, according to the GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey. Forty percent of developers surveyed say they use it “as part of their job,” an increase from 36 percent in 2025. Usage was higher with game developers that work on free-to-play games at 58 percent and mobile-only studio workers at 70 percent.
More game developers are starting to use generative AI
The GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey shows an increase in AI usage among game developers.
The survey is being published as the game industry continues to reckon with generative AI tools. While many game developers, particularly indie developers, have spoken out strongly against the technology, AI is at the center of indie awards conversations in part because Big Walk developer House House “sparingly” used LLMs to assist with technical challenges in the “final stretch” of development. AI is also increasingly being used to reverse-engineer retro games. And in a post on Thursday, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma seemed to indicate that AI will be central to Xbox’s future, saying that “A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars.”
Seventy three percent of the survey’s respondents said they used AI for research and brainstorming, while 62 percent used it for data analysis and summarization, and 56 percent for code generation and debugging. Twenty two percent of respondents used generative AI for concept art or visual ideation, and 8 percent used it for production art or final game assets.
The survey also included grim numbers about layoffs, with 34 percent of respondents saying they have been laid off sometime in the past two years.

articles.title: Superman : Henry Cavill de retour dans le rôle ? L'acteur s'exprime
articles.text:
Skydance, propriétaire de DC Studios depuis son rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery en octobre, a annoncé ce lundi 9 novembre le départ du duo Gunn/Safran. Jeremy Latcham, ancien cadre de Marvel Studios, prendra la tête du studio le 1er décembre. Henry Cavill s’exprimait, lui, dans un entretien accordé au site Inverse. L’acteur de 43 ans faisait la promotion de Mustache Protocol, un jeu vidéo rétro façon années 80 qu’il a conçu avec Google, à l’aide des outils d’IA de son nouvel ordinateur portable, le Googlebook. Mais la discussion a rapidement basculé sur son avenir chez DC et son rôle de Superman.
Henry Cavill dans Superman ?
Le journaliste d’Inverse lui a demandé s’il reprendrait la cape, par exemple dans la peau du Superman vieillissant de la bande dessinée Kingdom Come. Henry Cavill a répondu en citant le dessin animé Fievel et le Nouveau Monde :
« Écoutez, il y a énormément d’histoires fantastiques. Il y a toujours beaucoup d’opportunités. Comme le chantait le pigeon à Fievel dans Fievel et le Nouveau Monde : “il ne faut jamais dire jamais”. Et j’adhère à ça. J’ai passé des moments tellement merveilleux à jouer Superman par le passé. Je ne dirais jamais jamais maintenant. »
En décembre 2022, moins de deux mois après avoir annoncé son retour à la suite de son caméo dans Black Adam, Henry Cavill avait dû faire ses adieux au rôle. James Gunn et Peter Safran, tout juste arrivés à la tête de DC Studios, voulaient raconter un Superman plus jeune. Le rôle est revenu en juin 2023 à David Corenswet.
Sa fille l’a reconnu sur un jouet Superman
Interrogé sur ce que la paternité a changé dans son rapport au rôle, Henry Cavill a raconté une scène récente avec sa fille :
« Parfois, des gens envoient des objets Superman à ma fille pour plaisanter. L’autre jour, nous avons ouvert un jouet Superman, elle l’a regardé et a dit : “C’est papa !”. Elle n’a que deux ans et quatre mois, donc je n’ai aucune idée de comment elle a su que c’était moi, quelle sorte de connexion cosmique c’était. Mais cela m’a vraiment touché d’une manière spéciale, parce que jouer Superman a évidemment été un tel honneur. »
Les deux dirigeants qui avaient écarté Henry Cavill quittent la tête de DC Studios. James Gunn garde toutefois la main sur Man of Tomorrow : il a écrit et réalisé le film, qu’il produit avec Peter Safran. Le film est en post-production et sortira aux États-Unis le 9 juillet 2027. Au-delà, Skydance n’a rien annoncé sur l’avenir de Superman au cinéma.

articles.title: Pour contrer la Citroën ë-C3, Dacia préparerait un tout nouveau SUV électrique à moins de 20 000 €
articles.text:
Dacia vient de renouveler la vieillissante Spring. Un bon début, même si la marque roumaine reste pour l’instant bloquée à un seul et unique véhicule électrique dans sa gamme. Pour réduire à l’avenir ses émissions de CO₂, cela ne suffira clairement pas. Si une Sandero à batterie est bel et bien dans les cartons, un autre invité surprise pourrait se joindre à la fête. Il s’agit d’un crossover qui n’était initialement pas prévu pour Europe…
Présenté en mars dernier, le Renault Bridger est un parfait inconnu puisqu’il ne s’agit qu’à l’heure actuelle d’un concept. Mais cette jolie étude de style sera promise à un bel avenir en arrivant dès 2027 sur les marchés émergents. Elle prendra alors la forme d’un petit crossover dépassant tout juste les 4 mètres de long, et qui sera décliné en versions essence, hybride et électrique. Ce véhicule inédit se placera ainsi sous le Renault Duster.
Objectif CO2 : pourquoi Dacia veut importer ce modèle en Europe
S’il n’était pas censé arriver chez nous, le Bridger pourrait voir sa feuille de route complètement bouleversée en raison du contexte actuel. Vu que Dacia doit rapidement électrifier sa gamme à moindre coût, adapter le Bridger au marché européen est une occasion rêvée pour atteindre les objectifs CO₂ imposés par l’Union européenne. Possible ainsi que le véhicule ait une carrière bien plus importante que prévu, portée par des horizons repoussés.
Parachuter le Bridger en Europe permettrait alors à Dacia de concurrencer frontalement les citadines électriques accessibles de Stellantis que sont les Citroën ë-C3 et Fiat Grande Panda. Ces deux véhicules ont d’ailleurs opté pour une stratégie similaire, à savoir un développement initialement pensé pour les pays émergents avant une arrivée sur le marché européen. Le Bridger se positionnerait ainsi entre la Spring et la future Sandero électrique.
4 nouvelles voitures électriques : la feuille de route de la marque roumaine
Dacia avait d’ailleurs confirmé lancer quatre modèles électriques d’ici 2030, la Spring étant la première sur la liste. Les Sandero et Sandero Stepway se placent aussi en quasi-certitudes. Le dernier membre de la vague demeure en revanche purement hypothétique. Un remplaçant du Jogger semble peu probable, au même titre qu’une déclinaison électrique du Striker. Tous les regards sont donc tournés vers le Bridger, même si le Hipster est aussi un bon candidat.
François Provost, le PDG du groupe Renault, avait d’ailleurs lâché un gros indice au Mondial de l’Automobile de Paris en affirmant que le Bridger a été « créé pour l’Inde, mais qu’il pourrait un jour arriver sur nos marchés également ». S’il est confirmé, le SUV pourrait débuter sous les 20 000 € et offrir entre 200 et 300 km d’autonomie. Son style cubique devrait être fidèle à celui du concept et Dacia ne devrait pas y apporter de trop grosses modifications.

articles.title: Nvidia board to meet to decide CEO Jensen Huang's future at the company: Reports
articles.text:
Nvidia board to meet to decide CEO Jensen Huang's future at the company: Reports
Reports say Jensen Huang had another extramarital affair with a senior executive of Nvidia, in addition to the relationship with a Chinese national Alice Huang, who was allegedly recruited as an intelligence asset by the Chinese government.
Jensen Huang's position as the CEO of Nvidia looks increasingly uncertain with new details of extra-marital affairs emerging. The board is meeting soon to decide whether to oust him from the company he co-founded in 1993, according to reports.
Reports say Jensen had another extramarital affair with a senior executive of Nvidia. This is in addition to the relationship he had with a Chinese national Alice Huang, who was allegedly recruited as an intelligence asset by the Chinese government.
Jensen has been the face of the chip company for 33 years. But recent developments have put him on sticky wicket with respect to his position in the company.
While the Nvidia board has already launched an investigation into the affair with Alice, a decision regarding Jensen's future in the company may be taken soon.
Artificial intelligence is a much sought-after technology today, and Nvidia has been the unquestioned leader in this space, with its advanced GPUs (graphic processing units). The relationship with the Chinese national reportedly enabled an illegal transfer of this technology to China, reports indicate.
AI is increasingly being seen as a national security asset, and the United States is keen to ensure that other countries do not get complete access to its technology. While China has emerged as a key rival in the AI race, it still lacks a decisive edge over the US.
The role of the US government comes into play here. Nvidia will come under scrutiny from the committee of the Congress, which is likely to question the company on whether its technology was illegally transferred to China.
Jensen has transformed Nvidia from a niche gaming graphics company into a hardware and software powerhouse of the global AI industry. He is seen as an influential individual determining the contours of any policy with regard to the industry. He is also well-networked with various heads of states across the world.
Jensen's potential exit raises a crucial question: who will succeed him? Reports indicate that there has been no succession planning at Nvidia as Jensen operates a flat management structure with around 60 direct reportees. It must be noted that both his children, Madison Huang and Spencer Huang, and his son-in-law Nico Caprez work at the company.
